title: Real-ROM regression on unmodified main: wizwarr and megaman both off their blessed goldens
description:
The real-ROM tier has TWO rows failing on an unmodified main (c514af3) that the
realrom-expected-baseline-fails memory records as GREEN. Neither is jitter and
neither is caused by the change that found them (grm-w3m).

EVIDENCE (the authorship test the memory prescribes: stash -u, rebuild with
build-and-test.sh check nes-banking, rm -rf build/realrom-cache, re-run
realrom-test.sh check --all --only megaman,wizwarr, then diff DUMP against DUMP
rather than dump against golden):

  wizwarr   baseline dump is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the with-grm-w3m dump.
            warnings 4 -> 7 in both. 100% pre-existing.
            Golden was blessed 2026-08-11 at b25f2db (grm-mej.3 increment 1) and
            the memory records it as passing since. The three added lines are
            honest-looking "bank state becomes unknown" warnings:
              81b3  call to bank-switch helper FUN_ee55, argument not recovered
              ffa1  call to bank-switch helper FUN_ee55, argument not recovered
              8631  mechanism write with a genuinely undeterminable value
            Note refs.intoOverlay and instrs.inOverlay are both 0 on this row, so
            the movement is purely in warning production.

  megaman   baseline refs 1745 / instrs 7427 / bankComments 160
            golden   refs 1704 / instrs 7429 / bankComments 156
            i.e. the BASELINE already differs from the golden by +41 refs and
            +4 bankComments. That is far outside the documented grm-g73 jitter
            signature (refs 1704<->1703, instrs 7429<->7431, opposite directions,
            bankComments/warnings CONSTANT). bankComments 156 is not an arbitrary
            number -- grm-p9y deliberately restored it by fixing the confidently
            wrong 'd571 bank -> 4' (grm-ii6). It is now 160 again.

WHY NOBODY NOTICED: the tier is opt-in and had not been run. build/realrom-cache/
.last-verified now reads c514af3 only because this session's run wrote it, so the
stamp cannot say when it last actually passed. This is precisely the grm-6kv /
grm-mu7 scenario CLAUDE.md's required-local-step rule exists to prevent -- a
synthetic gate that stays green while pinned real ROMs rot.

CANDIDATE COMMITS, not bisected. The memory's last green observation for these
rows is 2026-08-16; the NES-analysis-touching commits at/after that date are:
  b62b65b  Validate NES placement banks in each window's own units (grm-n5f)
  12afd36  Let explicit placement override partially-known bank fields (grm-v6o)
Both directly touch NES banking/placement and are the prime suspects. Also in
range but less likely: d9402c2 (FixSkipInstructions, a script), 7003adb
(isBasicStart, C64-only), and the grm-hap loader commits 22645ad/d000bac (CBM).

NEXT STEP: bisect over those candidates with realrom-test.sh check --all --only
megaman,wizwarr, rebuilding at each step (the rebuild is NOT optional -- see the
realrom-ab-needs-rebuild memory; skipping it fails silently in the direction you
want). Then decide per row whether the OUTPUT or the GOLDEN is wrong -- do not
assume the golden is stale. A moved bankComments line is a claim about a real
cartridge, and megaman's 156 has already been fought over once.
acceptance_criteria: Culprit commit identified for each row; per-row ruling on whether output or golden is wrong; both rows green or deliberately re-blessed with the reasoning recorded; realrom-expected-baseline-fails memory updated.
close_reason: Root-caused to the Ghidra 12.1.3 retarget (b3541b6) for both rows; owner chose option (a), leave failing and documented. Ongoing state tracked on grm-qp5x.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Additional measurement, 2026-08-21, refining the megaman half of this bead.

Four megaman runs (one at baseline c514af3, three with grm-w3m applied) gave, as
refs.intoOverlay / instrs.inOverlay / bankComments, with warnings pinned at 32:

  baseline      1745 / 7427 / 160
  with-fix #1   1745 / 7427 / 160   <- BYTE-IDENTICAL to the baseline dump
  with-fix #2   1744 / 7423 / 161
  with-fix #3   1742 / 7423 / 162

Two conclusions, which must not be conflated:

1. grm-w3m does NOT move megaman -- with-fix #1 reproduces the baseline dump
   byte for byte. That bead is cleared and committed (bc8a1e4).

2. megaman's run-to-run jitter is WIDER than realrom-expected-baseline-fails
   documents: that memory asserts bankComments and warnings are constant and only
   refs/instrs move by 1-2 in opposite directions. bankComments in fact varies
   160/161/162 and refs spans 1742-1745. Recorded as the new bd memory
   realrom-megaman-jitter-is-wider.

Consequence for THIS bead: the megaman row cannot be settled by a single run, and
no single run can be blessed -- the golden would capture one sample of a
multi-stable distribution. Whoever picks this up should establish the distribution
first (several runs at a fixed commit), and only then ask which value is correct.
The +40 refs / +4 bankComments gap against the golden is far outside the jitter
band, so the pre-existing regression is real and separate from the jitter.

wizwarr is unaffected by this refinement: it is deterministic here (byte-identical
across the with/without-fix A/B) and simply sits 3 warnings above its golden.
It is the cleaner row to bisect first.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
TRIAGE BEFORE MEASURING: both named suspects are exonerated by their own recorded
gate runs, and the candidate window moves later. Also, half this bead is a duplicate.

1. WIZWARR IS grm-qp5x, NOT A NEW REGRESSION. This bead's wizwarr evidence
   (warnings 4 -> 7; the added lines at 81b3 and ffa1, both "call to bank-switch
   helper FUN_ee55 whose bank argument could not be recovered", plus 8631 as an
   undeterminable mechanism write) is character-for-character the signature
   grm-qp5x recorded on 2026-08-20 from four runs on a fixed 12.1.3 build. That
   bead's ruling: 12.1.3 genuinely degraded bank recovery on this row, it never
   returns to 4, WHICH sites lose the argument varies run to run, and the row
   therefore CANNOT be blessed. So wizwarr is not unexplained -- it is a known,
   root-classified 12.1.3 regression with an open decision for the owner, and it
   should be tracked in one place rather than two.

2. BOTH NAMED SUSPECTS ARE EXONERATED BY THEIR OWN COMMIT MESSAGES. The bead
   named b62b65b (grm-n5f) and 12afd36 (grm-v6o) as prime suspects. Each records
   a full real-ROM run in its own gate line:
     b62b65b  "realrom-test.sh check --all pass=30 fail=1, the fail being smb3's
              documented baseline"
     12afd36  "realrom-test.sh check --all 30 pass / 1 fail / 0 skip, the fail
              being smb3's documented baseline on both its dimensions"
   Thirty passing rows with smb3 as the sole failure means megaman and wizwarr
   were both GREEN at b62b65b (2026-08-16 13:30), which is the later of the two.
   The regression is after that, not at either commit.

3. THE REVISED CANDIDATE WINDOW is therefore 2026-08-16 13:30 .. c514af3, and
   the 08-17/08-18 block in it is all SPC700 work that cannot touch NES analysis.
   What remains, most to least likely:
     b3541b6  Retarget to Ghidra 12.1.3          <-- prime suspect
     eae475e  MapCompiler: enforce layout/strategy contracts
     d000bac  descriptors: retire load_target and the unread formats keys
     22645ad  CBM loader: derive PRG placement metadata (CBM, unlikely to reach NES)
     6bc9b95  build: make `test` depend on buildMap/buildGdt
     8758b6f  banktest: nesuxhelpertest vectors (fixture only)
   bc8a1e4 (BoardBankAnalyzer rerun gating) is ruled out for megaman: the
   regression is already present at c514af3, which precedes it.

   b3541b6 leads because it is the one change already PROVEN to move one of these
   two rows (grm-qp5x, wizwarr), and because its only functional edit is
   gradle.properties' ghidraTargetVersion -- no source change at all. That makes
   the toolchain a cleanly toggleable single variable rather than something
   needing a bisect.

NEXT: measuring the 12.1.2-vs-12.1.3 A/B at unmodified HEAD (source held fixed,
ghidraTargetVersion flipped, rebuild + cache wipe per side, 3 runs at 12.1.2 and
2 at 12.1.3 because megaman's jitter is wide -- see realrom-megaman-jitter-is-wider).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEASURED: BOTH ROWS ARE THE 12.1.3 RETARGET (b3541b6). NOTHING OF OURS REGRESSED.

METHOD. Source held byte-identical at 591834e in a dedicated worktree; the ONLY
edit was gradle.properties' ghidraTargetVersion, which is legitimate as a single
toggle because b3541b6's only functional edit was that same line -- the retarget
changed no source. Rebuild (build-and-test.sh check nes-banking) and
rm -rf build/realrom-cache on every side and before every run, so no run was
served from cache and no side measured the other's build. Extension shas differ
between phases as required (fc652a5f at 12.1.2, faff4bad at 12.1.3), which is the
realrom-ab-needs-rebuild check passing.

RESULTS (megaman refs/instrs/bankComments/warnings; wizwarr warnings):

  12.1.2  run 1   1703 / 7431 / 156 / 32      wizwarr 4   PASS, diff EMPTY
  12.1.2  run 2   1703 / 7431 / 156 / 32      wizwarr 4   PASS, diff EMPTY
  12.1.2  run 3   1703 / 7431 / 156 / 32      wizwarr 4   PASS, diff EMPTY
  12.1.3  run 1   1744 / 7423 / 161 / 32      wizwarr 7   FAIL
  12.1.3  run 2   1744 / 7430 / 160 / 32      wizwarr 7   FAIL

WIZWARR: exact golden (warnings 4, empty diff) in all three 12.1.2 runs; the
known 81b3/8631/ffa1 regression in both 12.1.3 runs. Fully explained, fully
reversed by the toggle. This is grm-qp5x reproduced under control, and it is the
first time that bead's claim has been tested against 12.1.2 with the SAME source
rather than against the pre-retarget commit.

MEGAMAN: also fully explained -- 1703/7431/156 IS THE GOLDEN, at the row's other
documented jitter pole. Do not read the -1/+2 as residual drift. The measuring
agent reported it as a partial result ("something beyond the Ghidra version is
also in play") because it did not have grm-g73's signature; that reading is
wrong. realrom-expected-baseline-fails records the pole pair exactly:
"refs.intoOverlay 1704<->1703 and instrs.inOverlay 7429<->7431 moving in OPPOSITE
directions ... bankComments/warnings constant", re-verified 2026-08-16 as
"refs 1704->1703 and instrs 7431 vs 7429, opposite directions, every other line
identical". Measured: 1703 and 7431, opposite directions, bankComments 156 EXACT,
warnings 32 constant, no sample.* line moved. That is the criterion met on every
clause, not approximately.

So the megaman regression this bead was filed for -- refs +41, bankComments 156
-> 160 -- exists ONLY at 12.1.3 and vanishes at 12.1.2 with our code unchanged.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE JITTER MEMORY: the widened band in
realrom-megaman-jitter-is-wider (refs 1742-1745, instrs 7423-7427, bankComments
160-162) is ITSELF a 12.1.3 artifact. At 12.1.2 the row was byte-stable across
three fresh imports. 12.1.3 therefore did two separate things to megaman: moved
the central value (+40 refs, +4 bankComments) and widened the variance
(bankComments now varies 160/161, which it never did before). That is why the
band looked "wider than documented" -- it was measured entirely post-retarget.

ONE HONEST ANOMALY, NOT SMOOTHED OVER: three of three 12.1.2 runs landed on 1703,
the MINORITY pole. grm-g73 measured the split 8/2 in favour of 1704 over ten
fresh imports, which makes 3/3 on the minority side a ~0.8% outcome. Either the
split has shifted, or it is sensitive to machine/timing state that differs here.
It does not affect the ruling -- both values are inside the documented two-pole
set and every other line matches golden -- but it should not be recorded as
"12.1.2 is stable at 1703" on the strength of three runs. The safe statement is
that 12.1.2 reproduces the golden's dump apart from the known flap.

RULING PER ROW (acceptance criterion 2): THE GOLDENS ARE RIGHT AND THE 12.1.3
OUTPUT IS WRONG, for both rows. This is not the usual "which side is stale"
judgement call, because the goldens are not merely plausible -- they are
reproducible on demand, exactly, from unchanged source. Neither row should be
blessed:
  - wizwarr would pin degraded output (lost bank-argument recovery at helper call
    sites), and grm-qp5x already established there is no stable value to pin.
  - megaman would pin BOTH a degraded value and a newly unstable one: bankComments
    moved 161 vs 160 between two consecutive runs, so a blessed golden would fail
    against itself.

STATUS: both rows are now known-baseline fails ATTRIBUTABLE TO THE TOOLCHAIN, not
to this repo. That extends grm-qp5x's open owner decision from one row to two:
(a) leave failing and documented until upstream responds, (b) root-cause as tmnt
was, (c) pin the rows' analysis options to make them version-independent.
Referred to the owner; (a) remains the state by default.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-22: OPTION (a) -- LEAVE BOTH ROWS FAILING AND DOCUMENTED.

The three options were (a) leave failing until upstream moves, (b) root-cause as
tmnt was, (c) pin the rows' analysis options to make them version-independent.
The owner chose (a) for now. (b) and (c) are not rejected, only not scheduled;
they stay available on grm-qp5x, which now owns the ongoing state for BOTH rows.

WHY (b) IS POOR VALUE HERE, recorded so the option is not re-litigated from
scratch. The tmnt campaign (grm-xljh, 2026-08-19) is the precedent and it cost:
a full 874 MB install clone, a rebuilt Decompiler.jar with the 12.1.2
DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer swapped in, and an instrumented build to supply a
positive control -- and it still ended at "the native decompile.exe, BY
ELIMINATION", not proven positively. The next step there is a C++ bisect needing
a native Ghidra build, and the obvious shortcut is blocked: PcodeOp.java:442
changed writeSignedInteger(ATTRIB_CODE, opcode) to writeOpcode(...), so the
Java<->native wire encoding moved this release and a 12.1.2 decompile.exe driven
by 12.1.3 Java would speak a different protocol -- a null result there is
uninterpretable.

AND THE ENDPOINT THAT MADE tmnt TRACTABLE IS NOT AVAILABLE HERE. tmnt could be
blessed because 12.1.3 was MIXED rather than simply worse on that ROM (8d8f's
bogus targets 1898/3a9d/a901/e065 gone, 894e newly resolving four sane targets,
bad-instruction bookmarks 50 -> 31) AND because it was deterministic --
byte-identical across three runs, so a stable value existed to pin. Neither of
these rows is deterministic at 12.1.3. So even a successful root cause would not
end in a bless; it would end in an upstream report. That inverts the usual
cost/benefit and is the substance of the (a) decision.

WHAT THIS BEAD DELIVERED, against its acceptance criteria:
 - Culprit identified per row: b3541b6, the Ghidra 12.1.3 retarget, for BOTH.
   Not either of the two commits the bead nominated -- b62b65b and 12afd36 each
   record "realrom-test.sh check --all pass=30 fail=1, smb3 only" in their own
   gate lines, so both rows were green at the later of them.
 - Per-row ruling: the GOLDENS ARE RIGHT, the 12.1.3 OUTPUT IS WRONG. Unusually
   firm for this project -- the goldens are not merely plausible, they are
   reproducible on demand, exactly, from unchanged source.
 - Rows neither green nor re-blessed: deliberately left failing per (a), which is
   the third disposition the criteria did not anticipate.
 - Memories updated: realrom-megaman-jitter-is-wider corrected (its wide band is a
   12.1.3 artifact and its "real pre-existing regression" claim is withdrawn), and
   realrom-12-1-3-toolchain-fails added as the authoritative row list.
 - CLAUDE.md's real-ROM section corrected: it claimed the curated manifest has no
   expected failure and that megaman merely flaps at ~20%. megaman IS curated and
   now fails every run on 12.1.3.

EXPECTED STEADY STATE going forward: realrom-test.sh check --all is pass=29
fail=2 (megaman, wizwarr), plus dodge's grm-g73 flap on top. A bare curated
`check` now has one deterministic expected failure again (megaman).

CLOSING. The investigative question is answered; the residual is the upstream
toolchain question, tracked on grm-qp5x.

title: Let explicit placement override partially-known bank fields
description: From docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-03. BoardBankAnalyzer treats a multi-bit bank field as known when any bit is known, fills unknown bits from initial state, and wrongly suppresses the user override.
acceptance_criteria: Partial multi-bit knowledge uses the override; full knowledge wins over it; unknown-without-override remains conservative; relevant JUnit and E2E gates pass.
notes:
Priority review 2026-08-11: confirmed, kept P1. Cheapest of the four P1s -- a one-line fix.

LINE NUMBERS IN THE REVIEW DOC HAVE DRIFTED. QR-03 cites BoardBankAnalyzer.java:3647-3658, which at HEAD is describeBits(). The actual code is at line 3764-3765:

    boolean bankKnown =
        (inState.knownMask() & instance.bankField().positionedMask()) != 0;

Correct test is '== instance.bankField().positionedMask()'. The docstring immediately above it (lines 3760-3763) already states the intended contract -- 'flow always wins when it knows' -- so the code contradicts its own comment.

General note for anyone working the QR-* beads: the review was written at 4af9bfe and HEAD has moved, so grep for the cited EXPRESSION, not the cited line number.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Fixed. `BoardBankAnalyzer.java` — the predicate at the reference-retargeting site tested
`(inState.knownMask() & bankField().positionedMask()) != 0` ("intersects") where the
contract is `== positionedMask()` ("contains"). Confirmed the notes' diagnosis; the line
had drifted to 3829 at the time of the fix.

## Shape of the change

Rather than patching the one expression, added `FieldSpec.fullyKnownIn(BankState)` and
routed all three users of the idiom through it:

- the override site (the DEFECT — was `!= 0`),
- `impossibleBank`'s mode-field gate (was already correct, open-coded),
- `checkBank`'s field gate (was already correct, open-coded).

Two correct copies plus one wrong copy of the same bit algebra is the condition under
which a fourth gets written wrong, so the predicate now has exactly one definition.
`FieldSpec` went `private record` -> package-private solely so the pure-JUnit tier can
construct one; nothing outside `BoardBankAnalyzer` uses it.

## Tests

New `src/test/java/retromachines/FieldSpecKnownTest.java`, 6 tests, pure JUnit (no
`ghidra.*` import, same discipline as `BankStateTest`). The load-bearing one is
`everyProperSubsetOfKnownBitsIsNotKnown`, which enumerates all 15 proper submasks of a
4-bit field via `sub = (sub - 1) & mask` — under the old predicate every one of those
returned "known". Also pins that a 1-bit field behaves identically under both forms,
which is exactly why the wrong test survived.

## Gates

- `build-and-test.sh check` (full): 52 pass / 0 fail, SUITE OK. NO golden moved, so the
  `needs-bless-review` label had nothing to review — this lands with zero golden churn.
- `realrom-test.sh check --all`: 30 pass / 1 fail / 0 skip. The single fail is `smb3`, the
  documented expected-baseline row, matching its signature on BOTH dimensions (warnings
  50->52 with FUN_c542 at 867b/ac6d and c6b5/c6c5 as pure sample-cap slide; plus the
  `+count symbols 18` frozen-golden drift). `megaman` and `dodge`, the two jitter rows,
  both PASSed.
- `gradle test`: green.

## SCOPE NOTE — what was verified, and what was not

The fix is CORRECT AND INERT, not a repair of observed misbehaviour. No fixture and no
real ROM changed output. A/B probe (details in grm-iqq) established why: no strategy
currently exercised produces a PARTIALLY-known bank field at a retarget site, so the old
`!= 0` predicate never actually fired wrong in anything we run. Both endpoints of the
knowledge lattice — fully known, fully unknown — behave identically before and after.

So this closes a real contradiction between the code and its own docstring, and pre-empts
a wrong answer the moment a partial state becomes reachable (smb3's MMC3 dumps already
show partial `r6`/`r7` forms). It does not fix a bug anyone has observed. Filed grm-iqq
for the E2E coverage gap and the route to a genuine partial-state fixture.

Acceptance criteria: partial-multi-bit-uses-override and full-knowledge-wins are covered
at the predicate level by the new JUnit; unknown-without-override is untouched code path
(still falls through to the `effective` initial-state fallback); JUnit and E2E gates pass.

title: Validate NES placement overrides in each window's bank units
description: From docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-02. NesRomLoader compares all placement values with the iNES 16 KiB PRG-bank count even when descriptors such as MMC3 use 8 KiB banks.
acceptance_criteria: A 32 KiB MMC3 fixture accepts banks 0-3 and rejects 4; GUI and headless validation agree; existing board behavior remains green.
notes:
Priority review 2026-08-11: confirmed, kept P1. NesRomLoader.java:315 is 'pair.getValue() >= prgBanks' with a message that literally says '16K PRG banks', applied to every window regardless of that window's own unit size. A 32 KiB MMC3 image has prgBanks==2, so banks 2-3 are rejected even though the loader can realize them. Real and user-visible.

SCOPE WARNING: the review's implementation guidance ('derive the legal bank set per named window from its compiled maps expression, window length, layout mode, state-field width, and actual PRG byte size') is a much larger build than the defect warrants. The defect is that the divisor is the iNES 16 KiB unit instead of the window's own length. Prefer computing the per-window bank count from window length and PRG byte size; only reach for the full maps-expression derivation if that proves insufficient.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Fixed in b62b65b.

Root cause was a units mismatch, not a bounds bug: the bank in a window:bank pair is a
banking.state FIELD value fed to that window's maps: expression, and it was compared with the
iNES container's 16 KiB PRG-bank count.

Did NOT use the scope note's suggested "window length / PRG size" divisor -- MMC1 disproves it.
Its prg_mode 0 W8000 is a 32 KiB window, but the expression ((prg_bank >> 1) * 0x8000) still
takes bank values in 16 KiB units, so window length and bank unit are independent. Instead
reused the predicate the loader's own realization loops already apply (NesRomLoader
realizeInvariantWindow / realizeVaryingWindows): evaluate the expression over the field's whole
value range, keep the results that land a whole window inside the image. That is not the
review's big "derive from maps expression + layout mode + state-field width + PRG size" build --
evalExpr/referencedFields/findField already existed, so the new DescriptorSupport.placeableBanks
is ~35 lines. Its payoff over any divisor rule: validation accepts a bank exactly when the load
can create a block for it, by construction rather than by agreement.

Behaviour changes beyond the bead:
- An override naming a fixed window (NROM PRG_LO, MMC3 WE000) is now rejected with "holds no
  switchable bank" instead of silently accepted. It was always inert -- BoardBankAnalyzer applies
  overrides only where instance.bankField() != null -- so only the message changes. No fixture or
  realrom manifest row uses one.
- The out-of-range message now names the window and the actual placeable set
  ("placeable banks: 0-3") instead of a container bank count.

Acceptance criteria, and one deviation:
- "32 KiB MMC3 fixture accepts banks 0-3 and rejects 4" -- covered by NesPlacementValidationTest
  (unit chunk) rather than a new E2E golden ROM. Reason: the headless harness can only express
  successful imports, so the "rejects 4" half -- the actual regression risk -- is not
  representable there; a rejection makes the import produce no blocks, which the harness reports
  as a generic row FAIL. The test drives the SHIPPED descriptors (read via the grm.moduleDir
  system property the test task already sets) through the real placeableBanks and the real
  validator, so it is the same code path minus descriptor loading. Say if an E2E fixture is
  wanted anyway.
- "GUI and headless validation agree" -- both routes call one placementError; only the private
  descriptor-loading wrapper differs.
- "existing board behavior remains green" -- see gates below. nesmmc1overridetest (W8000:5 on a
  128 KiB MMC1) still validates and its golden is byte-identical.

Gates: build-and-test.sh check SUITE OK (all chunks). realrom-test.sh check --all pass=30 fail=1
skip=0; the fail is smb3's documented baseline (count warnings 50->52 plus the frozen golden's
missing symbols block, per realrom-expected-baseline-fails / -smb3-symbols, blocked on grm-67g).
dodge and megaman both PASSed this run. Staleness stamp now at HEAD.

title: Never bless a banktest candidate whose criteria failed
description: From docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-01. run-banktest.sh copies fresh and cached candidates into expected/ before/after observing SUITE FAIL, so a failing run can overwrite a known-good oracle.
acceptance_criteria: Failing fresh and cached candidates leave golden files byte-identical and return nonzero; passing check/review/bless remains supported; final writes are atomic.
notes:
Priority review 2026-08-11: confirmed verbatim, kept P1. run-banktest.sh:311-314 sets fail=1 and falls through; :325-328 copies into expected/ anyway. Cache path is worse -- :256 copies BEFORE the criteria check at :258-261.

IMPORTANT context the review did not surface: this is DELIBERATE, not an oversight. The comment at run-banktest.sh:244-245 states the intent -- 'Mirrors the non-cache bless below: copy the candidate regardless, but flag the suite if its cached criteria failed.' Someone chose to always produce a candidate for inspection. Whoever fixes this is overturning a design decision, so confirm the intent with the user rather than treating it as a plain bug. The argument for changing it: bless is the only thing between a bad run and a committed oracle, and CLAUDE.md's entire gate discipline rests on goldens being trustworthy.

Mitigations that already exist (and are why this is not P0): bless is a manual command, it prints FAIL, it exits nonzero, and the change is visible in git diff before commit.

The atomic-write half of the fix is shared with grm-z34, which now depends on this bead.
close_reason: Ruled and implemented: bless fails closed on criteria failure, with --force-criteria override; both bless routes now share bless_candidate(); atomic temp+rename. Full gate green (39 fixtures SUITE PASS, SUITE OK).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: Parked as a DECISION in docs/human-research-todo.md section 4 (2026-08-11). Not agent work: the bless-on-failure behavior is deliberate per run-banktest.sh:244-245, so fixing it overturns a design decision rather than a defect. The todo item lays out both cases. Do not implement until the user rules.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RULED 2026-08-12 by the user: fail closed, with an explicit --force-criteria override. Implemented.

Key correction to this bead's framing: the 'deliberate design decision' is real but was made about a DIFFERENT harness. The unconditional bless dates to the suite's first commit (159ce7e, 2026-07-08); the candidate cache arrived two weeks later (c915ec2, grm-lne) and its comment only says it MIRRORS the older behavior. Nobody ever weighed bless-over-FAIL against the check-then-bless cache workflow.

Two findings closed the argument:
1. The stated rationale ('always produce a candidate for inspection') was never load-bearing. check already writes $WORK/<name>.dump and prints the full diff -u, and since grm-lne also persists the candidate + a .crit verdict in build/banktest-cache. Diagnosing a failure never required overwriting expected/.
2. The golden carries NO record of the verdict -- the dump is only the BANKDUMP section, CRITERION/SUITE lines are extracted separately. So a blessed-over-a-failure oracle is byte-indistinguishable from a good one, which makes 'visible in git diff' false as a mitigation: git diff shows only that the dump moved, which is what bless is FOR.

Also noted: bless was never 'bless no matter what'. status!=0 and missing BANKDUMP already returned before the copy; only SUITE FAIL fell through. The fix makes the three cases uniform.

Implementation: extracted a single bless_candidate() helper that BOTH the cached fast path and the fresh-import path call, because the two had already drifted in four ways (only cached showed the golden diff; they flagged criteria on opposite sides of the copy; only cached printed the SUITE verdict line; only cached announced a missing golden). Parity now holds by construction. Refusal is per-row (good rows still bless), sets fail=1, and is named in an end-of-run 'REFUSED to bless' summary. Missing or empty .crit counts as failure (fail closed; the cache is disposable). --force-criteria blesses anyway, exits 0, and reports every forced row; rejected in check mode by both front ends. Fresh path now also prints the SUITE line (same regex that writes .crit).

Atomic temp+rename included, so this bead's own 'final writes are atomic' criterion is met for run_one's golden writes. grm-z34 retains only its remaining non-run_one write sites.

Verified: unit-level test of bless_candidate (refuse/force/create, no temp leakage); end-to-end on petscii-strings through the cached route with a tampered .crit -- REFUSED left the golden byte-identical and exited 1, --force-criteria blessed and reported. Docs updated in docs/testing.md and CLAUDE.md; section-4 item retired to the Answered table.

title: [BUG] Helper with TWO mechanism writes ($8000 select + $8001 data): argumentSurvivesPrologue anchors on firstSite, killing smb3's r7=27/26 (regressed by d612bff, not 788f09b)
description:
REGRESSION shipped on main by 788f09b (grm-2dr increment 1, pass-through wrapper helpers). Found
via grm-bj6; proven by human disassembly 2026-08-09. smb3's golden is the CORRECT baseline and is
deliberately unblessed.

THE DEFECT IN ONE LINE: inside an MMC3 helper that performs BOTH halves of the two-write protocol,
argument recovery attributes the register-SELECT constant written to $8000 to the BANK field
written at $8001.

    ffc2:  LDA #$47 ; STA $0721 ; STA $8000 ; LDA $0720 ; STA $8001

$8000 takes the select/mode byte ($47 -> register 7, prg_mode 1); $8001 takes the bank, which
here comes from RAM shadow $0720, NOT from a register argument. Production now reports
r7 = $47 & $3F = 7.

PROOF, from the dump's own 'known:' bit fields:
    ca23 OLD  011011 = 27 = $1B      ca23 NEW  000111 = 7
    ca2e OLD  011010 = 26 = $1A      ca2e NEW  000111 = 7   (byte-identical to ca23)
    $47 & $3F = 7

CORROBORATION:
  - Two distinct call sites collapsing to ONE value = value taken from the helper's own constant.
  - Built-in control: c5f5/c9f7 are LDA #$47 ; STA $8000 ; LDA #$1a ; STA $8001 (direct, no
    shadow update) and are reported correctly as r7=26=$1A. So $1A is a real bank here and the old
    ca2e=26 is consistent; 7 matches no call-site constant anywhere.
  - The PRE-regression recovery had a correct mechanism: 'LDA #bank ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2' is
    grm-mu7's argumentCells/argumentReloadSource save-restore model reading the shadow. It worked.

BLAST RADIUS on smb3: refs.intoOverlay 846->822, instrs.inOverlay 4263->4173 (a 90-instruction
LOSS -- wrong bank retargets into a wrong/absent overlay), c631 gains a bogus 'r7=7? via FUN_ffc2',
f894 loses a bankcomment. Any MMC3 title whose helper carries both writes is exposed; smb3 is
simply where it was caught.

WHY IT PROBABLY BIT NOW: 788f09b re-keys a helper's model onto a predecessor, and
argumentSurvivesPrologue walks LINEARLY BY ADDRESS with no reference to function boundaries. Note
ffbf (JSR $ffd1, then FALLS THROUGH into ffc2) is address-contiguous with ffc2 and is exactly the
pass-through shape that pass admits. A linear walk that now starts earlier, or a model re-keyed
onto ffbf, can reach the LDA #$47 and treat it as the argument. THAT IS A HYPOTHESIS, not the
diagnosis -- confirm in code before fixing.

WHAT A FIX MUST PRESERVE: the select byte and the bank byte are DIFFERENT operands of the same
protocol. Recovering select=7,prg_mode=1 from $47 is CORRECT and must keep working; only its leak
into the r7 field is wrong. And when the bank genuinely comes from a shadow the caller wrote, the
shadow model must win -- silence is better than a confident wrong number.

ACCEPTANCE: smb3 realrom check PASSES against the CURRENT (unblessed) golden, i.e. ca23 r7=27,
ca2e r7=26, refs 846, instrs 4263, no bogus c631 comment. Then close grm-bj6. Do NOT bless smb3 to
make this green.

REPRO: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --only smb3 H:/emulators/nes/roms
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DIRECT PROOF AT THE CALL SITE, 2026-08-09 (human, follow-up to the trace above). The two call
sites are preceded by exactly the shadow-establishing idiom:

    ca23:  LDA #$1b ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2      ->  $1B = 27
    ca2e:  LDA #$1a ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2      ->  $1A = 26

That is no longer an inference. The old golden's r7=27 and r7=26 are literally the call-site
constants, recovered through shadow $0720 exactly as grm-mu7's argumentCells/argumentReloadSource
model is designed to do. The regression replaced two CORRECT, DISTINCT, call-site-sourced values
with one wrong constant lifted from the helper's own body ($47 & $3F = 7).

This also pins the shape of a correct fix. The recovery that must be restored is:
  caller writes an immediate to the argument CELL ($0720)  ->  helper reloads that cell  ->  helper
  stores it to $8001.
The value the fix must NOT follow is the immediate feeding the OTHER mechanism write in the same
helper body (#$47 -> $8000). Both writes are mechanism writes; only one carries the bank. Whatever
change 788f09b made to how the argument-bearing load is chosen, it now prefers the $8000 chain
over the $8001 chain, and the $8001 chain is the one that terminates in the caller's constant.

A fix that restores 27/26 by disabling wrapper recognition for MMC3 would be wrong for the same
reason: the target is picking the right one of two mechanism writes, not avoiding the helper.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
BLAME CORRECTED BY BISECTION, 2026-08-09. The regression is d612bff (grm-mu7, 'Decline a helper
argument the helper's own prologue clobbers'), NOT 788f09b. This bead's original 'why it probably
bit now' hypothesis is REFUTED -- do not spend time on it, and do not investigate ffbf's
pass-through admission, which is also cleared.

Bisection, each commit BUILT AND INSTALLED per-worktree rather than measured against a shared
install (the shared %APPDATA% install was stale and produced false reproductions at every commit
until each was built -- worth remembering for any future bisect in this repo):
    ce1dfc9 golden blessed              PASS
    c7278ae grm-hum arg recovery        PASS
    50f2c2c grm-nju thunks              PASS
    d612bff grm-mu7 prologue decline    FAIL, r7=7   <-- introduced here
    ea2df90 / 0083b3a / 788f09b / f8cd931            FAIL, r7=7
788f09b's diff never touches findHelpers, argumentSurvivesPrologue or recoverCallArgument.
d612bff's own commit message names the exact shape it was built for -- 'A helper that reloads the
bank from RAM breaks that assumption' -- which is precisely ffc2. It declined too much.

MECHANISM, as far as it is proven: findHelpers merges ffc2's two mechanism writes into ONE
HelperModel with firstSite = the SELECT write (STA $8000, min address) and switchSite = the DATA
write (STA $8001, max address). argumentSurvivesPrologue walks entry..firstSite, so it walks
ffc2..ffc7 -- which begins with LDA #$47 and therefore clobbers A immediately, and the guard
declines. That verdict is CORRECT for the select write and WRONG for the data write: the caller's
byte does survive to $8001, via LDA $0720 reloading the shadow the caller wrote. One firstSite
anchor cannot express 'this deposit's consumption point is switchSite, not firstSite' -- a
distinction that only arises for select-data's two-write shape, since register-write and
serial-shift helpers consume at firstSite genuinely.

STILL OPEN, and a fix must explain it: a declined argument yields UNKNOWN, which should surface as
a warning, not a confident value. Production emits r7=7 with ALL SIX r7 bits marked KNOWN. So the 7
arrives by some path other than a discarded argValue -- candidates being constState (line 685
serves helper.constState() at every call site, which would explain both sites collapsing to one
number), or StoredValueScanner resolving LDA $0720 to $47 (note the helper stores $47 to $0721
immediately before, and $0721 is ADJACENT to $0720). Under investigation.

DETERMINISM CONFIRMED, so single measurements are trustworthy here: two runs of
'check --only smb3' with separate REALROM_WORK_DIRs gave byte-identical dumps (fe66a525...),
matching grm-bj6's earlier two-full-set-run observation. smb3 is NOT part of the grm-4nr/grm-g73
bistable family; do not treat a single smb3 result as suspect.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FULLY DIAGNOSED 2026-08-09. It is a TWO-COMMIT INTERACTION, and the earlier
'blame d612bff' correction is itself half the story. Neither commit is wrong for the case it was
built for; together on a two-write helper they ship a confident wrong bank.

FIRST, the branch question is settled. I had doubted that ffc2's two writes reach findHelpers'
MERGE branch (:914) rather than its DEGRADE branch (:943), since a select write and a data write
own different bits. They DO merge, because effectMask does not come from the individual write --
BoardBankAnalyzer:675 constructs every SwitchResult with matchedMechanism.effectMask(), the
MECHANISM's declared mask, which is identical for both writes. So ffc2 gets ONE HelperModel with:
    firstSite  = STA $8000  (min address, the SELECT write)
    switchSite = STA $8001  (max address, the DATA write)
    argReg     = 'A', constState = null (the two sites' results disagree, so :915 nulls it)

STEP 1 -- d612bff (grm-mu7) LOST the correct value. recoverCallArgument:1744 runs
argumentSurvivesPrologue over entry..firstSite, i.e. ffc2..ffc7. The very first instruction is
LDA #$47, which clobbers A, so the guard declines. That verdict is RIGHT for the select write and
WRONG for the data write: the caller's byte does reach $8001, through LDA $0720.

    (Note how 27/26 were originally recovered -- not by any shadow model. The idiom
    'LDA #$1b ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2' leaves A STILL HOLDING $1b at the call, and argReg is
    'A', so the plain caller-register scan read it. Correct here, but only because the idiom
    happens to leave the value in A -- which is exactly the unsound assumption d612bff set out to
    kill, and Bionic Commando's FUN_dca8 is the case where it really is wrong.)

STEP 2 -- 0083b3a (grm-cxb) turned the loss into a confident WRONG value. It added
valueSuppliedInsideHelper (:2014), so a declined argument no longer stays unknown:
    recoverCallArgument:1746   local = valueSuppliedInsideHelper(program, helper, reg, stateMask);
and that method resolves the register AT firstSite (:2016-2024). For Kid Icarus's FUN_eb07 --
its motivating case, a serial-shift chain where every site carries the same byte -- firstSite is
exactly right. For ffc2 it reads A at STA $8000, which is $47, and the deposit then happens at
switchSite via SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy's odd/data branch: setFieldFromByte(empty, r7, $47),
and r7 is 6 bits wide, so $47 & $3F = 7. That is the confident 7, with all six bits known.

    So the earlier bisect line 'd612bff FAIL, r7=7' conflates two different failure modes.
    valueSuppliedInsideHelper did not exist at d612bff, so at THAT commit the sites should warn
    with an unknown bank, not report 7. The r7=7 signature can only start at 0083b3a.

STALE JAVADOC to fix alongside: recoverCallArgument's javadoc (:1719) still says a failure
'withholds argValue (leaving it unknown)'. 0083b3a made that false and did not update it -- which
is very likely why this went unnoticed.

THE GENERAL DEFECT, stated once: valueSuppliedInsideHelper resolves at firstSite while the deposit
consumes at switchSite. For every single-value mechanism those coincide, so the bug is invisible.
select-data is the first shape where one helper carries TWO mechanism writes with DIFFERENT
values, and there firstSite's value belongs to the OTHER write.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SOUNDNESS HALF IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED 2026-08-09 (NOT committed pending a decision, see below).

THE CHANGE. valueSuppliedInsideHelper read the argument register at firstSite; which site to read
is now the STRATEGY's call, because the two multi-site shapes want OPPOSITE answers:
  BankSwitchStrategy.suppliesHelperValueAtFirstSite()  default TRUE  -- unchanged for everyone
  SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy overrides to            FALSE         -- read at switchSite
A global switch to switchSite would have been wrong: serial-shift's Kid Icarus FUN_eb07 does
LDA #$0F / STA $9FFF / LSR A / STA $9FFF / ..., so the committed byte is live at the FIRST write
and the last write's A has already been shifted away. Also fixed recoverCallArgument's javadoc,
which still claimed a prologue decline 'withholds argValue (leaving it unknown)' -- false since
0083b3a, and very likely why this defect went unnoticed.

RESULT ON smb3: the confident wrong r7=7 is GONE. But the correct 27/26 do NOT come back, and
coverage falls further than the broken build's:
                    golden(correct)   broken     with this fix
  refs.intoOverlay        846           822          807
  instrs.inOverlay       4263          4173         4088
  bankComments            104           102          102
ca23/ca2e now produce NO comment at all. That is expected and is the honest answer for THIS fix:
the value at $8001 comes from LDA $0720, a RAM read, which is unresolvable from inside the helper
(the same decline Bionic Commando's FUN_dca8 gets, by the same rule).

SO THE FIX IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. Restoring 27/26 needs a capability this engine does not
have: the caller writes the bank to shadow $0720 and the helper reloads it, so the value crosses
the call boundary THROUGH MEMORY. argumentCells/argumentReloadSource already model exactly this
save/restore shape but only WITHIN one helper body (BoardBankAnalyzer:1881-1971) -- a cell enters
the set when the HELPER stores to it. Here the store is in the CALLER. The missing piece is an
INBOUND argument cell: helper reloads reg from cell C before switchSite, C is never written inside
the helper, therefore C carries the caller's value; then resolve C's stored value at the call site
(LDA #$1b / STA $0720 -> 27). That is squarely grm-mej's charter ('everything still unrecovered
is unrecovered because the bank value passes through MEMORY or the STACK first').

COLLATERAL, and it needs a human. Full realrom --all: pass=22 fail=3 skip=6.
  smb3      expected, above.
  ff1       NOT mine -- refs +33 / instrs +44, count lines only, exactly grm-4nr's documented
            signature, and ff1 is MMC1/serial-shift which this change does not touch.
  rcransom  MINE, and unresolved. Two bank comments become two warnings:
              f1d0  'select=6,prg_mode=0,r6=0,r7=1 via FUN_ff07'  -> warning
              f21d  'select=6,prg_mode=0,r6=0,r7=1 via FUN_ff29'  -> warning
            Same board (MMC3), same strategy, same 'via FUN_xxx' shape, and the values were
            produced by the SAME firstSite path that shipped smb3's wrong 7 -- so the strong prior
            is that they were wrong or accidental too. But that is a prior, not evidence. Deciding
            it needs someone to read what ff07/ff29 do with their select and data writes; it is
            the identical question smb3's trace answered, on a title whose helpers grm-8iy.4
            already flags as having zero constant-arg call sites.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
HELD, NOT COMMITTED, 2026-08-09 -- user decision: nothing lands until rcransom's f1d0/f21d are read
by a human, because that measurement decides whether this change removes two WRONG comments or two
RIGHT ones.

The soundness change is in the working tree, uncommitted, and saved to build/grm-67g-soundness.patch
(gitignored, so it survives a clean checkout of tracked files but NOT a 'git clean -x'). Three files,
67 insertions / 7 deletions. It is reconstructable from scratch from the description in the previous
comment if the patch is lost -- it is small and the design rationale matters more than the diff:

  1. BankSwitchStrategy: new default method suppliesHelperValueAtFirstSite() returning TRUE, with
     the javadoc explaining why the two multi-site shapes need opposite answers (serial-shift's Kid
     Icarus FUN_eb07 re-derives by LSR from the first write; select-data's two writes hold different
     values).
  2. SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy: overrides it to FALSE.
  3. BoardBankAnalyzer.valueSuppliedInsideHelper: reads the register at firstSite or switchSite per
     that method instead of always firstSite. Plus the stale-javadoc fix on recoverCallArgument
     (:1719 still claimed a decline leaves argValue unknown -- untrue since 0083b3a, and probably
     why this was never caught).

DO NOT land it as-is on the assumption rcransom's two comments were artifacts. That is a strong
prior -- same board, same strategy, same firstSite path -- but the whole reason smb3 got a correct
verdict is that someone read the ROM instead of reasoning from shape. Give rcransom the same.

Gate before landing, whichever way rcransom goes: full realrom --all must show exactly the expected
set. Today it is pass=22 fail=3 skip=6, where ff1 is grm-4nr jitter (refs +33 / instrs +44, count
lines only, and ff1 is MMC1 so this change cannot touch it), smb3 is intended, and rcransom is the
open question.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SOUNDNESS FIX LANDED 2026-08-09, unblocked by grm-1fv. The bead stays OPEN: this removes the wrong
answers but does not restore smb3's correct ones.

grm-1fv's human trace turned rcransom from feared collateral into a SECOND correctness win.
FUN_ff07/FUN_ff29 are interrupt-exit restore routines writing R6/R7 from shadows $fc/$fd and
rewriting $8000 from $ff/$fb, so their old comments were wrong twice over -- a select value taken
from the FIRST of several select writes, and stale r6/r7 claimed as fully known across a helper
that overwrites both. Warnings are the honest answer there. rcransom BLESSED accordingly; it now
passes.

STATE OF THE REAL-ROM TIER after the fix (full --all, run twice):
  rcransom  PASS, stable
  smb3      FAIL, INTENDED -- its golden pins the correct 27/26 and stays the target
  megaman / ff1 / rcproam  flap between runs, the known grm-4nr/grm-g73 bistable set; one run
                           showed ff1 alone, the next megaman+rcproam. Not attributable here.
Full gate (build-and-test.sh check): SUITE OK.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD -- the inbound argument cell. smb3's ca23/ca2e now produce no comment
rather than a wrong one, and refs/instrs sit at 807/4088 against the golden's 846/4263. Recovering
27/26 needs the caller's value to be followed ACROSS the call through RAM:

    caller:  LDA #$1b ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2
    helper:  ... LDA $0720 ; STA $8001        <- switchSite

argumentCells/argumentReloadSource (BoardBankAnalyzer:1881-1971) already model exactly this
save/restore shape, but a cell only enters the set when the HELPER stores to it. The missing rule:
if the helper reloads argReg from cell C before switchSite and C is never written inside the helper,
then C carries the CALLER's value -- so resolve C's stored value at the call site instead of
scanning for argReg there. Note that also fixes the reason the old recovery was fragile: it worked
only because the idiom happens to leave the bank in A.

DO NOT bless smb3 to close this. The acceptance is unchanged: smb3 PASSES against the current
golden (ca23 r7=27, ca2e r7=26, refs 846, instrs 4263).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
INCREMENT 2 LANDED 2026-08-09: the inbound argument cell. smb3's r7=27/26 are RECOVERED.

MEASURED, smb3 realrom check against the current (still unblessed) golden:
    refs.intoOverlay   807 -> 846   MATCHES golden
    instrs.inOverlay  4088 -> 4263  MATCHES golden
    bankComments       102 -> 104   MATCHES golden
    ca23  r7=27 via FUN_ffc2        MATCHES golden
    ca2e  r7=26 via FUN_ffc2        MATCHES golden
    c631  still a warning, no bogus comment   MATCHES golden
Every acceptance item in this bead's description is met. Nothing was blessed to get there.

THE RULE. If the helper's LAST write to argReg before its value-consuming site is a plain load
from cell C, and nothing between the entry and that site could have written C, then C still holds
what the CALLER put there -- so resolve C at the call site instead of scanning for argReg there.

  BoardBankAnalyzer.inboundArgumentCell   the proof inside the helper (package-private for JUnit)
  BoardBankAnalyzer.helperValueSite       extracted from valueSuppliedInsideHelper; now two consumers
  StoredValueScanner.callerCellValue      the other half, at the call site
  StoredValueScanner.writesMemory         private -> package-private (the union matters here)
  recoverCallArgument                     the decline branch now has THREE outcomes, tried in order:
                                          caller's cell, helper's own constant, unknown

It is the exact DUAL of argumentSurvivesPrologue's argumentCells: that set admits C only when the
HELPER stores argReg into it, this admits C only when the helper never does. Mutually exclusive by
construction, which is why the ordering in recoverCallArgument is not a judgement call.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S FIRST COMMENT, which the 21:16 comment already suspected. The
pre-regression 27/26 were NOT the argumentCells/argumentReloadSource shadow model. Before d612bff
there was no prologue guard at all, so `local` was simply the caller-side REGISTER scan, and
"LDA #$1b / STA $0720 / JSR $ffc2" happens to leave $1b still in A. The shadow was never followed.
This increment did not restore a mechanism; it built the one that was always missing, and it keeps
working when the caller's A is clobbered -- which the new fixture proves with a decoy.

BLAST RADIUS, measured not argued:
  full synthetic gate (build-and-test.sh check)   SUITE OK
  nes-banking with the analyzer change ALONE      all 13 fixtures BYTE-IDENTICAL
  c64/pet/c128/basic chunks                       untouched
  realrom --all                                   pass=23 fail=2 (was pass=22 fail=3)
  Not one of the ~15 other FUN_ffc2 sites moved, so the hand-off for a human ROM read never fired.

The two remaining realrom failures are both OTHER beads:
  smb3   grm-evn. Sole residual is warnings 50 -> 52, the FUN_c542 sites at 867b and ac6d. PROVEN
         to predate this change: the same +2 appears when the identical check runs against the
         PRE-change extension. smb3's golden cannot go green until grm-evn is settled.
  dodge  grm-4nr. Bistable, count-line-only (refs 2739 <-> 2736), flaps run to run with the build
         held constant. Third instance; recorded there.

NEW SYNTHETIC COVERAGE (nesmmc3test2, criteria G8/G9/G10), because the realrom tier is not part of
build-and-test.sh and so cannot be what protects this -- mknesbanktest.py:1215 says exactly that
about grm-mu7's first guard:
  G8  CallerE: LDA #$47/STA $8000, LDA #$05/STA $0720, LDA #$03, JSR H2 -> r7=5, no warning.
      The $03 DECOY IN A IS THE POINT: register-sourcing would give r7=3. Proves cell-sourcing.
  G9  CallerF: an intervening JSR between the store and the call -> warning, no value.
  G10 CallerG/H3: the helper writes $0720 ITSELF -> r7=7 (its own $47, which is the TRUTH), never
      r7=5 (the caller's dead byte). NOTE this criterion was authored expecting "warning, not
      r7=7" and that was WRONG: H3 really does put $47 into $8001, so 7 is correct and
      valueSuppliedInsideHelper recovers it properly. The wrong answer to guard against is the
      caller's byte. Different defect from the one that shipped -- smb3's r7=7 was wrong because
      it was read at the $8000 SELECT site, which increment 1 fixed.

TRAP WORTH REMEMBERING, cost two gate runs: EVERY BANK NUMBER IN A SYNTHETIC FIXTURE MUST BE IN
RANGE. The first draft transcribed smb3's real $1B/27 into an 8-bank image. The rule recovered 27
perfectly and BoardBankAnalyzer then refused to annotate it ("bank index with no corresponding
image slice is a value-RECOVERY bug", grm-hum), so the positive case failed on a CORRECT recovery
-- and worse, the negative controls passed vacuously, since an out-of-range wrong answer is
suppressed on its way out whatever produced it. The criterion messages now print the warning text
(new VerifyBankTest.warningBookmarkText) because a requirement violation and an unrecoverable
argument are indistinguishable from the criterion line alone; that is what finally diagnosed it.

title: Argument-marshalling wrappers that write no mechanism are not recognized as helpers (blmaster e61b, tmnt cea5, cv2 c183/c185)
description:
A BANK-SWITCH HELPER'S ARGUMENT IS OFTEN MARSHALLED BY A FUNCTION THAT WRITES NO MECHANISM.
Such a function is not a helper by the current definition, so calls into it never count as calls
into a helper and their adjacent immediates are never considered. Two hand-confirmed instances
in two titles, reaching the real helper by two different edges.

INSTANCE 1 -- blmaster FUN_e61b, reached by TAIL JMP (grm-8iy.5 section 2).

    caller: LDA #5  --JMP-->  e61b: STA $DB  --JSR e627-->  e63c: 5x STA/LSR $FFFF

  e61b writes no mechanism. It stores the argument to the $DB shadow and calls the real helper.
  TWELVE call sites reach it; five of them by JMP rather than JSR. Consistent with the probe
  reporting TALLY.mech tailCall=0 -- the tail calls land on e61b, which is not in the mech set.

INSTANCE 2 -- tmnt FUN_cea5, reached by FALLTHROUGH INTO ANOTHER FUNCTION (2026-08-06).

    cea5:  STA $21          ; FUN_cea5, two bytes, no mechanism write
    cea7:  <serial chain>   ; FUN_cea7, the actual helper

  Ghidra creates functions at BOTH addresses (confirmed), so cea5 is a complete function whose
  entire body is one store and whose only exit is falling through into cea7. SEVEN call sites
  reach it, every one carrying a non-home constant: LDA #1 (x3), LDA #6 (x2), LDA #3, LDA #4.

THE COMMON SHAPE: a function that (i) writes no mechanism itself, (ii) reaches a mechanism-writing
function with the argument register intact, and (iii) is what callers actually call. The EDGE
varies -- tail JMP, fallthrough, and grm-nju already handles thunks and one-instruction
trampolines -- but the definition gap is the same one each time.

  grm-nju (CLOSED)   thunks, one-instruction JMP trampolines      HANDLED
  blmaster e61b      multi-instruction function, entered by JMP   NOT HANDLED
  tmnt cea5          two-byte function, entered by fallthrough    NOT HANDLED

NOTE THIS IS WHY grm-8iy.3's RULING-OUT WAS MISLEADING. It used viaThunkOrTrampoline=0 and
midBodyEntry=0 to conclude grm-nju's shapes could not explain cv2/blmaster/tmnt. Both numbers
were correct. Both measure only the two edges grm-nju implemented, so neither could ever report
these.

PROPOSED DIRECTION (not decided): widen the helper definition from "function containing a
mechanism write" to "function that reaches a mechanism write with the argument register
unmodified", following call, tail-call and fallthrough edges, bounded to a small number of hops.
The argument register must be tracked across the relay -- and grm-mu7's prologue-clobber guard
already exists for exactly the question of whether it survives.

CAUTION -- EACH WRAPPER HAS ITS OWN SEMANTICS AND THEY ARE NOT THE HELPER'S. blmaster e61b
writes the $DB shadow; tmnt cea5 writes the $21 shadow; the helpers they reach (e63c, cea7)
write no shadow at all. tmnt cea7 is separately callable and three sites do call it directly.
A model that collapses wrapper and helper into one signature gets the shadow side-effect wrong.

ACCEPTANCE: blmaster reports its twelve e61b call sites and tmnt its seven cea5 sites as calls
into a bank-switch helper, with the adjacent immediates recovered. Expect nine non-home banks on
blmaster (5, 2, and the ea41 path) and seven on tmnt (1, 1, 1, 6, 6, 3, 4).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CV2 IS A THIRD TITLE AND A FOURTH+FIFTH INSTANCE -- AND IT BREAKS THIS BEAD'S DEFINITION
(2026-08-06). Ghidra creates functions at c183, c185 AND c187 (confirmed). So cv2 is a wrapper
case, not a pre-body-entry case; grm-i7v is closed with no instances.

    FUN_c183:  STA $1C        ; forwards caller's A, writes the shadow   -> falls through
    FUN_c185:  LDA $1C        ; ESTABLISHES A from the shadow            -> falls through
    FUN_c187:  <serial chain> ; the real helper

TWO WRAPPERS STACKED, each a complete two-byte function, each reaching the helper by falling
through into the next function.

DEFINITION GAP THIS EXPOSES. This bead currently proposes "a function that reaches a mechanism
write with the ARGUMENT REGISTER UNMODIFIED". c185 fails that by construction -- it overwrites A
from $1C, which is its entire purpose. So a wrapper does one of TWO things and both must be
modelled:

  FORWARDING wrapper   passes the caller's argument through, possibly with a side effect
                       (blmaster e61b writes $DB; tmnt cea5 writes $21; cv2 c183 writes $1C)
  ESTABLISHING wrapper supplies the argument itself from memory, ignoring the caller
                       (cv2 c185 loads $1C; compare tmnt ced0/cf0b, which do the same as
                       separate non-fallthrough functions)

The recurring semantic triple across all three titles is set-and-remember / set-transient /
restore. Only the first two are forwarding; restore is always establishing.

INTERACTION WITH grm-mu7 -- CHECK THIS BEFORE IMPLEMENTING. grm-mu7's prologue-clobber guard
declines a helper argument when the helper's own prologue clobbers the argument register. c185
clobbers A by design, so the guard fires -- correctly by its own rule, wrongly in effect, since
the shadow load IS the value. grm-cxb ("fall back to the helper's own value when the caller's
cannot reach") is presumably what should take over. Confirm it does, or an establishing wrapper
will be silently declined rather than resolved.

UPDATED INSTANCE TABLE:
  blmaster e61b   forwarding, entered by TAIL JMP        12 call sites
  tmnt     cea5   forwarding, entered by FALLTHROUGH      7 call sites, all non-home constants
  cv2      c183   forwarding, entered by FALLTHROUGH     10 call sites (9x LDA #4, 1x LDA #0)
  cv2      c185   ESTABLISHING, entered by FALLTHROUGH    3 call sites (restores)
  tmnt     ced0   establishing, ordinary function         restores from $21
  tmnt     cf0b   establishing, ordinary function         restores from $59 (a read-back value)

THIRTY-TWO CALL SITES ACROSS THREE TITLES, all three of which currently resolve ZERO
instructions into overlay space. This is the largest single gap identified in the grm-8iy
cluster, which is why the priority is being raised.

REVISED ACCEPTANCE: blmaster reports 12 e61b sites, tmnt 7 cea5 sites, cv2 10 c183 sites, with
adjacent immediates recovered -- expecting non-home banks 5/2 on blmaster, 1/1/1/6/6/3/4 on
tmnt, and 4 (x9) on cv2. The establishing wrappers (cv2 c185, tmnt ced0/cf0b) additionally need
their shadow read (grm-mej.2) and are not required for a first increment.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
WIZWARR IS THE FOURTH TITLE WITH THE FALLTHROUGH-WRAPPER STACK, ON A DIFFERENT BOARD FAMILY
(2026-08-06, from the wizwarr def-use pass on grm-8iy.5).

  ce8b  sets the AxROM register from A on entry, then clears VRAM at $2000   <- mechanism writer
  ce89  sets A to zero, then FALLS THROUGH to ce8b                            <- establishing
  ce84  sets A to #$10, CALLS ce8b, then FALLS THROUGH to ce89                <- forwarding

Structurally identical to cv2's c183/c185/c187. The PAYOFF here is nil -- the values carried are
VRAM page bits at bank 0, not bank selections -- so wizwarr does not add call sites to this
bead's count.

WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING ANYWAY: wizwarr is AxROM, not MMC1. The first three instances
(blmaster, cv2, tmnt) are all MMC1 serial-shift boards, which left open whether the wrapper stack
was an artifact of that mechanism -- a five-write chain is bulky enough that sharing a tail is
worth the trouble. ce8b is a SINGLE-WRITE latch and the idiom appears anyway. So this is a
general 6502 code-organisation habit, not an MMC1 consequence, and a fix should not be scoped to
serial-shift boards.

Also note ce84 is currently reached only from RESET. Other callers may exist behind grm-k5m (the
undisassembled RAM-resident routines) or grm-pfp (the entry point hidden inside a BIT operand),
so wizwarr's contribution here should be re-counted once those land.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
INCREMENT 1 LANDED 2026-08-08 -- pass-through (fallthrough) wrappers only. Bead stays OPEN for
increment 2 (the blmaster call edge); see the end.

=== WHAT SHIPPED ===

BoardBankAnalyzer only, NO existing method body changed:
  - findPassThroughWrappers(program, helpers, switchResults), run AFTER composeTailCalls, so a
    wrapper inherits the composed model. Rounds over a List.copyOf snapshot (determinism),
    capped by MAX_WRAPPER_CHAIN = 3; termination is structural, the cap is policy.
  - isPassThroughInto(...), package-private static so JUnit can pin it. Six conditions: single
    contiguous body starting at the entry; every instruction disassembled, zero flows (which
    excludes JSR and therefore blmaster BY CONSTRUCTION), not terminal, and its fallthrough
    equal to getMaxAddress().next() (the OVERRIDE check); no switchResults key in the body; and
    the walk lands exactly on the target.
  - HelperModel.atFallThroughWrapper(wrapper) -- function is the WRAPPER (helperLabel :1212
    compares entry against function.getEntryPoint(), so keeping the helper there would have
    rendered a false "mid-body entry in ..."), constState INHERITED as an identity: the
    admission predicate proves the wrapper body changes no tracked bank bit.

WHY IT NEEDED NO OTHER CHANGES: argumentSurvivesPrologue walks LINEARLY BY ADDRESS with no
reference to function boundaries, so re-keying entry onto a contiguous wrapper makes that one
existing walk cover the wrapper body plus the helper prologue. cv2's STA $1C / LDA $1C pair is
load-bearing rather than incidental -- without grm-mu7 increment 2's memory save/restore model
the LDA reads as a plain clobber and nothing resolves.

A SOUNDNESS NOTE WORTH KEEPING (verified against the Ghidra source, now in the javadoc): Ghidra
function bodies CANNOT OVERLAP -- createFunction and setFunctionBody both convert an
OverlappingNamespaceException into an OverlappingFunctionException. Body assignment is
first-come-claims-it, so a wrapper's body is guaranteed clipped at or before the target and
bounding the walk by getBody() is safe. The same rule is why grm-78b is this bead's mirror
image: whether a fallthrough chain surfaces as ONE function or as WRAPPER PLUS HELPER is decided
purely by what got created first. Separately: the DECOMPILER is not bounded by function bodies
at all (Funcdata::startProcessing calls followFlow over the whole address space), so decompiler
output is not evidence about where a body ends.

=== TESTS ===

Tier 2: new HelperWrapperProgramTest (9 cases -- 2 admit, 7 reject: JSR in body, conditional
branch, RTS-terminal, disassembly gap, overshoot, fragmented body, fallthrough override). The
last two carry explicit anti-vacuity assertions that the fixture really is in the intended state
first. Plus one HelperPrologueProgramTest case over cv2's exact byte sequence. 30/30 pass.

Tier 3: new neswrappertest fixture (W1-W13), deliberately SEPARATE from nesmmc1test so that
golden stays byte-identical and readable as a pure regression signal. Includes both negative
controls -- a JSR-bodied predecessor and an RTS-terminal predecessor, each adjacent to a real
helper -- and direct calls to every helper proving the negatives fail on their own shape rather
than because their neighbour is broken. Full gate: SUITE OK, and ALL 45 pre-existing goldens
unchanged. That is itself the finding this fixture exists to fix: the synthetic tier structurally
cannot see this class of change, which is how grm-mu7 regressed three real ROMs while green.

=== REAL-ROM RESULTS (19 GME titles) ===

  title      refs.intoOverlay  instrs.inOverlay  bankComments  warnings
  tmnt            0 ->   44        0 ->  103       10 -> 18      31 (=)
  ultimaav      175 ->  225      678 ->  867        1 ->  8      27 -> 33
  cv2             0 ->    1        0 ->    8        2 ->  4      24 -> 26
  rcransom        0 (=)            0 (=)           38 -> 40       5 ->  3
  wizwarr         0 (=)            0 (=)           15 (=)         5 ->  7
  zelda2          =                =                =            27 -> 31
  lifeforce       =                =                =             3 ->  6
  blmaster, kicarus, dodge, megaman, and the rest: BYTE-IDENTICAL

NOTHING DECREASED ANYWHERE. Seven goldens blessed.

TMNT IS THE HEADLINE and matches the hand prediction: +8 bank comments against 7 predicted
non-home sites at cea5, and the title goes from zero to 103 instructions in overlay space.

ULTIMAAV WAS NOT PREDICTED and is the better news: two wrappers nobody had traced by hand,
FUN_f331 (5 new comments) and FUN_f313 (2), worth +189 overlay instructions. The rule
generalising past the four hand-traced titles is the point.

WIZWARR BEHAVED EXACTLY AS PREDICTED, including the non-result: ce89 admitted (2 honest
declines, payoff nil because its values are VRAM page bits at bank 0), ce84 NOT admitted because
its body contains a JSR. wizwarr is AxROM, so this is the cross-board-family check that the rule
is not an MMC1 artifact. It passed.

ZELDA2 / LIFEFORCE / WIZWARR warning rises are all the same shape and all honest: newly-admitted
wrappers (FUN_ffc9; FUN_e618/FUN_e619; FUN_ce89) whose arguments do not resolve, so a previously
SILENT miss became a conservative one. Nothing was lost -- bankComments, refs and instrs are
unchanged on all three. Same side effect grm-nju documented.

FF1 IS THE KNOWN FLAKE, NOT A REGRESSION, and this was demonstrated rather than assumed. Its
diff was refs -33 / instrs -44 / warnings -14 with ZERO sample-line changes, which is grm-4nr's
recorded signature exactly. Two further runs of the same code on the same input:
    run 1: refs 1847 / instrs 7382 / warnings 604   FAIL
    run 2: PASS (matched the golden exactly)
ff1's golden was deliberately NOT blessed.

=== SHORTFALL, FILED SEPARATELY ===

cv2 delivered +2 bank comments against +10 predicted. The mechanism works -- c4de recovers
prg_bank=4 via FUN_c183 and retargets to W8000_M3_B4::8326 -- but eight of the ten hand-found
c183 call sites emit neither a comment nor a warning. Filed as grm-093 (P4) with the two
candidate explanations and the cheap check that distinguishes them; also mirrored into
docs/human-research-todo.md. Note one branch of that question (calls reaching a helper by plain
JMP never passing runDataflow's isCall() gate) would ALSO cost blmaster, so grm-093 may end up
raising increment 2's ceiling.

=== INCREMENT 2, STILL OPEN ON THIS BEAD ===

blmaster FUN_e61b: twelve call sites, reached by an internal JSR from a wrapper that is NOT
address-contiguous with its helper. Its dump is byte-identical after increment 1, which is the
intended scope check -- isPassThroughInto's zero-flows condition excludes it by construction.
Increment 2 needs interprocedural argument propagation (a wrapper effectively acquiring a bank
parameter sourced from its own callers), which is a different feature from wrapper admission and
was deliberately not attempted here. Check grm-093's outcome first: if the answer is the JMP
gating, that is a cheaper and broader fix than interprocedural propagation and should come first.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
INCREMENT 2 LANDED 2026-08-09 (d147ea3) -- CALL-EDGE WRAPPERS. blmaster measured; corpus sweep
still running at time of writing.

=== THE RECLASSIFICATION, NOW EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED ===

grm-093 and docs/human-research-todo.md both recorded that blmaster was BLOCKED UPSTREAM on
grm-mej.2, because e61b was "a shadow-ESTABLISHING wrapper of exactly the class cv2's c185 belongs
to". That was wrong, and the fix required no grm-mej work at all:

  cv2 c185      loads $1C, which a DIFFERENT FUNCTION (c183) wrote   -> establishing
  blmaster e61b stores AND reloads $DB inside ONE CONTIGUOUS BODY    -> forwarding

e61b is cv2's c183+c185 pair FUSED INTO ONE FUNCTION, not c185 alone. The span is exactly what
grm-mu7 increment 2's argumentCells/argumentReloadSource save-restore model already covers. What
actually blocked it was the CALL EDGE, which is this bead's own remaining scope. Per the ruling at
plan time the correction was held until measured; it is measured, so both records are now updated.

=== WHAT SHIPPED ===

  HelperModel gains a nullable Relay(callSite, calleeEntry) + atCallEdgeWrapper. The prologue
  becomes a LIST of spans: PrologueSegment, an argumentSurvivesPrologue overload that is a literal
  AND, and prologueSegments deriving [entry, callSite) and [calleeEntry, firstSite).

  THE PREDICATE ITSELF NEEDED ZERO CHANGES. Its loop bound is `cursor < to`, so passing the relay
  JSR's address as segment 1's end stops the walk BEFORE inspecting it -- the isCall() early-return
  never fires on the boundary instruction. Segment 2 is empty for e63c, whose STA $FFFF IS its
  entry, and an empty segment is trivially true.

  findCallEdgeWrappers, wired LAST so relays resolve through increment 1's wrappers. ONE ROUND,
  counted against the immutable input map: the exactly-one-helper-call rule is NON-MONOTONE in the
  helper set, so with rounds the answer would depend on candidate iteration order. Counting against
  the input makes the pass a pure, order-independent function -- a STRONGER property than increment
  1's snapshot, which would not have fixed this.

TWO GATES, AND NEITHER SUBSUMES THE OTHER -- the least obvious thing in the increment, and the
plan's first draft got it wrong. A BRANCH DOES NOT MAKE argumentSurvivesPrologue DECLINE: a nonzero
getFlows() only clears straightLine/argumentCells and the walk CONTINUES. So a prefix that branches
around the relay but never writes argReg passes the VALUE gate, and admitting it would rest every
claim about the wrapper's effect on a call that might not run. The STRUCTURAL gate is
isPassThroughInto REUSED with target = the relay call site -- an exact reuse, not opportunistic:
the prefix of a call-edge wrapper up to its relay IS a pass-through into that call site.

THREE CONSUMER FIXES, all found by walking the checklist rather than by a failing test:
  - valueSuppliedInsideHelper and callSiteRegisters stop addresses must be the WRAPPED helper's
    entry. The wrapper's would let a backward scan run off the helper's entry into the wrapper's
    tail and read it as prologue -- the exact hazard valueSuppliedInsideHelper's own javadoc warns
    about.
  - midBodyEntryHelper now declines a relay model OUTRIGHT. A relay model's firstSite lives in a
    different function and so exceeds every address in the wrapper's body, meaning the existing
    entry>firstSite test admitted EVERY mid-body address -- including ones past the relay call,
    where no bank switch happens on that path at all.

=== BLMASTER: THE TARGET, MEASURED ===

  count bankComments      5 -> 9    (+4)
  count warnings         24 -> 32   (+8)
  count refs.intoOverlay  0 (=)
  count instrs.inOverlay  0 (=)

  new: c55f  prg_bank=0 via FUN_e61b      (JSR, LDA #0)
       c57a  prg_bank=0 via FUN_e61b      (JSR, LDA #0)
       e2c3  prg_bank=2 via FUN_e61b      (JSR, LDA #2)  <- non-home, as predicted
       df07  prg_bank=5 via FUN_e61b      (JMP, LDA #5)  <- non-home, and see below
  new warnings: cc6a, df0c, e304 -- "call to helper FUN_e61b whose bank argument could not be
       recovered". All LDA $D3 restore sites: a previously SILENT miss became a conservative one.

  EVERY ONE OF THE FOUR PLAIN-IMMEDIATE CALL SITES RESOLVED. The bead predicted the three JSR ones
  and hedged df07 on whether shared-return retyped it; it did. Nothing decreased anywhere.

  THE JMP FINDING IS A BONUS DELIVERABLE AND IT REFUTES grm-093's HYPOTHESIS (b). That bead closed
  saying the isCall() gate (BoardBankAnalyzer:676) was unmeasurable corpus-wide and that blmaster
  would be the probe once its helper stopped being rejected. It is now the probe, and there is NO
  REACH ASYMMETRY: resolved sites split 3 JSR / 1 JMP, declined sites split 1 JSR / 2 JMP. Recorded
  in full on grm-093; do not file an isCall() bead.

  HONEST LIMIT WORTH NAMING: instrs.inOverlay stayed 0. The banks are now recovered but nothing
  retargets against them yet on this title -- no nearby windowed access resolves under the
  recovered state. So this is a real annotation gain, not yet an overlay-coverage gain.

=== TESTS ===

  Tier 2: new HelperCallEdgeWrapperProgramTest (12 cases). Pins BOTH gates separately -- including
  a case asserting the value gate ACCEPTS the branching prefix, so a future change that made it
  reject branches would not silently render the structural gate's point moot. Also pins the two
  cross-segment reset properties (stack and memory), which would silently become true if the reset
  were removed, and the empty-list guard against a vacuous true. Increment 1's 9 cases still pass.

  Tier 3: new nesrelaytest fixture (R1-R11 + R2b/R3b/R7b, 15 criteria), deliberately a SEPARATE ROM
  so neswrappertest.dump staying byte-identical remains the proof increment 2 left increment 1
  alone. Four negative controls -- two-helper-call, non-helper-call, branching, argument-clobbering
  -- each with its OWN helper so a rejection cannot be confused with a broken helper, plus R7b as
  the anti-vacuity check that the helper behind the value-gate control still resolves.

  FULL GATE: SUITE OK. Exactly one golden ADDED, ZERO existing goldens modified.

=== FILED / STILL OPEN ===

  grm-k90 (P3): wrapper models hand the caller's X/Y to depositHelperArgument without proving they
  survive the wrapper body. NOT new to increment 2 -- increment 1 carries it identically -- and
  forcing X/Y unknown could only DECREASE annotations, which acceptance forbids. contra is the
  title to read.

  NOT A TEST GAP BUT WORTH KNOWING: the midBodyEntryHelper relay decline is not directly pinned.
  Constructing a stable mid-body entry into a wrapper synthetically is unreliable, because a JSR
  target normally gets a Function created and so stops being mid-body. The guard is blunt
  (relay != null) precisely so it cannot be wrong.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORPUS SWEEP COMPLETE (--gme, 19 titles, 2026-08-09). NOTHING DECREASED ANYWHERE.

  blmaster   bankComments 5 -> 9, warnings 24 -> 32       BLESSED (the target; table in prior comment)
  ff1        warnings 33 -> 34                             BLESSED (see below)
  17 others  BYTE-IDENTICAL: bionic, cv2, dodge, drmario, kicarus, lifeforce, lwings, smb2,
             megaman2, megaman3, rcproam, rcransom, tetris, tmnt, ultimaav, wizwarr, zelda2

TMNT, CV2, ULTIMAAV AND WIZWARR ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL, which is the scope check that matters most:
those are the four titles increment 1 moved. Increment 2 touched none of them, confirming the
call-edge pass is additive to pass-through admission rather than a re-interpretation of it.

FF1 IS A REAL FIND, NOT THE KNOWN FLAKE -- and this was demonstrated, not assumed. The recorded
grm-4nr signature is refs -33 / instrs -44 / warnings -14 with ZERO sample-line changes. What
appeared instead was:
    refs.intoOverlay   1847 (=)
    instrs.inOverlay   7382 (=)
    bankComments       75 (=)
    warnings           33 -> 34
    new: f209 [NesBankingAnalyzer] call to bank-switch helper FUN_f284 whose bank argument could
         not be recovered at this call site
Counts otherwise pinned to their stable values, and one new warning naming a helper the golden had
never heard of. Re-run once more: byte-identical. So FUN_f284 is a call-edge wrapper nobody had
traced by hand, its caller at f209 cannot resolve the argument, and a previously SILENT miss became
a conservative one. Blessed.

That makes ff1 the increment's ultimaav -- the rule generalising past the hand-traced title is the
point, and it is the second time a wrapper increment has found one.

SEPARATE FINDING, NOT OURS: dodge is a THIRD BISTABLE GOLDEN (refs 2739 -> 2736, zero sample-line
changes; PASS / FAIL / PASS across three runs of the same binary within 20 minutes). Recorded on
grm-g73 with the full reproduction, since its single-line delta makes it the cleanest minimal
reproducer of that family yet. Its golden was NOT blessed.

WHAT IS STILL NOT MEASURED: the --all set beyond --gme, which adds contra, megaman and smb3. That
was deliberately deferred -- smb3's golden is stale (grm-bj6) and contra has the run-scope
dependency (grm-lwu), so both need human-side answers before their diffs mean anything. Note the
--gme sweep is unaffected by either: neither title is in it, so the numbers above are from a clean
baseline.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CLOSING. THE DEFINITION GAP THIS BEAD IS ABOUT IS CLOSED; the sites that remain are blocked on
other beads' mechanisms, not on wrapper recognition.

THE ORIGINAL INSTANCE TABLE, FINAL STATE:

  blmaster e61b   forwarding, TAIL JMP + interior JSR   increment 2   4 of 12 resolved, 3 now warn
  tmnt     cea5   forwarding, FALLTHROUGH                increment 1   done (+8 comments, 0 -> 103
                                                                       instrs in overlay)
  cv2      c183   forwarding, FALLTHROUGH                increment 1   done -- 2 of 2 that EXIST as
                                                                       instructions (grm-093)
  wizwarr  ce89   establishing, FALLTHROUGH              increment 1   admitted; payoff nil by
                                                                       design (VRAM page bits)
  cv2      c185   ESTABLISHING                           grm-mej.2
  tmnt     ced0/cf0b  establishing                       grm-mej.2

BE CAREFUL READING "4 of 12" AS A SHORTFALL -- IT IS NOT ONE. The twelve sites were never twelve
instances of this bead's problem. Broken down by what each site actually carries:

  4  plain immediate   ALL FOUR RESOLVED. This is 100% of the sites whose argument this bead's
                       mechanism could ever have recovered.
  6  LDA $D3 restore   Need shadow-RESTORE modelling. grm-mej scope, and correctly so: no wrapper
                       definition recovers a value the caller read out of RAM. Three of them now
                       WARN where they were previously silent, which is the honest half of the win.
  1  ea41 computed     4x LSR of a set-valued {4,6}. grm-wul scope.
