  1  e694 relay        STA $D3 then JMP; shadow again.

So the ceiling this bead could reach was four, and it reached four. The bead's own ACCEPTANCE text
("blmaster reports its twelve e61b call sites") was written before the section-3 def-use table
existed and counted call sites rather than recoverable arguments -- the same over-counting
correction already applied to grm-8iy.5's "24 of 30 direct stores" and to grm-093's "ten c183
callers". Recording that here so the next reader does not re-open this looking for eight missing
recoveries that were never this bead's to find.

WHAT ACTUALLY GENERALISED, which is the better measure of the two increments:
  increment 1  predicted tmnt; ALSO found ultimaav FUN_f331/FUN_f313 (+189 overlay instrs)
  increment 2  predicted blmaster; ALSO found ff1 FUN_f284
Both times the rule reached past its hand-traced titles. That was the point.

REMAINING WORK, all tracked elsewhere: grm-mej.2 (the six shadow-restore sites, cv2 c185, tmnt
ced0/cf0b), grm-wul (ea41's set-valued {4,6}), grm-k90 (X/Y survival through a wrapper body),
grm-bj6 + grm-lwu (the --all corpus titles this sweep deliberately did not measure).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CONTRA GOLDEN BLESSED 2026-08-09, closing the last of increment 1's two skipped goldens from this
side. 788f09b re-blessed seven realrom goldens and skipped smb3 and contra; contra is now done
(grm-3t8), smb3 remains open (grm-bj6) because its diff is dataflow rather than annotation.

Human confirmation that the recognition is CORRECT, not just different: contra's FUN_c139 sets the
bank shadow $07ec from the bank id at $8000 and FALLS THROUGH to the PRG register write at c13f --
a textbook pass-through wrapper, on a UxROM/MemoryLatch title. So increment 1's admission rule
fires correctly on a board family well away from the MMC1 cases it was developed against, which is
independent evidence for the 'wrapper idiom is not an MMC1 artifact' finding already recorded here.

Diff was 4 added helper-call warnings (c094/c0a2/c21b/c9c0) and the count line, nothing else --
refs 257, instrs 849, bankComments 2 all unchanged. All four are NON-recoveries, so this is the
familiar silent-miss-becomes-conservative-miss effect, not new coverage.

title: realrom bless served a stale cached candidate after an id rename
description:
REPORTED: 'realrom-test.sh bless --gme <romdir>' re-blessed the curated titles as well as the GME ones, and undid the wizwarr->ironsword rename -- expected/ironsword.dump came back saying 'REALROM program wizwarr.nes'.

ROOT CAUSE (two independent cache-key omissions, both fixed):
1. realrom_cache_key() hashed rom_sha + opts + RealRomDump.java + ext_id but NOT the row id. The id IS part of the output: import_and_dump names the ROM copy after it, so it reaches the dump as 'REALROM program <id>.nes'. Renaming a row therefore left the key identical and bless served the pre-rename candidate straight into the golden. It went unnoticed because the only other changes in that commit were Java COMMENTS, which do not alter bytecode, so the CRC-based ext_identity() was unchanged too.
2. ext_identity() fingerprinted only '*.jar' under Extensions -- but the compiled board descriptors ship LOOSE as data/machines/*.map next to the jar (only the two charset maps are inside it). So editing machines/nes-*.yaml, the single most common change in this repo and the one that directly determines the block/overlay layout the dump records, ALSO left the key unchanged. Worse instance of the same bug than the reported one; found while diagnosing it.

FIXES: id added to the key; ext_identity() now also sha256s the loose non-jar Extensions files; and on a cache HIT, bless asserts the candidate's 'REALROM program' == <id>.nes and 'REALROM sha256' == the manifest row before accepting it, discarding and re-importing otherwise -- so the NEXT key omission fails loudly rather than silently blessing a stale dump.

ALSO FIXED (the reported surprise): --gme was additive. It now SELECTS: no flag = curated manifest.tsv, --gme = manifest-gme.tsv only, --all = both. Every run announces the set. Additive was chosen from a design preview and was wrong in practice -- 'bless --gme' re-blessing twelve untouched goldens costs real work to undo.

VERIFIED against the real ROM (/h/emulators/nes/ROMs): 'bless --only ironsword' re-imports instead of reusing the stale entry and reproduces the committed golden BYTE-IDENTICALLY (which also proves the git-checkout restore was correct, not merely plausible); planting a wrong-program-name dump at the NEW key is rejected with 'stale cache entry ignored ... re-importing' and still yields the correct golden. Set selection gives 12/19/31 rows for none/--gme/--all.

NOTE: the 149 pre-existing build/realrom-cache entries are now unreachable (keys changed). Harmless -- the dir is gitignored and regenerates.
close_reason: Fixed and verified against real ROMs. Cache key now includes the row id; ext_identity() now hashes the loose data/machines/*.map descriptors as well as jars; bless asserts a reused candidate names this row and this ROM; check audits every existing golden at startup (no ROMs needed). --gme now selects rather than adds, with --all for both. Committed ece0722.

title: Bank-switch helper argument recovery: memory-latch sites resolve to unknown, poisoning discrete-mapper state
description:
Follow-up to grm-3x1 (2026-07-31), which closed the memory-latch REACHABILITY gap and
proved that reachability was never the whole problem. All five moved real-ROM titles now
SEE their latch stores and recover NOTHING from them.

MEASURED (all 12 hash-pinned titles, before -> after grm-3x1):
  title         overlay refs   bank comments   warnings
  contra          0 ->    0       0 ->   0      1 ->  6
  dragonpower     0 ->    0       0 ->   0      3 ->  6
  shenlong        0 ->    0       0 ->   0      1 ->  6
  wizwarr        17 ->   17      11 ->  11      4 ->  8
  megaman      1781 -> 1703     153 -> 151      3 -> 37

TWO DISTINCT SYMPTOMS, one root cause.

(1) NO NEW ANNOTATIONS. Contras board-level "no mechanism write was observed" warning is
gone -- replaced by a per-site warning at c142 ("mechanism write with a genuinely
undeterminable value") plus five "call to bank-switch helper FUN_c13f whose bank argument
could not be recovered at this call site". So the helper IS identified; the ARGUMENT is
not recoverable at any call site. Same shape on dragonpower/shenlong (FUN_ffbe, FUN_8eeb)
-- both GxROM Dragon Ball titles, so likely one shared engine.

(2) MEGAMAN REGRESSED -78 overlay refs / -2 bank comments / +34 warnings. Mechanism:
StoredValueScanner aborts a backward scan when it steps over a mechanism write (class
javadoc: "a base value read further back would predate that write, so falling back to the
in-state would be unsound"). Making more writes visible therefore makes more scans abort.
Watch FUN_c39c: it appears in 11 of the 34 new warnings as an unrecoverable helper.
Site 9067 specifically degraded from "bank -> 6 (bank=6) via FUN_d846" to a warning.

WHY IT MATTERS BOTH WAYS. The optimistic reading is that megamans 1781 refs came from a
model blind to 7 of its 25 switch sites, so shrinking them is a correctness gain. The
pessimistic reading is that we traded correct annotations for warnings. NOBODY HAS
CHECKED WHICH -- that determination is the first task here, and it decides whether
megaman ever gets blessed (it is measurement-only per grm-g73).

LIKELY DIRECTION: the helper-evaluation path already works for megamans absolute sites
("via FUN_d131" etc), so the machinery exists; what is missing is recovering the bank
argument at the CALL SITE when the value arrives via a register the callers set from a
table/variable rather than an immediate. grm-hb6.4 (per-game site hints as dataflow
seeds) is a plausible lever for the genuinely unrecoverable remainder.

DO NOT "fix" this by relaxing the mid-scan abort without an argument -- the abort is
sound and the grm-3x1 javadoc records why.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:

Blessing it would have erased the record.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER FIXES THIS: megaman.dump is now the ONLY realrom golden lacking a 'REALROM prgsha256' line. When this bead is fixed and megaman is re-blessed, expect that line to appear alongside the count/warning changes -- it is grm-hb6.1's, not a symptom of this bug. Its verified value for the pinned dump (sha256 e5bbc798...) is:
  REALROM prgsha256 05117c775581eb63f7686f58c24f1c9da0fa0669eede1e7bad12eed40e58935e

DIAGNOSTIC TRAP worth knowing (fog class grm-g73 already records): because megaman is the one golden never re-blessed, it is still CRLF in the working tree from git checkout, while the bless script writes LF. Its check diff therefore presents as a WHOLE-FILE replacement (78 lines deleted, 101 added) rather than as the handful of lines that actually differ, which badly overstates the apparent regression at a glance. Read the counts, not the diff size. comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ROM GROUND TRUTH (2026-08-01). All 5 ROMs located and SHA-256 verified against
tools/banktest/realrom/manifest.tsv BEFORE disassembly, so this is pinned to exactly the
dumps the goldens describe. ROM dirs: H:/emulators/nes/roms and Z:/nes/db.

CONTRA helper is 3 instructions; the bug is visible in them:
  C13F: B9 D0 FF  LDA $FFD0,Y   <- helper entry; bank argument arrives in Y
  C142: 99 D0 FF  STA $FFD0,Y   <- the "genuinely undeterminable" warning
  C145: 60        RTS
Bank table $FFD0 = 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 (fixed $C000 window). findHelpers sets
argReg = storeRegister(STA) = 'A'; the argument is really in Y. Call sites:
  C0C9 LDY #$01 / C0CB JSR      -> bank 1   RECOVERABLE
  C0D1 PLA / C0D2 TAY / C0D3 JSR-> CPU stack (NMI save/restore)
  C146 LDY $07EC / C149 JMP     -> RAM save slot (JMP tail call; Ghidra CALL_TERMINATOR)
  C155 LDY #$01 / C157 JSR      -> bank 1   RECOVERABLE
  C161 LDY $07ED / C164 JSR     -> RAM save slot
The 3 unrecoverable sites are ONE idiom: save current bank / switch / restore. NMI does
C0C1 LDA $8000 / PHA ... PLA / TAY / JSR $C13F -- it does not know what bank it interrupted,
so it reads the bank number back out of the cartridge. C139/C14F do the same into $07EC/$07ED;
C146/C15E restore from them.

VERIFIED BY CONTENT: Contra's $8000 is a BANK-IDENTIFYING byte -- byte 0 of bank N equals N
for all 8 banks (00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07). So LDA $8000 IS a read of live bank state.
Megaman does NOT use this trick (its per-bank byte-0 values are 00 00 00 00 00 00 06 00).
Per user: the identifier is not common but not rare, and its LOCATION VARIES game to game --
prefer a per-game hint over content deduction, for documentary value.

MEGAMAN: bank table at $C000 = 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07. ZP $42 is a write-through
"current bank" shadow (every mechanism write is immediately preceded by STA $42 of the same
register). ZP $31 is a partial address encoding banks as 0-6 / 7-$C (not investigated).
  D131: LDA #$06 / STA $42 / STA $C006     ; works today
  C3B3: LDA #$05 / STA $42 / STA $C005     ; works today
  C39C: LDA $31 / CMP #$06 / BCC / SBC #$06 / TAX / STA $42 / STA $C000,X
                                           ; bank from RAM $31 -- its 11 warnings are HONEST
  FUN_d846:
    D846: LDA #$06 / STA $42 / STA $C006   ; switch #1 -> bank 6
    D855: LDA #$00 / STA $0C / ASL A
    D85A: TAX                              ; X = 0, statically known
    D85B: LDA $D81E,X                      ; $D81E = 00 02 00 02 00 02 00 01 ... -> A = $00
    D85E: TAY / D85F: STA $42
    D861: STA $C000,Y                      ; switch #2, newly visible after grm-3x1

VERDICT ON THIS BEAD'S HEADLINE QUESTION: megaman's 1781->1703 shrink is a CORRECTNESS GAIN.
JSR $D846 leaves the board in bank 0, NOT bank 6 -- switch #2 overwrites switch #1 before the
RTS. The pre-grm-3x1 golden's "bank -> 6 (bank=6) via FUN_d846" at site 9067 was WRONG, and the
78 overlay refs retargeted into PRG_LO_B6 on the strength of it were wrong with it. grm-3x1
correctly stopped believing a falsehood. This bead replaces the wrong 6 with a right 0 --
so do NOT expect 1781 back: bank 0 is PRG_LO's home bank, realized in BASE space, so refs
resolved under a known bank=0 are base-space refs and are not counted by refs.intoOverlay.

DRAGON POWER / SHEN LONG (GxROM 66), byte-identical engine, deferred:
  FFBE: LDA $F2 / ASL A / ASL A / ORA $F9 / TAY / LDA $FFCC,Y / STA $FFCC,Y / RTS
  FFDC: PLA/CLC/ADC #1/STA $17 / PLA/ADC #0/STA $18 / PLA / STA $F2 / FFEA: JSR $FFBE
        / JMP ($0017)
$F2 = current-bank shadow. $FFDC is an INLINE FAR-CALL: LDA #bank / PHA / JSR $FFDC pops the
return address, increments it, switches bank, and jumps -- execution resumes at the NEXT
instruction in a DIFFERENT bank.

VERIFIED BY CONTENT: the cross-bank invariant region is real and holds the whole switch engine.
Measured per-offset across all four 32 KiB banks:
  dragonpower  $FF68-$FFF9 (146 bytes)   contains $FFBE helper, $FFCC table, $FFDC trampoline
  shenlong     $FEE0-$FFF9 (282 bytes)   same
TRAP FOR THE IMPLEMENTER: this MUST be computed per-offset, NOT as a common suffix. $FFFA-$FFFF
genuinely differ per bank (each bank has its own NMI and IRQ handler; only RESET is common,
$FF88 in every bank of both games), so a suffix test reports ZERO invariant bytes. I got this
wrong on the first pass and nearly reported the opposite conclusion.

STRUCTURAL BLOCKER for GxROM/AxROM, independent of dataflow: both descriptors declare a single
PRG_ALL $8000-$FFFF window with no fixed bank (machines/nes-gxrom.yaml:52-57,
nes-axrom.yaml:33-37), so every cart offset is overlay-covered and
MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.bankInvariantRomByte returns null for EVERY address those
programs can name. The $FFCC table is unreadable to the engine even with a perfect index.
That is a third gap beyond the stack and the ZP shadow.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION (2026-08-01, same day): MY EARLIER VERDICT IN THIS BEAD WAS WRONG. The prior
comment claimed "JSR $D846 leaves the board in bank 0, not bank 6" and concluded megaman's
1781->1703 shrink was a CORRECTNESS GAIN. Both claims are FALSE. Corrected below; the rest of
that comment (Contra, GxROM, the content measurements) still stands.

WHAT I MISSED: I read FUN_d846 as straight-line code. It is a LOOP. $D887 is BNE $D859, so
$D859 is the loop head:

  D855: LDA #$00 / D857: STA $0C          ; chunk counter = 0
  D859: ASL A                             <<< LOOP HEAD (BNE $D887 targets here)
  D85A: TAX                               ; X = 2 * counter
  D85B: LDA $D81E,X                       ; per-chunk BANK number from the table
  D85E: TAY / D85F: STA $42
  D861: STA $C000,Y                       ; switch to THIS CHUNK's bank -- varies per iteration
  D864..D87F:                             ; copy a CHR chunk through ($04) to $2007 (PPU)
  D881: INC $0C / D883: LDA $0C / D885: CMP #$0A / D887: BNE $D859   ; 10 chunks
  D889: LDA #$06 / D88B: STA $42
  D88D: STA $C006                         ; RESTORE bank 6 after the loop
  D890: JSR $BFF6 / D893: JMP $C3B3
  index table $D81E.. = 00 02 00 02 00 02 00 01 00 01 00 03 00 03 02 01 02 01 00 08
  (even entries are banks, odd entries are chunk counts)

So FUN_d846 is a CHR upload loop that hops among banks 0/2 while copying, and ends on bank 6.

CONSEQUENCES, all the opposite of what I said before:
1. The warning at $D861 is HONEST. The bank genuinely differs per iteration and no static
   value exists. The analyzer declines because isControlFlowJoin fires at $D859 -- the
   join guard doing exactly its job. (NOT the mid-scan mechanism-write abort; that never
   fires on this chain.)
2. FUN_d846's post-call state IS bank 6, set at $D88D immediately before the exit path.
   The pre-grm-3x1 golden's "bank -> 6 (bank=6) via FUN_d846" at site 9067 was CORRECT.
3. Therefore megaman's 1781 -> 1703 is a REGRESSION, not a gain. The 78 refs into PRG_LO_B6
   were right, and this bead needs to restore them.
4. GAP 1 (known-index resolution) does NOT fix megaman and was never going to -- verified
   empirically: Increment 1 landed green and left megaman byte-identical at 1703/151/37.
   $D861 stays unresolvable, correctly.
5. THE FIX IS GAP 2 (increment 2). findHelpers keeps switchSite = MAX address = $D88D and
   drops constState to null because the three sites disagree (6 / unknown / 6). The
   mini-inline then evaluates $D88D under the call site's registers: LDA #$06 / STA $42 /
   STA $C006 -> bank 6, caller-independent. That restores the annotation and the 78 refs
   FOR THE RIGHT REASON -- derived from the site that actually executes last, instead of
   from a constState coincidence that happened to read the first site before grm-3x1 made
   the other two visible.
   This also makes findHelpers' max-address switchSite rule (BoardBankAnalyzer:864-871)
   load-bearing on a real cartridge for the first time, not just on serial-shift chains.
REVISED PREDICTION for megaman after increment 2: refs.intoOverlay back to ~1781 (not
"do not expect 1781 back" as I wrote before), bankComments ~153, warnings 37 minus the
FUN_d846 call sites. The 11 FUN_c39c warnings stay -- those really are RAM-sourced.

METHOD NOTE, worth keeping: the abstracted unit test passed while the real ROM did not move
at all. A verbatim reproduction of the bytes at their real addresses ALSO passed, because
ProgramBuilder had no back edge -- the abstraction and the transcription were both wrong in
the same direction. What settled it was raising RealRomDump's SAMPLE cap to see the actual
bookmark at $D861, then byte-scanning the ROM for branches targeting $D84A-$D862. Also note
tools/banktest/BankReachProbe.java is STALE: its writesInRange is a verbatim copy of the
PRE-grm-3x1 tier-1-only version (its javadoc still cites :193-203), so its today= column
reports NO for every indexed site that production actually does see via tier 2. It sent me
down a blind alley; file a fix.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SECOND CORRECTION + NEW DEFECT CLASS (2026-08-01): a helper's effect must follow TAIL CALLS.
Reported by the user and confirmed against the ROM.

FUN_d846 does not end at $D88D. It ends:
  D890: JSR $BFF6
  D893: JMP $C3B3        <- TAIL CALL out of the function
and FUN_c3b3 is a "set bank 5" routine:
  C3B3: PHP / PHA / LDA #$05 / STA $42 / C3B9: STA $C005 / PLA / PLP / RTS
So on return from JSR $D846 the live bank is 5 -- not 6, and not 0. My previous correction
got the loop right and the exit wrong.

THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF. Scanning every megaman function that contains a mechanism write, for
its exit terminator:
  FUN_c55d   TAIL JMP $C3B3 at $C573   -> helper FUN_c3b3
  FUN_d131   TAIL JMP $C3B3 at $D159   -> helper FUN_c3b3
  FUN_d846   TAIL JMP $C3B3 at $D893   -> helper FUN_c3b3
  FUN_c05a   TAIL JMP $C079,  FUN_c219 TAIL JMP $907E,  FUN_c3bf TAIL JMP $BFF3
  FUN_f105   TAIL JMP $F105  (self -- a CYCLE GUARD is mandatory, this is not hypothetical)
  the rest end RTS/RTI.

CONSEQUENCE -- a pre-existing wrong-answer class, independent of grm-3x1 and grm-hum:
HelperModel summarizes a helper by the max-address recognized write in ITS OWN BODY
(BoardBankAnalyzer:864-871). For any helper that tail-jumps to another bank-setting routine,
that is the wrong site. FUN_d131 is the clearest case: its only own site is $D135 STA $C006,
so constState = bank 6 and EVERY call to it currently folds bank 6 -- while the real
post-call state is bank 5. That annotation is shipping today and is wrong.

So "restore megaman to 1781 refs" is NOT the goal. The 1781 number was wrong in two
independent ways: bank 6 for FUN_d846 (should be 5), and the same error at FUN_d131 and
FUN_c55d call sites. Increment 2 as briefed would faithfully REINTRODUCE bank 6 -- a
confident falsehood. It must not be blessed in that state.

REQUIRED MODEL FIX (increment 2b): a helper's effect is the bank state at its EXIT, following
tail calls -- not the highest-address write inside its own body. Minimal tractable form:
when a helper's function terminates in a JMP/CALL_TERMINATOR to another recognized helper,
COMPOSE the two effects (callee wins on the bits it owns). Bounded depth, and a cycle guard
is required -- FUN_f105 tail-jumps to itself.
The principled statement to put in findHelpers' javadoc: switchSite means "the last recognized
write on the path to the helper's RETURN", and the max-address rule is only a valid proxy for
that while control cannot leave the function body. A tail call is exactly when it can.
Note the engine ALREADY has the ingredients: runDataflow treats a CALL_TERMINATOR jump as a
call and folds the callee helper's effect, so the state at the end of FUN_d846 is already
computed correctly -- it is only the HelperModel SUMMARY that ignores it.

The honest fallback, if composition is deferred: decline (warn) when a helper tail-calls
another helper, rather than assert the body-local answer. Losing 78 refs beats shipping a
wrong bank.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SESSION HANDOFF (2026-08-01). Increments 1+2 are DONE and pushed to branch
grm-hum-increments-1-2 (commit c7278ae). NOT merged to main -- the headless gate is red by
design, see below. Read that commit message first; it records the measurements.

STATE: unit suite green (142 tests). Every C64/PET/C128 golden byte-identical. Real ROMs
measured: contra 0 -> 257 overlay refs and 0 -> 2 bank comments (its first overlay refs ever);
megaman 151 -> 157 comments, 37 -> 31 warnings, refs unchanged at 1703; every other pinned
title byte-identical.

NEXT: increments 2b and 3. A subagent was launched for both and died to the session limit
BEFORE writing any edits, so nothing is half-applied -- the tree is exactly 1+2. Its brief is
reproduced by the plan file plus the two comments above this one.

2b -- TAIL-CALL COMPOSITION. This is the blocking item: megaman's 6 new comments include a
falsehood (9067 says "bank -> 6 via FUN_d846"; the answer is 5, because FUN_d846 ends
JMP $C3B3 and FUN_c3b3 latches bank 5). findHelpers summarizes a helper by the max-address
mechanism write in its OWN body, which is a valid proxy only while control cannot leave the
body. Compose a helper's effect with its tail-callee's when the callee is a recognized helper
with a caller-independent effect; DECLINE (warn) on caller-dependent callees, disagreeing
multi-exit paths, cycles, or depth-cap. FUN_f105 tail-jumps to ITSELF so the cycle guard is
mandatory. runDataflow ALREADY folds a CALL_TERMINATOR jump's callee effect -- only the
HelperModel SUMMARY discards it, which is why this is a summary fix and not a dataflow fix.
Do not break nesbanktest2: its trampolines end in RTS, so max-address is right there. The rule
must be NARROWED, not replaced.

3 -- IMPOSSIBLE-BANK GUARD. Warn + suppress annotation/retarget when a recovered bank index
exceeds the image's bank count. Deliberately do NOT model hardware aliasing (user ruling,
recorded in docs/vision-board-banking.md section 10 item 10).

ACCEPTANCE ALREADY WIRED (tools/banktest, committed): nesuxhelpertest fixture in the
nes-banking chunk carries both real idioms plus a synthetic tail call (FUN_c160 sets bank 3
then JMPs to FUN_c170 which sets bank 2; FUN_c170 is also JSR'd from RESET so Ghidra makes it
a separate function and the JMP is a genuine inter-function tail call). Criteria U1-U10:
U1-U7 PASS today; U8 needs increment 3; U9/U10 need 2b. U3 is the anti-overreach criterion --
it asserts a RAM-sourced helper argument stays UNRESOLVED. If someone makes U3 pass by
resolving it, that is the one thing this bead must not do.

TWO GOLDENS PENDING A BLESS, deliberately not done:
1. nesbanktest2 -- increment 2 turned two honest warnings into two CORRECT annotations
   (FUN_c010 -> bank 2, FUN_c020 -> bank 1). Verified against the fixture source. Blessable
   now or after 2b; if 2b changes it, 2b is wrong.
2. nesuxhelpertest -- no golden committed on purpose. Create it only once U1-U10 are green,
   or it pins the wrong behavior as expected.
3. megaman -- DO NOT BLESS until 2b lands. Its current dump contains the bank-6 falsehood.
   Note its golden was never a clean baseline anyway: FUN_d131 and FUN_c55d have been folding
   bank 6 (should be 5) since long before grm-3x1, so the re-bless will move lines for reasons
   unrelated to this bead. Account for each count line rather than targeting any number --
   in particular do NOT treat the historical 1781 as the goal; it was wrong two ways.

Bless with: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh bless --only megaman,contra H:/emulators/nes/roms
(ROM dirs H:/emulators/nes/roms and Z:/nes/db; all 5 SHA-256s verified this session.)

FILED THIS SESSION: grm-8cq (BankReachProbe's today= column is stale -- it mirrors the
PRE-grm-3x1 tier-1-only writesInRange, so every refless indexed site reports today=NO while
production does see it via tier 2; it cost this session a blind alley).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
2b BLAST-RADIUS MEASUREMENT (2026-08-01, session 2). Scanned every pinned title's helper for
its exit terminator, to predict which goldens increment 2b may move:

  contra       FUN_c13f  ends RTS at $C145   -> max-address switchSite already VALID
  wizwarr      FUN_ffc0  ends RTS at $FFD9   -> valid
  dragonpower  FUN_ffbe  ends RTS at $FFCB   -> valid
  megaman      FUN_d846  TAIL JMP $C3B3 at $D893   } all three land on FUN_c3b3,
               FUN_d131  TAIL JMP $C3B3 at $D159   } which latches bank 5
               FUN_c55d  TAIL JMP $C3B3 at $C573   }
               FUN_c05a  TAIL JMP $C079, FUN_c219 TAIL JMP $907E, FUN_c3bf TAIL JMP $BFF3
               FUN_f105  TAIL JMP $F105 (ITSELF -- cycle guard is mandatory)

PREDICTION for 2b: megaman is the ONLY real-ROM golden that moves. Contra keeps its 257 refs /
2 comments unchanged; wizwarr, dragonpower, shenlong, the four Bandai titles, zelda and smb3
stay byte-identical. On the synthetic side nesbanktest2 must ALSO stay put (its trampolines end
in RTS -- if 2b moves it, 2b over-reached and narrowed the wrong rule), and nesuxhelpertest's

If contra moves, 2b broke the straight-line RTS case. If nesbanktest2 moves, same. Either is a
