comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
REGRESSION FOUND, AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER REPORT (2026-08-02).

WIZWARR IS REGRESSED, AND INCREMENT 2 DID IT -- not 2b. Isolated by stashing the 2b/3 working
changes and re-running wizwarr at commit 918a70e (increments 1+2 only): identical numbers, so
2b is exonerated.

  wizwarr    golden        inc2 and inc2+2b+3
  refs         17    ->      0
  bankComments 11    ->      4
  warnings      8    ->     11
  lost: bank -> 7 / 3 / 1 / 1 / 4 / 6 / 4 via FUN_ffc0 at 80c2/d56e/d691/e5b1/e924/e92b/e942
  lost refs incl. 80ca -> PRG_ALL_B7::8c4b and 80cd -> PRG_ALL_B7::8b8b, i.e. DOWNSTREAM of
  the 80c2 call -- the annotation was load-bearing, not cosmetic.

MY EARLIER CLAIM WAS WRONG. The increments-1+2 commit message and my report to the user both
say every real-ROM golden except megaman/contra stayed byte-identical. That was based on an
INCOMPLETE run: after increment 2 I only ran `--only megaman,contra`. The last FULL real-ROM
run predated increment 2. Lesson: run the full realrom set before claiming a blast radius,
or say explicitly which titles were actually measured.

ROOT CAUSE -- same family as the megaman tail call, different mechanism:
  FUN_ffc0 (AxROM, bank arg in A) is a CALL-INTO-ANOTHER-BANK-AND-RETURN trampoline:
    FFC0: STY $C1 / STA $C3          ; save target-pointer low byte and the bank arg
    FFC4: LDA $C5 / PHA              ; save the CURRENT bank shadow on the stack
    FFC7: AND #$18 / ORA $C3         ; splice the requested bank into the shadow
    FFCB: STA $C5
    FFCD: STA $8000                  ; <<< THE COMMIT -- switch to the target bank
    FFD0: JSR $FFDA                  ; -> JMP ($00C1), call the routine in that bank
    FFD3: PLA / STA $C5
    FFD6: STA $8000                  ; <<< THE RESTORE -- value came from PLA, unrecoverable
    FFD9: RTS
  findHelpers picks switchSite = MAX ADDRESS = $FFD6, the RESTORE. Increment 2 mini-inlines
  that site, scans back, hits PLA (an A-modifier) and gets UNKNOWN -- so every call site
  declines. The PRE-increment-2 convention (recover argReg at the CALL SITE and deposit it
  verbatim) was RIGHT for this helper, because the argument in A is exactly what $FFCD commits.

So max-address switchSite is wrong in BOTH directions:
  megaman FUN_d846 -- too EARLY (the real effect is past the body, via a tail call)
  wizwarr FUN_ffc0 -- too LATE  (the real commit is the FIRST write; the last is a restore)
The unifying statement is the one 2b already put in the javadoc -- "the last recognized write on
the path to the helper's RETURN" -- but neither max-address NOR min-address implements it. A
switch/call/restore pair nets to NO CHANGE on return, which is a third answer again.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION (not yet implemented, needs a decision):
  Prefer the mini-inline only when it RESOLVES; fall back to the legacy argReg-at-call-site
  recovery when it yields unknown. That restores wizwarr (legacy path resolves A) and keeps
  contra (mini-inline resolves Y, legacy would not) and megaman (2b's composition resolves).
  It is a strict improvement over both conventions taken alone. Downside: it is a heuristic
  union of two models, so it wants a comment saying WHY rather than looking like a hack.
  The principled alternative -- model save/restore pairs so the helper's net effect is
  "unchanged" -- is more correct but bigger, and would ALSO drop wizwarr's 17 refs unless
  callers genuinely observe the switched bank downstream (the B7 refs above suggest they do,
  which needs checking before committing to that model).

STATUS: 2b and 3 are otherwise GOOD -- unit 145/145, full headless gate 368/368 criteria PASS,
nesuxhelpertest U1-U10 all PASS, megaman's bank-6 falsehood is gone. Only wizwarr blocks.
DO NOT bless any real-ROM golden until wizwarr is resolved.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RESOLVED (2026-08-02). wizwarr PASSES; only contra and megaman differ, which is the intended
blast radius. Full realrom: pass=9 fail=2 skip=1.

TWO THINGS WENT WRONG AND BOTH ARE WORTH RECORDING.

1. THE FIX. The user spotted that my proposed "use the FIRST write instead of the last" repair
   could not work: at $FFCD, A = ($C5 & $18) | $C3, and `ORA $C3` is NON-IMMEDIATE, so
   StoredValueScanner stops there (:233). Neither of FUN_ffc0's switch sites mini-inlines --
   $FFCD needs $C3, $FFD6 needs a PLA. Confirmed by inspection; they were right.
   Note bits 0-2 (AxROM's whole tracked field, `bits: 3`) come ENTIRELY from $C3, which
   $FFC2 stored from the caller's A. So the legacy convention "the argument register holds
   the field value" is not merely lucky on this helper -- it is exactly what the code computes.
   The engine cannot DERIVE it only because it lacks zero-page store-to-load propagation
   (bead A territory).
   Implemented: MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.depositHelperArgument prefers the evaluated
   answer and falls back to the conventional argValue when the evaluation pins down nothing.
   A fallback can only fill in where evaluation was silent, so it can never overwrite a derived
   answer with a weaker assumed one. Contra is recovered only by evaluation (argument in Y,
   invisible to the convention); wizwarr only by the convention (argument laundered through ZP,
   invisible to evaluation). Neither model dominates -- that is why it is a union, and the
   javadoc says so.

2. A MEASUREMENT TRAP THAT COST TWO WRONG CONCLUSIONS. `build-and-test.sh check unit`
   DELIBERATELY SKIPS the extension build/install (documented in CLAUDE.md). realrom-test.sh
   runs against the INSTALLED extension. So `check unit && realrom-test.sh check` measures the
   PREVIOUS build. I did exactly that, saw wizwarr unchanged, and concluded the fix had failed
   -- it had actually worked. Re-running after `check nes-banking` (which does build+install)
   showed the pass.
   RULE: before any realrom run, build+install via a HEADLESS chunk (`check nes-banking`) or the
   full gate. Never trust a realrom measurement that follows only `check unit`.
   This ALSO retroactively explains nothing about the earlier wizwarr regression -- that one was
   real and is now fixed -- but it is the same shape as the grm-8cq stale-probe trap: the tool
   answered a question about a different build than the one under test.

FINAL REAL-ROM STATE (all measured against a freshly installed extension):
  contra   0 -> 257 refs, 0 -> 849 instrs, 0 -> 2 comments, warnings 6 -> 6
           (c0cb/c157 -> bank 1 via FUN_c13f; c0d3 stack, c149/c164 RAM, c142 helper-interior
           still honestly warned; 2 new warnings in bank-1 code that only became analyzable
           because of the new refs)
  megaman  1781 -> 1704 refs, 7437 -> 7429 instrs, 153 -> 156 comments, 3 -> 32 warnings
           9067 bank -> 5 via FUN_d846   (was the pre-grm-3x1 golden's WRONG bank 6)
           91bf/949e/a044/a082 bank -> 5 via FUN_d131   (was wrongly bank 6, shipping for ages)
           9d05 bank -> 5 via FUN_c55d
           The 11 FUN_c39c warnings remain -- bank from RAM $31, genuinely unrecoverable.
           refs do NOT return to 1781 and should not: 77 of those were retargets into
           PRG_LO_B6 justified by the wrong bank-6 claim at FUN_d846/FUN_d131/FUN_c55d call
           sites. They are gone because they were wrong.
  wizwarr, dragonpower, shenlong, db3, dbz2, dbz_datach, dbz_saiyan, zelda, smb3: byte-identical
  smb: SKIP (ROM not present in the supplied dirs)

Synthetic: unit 145/145; full headless gate 368/368 criteria PASS; nesuxhelpertest U1-U10 all
PASS including U3 (the anti-overreach criterion) unchanged.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
THE MEGAMAN DETERMINATION IS ANSWERED (hand RE + current goldens, 2026-08-06). This bead said
"NOBODY HAS CHECKED WHICH -- that determination is the first task here, and it decides whether
megaman ever gets blessed." Checked. The answer is the OPTIMISTIC reading, and by a wider margin
than this bead allowed for.

=== 1. CURRENT COUNTS vs THE TWO HISTORICAL POINTS ===

                        pre-grm-3x1    post-grm-3x1    current 2026-08-06
  refs.intoOverlay          1781           1703              1704
  instrs.inOverlay           --             --               7429
  bankComments               153            151                156
  warnings                     3             37                 32

  NOTE the 1703 -> 1704 move is NOT a gain: grm-g73 measures megaman as bistable run-to-run at
  exactly refs -1 / instrs +2, so 1703 and 1704 are the same result seen twice. Do not read a
  one-ref delta on this title as signal until grm-g73 closes.

  THE HEADLINE: bankComments 156 now EXCEEDS the pre-regression baseline of 153. The annotation
  channel is RICHER than before grm-3x1, not poorer. warnings are also down 37 -> 32 since the
  low point (grm-4kc, grm-nju, grm-mu7 all landed in between). Only refs.intoOverlay remains
  below its old peak, at -77.

=== 2. SITE 9067, THE NAMED DECISIVE CASE: THE OLD ANNOTATION WAS WRONG ===

This bead recorded 9067 degrading from "bank -> 6 (bank=6) via FUN_d846" to a warning. Current
state: NO bookmark, and the generated comment reads "bank -> 5 (bank=5) via FUN_d846".

HAND TRACE OF FUN_d846 shows 5 is correct and 6 never was:
  - sets PRG bank and $42 to #6 at entry (redundant -- the chunk loop overrides immediately)
  - sends 10 chunks to the PPU, setting PRG bank from a stride-2 table at d81e per chunk
  - sets PRG bank and $42 to #6 again, then calls b53f via the thunk at bff6
  - finally JMPs to c3b3, which sets PRG bank and $42 to #5 and returns

So d846's EXIT state is bank 5. The old "bank=6" came from the last write inside d846's own
body -- the #6 before the b53f call -- because nothing followed the tail JMP into c3b3. The
sequence at this site is therefore:

    1781-refs era     bank -> 6     WRONG
    after grm-3x1     warning       honest but unhelpful
    current           bank -> 5     CORRECT

THIS IS A THIRD OUTCOME THIS BEAD DID NOT CONSIDER. The framing was "correctness gain" vs
"correct annotations traded for warnings". At the decisive site it was neither: a WRONG
annotation was replaced by an honest warning and then by the RIGHT value. The old 1781 refs
did not merely come from a blind model -- at least one of them was a wrong bank.

=== 3. FUN_c39c'S 11 WARNINGS ARE HONEST DECLINES, NOT LOST INFORMATION ===

c39c appears in 11 of the 34 warnings this bead flagged. Hand trace: it saves P, A and X, then
sets PRG bank and $42 from ZP $31, subtracting 6 first when $31 > 6. $31 is INC'd, DEC'd, zeroed
at several sites, and elsewhere loaded from tables or by more exotic routes.

That makes $31 a STATEFUL COUNTER with a wrap-adjust (7->1 ... 12->6). Its value at a given site
depends on execution history rather than on any dominating definition, so no constant-
propagation model recovers it, and no amount of helper-argument work will. The analyzer is
correctly declining. Recovering these would need value-range or path-sensitive tracking of $31,
which is a different and much larger project -- do not file it against helper-arg recovery.

=== 4. VERDICT ===

Both halves point the same way. The surviving annotations got BETTER (156 > 153, with at least
one previously-wrong value now correct), and the new warnings are HONEST (c39c's argument is
genuinely unrecoverable). The pessimistic reading -- correct annotations traded for warnings --
is not supported at the one site this bead nominated to decide it.

MEGAMAN SHOULD BE BLESSABLE ON THE MERITS. It is still blocked from actual blessing by grm-g73
(run-to-run bistability), which is an independent problem and unaffected by this finding.

HONEST LIMIT OF THIS EVIDENCE: 9067 is one site out of a 77-ref delta. It was THIS BEAD'S named
decisive case and it resolves cleanly, but it does not prove every lost ref was wrong. If a
stronger guarantee is wanted, the remaining work is to sample a handful more of the lost refs --
not to re-open the framing.

=== 5. WHAT THIS BEAD STILL OWNS ===

The megaman determination was only its FIRST task. The bead's main body -- contra,
dragonpower and shenlong at 0 refs / 0 bank comments, with the helper identified but the
ARGUMENT unrecoverable at every call site (FUN_c13f, FUN_ffbe, FUN_8eeb) -- is untouched by
this and remains open. dragonpower and shenlong are both GxROM Dragon Ball titles and likely
share one engine, so treat them as one investigation.

=== 6. SPUN OUT OF THIS TRACE ===
  - $42 is hand-confirmed as megaman's write-through bank shadow (noted on grm-mej.2).
  - d846's 10-chunk loop takes its bank from a stride-2 table at d81e -- grm-m95's shape, ten
    switch sites in one loop (noted on grm-m95).
  - d846 is a real-ROM case where tail-call composition changes the answer (noted on grm-432).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CONTRA DEF-USE PASS COMPLETE (human, 2026-08-09). All TEN warnings in the current blessed
golden are now classified. Contra needs no further tracing -- what remains is one fix, two
out-of-scope classes, and two phantoms.

THE SWITCH ENGINE, as read from the ROM:
  c13f  LDA $ffd0,Y / c142 STA $ffd0,Y / c145 RTS   ; bus-conflict latch. Bank arrives in Y.
                                                    ; c13f does NOT touch the shadow.
  c139  LDA $8000 / STA $07ec  -> falls through into c13f
                                                    ; shadow-SETTING wrapper ($8000 is contra's
                                                    ; bank-identifying byte, = N in bank N)
  c146  LDY $07ec / c149 JMP $c13f                  ; RESTORE current bank from shadow
  c14c  save A+Y / STA $07ed from $8000 / LDY #1 / c157 JSR $c13f / restore
                                                    ; "call into bank 1, remembering the old one"
  c15e  save A+Y / LDY $07ed / c164 JSR $c13f / restore
                                                    ; counterpart RESTORE from the second shadow
So there are TWO shadows, not one: $07ec (general current-bank) and $07ed (the save slot used
only by the c14c/c15e bracket).

ALL TEN WARNINGS, with "what computes the argument immediately before it?":

  site   callee   arg class                                   value        disposition
  ----   ------   -----------------------------------------   ----------   -----------------
  c094   c139     immediate  LDY #1                            bank 1       RECOVERABLE -- bug
  c0a2   c139     immediate  LDY #1                            bank 1       RECOVERABLE -- bug
  c21b   c139     immediate  LDY #6                            bank 6       RECOVERABLE -- bug
  c9c0   c139     ROM table  $c952,X (stride 3) AND #7 / TAY   {0,2,4,5,6}  honest (multi-valued)
  c0d3   c13f     read-back  LDA $8000 / PHA .. PLA / TAY      unknown      grm-mej (read-back)
  c149   c13f     shadow     LDY $07ec                         unknown      grm-mej (restore)
  c164   c13f     shadow     LDY $07ed                         unknown      grm-mej (restore)
  c142   --       mechanism write in the helper's OWN body     unknown      honest by construction
  8efc   --       NOT CODE                                     --           phantom, see below
  811a   ov call  NOT CODE                                     --           phantom, see below

(1) THE THREE RECOVERABLE SITES ARE ONE BUG, AND IT IS THE WRAPPER LEVEL.
c0cb and c157 are the SAME idiom -- LDY #imm then call -- and they resolve today (they are the
golden's two bank comments). The only difference at c094/c0a2/c21b is that the call goes to the
WRAPPER c139 instead of straight to c13f. c139's body is LDA $8000 / STA $07ec: it clobbers A
and leaves Y completely untouched, so the caller's Y does reach the mechanism write.

HYPOTHESIS, from reading BoardBankAnalyzer (NOT yet verified by a run): argReg is 'A' (the STA's
store register), memory-latch recovers contra by re-evaluating STA $ffd0,Y under callSiteRegisters
instead, but recoverCallArgument gates that on argumentSurvivesPrologue for argReg ONLY -- and
across c139's prologue A is dead. The survival test is being run on the nominal argReg rather than
on the register the strategy will actually read. If that is right, the fix is exactly grm-k90's
proposed one (run argumentSurvivesPrologue per register, pass through the survivors); see the
comment filed there.

(2) c9c0 IS AN HONEST DECLINE, and it is a CHR-pointer dispatcher, not PRG control flow.
FUN_c9a3 takes an index in A, computes X = A*3, and does LDA $c952,X / AND #7 / TAY / JSR $c139.
The table at $c950 is 3 bytes wide -- pointer plus a bank and a double-byte flag in byte 3 -- and
addresses CHR data uploaded to the PPU. Banks 0 (1x), 2 (1x), 4 (12x), 5 (8x), 6 (5x) appear.
On exit the function calls the c146 helper to restore PRG from $07ec. Five distinct banks reach
one site, so no single static value exists; this is set-valued/path-forking territory (the
grm-wul shape), not a defect. It is also the ONLY genuinely table-driven site contra has.

(3) THREE SITES ARE grm-mej SCOPE, NOT CONTRA DEFECTS. c0d3, c149 and c164 all answer the same
question -- "what bank was I in before?" -- from state the caller never wrote: the cartridge
itself ($8000 read-back through the CPU stack) or a RAM shadow ($07ec / $07ed). This is the same
disposition rcransom got (grm-1fv): unknown IS the honest answer at these sites, and they become
resolvable only under shadow propagation. Note c0d3's context confirms the engine is otherwise
healthy -- the LDY #1 / JSR $c13f inside the same bit-7-of-$1b conditional IS detected, and its
following JSR at c0ce correctly retargets to 1:$80d5.

(4) 8efc AND 811a ARE PHANTOMS -- A SECOND INSTANCE OF grm-eyn'S OVER-READ.
Both are cruft from a switch-table overrun at 8492: 8efc is data mistakenly disassembled, and
811a picked up 8efc's bogus reference. THE "THIRD HELPER IN OVERLAY SPACE" IS NOT REAL --
FUN_PRG_LO_B1__8259 exists only because of the overrun, so do not trace it. Two of contra's ten
warnings are therefore not banking findings at all; they are downstream of a Ghidra decompiler
defect this project has already diagnosed (grm-eyn) and drafted an upstream fix for (grm-b3m).
Commented on grm-eyn as a second-title instance.

NET: contra's realistic ceiling is 3 more resolved sites (c094/c0a2/c21b, bank 1/1/6) from one
fix, plus 3 more if grm-mej lands. c142, c9c0, 8efc and 811a should never resolve.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DRAGONPOWER / SHENLONG: WHAT THE DEF-USE PASS STILL OWES (scoping only, 2026-08-15).
No new RE here -- this separates what the 2026-08-01 comment settled from what section 2 of
docs/human-research-todo.md still wants, because the two were being conflated.

SETTLED 2026-08-01 (engine ANATOMY, reconnaissance written before this method existed):
$FFBE helper body, $FFDC inline far-call trampoline, $F2 = PRG shadow / $F9 = CHR shadow, the
per-offset cross-bank invariant regions ($FF68-$FFF9 dp / $FEE0-$FFF9 sl), and the grm-e7v
structural blocker. Anatomy does NOT predict dispositions: contra had a fully-disassembled helper
from the same comment and its 8/9 pass still produced four new dispositions, two of them sites
that were not code.

NOT STARTED: none of grm-8iy.5's four tables exist for these titles.

THE WHOLE WARNED POPULATION (blessed goldens, 6 each, both at 0 refs / 0 bank comments):
  shared by both    8ee4  9913  ffc8  ffea
  dragonpower only  e3bb  e906
  shenlong only     a03f  d9a9
8ee4/9913/ffea are helper call sites; the rest are raw mechanism writes.

FIVE OPEN QUESTIONS:
1. Is FUN_8eeb PRG or CHR? Never disassembled. Mapper 66 packs CHR in bits 4-5 and PRG in bits
   0-1 of ONE write, so $FFBE's LDA $F2 / ASL / ASL / ORA $F9 composes a COMPOSITE REGISTER
   (wizwarr's $00 shape, not a bank number). If 8eeb is the CHR path, 8ee4 is cv2-class noise
   for refs.intoOverlay.
2. Call-site table. ffea is INFERABLE as the trampoline's own JSR $FFBE (bank via caller PHA ->
   stack -> grm-mej.3) but unconfirmed; the load-bearing unknown is WHO CALLS $FFDC AND WITH WHAT.
   9913 and 8ee4 wholly open. ffc8 is probably the helper's own STA $FFCC,Y -- contra's c142
   disposition, one address to confirm.
3. The four unexplained mechanism writes e3bb/e906/a03f/d9a9 sit OUTSIDE the invariant region --
   per-bank code switching without the helper. Unread, and the most likely to be answerable
   WITHOUT grm-e7v/grm-mej.
4. Wrapper set: not enumerated. $FFDC is a trampoline, not an argumentSurvivesPrologue-sense
   wrapper. Has teeth now that grm-k90 shipped (contra 2->5, plus unanticipated wizwarr/lifeforce).
5. Shadow-writer table: $F2/$F9 named, writers not. Write-through adjacency is grm-mej.2 route (a)
   and free; written far from the switch needs a grm-hb6.11 hint. Also settles whether both titles
   really use the same ZP pair.

CHEAP PREREQUISITE: byte-compare $FF68-$FFF9 across the two ROMs. "One trace covers two" is
asserted, not measured -- the invariant regions are DIFFERENT SIZES (146 vs 282) and two of six
warnings are at different addresses.

SEQUENCING, a judgment call: a perfect call-site table still leaves both at 0 refs until grm-e7v
(open, unlocks $FFCC), grm-mej.2 (unlocks $F2/$F9 reads) and grm-mej.3 (unlocks the stack-passed
bank at the trampoline) land. Trace now for Q3/Q4; defer past grm-e7v if the expected answer
everywhere is "blocked on infrastructure".

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DRAGONPOWER / SHENLONG: the def-use pass is effectively DONE, from the project owner's hand
disassembly 2026-08-15. Five of the six warned sites per title are now dispositioned, and the
prerequisite byte-compare is settled. Do not re-trace either title; what remains is two
addresses on shenlong.

=== "ONE TRACE COVERS TWO" IS NOW MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED ===

Owner: dragonpower's "all 4 banks are essentially identical ff88-fff9", and for shenlong "all 4
banks are essentially identical to each other AND to dragonpower". So the two titles share one
switch engine, byte for byte, and every finding below transfers. This retires the cheap
prerequisite the human-research item called for. (Note it does not exactly reproduce the 8/1
comment's measured invariant bounds -- $FF68-$FFF9 dp / $FEE0-$FFF9 sl -- but "essentially
identical" is an eyeball over the engine proper; the two are consistent, the earlier one is the
measurement.)

=== THE ENGINE, COMPLETED ===

  $FFBE  LDA $F2 / ASL / ASL / ORA $F9 / TAY / LDA $FFCC,Y / STA $FFCC,Y / RTS
         Recomposes the mapper-66 composite register from the two shadows. TAKES NO REGISTER
         ARGUMENT -- its input is $F2 (PRG) and $F9 (CHR), both memory.
         Called from $9913 as the FIRST INSTRUCTION of a function, and from $FFEA.
  $FFE8  STA $F2 / JSR $FFBE / JMP ($17)
         The far-call entry. Bank arrives in A, is deposited to the shadow, then $FFBE applies
         it and control transfers through the $17/$18 vector.
  $FFDC  Sets $17/$18 from the CALLER'S RETURN ADDRESS + 1, pulls the saved bank off the stack,
         falls through to $FFE8. This is the far-RETURN: a routine ends with JSR $FFDC and
         execution resumes at the next instruction in the original bank.

  Call-site example, fully recovered: $983F saves $F2 on the stack, sets $17/$18 from a
  3-byte-stride table (entries at $8000, $8003, $8006, ... 6 entries) indexed by Y, then
  LDA #1 / JSR $FFE8. So a CONSTANT bank argument (1) does exist at a real call site.

  Shadow-writer table (check #3, and this is the clean answer): $F2 IS WRITTEN BY EXACTLY ONE
  INSTRUCTION, the STA $F2 at $FFE8 -- "in so-far disassembled code", so treat as strong but not
  closed. One writer means the shadow's value is always the far-call's A argument, which is the
  best possible case for grm-mej.2.

=== SITE-BY-SITE DISPOSITION (the six warnings per title) ===

  8ee4  PHANTOM. Over-read jump table at $8F00 ($1E = 30 actual entries); no bank switching
        there at all. THIS ALSO ANSWERS QUESTION 1: "FUN_8eeb" is neither the PRG nor the CHR
        helper -- IT IS NOT CODE. There is no co-equal second helper. Do not look for one.
  e3bb  PHANTOM (dragonpower). Data, not code, from an over-read jump table at $91AF.
  e906  PHANTOM (dragonpower). Bogus mid-instruction disassembly from an over-read jump table
        at $9076.
  ffc8  HELPER'S OWN MECHANISM WRITE, honest by construction -- contra's c142 disposition.
        Confirmed by arithmetic over the $FFBE body: LDA $F2 (ffbe) ASL (ffc0) ASL (ffc1)
        ORA $F9 (ffc2) TAY (ffc4) LDA $FFCC,Y (ffc5) STA $FFCC,Y (ffc8). The question item asked
        for "one address to confirm"; it confirms.
  ffea  THE TRAMPOLINE'S OWN JSR $FFBE, inside $FFE8, likewise by arithmetic: STA $F2 occupies
        ffe8-ffe9, so the JSR sits at ffea. The item's inference was right, but the MECHANISM IS
        NOT THE STACK -- A is deposited to $F2 one instruction earlier, so this is a shadow
        (grm-mej.2) case, not the grm-mej.3 stack case the item predicted.
  9913  CALL TO $FFBE WITH NO ARGUMENT. $FFBE reads $F2/$F9 and takes nothing in a register, so
        "bank argument could not be recovered at this call site" is a MISFRAMING here, not a
        finding: there is no argument to recover. Strongly suspect this and ffea are instances
        of grm-xym (no-argument helpers reporting helperArgReg and emitting a spurious
        unrecoverable-argument warning) -- worth checking before any dataflow work.
  a03f  OPEN (shenlong only). Not covered by the owner's pass.
  d9a9  OPEN (shenlong only). Not covered by the owner's pass.

=== WHAT THIS CHANGES ===

THREE OF DRAGONPOWER'S SIX WARNINGS ARE grm-eyn PHANTOMS, from three DIFFERENT over-read tables
($8F00, $91AF, $9076) in one title. That is a much denser instance than megaman's single a737
table, and it is on a title at 0 refs / 0 instrs -- so grm-eyn's blast radius is bigger than the
megaman case suggested. Recorded there.

The remaining real population on dragonpower is THREE sites (9913, ffc8, ffea), of which one is
the mechanism write itself and two are plausibly grm-xym noise. Question 4 (the wrapper set) is
answered by elimination: there is no wrapper in the argumentSurvivesPrologue sense -- $FFE8 is
the entry, $FFDC the return, $FFBE the applier, and nothing else carries a bank.

The ceiling is unchanged and still gated on infrastructure, per the item's own sequencing note:
$FFCC is unreadable until grm-e7v (single fully-overlaid PRG_ALL window ⇒ bankInvariantRomByte
returns null), and following A -> $F2 -> $FFBE's LDA $F2 needs grm-mej.2 plus arithmetic in the
deposit (ASL/ASL/ORA $F9 -- a COMPOSITE register, wizwarr's $00 shape, not a bank number).
grm-mej.3 is NOT on the critical path here after all.

REMAINING HUMAN WORK, now small: read shenlong's a03f and d9a9. Given the engine is byte-identical
across the two titles and dragonpower's two title-unique sites were both jump-table phantoms, the
prior strongly favours these being phantoms too -- but that is a prediction, not a reading.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CLOSED OUT 2026-08-15 (same day, owner follow-up). The two remaining shenlong sites are read:

  a03f  mid-instruction disassembly from an over-read jump table at $87D0
  d9a9  mid-instruction disassembly from an over-read jump table at $9076

Both are grm-eyn phantoms, as predicted from dragonpower's pair. DRAGONPOWER AND SHENLONG ARE
NOW FULLY DISPOSITIONED -- there is nothing left to trace on either title.

FINAL SCORECARD, and it is identical for the two titles (6 warned sites each):

  8ee4   phantom   -- over-read table $8F00 (both titles)
  a03f   phantom   -- over-read table $87D0 (shenlong)
  d9a9   phantom   -- over-read table $9076 (shenlong)
  e3bb   phantom   -- over-read table $91AF (dragonpower)
  e906   phantom   -- over-read table $9076 (dragonpower)
  ffc8   honest by construction -- $FFBE's own STA $FFCC,Y mechanism write
  ffea   real      -- $FFE8's internal JSR $FFBE; bank arrives via shadow $F2 (grm-mej.2)
  9913   suspect   -- call to $FFBE, which takes NO register argument (probably grm-xym)

So each title is 3 phantoms + 1 by-construction + 2 engine-internal, and ALL FOUR of the
"unexplained mechanism writes outside the invariant region" that this item was built around
were the same artifact. That hypothesis -- per-bank code switching without the helper -- is
DEAD on both titles. There is exactly one switch engine and it is the $FFE8/$FFBE/$FFDC trio.

READ THIS CAREFULLY, because it is easy to overclaim: having no UNEXPLAINED sites is not the
same as resolving anything. Both titles still sit at 0 refs / 0 bank comments, and the reason is
unchanged and already known -- grm-e7v (single fully-overlaid PRG_ALL window, so
bankInvariantRomByte returns null and the $FFCC table is unreadable) plus grm-mej.2 (following
A -> $F2 -> $FFBE's LDA $F2, through an ASL/ASL/ORA $F9 composite-register deposit). What the
pass established is that NO NEW MECHANISM IS MISSING: the entire gap on these two titles is
attributable to grm-eyn, grm-xym, grm-e7v and grm-mej.2, with no residual unknown. That is a
real result for grm-8iy's scorecard -- two of its eight zero-instruction GME titles are now
fully accounted for by named beads.

Nothing here needs a human again. Remove from docs/human-research-todo.md section 2 entirely.

title: Backward value scan lacks single-predecessor check; over-confident value at CFG join
description: StoredValueScanner.java:114. resolveStoredValue only validates the prev->cur fall-through edge, never that cur has a single predecessor, so at a control-flow join it attributes the fall-through path value to the store with full confidence. Failure: LDA #$05 / BEQ t / LDA #$0A / t: STA $8000 returns fullyKnown 0x0A, ignoring A=$05 on the BEQ path. The immediate-fold and AND/ORA-fold paths bypass the engine merge (resolveLoad path is safe as it uses merged inStateAtStore). Fix: require block-leader / single-predecessor before folding a local immediate. Verdict CONFIRMED. Found by /code-review high.
notes: Fixed (commit pending): resolveStoredValue now aborts to unknown() at a control-flow join, detected via isControlFlowJoin (incoming flow Reference to cur from an addr other than prev). RESIDUAL: unresolved computed/indirect jumps leave no reference, so a join reached only by a jump table is not detected -- conservative in the safe direction (worst case a fold we'd otherwise make), not a wrong-value risk.
close_reason: Fixed in board-banking value-recovery hardening commit; verified compiles + buildExtension against Ghidra 12.1.2

title: recoverCallArgument guesses bank register (A-first), recording wrong bank
description: BoardBankAnalyzer.java:558. recoverCallArgument tries A then X then Y and returns the first that resolves to any immediate, not the register the helper actually reads. Failure: LDX #3 / LDA #$80 / JSR SelectBank (helper takes bank in X, its store not locally resolvable) -> A-first scan returns $80, engine records bank 0x80 instead of 3; downstream refs retargeted to wrong overlay, EOL comment lies. Fix pattern: propagate unknown() when the convention is ambiguous rather than a confident guess. Verdict CONFIRMED. Found by /code-review high.
notes: Fixed (commit pending): recoverCallArgument now scans the register the helper actually stores into its mechanism (HelperModel.argReg from StoredValueScanner.storeRegister on the switch site) instead of the A-first guess. Strictly dominates old behavior: the STX-helper failure now records the correct bank; transform helpers degrade to prior behavior, never worse. RESIDUAL follow-up: a helper that stores a DIFFERENT register than the caller loads (e.g. TXA / STA mechanism) still mis-attributes, needing recursive convention inference inside the helper body. Not filing separately unless it bites.
close_reason: Fixed in board-banking value-recovery hardening commit; verified compiles + buildExtension against Ghidra 12.1.2

title: Build pipeline: YAML -> .gdt data-type archive generator (Gradle task)
description: Per gib.1.2 review decision (struct source of truth, option 3 from the start): a Gradle build task with Ghidra jars on the classpath walks the descriptor/types YAML and emits a .gdt data-type archive via FileDataTypeManager.createFileArchive(). The loader consumes ONLY the .gdt (standard archive API, no YAML parser in runtime). Rules: .gdt is a build artifact — never committed, never hand-edited, CI always regenerates. Deliverables: (a) YAML->DataType builder (structs, flags/enums, field comments); (b) Gradle task wiring; (c) generated c64ref-derived struct YAML for VIC-II/SID/CIA feeding it (or stub until the c64ref generator lands). Bonus: the .gdt doubles as a standalone publishable artifact usable in stock Ghidra.
close_reason: YAML->.gdt build pipeline complete and independently verified: gradle buildGdt emits build/c64.gdt (5 named types, reopen-verified via openFileArchive); buildExtension confirms snakeyaml stays build-only (absent from shipped zip). Commit b636540.

title: Design: memory map schema and system descriptor format
description: Design the data model that describes a game system architecture: ROM regions (cart, BIOS), RAM regions, IO port ranges, mirroring rules, initial data type definitions (structs, enums). Goal: one descriptor file per system (YAML or JSON) drives the loader with zero hard-coded system knowledge in Java/Python. Output: draft schema + one worked example (e.g. SNES).
notes:
DESCRIPTOR DATA SOURCES (2026-07-03 survey):
- mist64/c64ref — canonical structured C64 reference (src/kernal/, src/c64io/, src/c64mem/); structured text + Python generator that can be adapted to emit JSON/YAML. THE upstream to consume.
- sajattack/c64-asm-labels — ready-made whole-memory-map label files in ACME/KickAssembler/radare2/VICE-.sym formats. CHECK LICENSE — derived from 'Mapping the Commodore 64' (Leemon), possible encumbrance like c64_ghidra.
- VICE .sym format ('al <hexaddr> .<label>') = de-facto C64 symbol interchange; Ghidra ImportSymbolsScript parses similar.
- KickAssembler built-in MOS6526_CIA/MOS6581_SID/MOS6569_VICII structs = cross-check for IO register offsets.
- c64-wiki Memory_Map banking table — the $0001 LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN combinations to encode as named bank configurations in the descriptor (the part no existing loader handles).
Schema implication: descriptor needs (a) regions, (b) named bank configurations selecting overlay sets, (c) symbol/label imports with provenance, (d) IO register struct definitions.
BANK-SWITCHING DESCRIPTOR DESIGN (user, 2026-07-03): decompose per-game banking info as MECHANISM + INITIAL STATE.
- C64: mechanism = write to $01; initial state = #$37 (BASIC+KERNAL+IO active, CHARROM inactive). Later add cartridge GAME/EXROM lines — note .crt header bytes 0x18/0x19 literally store EXROM/GAME line state, so for cartridges initial state can come from the container, like iNES headers do for NES.
- NES: mechanism = the Mapper (defines memory segmentation + what constitutes register reads/writes); initial state = PCB-specific -> descriptor-friendly.
- Implication for schema: MECHANISM is code-shaped (pluggable strategies — NES mappers will need several categories of register-access handling, e.g. MMC1's serial 5-write loading), INITIAL STATE is pure data. Descriptor names a mechanism + parameters + initial state; the earlier 'named bank configurations' idea becomes the STATE SPACE the mechanism transitions through.
- C64 = deliberately simple POC of the mechanism plumbing (single-register write) before NES stresses programmability.
DRAFT 1 DELIVERED (2026-07-03): ghidra/SCHEMA.md (design notes) + ghidra/descriptors/c64.yaml (worked example; YAML-validated, 8 bank states / 3 windows / 7 fixed regions).
Key schema decisions in draft:
- windows/occupants model: banked ranges declare candidate occupants; states assign occupant per window. Enumerated states table (C64: 8 PLA rows) OR mechanism-computed (NES) — schema allows both.
- context_register field links descriptor to the bundled 6510 language's bank context field (TMode-style); agreement needs a build-time check (open question 3).
- symbol sets are user-toggleable with game-RE defaults (kernal-api ON, kernal-zeropage/basic OFF since games reuse those).
- 'kind: entry' symbols create functions on EMPTY ROM slots so KERNAL calls resolve to named stubs without ROM bytes.
- descriptor states hardware facts (repeat_to mirrors); loader chooses representation.
OPEN QUESTIONS for user review (in SCHEMA.md): (1) struct source of truth: inline YAML vs c64ref-generated vs .gdt archives; (2) symbol interchange: YAML canonical + VICE .sym importer, or .sym canonical; (3) descriptor<->language agreement check for context register.
TODO before close: verify ROM SHA1s against real ROM set (placeholders emptied); adapt c64ref generator for the generated/*.yaml sources; VICE cross-check of the 8-state table.
SCHEMA REVISION 1.1 (user input, 2026-07-03): READ/WRITE ASYMMETRY. Bank mapping must differentiate read vs write targets — C64 writes under BASIC/KERNAL ROM always reach the RAM beneath; $D000 varies by state (IO: r/w both chips; CHARGEN: read ROM, write RAM). Modeled as occupant property 'on_write' (not per-state): omitted=self, <occupant>=write-through, 'mechanism'=writes are bank-mechanism events (NES mapper writes — doubles as analyzer watch-list), 'none'=open bus (Ultimax later). Per-state variance falls out of occupant selection automatically.
GIB.2 IMPLICATION recorded in SCHEMA.md: Ghidra resolves references to ONE address space — LDA $A000 and STA $A000 in the same bank state cannot target different blocks. Context-aware resolution hook must be ACCESS-TYPE-AWARE: (context, address, access) -> block. Loader-policy mitigation meanwhile: analyzer annotates stores into ROM-mapped ranges with reference to on_write target.
REVIEW DECISIONS (user, 2026-07-03) — SCHEMA.md open questions resolved:
(1) Structs: YAML canonical, .gdt generated at BUILD time FROM THE START (not staged via load-time builder). Loader only consumes .gdt. New bead grm-1.5 (blocks gib.1.3) for the generator + Gradle task. .gdt = build artifact, never committed; CI regenerates.
(2) Symbols: YAML canonical + VICE .sym importer (community files, cc65/KickAss output).
(3) Descriptor<->language: LOAD-TIME check — loader verifies language declares banking.context_register, clear error on mismatch.
IMPLICATION flagged to user: building the Gradle/.gdt pipeline is the first real EXTENSION CODE, which per the incubation rule ('extension gets its own repo from creation time') approaches repo-birth.
close_reason: Schema/system-descriptor format validated end-to-end by the grm-1.3 POC: the compiled c64.map + c64.gdt (from machines/c64.yaml) drove a real Ghidra 12.1.2 C64 PRG import — regions, banked windows (home-in-base), IO chip structs, and KERNAL symbols all applied correctly (headless-verified, CHROUT Function@base:ffd2). Schema documented in docs/SCHEMA.md + docs/MAP_FORMAT.md. Residual schema growth (cartridge EXROM/GAME bits, .crt, flow-tracked banking) is tracked under the gib.2 line, not this design bead.

title: Survey Ghidra loader/extension API and existing console loaders
description: Audit: what API surface does Ghidra expose for loaders? What existing open-source console loaders exist (NES, SNES, PS1)? Determine if extension vs. script vs. core loader plugin is the right artifact type. Survey: GhidraNES, ghidra-snes-loader, ghidra-psx-ldr, etc. Output: a short design note on the extension/loader API contract and gaps vs. our needs.
notes:
PRIOR ART SEEDS (from user, 2026-07-03):
- https://github.com/hippietrail/RetroGhidra — multi-retro-system Ghidra extension; POSSIBLE CONTRIBUTION TARGET instead of reinvention; survey must include contribute-vs-build verdict
- https://github.com/c64cryptoboy/c64_ghidra — possible useful C64-specific material
- https://cesarmiquel.github.io/tech/art/science/design/2020/03/13/week-13.html — general Ghidra console-RE article, many good links
- HN 46882389 (Ghidra MCP tools) — spun off to bead game-music-extraction-gib.3
IN-TREE FINDINGS (D:/git/ghidra): 6502 + 65C02 languages exist, NO 6510 variant (identical ISA; $00/$01 port is a memory-map annotation concern, not decode). No console loaders in-tree; nearest templates: BinaryLoader, MotorolaHexLoader (opinion package).
RETROGHIDRA SURVEY VERDICT (2026-07-03): BUILD NEW, upstream shallow pieces later as goodwill.
- ~29 loaders, all uniformly SHALLOW: parse header -> createInitializedBlock -> entry point. No loader anywhere models IO registers, full hw memory maps, or banking; zero use of overlay address spaces (even Atari 2600 mirrors are just separately-named blocks).
- C64 support = thin CommodorePrgLoader.java (single CODE block, no C64 labels), C64CrtLoader.java (3 labels), D80 filesystem. No KERNAL labels, no VIC/SID/CIA, no banking.
- Architecture = one Java class per format, knowledge as Java constants; NO data-driven layer (an unused GSON GhidraLabel.java hints it was considered). Our descriptor-driven design would FIGHT their architecture, not extend it.
- Apache 2.0; alive but small (35 stars, ~4-5 contributors, bursty maintenance; Ghidra 12.x compat PR #23 open with engagement but unmerged).
- Use as REFERENCE for Ghidra API boilerplate only. After our C64 loader works, consider upstreaming format-detection pieces as standalone PR.

C64_GHIDRA SURVEY (2026-07-03): c64cryptoboy/c64_ghidra has working C64BinLoader.java (PRG load-addr detection, override option, zp/stack blocks, overlay mode) and c64LabelAddrs.py (74KB comprehensive KERNAL/BASIC ROM+RAM symbol tables). NO LICENSE SPECIFIED -> cannot reuse code/data verbatim; either ask author or regenerate labels from primary sources. No banking model, no VIC/SID/CIA annotations.

GHIDRA-MCP (2026-07-03): bethington/ghidra-mcp very active, Apache 2.0, 256 tools; assumes binary already loaded, modern-platform-oriented. Useful AFTER loader works (agent-driven verification of blocks/labels). Recorded on gib.3. HN criticisms: tool-count bloat degrades LLM tool use; fork quality concerns vs LaurieWired original.
BROAD SURVEY (2026-07-03): Three memory-map patterns exist in the wild, all painful:
(1) Overlay blocks at same vaddr (fortenbt/Ghidra-SMB3INES-Loader, Dan Sanderson C64 Crossroads walkthrough) — hardware-truthful but cross-block flow analysis breaks;
(2) Separate non-overlapping blocks per bank (kylewlacy/GhidraNes, 40+ mappers) — no addr conflicts but loses runtime-address correspondence;
(3) Manual annotation after flat load (Sanderson: ~38 hand edits for a small program).
NOBODY does descriptor-driven automation — that is the confirmed gap.
Key references: SMB3 loader = best overlay+symbol-injection example (11,500 symbols); achan1989/ghidra-snes-loader = best LoROM/HiROM mirror modeling (study for SNES phase); zeroKilo/C64LoaderWV (.d64); Dan Sanderson https://dansanderson.com/mega65/crossroads-part-2/ = clearest description of the manual workflow our loader automates; retroreversing.com/ghidra = curated plugin list.
GHIDRA-C64HELPERS CONTENTS (user inspection, 2026-07-03): (a) 6510-specific processor definition — easily incorporated into our extension (extensions can bundle languages; resolves the no-6510-in-tree gap properly instead of aliasing 6502); (b) PETSCII visualizer — feeds the generalized string-detection feature (bead grm-1.4).
close_reason: Survey complete. Deliverable: ghidra/SURVEY.md in GME (migrates with epic). Verdict: build new extension; RetroGhidra as API reference only. Key findings: descriptor-driven automation is a confirmed empty niche; upstream banked-memory space is open with 6 motivating issues and a clear proposal shape (TMode-style context + context-aware address resolution hook); c64ref is the clean descriptor data source; 6510 language bundle-able from ghidra-c64helpers precedent.

title: Adjudicate the 11 real-ROM rows grm-913 weakened; bless the honest ones
description:
grm-913 weakened the interrupt-entry bank seed from fullyKnown(initial_state) to unknown, and the
full real-ROM A/B (2026-08-22, both sides rebuilt) moved 11 rows. NONE of those goldens were
blessed: whether each moved line is an HONEST loss or a RECOVERABLE one is a claim about a real
cartridge, and CLAUDE.md's rule is that a moved bankComments line gets read against the ROM before
either side is called wrong. Until this bead is answered the 11 rows FAIL on an unchanged tree by
intent -- same standing as the megaman/wizwarr 12.1.3 rows, and NOT a regression to bisect.

THE ROWS, and what moved in each (full table and the A/B method in grm-913's 2026-08-22 comment):

  row        bankComments   warnings   claims weakened to "?"   new "requirement violated"
  smb3        104 -> 103     52 -> 52           19                        0
  rcransom     38 ->  34      5 -> 23           11                       10
  zelda        16 ->  16     13 -> 13            7                        0
  rcproam      10 ->  10     22 -> 22            6                        0
  blmaster      9 ->   9     32 -> 32            4                        0
  cv2           4 ->   4     23 -> 23            3                        0
  smb2          4 ->   4      2 ->  9            3                        2
  tmnt         12 ->  12     28 -> 28            2                        0
  ultimaav      8 ->   8     17 -> 17            2                        0
  zelda2        6 ->   6     25 -> 25            2                        0
  megaman2     75 ->  71     32 -> 36            0                        0

THE QUESTION AT EACH SITE is narrow, and it is the same one every time: the analyzer previously
said "bank = N, certain" and now says "bank = N?, with the r6/r7 (or equivalent) bits ASSUMED from
initial_state". Was the old certainty real -- i.e. is the bank genuinely knowable at that point by
some route the engine could learn -- or did it come from the entry seed and nowhere else? Only the
second case is an honest loss. START WITH RCRANSOM: it is the epicentre, and it is already traced
(docs/human recon notes.txt, grm-1fv: ff07 runs just before the NMI handler returns and ff29 just
before the IRQ handler's, both restoring r6/r7 from shadows $fc/$fd). The weakened fields there are
exactly r6/r7, which is what this bead's premise predicts, so rcransom is the cheapest place to
confirm or refute the whole change.

THE THREE OUTCOMES, and what each implies:
  (a) HONEST -- bless the row. The old number was fabricated by the seed.
  (b) RECOVERABLE -- do NOT bless; the bank really is derivable across the interrupt boundary and
      the engine should learn how. That is grm-mej scope (the exit half is grm-p9y, and the
      grm-1fv finding already names "bank state across an INTERRUPT boundary" as an unmodelled
      gap). File the mechanism, not the row.
  (c) The new "requirement violated" warnings (12, of which 10 are rcransom's) need their own look:
      an honest one says the callee needs r6/r7 and the interrupt-context caller genuinely cannot
      supply them. A spurious one would be the grm-mej.2 SS2d failure mode recurring under newly
      unknown entry state -- nesmirrortest's M8 criterion guards the old shape, not this one.

WHY THIS IS NOT AGENT WORK: 11 rows and ~70 lines, each needing "what does this game actually do
here", which is a disassembler minute and an agent build/measure/interpret cycle. Per CLAUDE.md.

title: megaman and wizwarr real-ROM rows: 12.1.3 regressions with run-to-run jitter, cannot be blessed
description:
WIZWARR IS BOTH A 12.1.3 REGRESSION AND NONDETERMINISTIC. Measured 2026-08-19, four runs on one
fixed 12.1.3 build of HEAD 0704755 + the retarget edits.

  golden (12.1.2)   warnings 4
  full --all run    warnings 7   new: 81b3, ffa1   (both "call to bank-switch helper FUN_ee55
                                                    whose bank argument could not be recovered")
  repeat run 1      warnings 6   new: 8631 (undeterminable mechanism write),
                                      ee52 ("... helper FUN_eedb ...")
  repeat run 2      warnings 7   new: 81b3, ffa1   (identical to the full run)
  repeat run 3      warnings 7   new: 81b3, ffa1   (identical to the full run)

It NEVER returns to 4, so 12.1.3 genuinely degraded bank recovery on this row -- this is not the
pure jitter that megaman/dodge/ff1 show, where the golden value does come back. But WHICH helper
call sites lose their bank argument varies run to run (FUN_ee55 at 81b3/ffa1 in three runs,
FUN_eedb at ee52 plus a mechanism write at 8631 in the fourth).

CONSEQUENCE: THIS ROW CANNOT BE BLESSED. There is no stable value to pin -- blessing would
capture one of at least two outcomes at random and make the row fail ~25% of the time against
its own new golden. Contrast tmnt, which was blessable precisely because its 12.1.3 diff was
byte-identical across three runs.

CLASSIFICATION SUMMARY for the five real-ROM failures on 12.1.3, now complete:
  tmnt     stable regression, ROOT-CAUSED (native decompiler drops the 8f34 jump table), BLESSED.
  wizwarr  regression + jitter. NOT blessed, NOT root-caused. This bead.
  megaman  jitter only, golden still achievable. Known, grm-g73.
  dodge    jitter only. grm-g73 / grm-b3m.
  ff1      jitter only. grm-g73 / grm-b3m.

LIKELY SHARED CAUSE, UNVERIFIED: wizwarr's losses are all "bank argument could not be recovered
at this call site", which is value recovery through a call -- the same class of dataflow that
tmnt lost when the decompiler stopped recovering a jump table. Both appeared with 12.1.3 and both
survived the GP-7023 revert experiment's conclusion that the native decompiler is responsible.
Worth testing wizwarr against D:/ghidra_12.1.3_PATCHED-style experiments only AFTER the upstream
issue gets a response -- do not spend another native-bisect round speculatively.

Note wizwarr is mapper 7 (nes_axrom), NOT the same board as tmnt (mapper 1, nes_mmc1), so
whatever this is, it is not board-specific.

OPEN DECISION for the owner: the 12.1.3 retarget was committed with this row failing, documented
here. Options are (a) leave it failing as a known-baseline row until upstream responds, (b) root
cause it the way tmnt was, or (c) pin the row's analysis options to make it version-independent.
(a) is the current state by default.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SCOPE WIDENED TO TWO ROWS, AND THIS BEAD'S OPEN DECISION IS NOW ANSWERED (a).
From grm-9wl6, closed 2026-08-22.

MEGAMAN JOINS WIZWARR. This bead's 2026-08-20 classification summary listed
megaman as "jitter only, golden still achievable (grm-g73)". That is no longer
right, and the correction matters: megaman is ALSO a 12.1.3 regression. Controlled
A/B with source held byte-identical at 591834e, flipping only gradle.properties'
ghidraTargetVersion (legitimate as a single toggle because b3541b6 changed no
source), rebuilding and wiping build/realrom-cache per side:

                 megaman refs/instrs/bankComments/warn     wizwarr warnings
  12.1.2 x3      1703 / 7431 / 156 / 32  (all identical)   4, diff EMPTY
  12.1.3 run 1   1744 / 7423 / 161 / 32                    7
  12.1.3 run 2   1744 / 7430 / 160 / 32                    7

megaman's 12.1.2 triple IS the golden: 1703/7431 is grm-g73's other documented
pole (refs 1704<->1703 and instrs 7429<->7431 in OPPOSITE directions), with
bankComments 156 exact, warnings constant, and no sample.* line moved -- every
clause of the jitter criterion, not approximately. So megaman's +40 refs and
+4 bankComments exist only at 12.1.3.

VALIDATION OF THIS BEAD'S OWN CLAIM: wizwarr matched its golden EXACTLY (empty
diff) on 3/3 runs at 12.1.2 with the SAME source that fails at 12.1.3. The
original measurement compared against the pre-retarget commit, so source and
toolchain moved together; this holds source fixed and isolates the toolchain.
The conclusion stands, now on stronger evidence.

12.1.3 DID TWO SEPARATE THINGS TO MEGAMAN: moved the central value AND widened the
variance. bankComments varies 160/161 between consecutive 12.1.3 runs and never
varied at all across three 12.1.2 runs. That is why megaman's jitter band looked
wider than documented when measured 2026-08-21 -- that measurement was entirely
post-retarget. See the corrected realrom-megaman-jitter-is-wider memory.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S "CANNOT BE BLESSED" RULING: it now applies to both
rows, for the same reason and independently established for each. wizwarr has no
stable value because WHICH call sites lose their bank argument varies; megaman
has none because bankComments moved 161 vs 160 on consecutive runs, so a blessed
golden would fail against itself.

OWNER DECISION 2026-08-22: option (a) -- leave both failing and documented until
upstream moves. (b) root-cause as tmnt was, and (c) pin the rows' analysis options
to be version-independent, remain available but unscheduled. The argument against
(b) is recorded in full on grm-9wl6: the tmnt precedent cost an install clone, a
patched Decompiler.jar and an instrumented positive control and still ended at
"native, by elimination", and unlike tmnt neither of these rows is deterministic,
so a successful root cause here would end in an upstream report rather than a
bless.

EXPECTED STEADY STATE: realrom-test.sh check --all is pass=29 fail=2, plus dodge's
grm-g73 flap. A bare curated check has a deterministic expected failure again
(megaman is on manifest.tsv; wizwarr is GME-only). Recorded in CLAUDE.md and in
the realrom-12-1-3-toolchain-fails memory.

title: Retarget to Ghidra 12.1.3
description:
Ghidra 12.1.3 was released 2026-08-18 (tag Ghidra_12.1.3_build, asset
ghidra_12.1.3_PUBLIC_20260817.zip, sha256
93a5d11a9ad510622acaaf908c556a7b9b764d338e78a7567f3689bf5081fd54).
We currently target 12.1.2.

RETARGET STEPS (the procedure in gradle.properties' own header comment):
1. USER-SIDE, agent cannot do it: install the release to D:/ghidra_12.1.3_PUBLIC,
   and move the read-only source checkout D:/git/ghidra to tag Ghidra_12.1.3_build.
   Both live outside the repo; CLAUDE.md forbids agents touching the checkout.
2. gradle.properties: ghidraTargetVersion=12.1.2 -> 12.1.3 (the single source of
   truth; install dir and banktest scripts derive from it).
3. extension.properties:5 version=12.1.2 -> 12.1.3.
4. Full gate: build-and-test.sh check, then realrom-test.sh check --all
   (analysis behaviour can move under a new Ghidra even with no diff of ours),
   plus spc700-vectors if GRM_SPC700_VECTORS is configured.
5. Prose/comment references to "12.1.2" as the validated-against version: docs/*.md,
   tools/banktest/*.sh comments, a few javadoc lines in src/main/java. Sweep with
   `grep -rn "12\.1\.2"`. Low priority, but the "validated against the pinned
   Ghidra_12.1.2_build checkout" headers in the design docs become false once the
   checkout moves -- either update them or say which tag they were written against.
6. .claude/settings.local.json has allowlist entries naming D:/ghidra_12.1.2_PATCHED
   (the local fork build for grm-b3m's jumptable fix) and D:/ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC.
   The PATCHED fork will need rebasing onto the 12.1.3 tag if grm-b3m work continues.

CHANGELOG REVIEW -- items plausibly relevant to this extension (full list:
Ghidra/Configurations/Public_Release/src/global/docs/ChangeHistory.md @ the tag):

HIGH -- check these deliberately:
 * "Basic Infrastructure. Added stricter filtering to characters used for symbol
   names. (GP-6843, Issue #9165, #9172, #9206)" -- we generate a LOT of symbol
   names (bank overlay names, PETSCII string labels, descriptor-derived labels).
   If the new filter rejects or rewrites any character we emit, golden files move
   and symbol creation may start failing. This is the single most likely source of
   golden churn in this release.
 * "Decompiler. Added Decompiler support for memory accesses that wrap from high to
   low addresses. (GP-6936)" -- directly in our territory: 16-bit spaces where
   $ffff+1 wraps to $0000. Could change decompiler output on 6502/65816/SPC700.
 * "GUI. Updated the Headless Analyzer to not write to the user's preferences.
   (GP-7096, Issue #9414)" -- our whole banktest harness is headless with an
   isolated user-settings dir (build/ghidra-home). Should be neutral-to-good, but
   the isolation mechanism comments in build-and-test.sh / lib/common.sh cite

TMNT ROOT CAUSE 2026-08-19: NOT OUR BUG. It is a loss of DISASSEMBLY COVERAGE, not a failure of
bank-value recovery, and our analyzer is correctly silent about it.

MEASURED A/B (same source tree, extension rebuilt on each side; extension-identity line changed,
so the comparison is real):

                              12.1.2 (PASS)      12.1.3 (FAIL)
  instructions                3529               2006
  functions                   120                67
  JMP ($e2) @ 8f34            113 targets        0   (only the READ->00e2 ref)
  JMP ($e2) @ 894e            0                  4   (8cfb, 8d22, 8d70, 8e66)
  JMP ($e2) @ 8d8f            16, several bogus  10, all plausible
  JMP ($e2) @ 86e0            4                  4   (identical)
  Bad-Instruction bookmarks   50                 31

All six lost bank comments are downstream of the 8f34 table ONLY. On 12.1.3 those addresses are
not instructions at all -- cfcf/d01f/d8e9/d8f7/dbc4/dbe1 are DataDB with no containing function.
Refs to cea5 go 7 -> 1; the single survivor is c359, which is exactly why one "via FUN_cea5"
comment remained in the dump. FUN_cfcd, FUN_d8cf and FUN_db71 are ordinary MMC3 routines whose
JSR $cea5 arguments resolve to coherent banks (6, 3, 1, 4), so this is real code lost, not noise.

WHY OUR COUNTS GO TO EXACTLY ZERO. BoardBankAnalyzer.runDataflow (src/main/java/retromachines/
BoardBankAnalyzer.java:646-659) seeds from external + function entry points and then walks
instr.getFlows()/getFallThrough(). Undisassembled bytes are invisible to that walk, so the six
sites never enter flow.stateIn(), the Phase-2 loop at :338 never reaches the callSwitches
annotation at :361-378, and retargetReferences at :391 is never called. That is why
refs.intoOverlay and instrs.inOverlay hit 0 while warnings stays at 28 -- nothing was examined
and failed; the sites do not exist. blocks.overlay/spaces.overlay are loader-time, hence
unchanged at 32. NOTHING IN OUR CODE IS RELYING ON ANYTHING IT SHOULD NOT BE.

GP-6936 REFUTED as the cause: zero LowlevelError / "beyond end of address space" in either log,
and the decompiler's pcode-error diagnostics are a BYTE-IDENTICAL multiset across the two runs
(183 lines, same addresses, same messages; 95 of them for 8e66 in both). The only GP-6936 Java
deltas reachable here are inert (GenericAddress.java:277,290 unsigned display formatting;
PcodeOp.java:442 writeOpcode).

GP-7023 IS THE SURVIVING CANDIDATE, ATTRIBUTION NOT YET PROVEN. Diffing the 12.1.2 install's
-src.zips against D:/git/ghidra on Ghidra_12.1.3_build: ghidra/program/util/** (SymbolicPropogator,
VarnodeContext, ContextEvaluator, ContextEvaluatorAdapter) IDENTICAL; app/plugin/core/analysis/**
IDENTICAL; Processors/6502/** .sla and .jar BYTE-IDENTICAL. Exactly one behaviour-relevant file
differs across the whole analysis path: DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer.java, and the entire diff is
GP-7023's two added overrides (evaluateContextBefore :496-510, followFalseConditionalBranches()
-> false :513-517).
Mechanism fits: FindFunctionCallback.process (:407-448) hands a computed jump to the decompiler
only if handleSimpleBlock returns false; resolveComputableFlow (:469-522) returns true iff its
restricted SymbolicPropogator run finds EXACTLY ONE computed flow ref, meaning "not a switch,
skip" -- and because evaluateReference returns false that path creates NO reference at all. The
site is dropped silently. That is precisely 8f34's fingerprint on 12.1.3: zero computed refs, NO
"Unable to resolve switch" bookmark, no log line. followFalseConditionalBranches()==false narrows
explored paths (can drop foundCount 2+ -> 1, newly skipped: 8f34); evaluateContextBefore stopping
earlier can drop 1 -> 0 (newly submitted: 894e, 8d8f cleaned up). Both directions are observed.
NOT PROVEN because decompile.exe also differs between installs, so a native change could explain
it too. Counter-evidence for the native theory: identical p-code diagnostics for 8e66, and the
12.1.3 failure is completely SILENT, which is the Java skip-path's signature rather than a
decompiler that tried and failed.

12.1.3 IS MIXED, NOT SIMPLY WORSE -- this matters for any "just revert it" reasoning. It is
BETTER on two of the four dispatchers (8d8f's 12.1.2 table contained obvious garbage targets
1898/3a9d/a901/e065 and is now clean; 894e went from unresolved to four sane targets), bad-
instruction bookmarks fell 50 -> 31 (gone: a7c2, a806, a912, a991, ad01, ad62, b03e, 9d8d, e065,
e2a6...), and 12.1.2's absurd BRK at a7de/ad30 typed as COMPUTED_JUMP->c412 is gone.

SEPARATE UPSTREAM DEFECT, worth reporting regardless of who wins on tmnt: when
resolveComputableFlow returns true it neither creates the reference it claims to have computed
nor records anything -- so a misclassified switch vanishes with no bookmark, no log line, and no
way for a downstream analyzer to know it happened.

title: test task does not depend on buildMap: check unit fails 6 tests in a fresh worktree
description:
The `test` task does not depend on `buildMap`, so `check unit` fails 6 tests in a fresh worktree

NesPlacementValidationTest reads the COMPILED descriptors at data/machines/nes-*.map, which are
gitignored build products generated by the per-descriptor `build<Id>Map` JavaExec tasks (aggregated
as `buildMap`). The `test` task dependsOn `sleighCompile` but NOT `buildMap`, so nothing in the
JUnit path ever produces them.

In the primary working tree this is invisible: a full `build-and-test.sh check` builds the
extension, which produces all 15 .map files, and they then persist in data/machines/ indefinitely.
The test has therefore passed for months on the strength of an artifact left behind by a
DIFFERENT chunk.

WHERE IT BITES: a fresh `git worktree` (or a fresh clone) that runs only `check unit` --
exactly the fast development loop CLAUDE.md recommends. Six tests fail:

    java.lang.AssertionError: missing shipped descriptor D:\git\grm-c9d3\data\machines\nes-nrom.map
        at NesPlacementValidationTest.map(NesPlacementValidationTest.java:67)

MEASURED 2026-08-17 during grm-c9d.3 increment 11. The worktree failed 6/414; main passed 414/414
on the same commit; `gradle buildMap` in the worktree then made it 414/414 there too. So it is
purely a missing build product, not a code defect and not environment-specific beyond that.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN DOCUMENTING: it produced a WRONG DIAGNOSIS, and a plausible
one. The failure looks like a pre-existing breakage in unrelated NES code -- it is in NES tests,
it reproduces on a stashed clean tree, and it survives `git stash`, which is the standard
attribution move and here gives a confidently wrong answer. An agent working SPC700 correctly
concluded "pre-existing, unrelated to my change" and was right about the first half and wrong
about the second: main was green the whole time. The next person to hit this in a worktree will
burn the same time, and may `git bisect` looking for a commit that does not exist.

Note the shape relative to the silent-noop-reports-green memory: this is the MIRROR image --
a check that did not run reports RED rather than green. Same root cause (something that looks
like configuration sits between you and the code under test), opposite and less dangerous
direction, since a false red gets investigated while a false green does not.

FIX: `test.dependsOn 'buildMap'`, alongside the existing `dependsOn 'sleighCompile'`. buildMap is
cheap (~5 s for all 15, and up-to-date-checked against the YAML inputs), so this costs nothing on
the common path. Consider whether the gdtBuilder half needs the same treatment -- `buildGdt`
produces data/machines/*.gdt by the identical pattern, and no current JUnit test happens to read
one, which makes it the same latent trap waiting for the first test that does.

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: making the test skip when the descriptor is absent. That
converts a loud failure into a silent no-op and lands squarely in the failure mode this project
has been bitten by four times. The assertion message is already honest about the cause; the
problem is that the dependency is missing, not that the test complains.

Verify: in a fresh worktree with no data/machines/*.map, `bash tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh
check unit` must pass 414/414 with no prior full-gate run.
close_reason: Closed

title: Rewrite SPC700 p-code semantics against the vector harness
description:
Rewrite the vendored SPC700 p-code semantics against the vector harness (grm-c9d.2). The decode
table stays; the constructor bodies are the deliverable.

THE ROOT DEFECT IS THE ADDRESSING SUBTABLES, not a list of instructions. ADDR8 exports
`*:2 tmp` (two bytes AT the direct-page address) and bodies then write `*:1 ADDR8`, dereferencing
that value a second time. ADDR16 has the same shape. MEASURED, not inferred (grm-y7d):

    MOV A,$10   (E4 10)  ->  tmp = zext(0x10)
                             ptr = LOAD[tmp]        <- deref 1, reads the WORD at $10
                             A   = LOAD[ptr]        <- deref 2
    MOV A,!$1234(E5 34 12)-> A   = LOAD[(ram,0x1234,2)]   -- absolute is affected too
    MOV $20,A   (C4 20)  ->  STORE(LOAD[0x20], A)   -- stores through, not to, $20

So essentially every memory-referencing constructor is wrong. Control flow is NOT affected --
`goto` on a dynamic varnode uses its address, and BCS resolved correctly in testing.

THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX. Ghidra's stock 6502 exports `*:1 imm8` and uses the symbol DIRECTLY as
a value (`A = OP1`); SPCdra exports a 2-byte dynamic varnode and dereferences again in the body.
Reconciling means either changing the subtable and revising every memory-touching body, or
splitting into two subtables -- address-valued for data, dynamic for jump targets -- and revising
the bodies accordingly. Decide which, then apply it uniformly.

KNOWN DEFECT LIST beyond the addressing root, all confirmed from real p-code (grm-y7d):
 * CMP sets carry INVERTED: `$(CF) = (A < operand)`; hardware sets C when A >= operand. So every
   CMP/BCS/BCC idiom decompiles backwards. Same inversion in aluSBC.
 * aluADC hardcodes `$(NF) = 0` -- emitted as INT_LEFT(const 0, 7). V is never computed in either
   aluADC or aluSBC.
 * ASL/ROL can never set carry: `$(CF) = (A & 0x80)` assigns a byte into the 1-bit bitrange
   PSW[0,1], keeping only bit 0, which is always 0. LSR/ROR use `& 0x01` and are correct by luck.
   WATCH FOR THIS CLASS GENERALLY -- SLEIGH truncates silently, no compile error.
 * INC/DEC (all forms) set no flags at all. MOVW/INCW/DECW/ADDW/SUBW/MUL/DIV likewise.
 * MOV dp,X (0xD8) and MOV dp,Y (0xCB) add the index to the address -- copy-paste from the +X forms.
 * ASL/LSR/ROL/ROR dp+X store the 2-byte ADDRESS to the UNINDEXED location (`*:1 ADDR8 = ptr`).
   Four instances.
 * OR1/AND1/EOR1 are logically wrong -- e.g. OR1 C,dp.bit ORs the bit in then tests non-zero, so
   carry becomes 1 unconditionally. The `/`-complement forms are worse.
 * The AND1/OR1/MOV1 family decodes its operand as two separate bytes rather than the hardware's
   packed 13-bit address + 3-bit index in one 16-bit operand. Length right, interpretation wrong.
 * TSET1/TCLR1 set no flags. 7 author `#TODO`s remain, 6 of them "Set flags NV..H.ZC".
 * NOP is a pcodeop, so every NOP emits an opaque CALLOTHER. Minor, free to fix.

DO NOT hand-review the result. Drive it opcode by opcode off grm-c9d.2 -- that is the entire reason
the harness comes first.
close_reason: Exhaustive vector tier: 254 PASS / 0 FAIL / 2 N/A of 256; 253,970 of 254,000 applicable cases pass, remaining 30 are classified Ghidra decode-boundary artifacts. DIV YA,X now implements the real restoring-division algorithm with verified V/H. No known semantic defect remains.
