comments.text:
COMMIT-DISCIPLINE CONSTRAINT, added 2026-08-16 because the user asked to keep upstream
contribution possible (grm-c9d.6): "it would be nice if we could PR our changes to spcdra in case
they want to incorporate them ... nice to have, not a requirement."

DO THE REWRITE AS SMALL, INDIVIDUALLY-SCOPED COMMITS ON A TRACKED BRANCH, one defect (or one tight
family) per commit, with a message that states the defect and the evidence. Do NOT land the whole
semantics rewrite as one commit, and do not mix the structural ADDR8/ADDR16 change in with the
self-contained flag fixes.

WHY, concretely: most of the defect list is independently upstreamable in one-to-few lines -- CMP
carry inversion, ADC's hardcoded N=0, the ASL/ROL 1-bit-truncation carry bug, flagless INC/DEC,
MOV dp,X's spurious +X, the four ASL/LSR/ROL/ROR dp+X wrong-stores, the OR1/AND1/EOR1 logic, the
bit-op operand decode. The ADDR8/ADDR16 root fix is the one wide structural change and is probably
NOT upstreamable as a patch. If those land intermingled, separating them later means re-deriving
the split by hand; if they land separately, offering the upstreamable subset is a cherry-pick.

This costs nothing if we never open a PR. It is the whole difference between "worth offering" and
"not worth the effort" if we do -- which is exactly the judgement the user reserved.

Note the ordering interaction with grm-c9d.2: driving the rewrite opcode-by-opcode off the vector
harness naturally produces one-defect-per-commit anyway, so this constraint is nearly free if the
harness is genuinely used as intended. It only becomes expensive if someone rewrites the spec in
one pass and validates afterwards -- which is the anti-pattern .2 exists to prevent.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
TWO ADDITIONAL DEFECTS found while vendoring (grm-c9d.1, 2026-08-16). Both were read out of
the spec source, NOT measured from p-code, so treat them as high-confidence leads for the
vector harness to confirm rather than as established the way the grm-y7d list is.

1. CALL / TCALL / PCALL NEVER PUSH THE RETURN ADDRESS. In spc700ops.sinc the
   "push16(&:2 inst_next);" line in these constructors is COMMENTED OUT. So the call
   constructors transfer control without writing a return address to the stack, and RET
   cannot work correctly against this semantics -- it pops whatever happens to be there.

   THIS ONE IS NEW. It is not in the grm-y7d defect table, which was built from a p-code
   dump of data-access and flag behaviour and never exercised a call/return pair. It is
   also more consequential than most of that list for THIS project's purposes: grm-1.7.3
   wants recovered SPC700 uploads to decompile into something readable, and a call/return
   convention the decompiler cannot see wrecks function recovery wholesale -- worse than a
   wrong flag, which only corrupts one branch.

   Watch for it in the vector suite: the SingleStepTests cases carry sp and a sparse ram
   list, so a CALL vector will show BOTH an sp mismatch and missing stack writes in
   final.ram. That signature (sp wrong AND ram writes absent) distinguishes this from an
   ordinary flag defect, which leaves sp alone.

   Whether upstream commented it out deliberately (e.g. to dodge a sleigh export-size
   problem with "&:2 inst_next") or as debugging left in place is unknown -- worth one
   look before writing the fix, since the same obstacle may still be there.

2. aluADC SETS $(NF) = 0 UNCONDITIONALLY and never calls resultFlags(result), where the
   sibling aluSBC macro does call it. This is the SOURCE of the already-measured grm-y7d
   finding "ADC A,#1 emits INT_LEFT (const,0x0,1),(const,0x7)" -- a literal zero shifted
   into bit 7. Not a new defect, but now localized to the macro rather than the opcode, so
   the fix is one macro rather than every ADC constructor. aluADC also never computes V at
   all, so BVS/BVC after ADC are equally wrong.

   The asymmetry with aluSBC is the tell, and it makes the fix shape obvious: give aluADC
   the same resultFlags(result) tail its sibling already has, then add the V computation
   both lack.

NOTE ON WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: neither was fixed in grm-c9d.1. That bead landed
the broken baseline unmodified on purpose so this rewrite has a diff base. Both are
verbatim upstream behaviour at fork point 295b552f.

BOTH ARE CANDIDATES FOR THE UPSTREAMABLE SUBSET (grm-c9d.6). Each is self-contained and
does not touch the ADDR8/ADDR16 structural question, so under grm-c9d.3's commit-discipline
constraint each should be its own commit and would cherry-pick cleanly.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DIRECT-PAGE P FLAG BELONGS IN THE ADDR8 COMMIT. Ruled 2026-08-17 when deciding whether to
sequence grm-c9d.5 before this bead. Answer: no -- proceed here, and fold P in.

ADDR8 today is:  ADDR8: imm8 is imm8 { local tmp:2 = zext(imm8:1); export *:2 tmp; }

That carries TWO defects in one line, and they are one edit:
  (a) the double dereference grm-y7d measured (export *:2 of a value later dereferenced again)
  (b) the direct page is hardcoded to page 0 -- P (PSW bit 5) is ignored entirely

Correct behaviour is a runtime (P ? 0x100 : 0) | imm8. It MUST be runtime rather than a
sleigh context variable, because SETP/CLRP mutate P during execution, so a decode-time
assumption would be wrong the moment a routine flips pages. Fixing (a) without (b) means
restructuring the same subtable twice.

THE VECTORS ALREADY MEASURE P, so this needs no external reference (this is what supersedes
grm-c9d.5's "mine Raikaru's P-flag handling" half -- see that bead):
  4120 of 8192 sampled cases (50.3%) run with P set
  E4 (MOV A,dp): 18 of 32 sampled cases have P=1
  worked case: initial ram [[372,15],...] -> final a=15, where 372 = 0x0174
i.e. MOV A,$74 with P=1 must read 0x0174. Per-opcode ground truth, free.

COMMIT SHAPE, consistent with this bead's existing commit-discipline constraint: the
ADDR8/ADDR16 restructure is the ONE structural commit and is the one least likely to be
upstreamable, so keep it strictly separate from the self-contained flag fixes (CMP/SBC
carry, ADC N/V, ASL/ROL carry truncation, flagless INC/DEC, MOV dp,X spurious index, the
dp+X wrong-stores, the bit ops). Expect the structural commit to flip a large block of the
222 failing rows at once, and each flag commit to flip a handful -- so the baseline diff
also tells you whether a commit did what you thought it did.

DO NOT READ Raikaru/ghidra-spc700 while doing this. Its provenance is unsettled (MIT with a
blank copyright line, plausibly derived from SPCdra) and grm-c9d.6 depends on our fixes
being cleanly ours to offer upstream. We have a better oracle; there is nothing to gain.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Increment 11 triage: the 49 remaining exhaustive failures are FIVE defects plus one artifact class

Re-triaged the exhaustive baseline (205 PASS / 49 FAIL / 2 N/A) by failure SHAPE rather than by
working down grm-y7d's original list. The 49 rows are not 49 problems -- the pass RATE and the
failing-category column partition them almost perfectly, and 24 of the 49 turn out not to be
defects at all.

THE PARTITION, and how each was read:

 * ~50% PASS with a huge $100-$1ff address list -- 09/29/49, the OR/AND/EOR dp,dp forms.
   Half the vectors have P=1, where the direct page is $0100. A pass rate of ~490/1000 IS the
   P=1 half failing. Increment 7 already fixed exactly this for the ADC/SBC dstaddr,srcaddr
   pair forms (zext(x:1) -> dpFold(x, ...)); the logical-op equivalents were simply missed.

 * ~99.5% PASS across SIXTEEN opcodes -- the whole [dp+X] and [dp]+Y family
   (07 17 27 37 47 57 67 77 87 97 A7 B7 E7 F7 read side, C7 D7 write side). Four to six failures
   per thousand is about the rate at which the pointer's low byte lands on $FF. These fetch a
   16-bit pointer OUT of the direct page, and that fetch must wrap inside the page. dpWordRead /
   dpIndex already exist from increment 6a and evidently are not used here. This is the same
   class of edge case CLAUDE.md cites as the reason the exhaustive tier exists at all: at 32
   cases per opcode the sampled tier sees roughly zero of these.

 * ~0.5% PASS with addresses in BOTH pages -- D8 MOV dp,X (6/1000) and CB MOV dp,Y (5/1000).
   The both-pages detail is the informative part: a missing P-fold fails only the P=1 half, so
   this is a distinct bug, not a variant of the first group. grm-y7d named "MOV dp,X stores to
   the wrong address" as a headline SPCdra defect and this is it, still standing.

 * 0/1000, category PC -- 1F JMP [!abs+X], the computed-indirect jump. Same territory as the
   increment 1 ADDR16/ADDR16V split (goto/call on a dynamic export uses the export's ADDRESS,
   not its value), so that comment is prerequisite reading rather than background.

 * 4/1000, category PSW -- ED NOTC, flagged during increment 10 and left. Complements carry and
   nothing else, so the suspicion is the 1-bit-bitrange truncation hazard.

NOT DEFECTS -- 24 of the 49 rows: opcodes at 998-999/1000 whose ONLY category is `execution`
(0E 13 24 25 3A 3B 45 51 58 5B 64 6B 9D A0 AC AF C0 D6 DF E4 E8 EE FA FB). This is the harness
boundary artifact: SleighInstructionDecoder refuses to decode when PC is within an instruction
length of $FFFF. Diagnosed earlier and deliberately left VISIBLE rather than hidden behind a
skip rule, so the row count overstates the defect count by about half. Anything landing at
999/1000 with category `execution` after a fix is finished, not partially fixed.

9E DIV YA,X stays out -- grm-hu76, needs the restoring-division algorithm first.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE SHAPE OF THE REMAINING WORK: 25 real failing opcodes across five root
causes, and one of those five causes accounts for sixteen of them. That is a much smaller
residue than "49 failures" suggests, and it is why the next increment is being run as five
separate commits rather than a sweep -- grm-c9d.6 needs each to be cherry-pickable, and the
16-opcode wrap fix in particular is a clean, self-contained gift for upstream.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Increment 11 landed: 205 -> 226 of 256 exhaustive, five commits, zero regressions

Merged to main. Sampled tier 245 -> 253. Full gate green (53/53 headless goldens, 414 JUnit,
0 failures). All five fixes are confined to spc700ops.sinc constructors -- spc700core.sinc is
untouched -- so the whole increment is cleanly cherry-pickable for grm-c9d.6.

 11a cbb50f7  OR/AND/EOR dp,dp wrote to the wrong page          205 -> 208
 11b e5385a7  [dp+X]/[dp]+Y pointer fetch did not wrap in page  208 -> 224
 11c 29efb8f  MOV dp,X / MOV dp,Y stored to dp+register         224 -> 226
 11d 5c69662  JMP [!abs+X] never dereferenced the jump table    0/1000 -> 999/1000
 11e a8d7b84  NOTC complemented a full byte into a 1-bit field  4/1000 -> 999/1000

11b IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, and it is the best evidence yet for why grm-c9d.2 was sequenced
before this bead. Sixteen opcodes -- the entire [dp+X] and [dp]+Y family -- fetched their 16-bit
pointer with a plain `*:2 ptr`, taking the high byte from base+1 instead of wrapping inside the
direct page. It is wrong only when the pointer's low byte is 0xFF, i.e. about 4 cases in 1000.
Every one of the sixteen sat at 994-999/1000, dpWordRead already existed from increment 6a, and
one substitution moved all sixteen to 1000/1000.

The sampled tier could not have found this. At 32 cases per opcode the expected number of
0xFF-boundary hits is well under one, so all sixteen read as PASS there -- and they are wrong on
real code, where a driver walking a pointer table hits dp=0xFF as a matter of course. This is the
concrete payoff for keeping the exhaustive tier as routine local verification rather than a
ceremonial final check.

11c CONFIRMS grm-y7d's ORIGINAL FINDING. "MOV dp,X stores to the wrong address" was on the
headline defect list from the start and was still standing. Both D8 and CB reused the indexed-store
pattern -- dpIndex(ADDR8, X, addr) -- folding the very register being STORED as a spurious index.
The diagnostic that separated it from 11a before either was opened: it failed at BOTH pages, and a
missing P-fold can only fail the P=1 half.

METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING: triaging by failure SHAPE (pass rate + failing-category column) rather
than by working down the known-defect list is what made this increment cheap. The pass rate alone
named each root cause -- ~490/1000 means "the P=1 half", a fixed ~995/1000 repeated across a whole
addressing-mode family means "boundary condition, one bug not sixteen", and ~5/1000 across both
pages means "not a P-fold bug at all". It also showed that 24 of the 49 failing rows were not
defects: opcodes at 998-999/1000 whose only category is `execution` are the harness boundary
artifact, so the row count overstated the remaining work by about half.

STILL OPEN on this bead:
 * 9E DIV YA,X -- grm-hu76, out of scope by design; the quotient itself is wrong, so no flag
   formula can be validated until the restoring-division algorithm lands.
 * The ~24 `execution` rows -- harness limitation, deliberately left visible rather than hidden
   behind a skip rule.

That leaves NO known semantic defect outstanding except DIV. The next question on this bead is
therefore what "done" means for the residue, not which opcode to fix next.

SIDE FINDING, filed as grm-lr0s: the `test` Gradle task does not dependOn `buildMap`, so a fresh
worktree running only `check unit` fails 6 NesPlacementValidationTest tests on missing
data/machines/*.map build products. It cost a wrong diagnosis here -- the failure survives
`git stash`, which is the standard attribution move, and so reads as pre-existing breakage in
unrelated NES code while main was green the whole time.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEASURED: the whole language now fails 972 of 254,000 cases, and 942 of those are DIV

Ran a scratch probe over ALL 254 applicable opcodes (excluding the two genuine N/A rows, SLEEP EF
and STOP FF) against the full 256,000-case suite, classifying every failing case rather than
counting failing ROWS. Result:

    totalFail=972   decodeExceptionFail=30   otherFail=942
    non-decode failures by opcode: {9E=942}
    decode-fail PC range: 0xfff9 .. 0xffff
    histogram: fff9 n=5, fffb n=10, fffc n=2, fffd n=3, fffe n=4, ffff n=6

So OUTSIDE DIV THERE IS NOT ONE SEMANTIC FAILURE LEFT IN THE LANGUAGE. 253,970 of 254,000 pass,
and the 30 misses are all Ghidra's decoder, not our spec.

WHY THIS REFRAMES THE RESIDUE, and why the row count was misleading: the baseline showed "28 FAIL
of 256", which reads as 28 broken opcodes. In fact 27 of those rows share THIRTY CASES between
them -- one or two each -- and every one is the same harness artifact. Counting rows instead of
cases overstated the remaining work by about two orders of magnitude. Worth remembering when
reading any per-opcode baseline: the row is a summary, the case count is the measurement.

THE BOUNDARY ARTIFACT IS NOW CHARACTERIZED PRECISELY, replacing the earlier inference:

 * The exception is specifically ghidra.pcode.exec.DecodePcodeExecutionException ("Unknown
   disassembly error (PC=...)"), thrown from SleighInstructionDecoder.parseNewBlock, which calls
   state.getConcreteBuffer(address, Purpose.DECODE) and needs a lookahead window that runs off the
   end of the 16-bit space. Confirmed against the local Ghidra checkout, which IS on tag
   Ghidra_12.1.2_build (see the memory correction below).
 * The earlier description -- "PC within an INSTRUCTION LENGTH of 0xFFFF" -- IS WRONG. A0 EI is a
   ONE-BYTE instruction and fails at 0xfff9, seven bytes from the top. The window is ~8 bytes, not
   the instruction length.
 * 0xFFFA is ABSENT from the histogram, so it is not a flat address band either: whether a case
   trips depends on the case, not solely on its PC. Any classifier must therefore key on the
   ACTUAL EXCEPTION TYPE and use the address only as a corroborating condition -- an
   address-range rule alone would be both over- and under-inclusive.

THESE ARE NOT "NO CORRECT ANSWER EXISTS" CASES, which is what separates them from SLEEP/STOP.
Real hardware executes EI at 0xFFF9 perfectly normally; there is a right answer and our spec
computes it. The harness simply cannot decode there. That makes the existing per-opcode N/A
mechanism the wrong tool (999 of the 1000 cases are fine) and FAIL the wrong verdict (our spec is
not at fault).

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN TOLERATING, which is the argument that changed my earlier
ruling to leave it visible: 27 rows currently sit at 999/1000. A genuine regression breaking ONE
more case would show 998/1000 and be waved off as "the artifact". The noise is masking exactly
the signal the baseline exists to provide, and it will keep doing so for as long as those rows
sit one case away from indistinguishable.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Increment 12 lands the last defect: 254 of 254 applicable opcodes now PASS

Exhaustive tier: 254 PASS / 0 FAIL / 2 N/A of 256. Sampled tier likewise. Full gate green
(53/53 headless goldens, 415 JUnit, 0 failures). Two commits:

  8c90b2f  DIV YA,X implements the real hardware algorithm (closes grm-hu76)   57/1000 -> 999/999
  45159ed  decode-boundary cases classified as a third category, not failures

CASE ACCOUNTING, verified independently against the baseline rather than taken from the summary:

    sum numerator 253,970 + sum denominator 255,970, boundary 30, total 256,000

255,970 counted + 30 boundary excluded = 256,000 exactly, and the 2,000-case gap between
numerator and denominator is precisely the two N/A rows (SLEEP, STOP) at 0/1000 each. That
reconciles to the case with the independent probe run before this increment, which measured 972
failures = 942 DIV + 30 boundary; DIV fixed leaves exactly the 30, all classified. Two
measurements taken different ways agreeing to the case is the real acceptance evidence here.

DIV: THE ALGORITHM, AND A DOCUMENTATION RESULT WORTH KEEPING. Derived from all 1000 cases as one
unified closed form -- no special-casing of X==0 and no branch on original Y vs X:

    temp = YA - (X << 9)
    if temp >= 0:  A = 255 - temp/(256-X),  Y = X + temp%(256-X)
    else:          A = YA / X,              Y = YA % X

X==0 needs no guard because temp is then just YA, always >= 0, so control never reaches the
division by X. The first attempt used :2 locals; X<<9 reaches 130560, overflows 16 bits and
silently flips the sign of the branch test on about a third of cases -- caught only by
re-checking against the vectors, which is the whole argument for having sequenced grm-c9d.2
before this bead.

V AND H MATCHED THE COMMONLY CITED DOCUMENTATION EXACTLY once A/Y were right (0 mismatches over
1000 cases): V = (original Y >= X), H = (original Y & 0xF) >= (X & 0xF). This is the FIRST time
in this whole rewrite that the received documentation has been confirmed rather than corrected --
MUL's N/Z from Y alone, MOVW dp,YA setting no flags, and H as an inverted borrow all contradicted
it. Also worth recording: V does NOT track the arithmetic branch. 275 of 1000 cases have
original Y >= X yet temp < 0, so they run the "else" arithmetic and still report V=1. V tracks
the register comparison, not which path executed -- a reasonable-looking simplification that
would have been wrong on a quarter of cases.

That vindicates increment 7's decision to REVERT its drafted V/H formula rather than ship it: the
formula was in fact right, but it could not have been VALIDATED then, because with the quotient
wrong the vectors could not distinguish a bad flag formula from a bad quotient. Shipping it would
have been unfalsifiable code that happened to be correct, which is not the same thing as verified
code and does not survive the next edit.

THE BOUNDARY RECLASSIFICATION, and why it reverses my earlier ruling to leave the artifact
visible. The predicate requires BOTH conditions -- a DecodePcodeExecutionException specifically
(not any RuntimeException) AND an initial PC within the top 8 bytes -- so a decode exception at
an ordinary PC still FAILs, and it is opt-in per runner (default off, so VectorHarness6502Test is
unaffected). The count stays on the page as a trailing "(N decode-boundary)" annotation with the
cases removed from BOTH numerator and denominator, and a cap of 100 (measured: 30) fails the
tier loudly if this ever starts absorbing more than the known artifact.

The argument that changed the ruling: 27 rows were sitting at 999/1000, so a real regression
breaking one more case would have read as 998/1000 and been waved off as the artifact. Leaving it
visible was meant to preserve signal and had started destroying it. Note this is a THIRD category,
distinct from the per-opcode N/A rows: for SLEEP/STOP no correct post-state exists, whereas
EI at $FFF9 has a perfectly ordinary right answer that our spec computes and only the harness
cannot reach.

STATUS: no known semantic defect remains in the SPC700 language. grm-c9d.3 and grm-hu76 both
close here. What is NOT claimed: the vectors verify SEMANTICS, not disassembly text -- that half
is pinned only by Spc700LanguageTest's 8 encodings, and grm-uy9s (differential comparison against
the nine hand-annotated .dis listings) is the bead that covers it. It was blocked on this bead
being substantially done, and now is not.

title: SingleStepTests/spc700 vector harness: per-opcode semantic verification chunk
description:
Wire SingleStepTests/spc700 per-instruction test vectors into the test tier as a new chunk, so
SPC700 p-code semantics can be verified opcode-by-opcode instead of by eye.

WHY THIS COMES BEFORE THE SEMANTICS REWRITE, not after: the vendored spec is wrong in ways that
hand-review demonstrably does not catch. SPCdra shipped for five years with CMP's carry inverted
and every direct-page access double-dereferenced, and its disassembly text looks perfect
throughout. Reviewing a rewrite by reading it would reproduce exactly that failure mode. With
vectors the job becomes a measurable loop, which is cheap agent work.

SOURCE: github.com/SingleStepTests/spc700 -- JSMoo-derived JSON, per instruction, with initial and
final register/flag state and bus activity. CHECK THE LICENSE BEFORE USE; the parent
SingleStepTests/ProcessorTests repo is archived. If the license does not permit vendoring, treat
it the same way the real-ROM tier treats ROMs: user-supplied, path from an env var, opt-in chunk.

Note the neighbouring use: docs/human-research-todo.md section 3 already names the ProcessorTests
65x02 suites as the vector source for the grm-o9k 6502 ADC/RRA flag fix. If a runner is built here
it should be built so that bead can reuse it -- same family of data, same shape of check.

SHAPE:
 * A runner that, per vector, sets initial state, executes ONE instruction's p-code, and compares
   final registers/flags/memory. Ghidra's p-code emulator (SystemEmulation) is the obvious vehicle.
 * Report per-opcode pass/fail so the rewrite can be driven opcode by opcode, and so a partial
   result is still useful.
 * Register as a chunk in tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh and document it in docs/testing.md's
   chunk map alongside the existing tiers.

ACCEPTANCE: the runner executes against the vendored (unmodified) spec and REPORTS FAILURES rather
than passing -- it must reproduce the known defects from grm-y7d's verification (CMP carry
inverted, INC/DEC flagless, ADC N=0, the ADDR8/ADDR16 double-deref). A vector harness that passes
against a spec known to be broken is not measuring anything.
close_reason: Harness landed; 34 PASS / 222 FAIL of 256 opcodes against the vendored spec, reproducing every grm-y7d defect plus CALL/RET stack and NOP-as-CALLOTHER. All 8 conditional branches pass 32/32, proving it discriminates. Baseline committed as a reviewable artifact; gate green (53/53 goldens).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION DECISIONS 2026-08-16, taken at the start of the .2 work.

LICENSE SETTLED: SingleStepTests/spc700 is MIT, "Copyright (c) 2024 SingleStepTests", LICENSE
present at the repo root. Compatible with this project's Apache-2.0 and with the NOTICE
preamble's framing once that preamble is widened (it currently says all vendored code is
Apache-2.0; the vector block will be the first MIT entry). The bead's fallback -- "if the
license does not permit vendoring, treat it like the real-ROM tier" -- is NOT needed on
license grounds. It is partly adopted anyway, on size grounds, below.

VECTOR SHAPE, measured from v1/00.json rather than assumed:
  {"name":"00 0000",
   "initial":{"pc":30256,"a":56,"x":78,"y":127,"sp":236,"psw":145,"ram":[[30256,0]]},
   "final":  {"a":56,"x":78,"y":127,"sp":236,"pc":30257,"psw":145,"ram":[[30256,0]]},
   "cycles": [[30256,0,"read"],[30257,null,"read"]]}
256 files (v1/<opcode>.json), 512 cases each = 131,072 vectors. ram is a SPARSE [addr,value]
list, so a case needs no memory image -- write three bytes, step once, compare. cycles is a
bus trace with no p-code analogue and is ignored; final.ram already captures every write.
This is close to the ideal shape for p-code verification.

SOURCING (user ruling): vendor a deterministic SAMPLE plus an env-var full run.
  - sample: first N=32 cases per opcode = 8,192 vectors, ~5 MB, committed, gated in `unit`.
    Prefix rather than seeded shuffle -- the suite's cases are already pseudo-random, and a
    shuffle would be one more thing to reproduce exactly.
  - GRM_SPC700_VECTORS points at a full clone for the exhaustive run; unset = refuse loudly,
    nonzero, never a quiet green. Same rule realrom-test.sh already enforces.
Why not vendor it all: ~76 MB uncompressed / ~15 MB packed against a 22 MB .git, and this
project uses git worktrees routinely for parallel agents, so every worktree pays it. The
sample/opt-in split mirrors the existing gated-synthetic + opt-in-real-ROM structure instead
of inventing a third pattern.

THE HARNESS ASSERTS A PER-OPCODE BASELINE, NOT RAW PASS/FAIL. This bead's acceptance
criterion -- "REPORTS FAILURES rather than passing" -- is right, but implemented as ordinary
JUnit assertions it would leave the project gate permanently red until grm-c9d.3 lands, which
is not a state this repo can sit in. So the run produces a per-opcode tally compared against
a committed baseline file:
    E8  MOV A,#imm    PASS  32/32
    E4  MOV A,dp      FAIL   0/32  A,PSW
Today it records the failing opcodes and the test passes, so the gate is green while the
defect list becomes a REVIEWABLE COMMITTED ARTIFACT -- which is this criterion in durable
form rather than a transient console message. During grm-c9d.3 each fix flips entries
FAIL->PASS and the baseline diff is the progress report, which is also what naturally
produces the small individually-scoped commits grm-c9d.3's constraint requires for
upstreaming. An opcode going PASS->FAIL turns the gate red.

Guarded against the obvious failure mode with two sanity assertions: fail if fewer opcodes
ran than the baseline lists, and fail if the run reports ZERO failures while the baseline
expects many. A vector harness that passes against a spec known to be broken is measuring
nothing, and that is exactly what this bead warns about.

REPORTING DETAIL THAT MATTERS FOR .3: the SPC700 flags are sleigh @define bitranges over
PSW ([0,1]=C [1,1]=Z [2,1]=I [3,1]=H [4,1]=B [5,1]=P [6,1]=V [7,1]=N), so there are no
per-flag Ghidra registers to diff. The report decomposes the PSW byte into named flags
itself -- "PSW 0x91 != 0x11" is nearly useless to the person doing the rewrite, "N differs"
is actionable.

BUILT LANGUAGE-AGNOSTIC ON PURPOSE. The runner takes a language id and a vector-name ->
Register map. grm-o9k (6502 ADC/RRA flag fix) needs the same loop against the 65x02
SingleStepTests suites, which share this JSON shape; docs/human-research-todo.md section 3
already names them as that bead's vector source. Developed against stock 6502:LE:16:default
so it did not block on grm-c9d.1 landing.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-17, plus the first measured case of the sample being too thin.

THE SUITE IS 1000 CASES PER OPCODE, NOT 512. Measured directly over a full clone: 256 files,
every one exactly 1000 cases, TOTAL 256,000 vectors. The "512" figure recorded when this bead
was filed came from a summarizer's count of v1/00.json and was simply wrong. Consequences:

  * the vendored sample (32/opcode, 8192 cases) is 3.2% of the suite, not 6.25%
  * the exhaustive GRM_SPC700_VECTORS run is ~256,000 cases, ~15s at the measured 58 us/case
    (the earlier "131,072 cases / 7.6s" estimate understated it by half)
  * the full working tree is correspondingly larger than the ~76 MB previously quoted, which
    only strengthens the original decision NOT to vendor it whole

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING BOOKKEEPING: grm-c9d.3 increment 4 hit a question the
sampled tier could not decide -- whether 16-bit direct-page word accesses (MOVW/INCW/DECW/
ADDW/SUBW/CMPW) wrap their high byte within the page when dp=0xFF. All six opcodes failed
PSW-only, never on an address, so there was no evidence either way and it was correctly filed
rather than guessed at.

THE FULL SUITE SETTLES IT IMMEDIATELY, AND THE ANSWER IS THAT THE WRAP IS REAL:

    BA 0164 (MOVW YA,dp)  P=0, dp=0xFF, populated ram [[0,77],[255,46],...]
        -> low byte from 0x00FF, high byte from 0x0000. Wraps within page 0.
    9A 00FB (SUBW YA,dp)  P=1, dp=0xFF, populated ram [[256,193],[511,24],...]
        -> low byte from 0x01FF, high byte from 0x0100. Wraps within page 1.

So *:2 at the folded address is wrong; the high byte must come from page | ((dp+1) & 0xFF).

AND HERE IS THE ARITHMETIC THAT EXPLAINS THE MISS, which is the reusable lesson: dp=0xFF
appears in 11 of BA's 1000 cases. A 32-case sample therefore expects 0.35 hits. It was never
going to find this, and no amount of re-running the gated tier would have changed that.

THE SAMPLE SIZE IS NOT RAISED IN RESPONSE. Doubling to 64 still expects only 0.7 hits, so it
would buy unreliability rather than coverage, at real repo cost. The correct division of
labour is the one already built: the sampled tier gates every commit cheaply and catches
regressions, and the exhaustive tier answers density questions like this one. What this
episode changes is when to REACH for the exhaustive tier -- not just as a final check, but
the moment the sampled baseline is silent on a specific structural question. A PSW-only
failure with no address mismatch is exactly that signal.

title: Vendor the SPCdra SPC700 decode table (Apache-2.0, our own language id)
description:
Vendor SPCdra's SPC700 decode table into this repo under Apache-2.0 with attribution preserved.
Approved by the user 2026-08-16 (see grm-y7d).

SOURCE: github.com/qwertymodo/SPCdra at 295b552f, Apache-2.0 (LICENSE file present; same license
as this project and as Ghidra itself). Files: data/languages/spc700-native.slaspec, spc700.sinc,
spc700.ldefs, spc700.pspec, spc700.cspec. The spc700-65816.slaspec variant is a pure mnemonic
renaming of the same opcodes -- take it or leave it, it is cosmetic.

SCOPE OF THIS BEAD IS THE DECODE TABLE AND THE PLUMBING, NOT THE SEMANTICS. The p-code bodies are
known broken (grm-y7d verification) and are rewritten in a separate bead against test vectors. Land
this one with the semantics as-is, clearly marked, so the rewrite has a baseline to diff against.

MUST DO:
 * OUR OWN LANGUAGE ID, not spc700:LE:16:default. A user with SPCdra installed alongside our
   extension would otherwise have two modules defining the same id. Pick a variant that cannot
   collide.
 * Attribution: retain the Apache-2.0 headers, add the origin (repo + commit) to NOTICE and to the
   slaspec header. This is the first third-party code vendored into the repo, so whatever pattern
   is set here is the precedent for grm-hb6.6 and grm-p5w.
 * Confirm it compiles in OUR build, not just via support/sleigh.bat. The extension ships
   data/languages already (see data/sleighArgs.txt in the installed tree), so wire it into the
   existing mechanism rather than inventing one.
 * A headless smoke fixture that disassembles a handful of known bytes and asserts the MNEMONIC
   TEXT -- that part is correct today and is what must not regress while the semantics are rewritten.

VERIFIED ALREADY, do not re-derive: the spec compiles clean under Ghidra 12.1.2's sleigh (21 KB
.sla, no errors/warnings), and opcode coverage is 256/256 -- 208 explicit op=0xNN plus three
low-nibble families (x1 TCALL, x2 SET1/CLR1, x3 BBS/BBC, 16 each), no collisions.
close_reason: Vendored at fork point 295b552f as SPC700:LE:16:retro; decode table + plumbing only, semantics deliberately unmodified. Full gate green (401 JUnit, 0 failures; all headless goldens byte-identical). Byte-identity to upstream verified independently.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-16 (user): THIS IS NOT THE FIRST VENDORED COMPONENT. This bead's description
claims the attribution pattern set here is a new precedent for grm-hb6.6 and grm-p5w. That is
wrong -- data/languages/6510_illegal.sinc is already vendored from anarkiwi/deity-informant
(Apache-2.0), and the pattern is established. FOLLOW IT, do not invent one.

THE EXISTING PATTERN, both halves required:
 1. NOTICE gets a delimited block naming: the path, one line on what the file is, the copyright
    holder, the license, and Upstream repo / Commit / Path -- plus an explicit statement of what
    was modified and why the naming is the way it is.
 2. The file itself gets a prepended header comment repeating upstream/commit/path, the copyright
    line, and the full Apache-2.0 boilerplate paragraph.

The NOTICE preamble already says "This product includes software developed by third parties, as
recorded below. All of it is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (see LICENSE), the
same license as this project" -- SPCdra fits that sentence unchanged, so only a new block is needed.

BUT NOTE THE ONE PLACE THE PRECEDENT DOES NOT TRANSFER, and it needs a deliberate decision here.
6510_illegal.sinc is vendored VERBATIM and its header says so in as many words: "keep
byte-identical to upstream so re-syncs stay a clean diff", with upstream's "illegal" terminology
retained even though this project says "undocumented" everywhere else. That discipline exists to
keep future re-syncs cheap.

SPCdra CANNOT be handled that way. grm-c9d.3 rewrites the semantics wholesale, so the vendored
files diverge permanently and by design -- a re-sync is never happening, and pretending otherwise
in the header would be a lie that misleads the next reader. So this is a FORK-AND-DIVERGE vendor,
not a track-upstream vendor, and the header/NOTICE wording must say which it is. Suggested split:
record the upstream commit as the FORK POINT rather than as a sync target, and state plainly that
the decode table is upstream's while the semantics are ours. That distinction is the actually
reusable precedent for grm-hb6.6, where harvested community disassemblies will also be transformed
rather than tracked.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ADDENDUM 2026-08-16: the user asked to keep upstream contribution possible (grm-c9d.6), which
slightly qualifies the fork-and-diverge framing in the correction above.

Both things are true and they are not in tension. The vendored files WILL diverge permanently --
grm-c9d.3 rewrites the semantics, so the header must not promise resyncability the way
6510_illegal.sinc's does. But "we never sync FROM upstream" does not mean "we never send TO
upstream". Word the attribution accordingly:

  * record the upstream commit as the FORK POINT, not a sync target
  * state plainly that the decode table is upstream's and the semantics are ours
  * do NOT add the "keep byte-identical to upstream" instruction that 6510_illegal.sinc carries --
    it would be false here and would mislead the next reader into avoiding necessary edits

Keeping a tracked fork branch (per grm-c9d.3's commit-discipline constraint) is what preserves the
outbound path; the NOTICE wording is about honesty on the inbound one.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION DECISIONS 2026-08-16, taken at the start of the .1 work.

LANGUAGE ID: SPC700:LE:16:retro (user ruling). The "retro" variant is what prevents the
collision this bead warns about -- SPCdra's own id is spc700:LE:16:default, and a user with
both extensions installed would otherwise have two modules defining the same id. This is the
same hazard README.md already documents for 6510:LE:16:default vs. other C64 projects, so
the README caveat is being extended rather than a new one written.

Unconfirmed detail flagged to the implementer rather than assumed: SPCdra pairs
processor="SPC700" with a LOWERCASE id="spc700:...", and that loaded fine during the grm-y7d
verification. Ghidra's exact casing rule for the processor segment is therefore not known.
The smoke test asserts the RESOLVED getLanguageID().getIdAsString() and whatever actually
works becomes the canonical string.

FILE LAYOUT follows the repo's own convention rather than upstream's, because the two differ:
this repo puts a thin prose header plus @include lines in the .slaspec and all content in
.sinc files (6510.slaspec is 15 lines). So:
  spc700core.sinc  <- SPCdra spc700.sinc, verbatim + our header
  spc700ops.sinc   <- SPCdra spc700-native.slaspec, verbatim + our header, .slaspec->.sinc
                      rename noted in the header, its own @include line dropped
  spc700.slaspec   <- ours, the thin shell
  spc700.ldefs / .pspec / .cspec
"core" matches the existing 6502core.sinc precedent.

SKIPPED spc700-65816.slaspec. It is a pure mnemonic renaming of the same 256 opcodes. Taking
it would double the surface grm-c9d.3 has to rewrite for zero semantic gain. If the 65816
mnemonic style is ever wanted it can be re-derived from the vendored table cheaply.

NO build.gradle CHANGE IS NEEDED, contrary to what "wire it into the existing mechanism"
might suggest. sleighCompile already runs SleighCompile with -a ./languages (compiles every
.slaspec in the dir) and globs its inputs/outputs over *.slaspec,*.sinc,*.pspec,*.cspec,
*.ldefs -> *.sla; buildExtension and test both dependsOn it; the packaging allowlist already
ships data/. Dropping the files in is the whole wiring job.

COPYRIGHT LINE: SPCdra declares no holder ANYWHERE -- its LICENSE appendix is the unfilled
"Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]" template and the source files carry no headers
at all. So there is nothing to "retain" as the bead description assumes, and no name to put
in. Attribution is to the project and repo. Contrast 6510_illegal.sinc, which could name
Josh Bailey because upstream declared it.

SMOKE TEST IS JUNIT, NOT HEADLESS -- a deliberate deviation from this bead's MUST DO list.
The reason is mechanical: run-banktest.sh's run_one always passes -loader <Loader>, and the
.spc loader is grm-c9d.4 (P4, not started), so there is nothing to import an SPC700 program
with yet. AbstractBundledLanguageTest grafts grm.moduleDir into the test application layout,
so a bundled language resolves in plain JUnit and ProgramBuilder gives exactly the
mnemonic-text assertions this bead asks for, with no harness plumbing at all.
UndocLanguageTest is the precedent. Revisit only if grm-c9d.4 lands a loader and an
end-to-end import fixture becomes worth having.

title: SPC700 as a primary platform: vendored language, verified semantics, .spc loader
description:
RULED 2026-08-16 (user): SPC700 is a PRIMARY PLATFORM for this project, not a side-effect of the
grm-1.7.3 SMC work. "SPC700 is an important part of reversing SNES games and should be considered
a primary platform, so the work is worthy." Vendoring the SPCdra sleigh under Apache-2.0 is also
approved. Both rulings recorded on grm-y7d, which is closed.

That reframes the deliverable. The SPC700 language is not merely a prerequisite for extracting an
IPL upload -- it is the disassembly target for SNES audio work generally, including .spc rips that
need no SNES-side extraction at all. This epic owns the language and the .spc loader; grm-1.7.3
keeps the cross-processor upload extraction and consumes what lands here.

SOURCING DECISION, settled by the grm-y7d evaluation (full brief + verification on that bead):
vendor SPCdra's DECODE TABLE (Apache-2.0, attribution preserved, our own language id), rewrite the
P-CODE SEMANTICS against SingleStepTests/spc700 vectors, and write our own .spc loader.

WHY NOT bundle as-is: the semantics are measurably broken -- verified against real p-code, not
inferred. ADDR8/ADDR16 double-dereference every data access (MOV A,$10 emits two LOADs and means
A = **(word**)0x10); CMP/SBC set carry inverted so every CMP/BCS decompiles backwards; ADC
hardcodes N=0; ASL/ROL can never set carry; INC/DEC set no flags at all; MOV dp,X stores to the
wrong address; ASL dp+X stores the 2-byte ADDRESS to the UNINDEXED location.

WHY NOT reimplement from scratch: the decode table is complete and correct -- 256/256 opcodes, no
collisions, correct operand text, correct instruction lengths, correct TCALL vector arithmetic
(0xFFE0 - (n+1)*2 = $FFDE - n*2). That is the tedious half and it is sound. The confirming
evidence is that the disassembly TEXT is right in every case tested while the p-code is wrong --
the decode table has been exercised for five years, the semantics never have.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
WORKFLOW CORRECTION 2026-08-16 (user). This epic's description, and grm-c9d.4's, lean on .spc rips
as the fast path to an AKAO disassembly target. THAT IS NOT THE PRIMARY WORKFLOW and the framing
should not drive prioritisation.

USER'S ACTUAL WORKFLOW, verbatim: "for GME purposes, we will generally not be working from .spc
files, but the game ROM, with reversing providing hints on where the code is and the entry point.
though if analyzers can find it automatically, all the better. the cross-platform code upload
aspect of 1.7 is all about this. being able to load spcs is a nice feature but not my primary
motivator."

CONSEQUENCES:
 * THE PRIMARY CONSUMER OF THIS EPIC IS grm-1.7.3 -- ROM-side recovery of the IPL upload,
   accumulating N transfers into one SPC700 Program. The language exists to make that Program
   readable. grm-1.7.3's P3 -> P2 bump stands, but for this reason rather than the one recorded
   when it was made.
 * grm-c9d.4 (.spc loader) is a NICE-TO-HAVE, dropped P3 -> P4. It is not on the critical path and
   nothing else in the epic depends on it. Do not sequence work as though it were.
 * The entry-point problem MOVES, and this is the substantive part. On the .spc side it is a
   snapshot-PC-is-not-the-entry-point problem that SPCdra solves with a manual bsnes-plus
   breakpoint. On the ROM side the upload site itself carries the answer: the IPL handshake
   transfers address+length+data records and the final handshake hands over a start address, so
   the entry point is RECOVERABLE FROM THE ROM-SIDE UPLOAD CODE. The user's "if analyzers can find
   it automatically, all the better" is an explicit invitation to make that automatic rather than
   hint-driven. That work belongs to grm-1.7.3, not to grm-c9d.4 -- but grm-c9d.4 should consume
   whatever mechanism 1.7.3 builds rather than inventing a second one.

Nothing about the sourcing decision or the defect list changes -- those were measured and stand.

title: CbmBasicWalker.isBasicStart reads two zero bytes as an empty BASIC program, so a machine-code PRG starting 00 00 is never disassembled
description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-16, while trying to answer a completely different question (whether the
6502 BIT-skip idiom is common in C64 code, grm-t3n / grm-pfp). The first real non-packed C64
program tried produced ZERO INSTRUCTIONS, and the import reported success.

THE PROGRAM: sid.obj.64.prg, a SID player, 3153 bytes of 6502 loading at $C000. Not packed, not
BASIC, no tricks -- just a machine-code PRG whose first bytes happen to be a zeroed workspace:

    00 c0 | 00 00 00 00 ... (0x15E bytes of zeros) ... 00 61 c1 60 01 02 04 ...
    ^load   ^payload starts here

THE BUG, in CbmBasicWalker.isBasicStart:

    long firstLink = (hi << 8) | lo;
    if (firstLink == 0) {
        return true;   // "trivially empty BASIC program"
    }

Two zero bytes at the load address were taken as proof the whole PRG is a BASIC program. So
AbstractCbmPrgLoader's entry-point block took its basicStart branch, deliberately did NOT mark a
function at the load address (correct FOR BASIC -- those bytes would be a line link, not code),
and logged that a CBM BASIC analyzer would find the real ML entry from a SYS line. There is no
SYS line, because it is not BASIC. Nothing else ever seeded disassembly.

MEASURED, before and after:
    before   CENSUS loadedBytes=3153 instrs=0 instrBytes=0 coverage=0.0% functions=39
    after    CENSUS loadedBytes=3153 instrs=1 instrBytes=1 coverage=0.0% functions=40
(The 39 pre-existing "functions" are the KERNAL/BASIC symbol-set marks in unloaded ROM blocks,
not program code. The single instruction after the fix is the BRK at $C000 -- see BELOW, that
part is this file's own shape, not a remaining defect.)

*** THE FAILURE MODE IS THE DANGEROUS ONE: SILENT, TOTAL, AND IT LOOKS LIKE SUCCESS. *** No
error, no warning bookmark, no failed import -- "Analysis succeeded", and an empty listing. A
user meeting this would reasonably conclude the extension does not work on C64 at all.

THE FIX: case (a) now also requires the payload to END at the terminator. A genuinely empty BASIC
program is EXACTLY its two-byte terminator (SAVE with no program writes a 4-byte file), so
anything with payload past loadAddr+2 is not one. The two cases separate cleanly, with no
heuristic:

    if (firstLink == 0) {
        return loadAddr + 2 >= limitAddr;
    }

WHY THIS DIRECTION IS OBVIOUSLY RIGHT, recorded so it is not re-litigated: the costs are wildly
asymmetric. Wrongly saying "not BASIC" about a genuinely empty BASIC program marks a function on
a 2-byte payload that contains nothing anyway. Wrongly saying "BASIC" about machine code loses
the entire program, silently. Two zero bytes were being treated as sufficient evidence for the
strongest available conclusion, and machine code beginning 00 00 is entirely ordinary -- a zeroed
field, a table, a vector slot.

COVERAGE ADDED: src/test/java/retromachines/CbmBasicStartSniffTest.java (Tier 1 -- ByteSource is a
one-method interface, so no Program needed). Five cases: the regression (machine code beginning
00 00), the real empty-BASIC case that keeps the branch honest, a real one-line SYS program, the
coincidental-early-$00 case the "first line must be clean" rule already guarded, and a truncated
payload. There was NO test of isBasicStart before this.

GATES: JUnit green; c64-loader, basic-petscii and basic-dialects chunks green with every golden
byte-identical (18 suites), which is the meaningful check -- those chunks are full of BASIC-start
PRGs and the fix must not have moved any of them.

*** WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, AND IT IS A SEPARATE QUESTION WORTH ITS OWN LOOK: THE LOAD ADDRESS IS
NOT ALWAYS THE ENTRY POINT. *** With the fix, sid.obj.64.prg gets a function at $C000 and
disassembles exactly one instruction -- BRK -- because $C000 really is data (0x15E bytes of
zeroed workspace; the first non-zero byte is at CPU $C15F). Marking the load address is the right
DEFAULT and is all a loader can know without running the program, but for object-file-shaped PRGs
it lands on data. Getting real coverage on such a file needs the entry from outside the file: a
SYS documented with the program, an emulator break, or a hand look. That is the same sourcing
problem grm-t3n records for the C64 tier generally, and it is why the BIT-skip incidence question
this session started from is STILL UNANSWERED for C64.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
FIX LANDED AND VERIFIED END TO END, 2026-08-16.

GATES: full synthetic gate SUITE OK with every golden byte-identical (the c64-loader,
basic-petscii and basic-dialects chunks are full of BASIC-start PRGs, so an unchanged set of
goldens there is the meaningful check that the fix did not cost the case the sniff exists for).
JUnit green including the five new CbmBasicStartSniffTest cases.

THE PAYOFF, on the program that exposed it: sid.obj.64.prg went from ZERO instructions to a
disassemblable program. With its three real entry points supplied from outside the file ($c1cd,
$c200, $c326 -- the load address is workspace, see below), it now yields 1024 instructions at
69.1% coverage, and the 6502 skip idiom this session was chasing turned up in it immediately:
BIT $28A9 at cadc hiding LDA #$28 at cadd, with TWO conditional branches already targeting that
address. Recorded on grm-t3n.

STILL TRUE AND NOT THIS BEAD'S JOB: the load address is not always the entry point. Post-fix,
$C000 disassembles to a single BRK because the first 0x15E bytes are a zeroed workspace. Marking
the load address is the right DEFAULT and all a loader can know without running the program;
supplying a real entry is a sourcing problem, tracked on grm-t3n.

title: smb3 FUN_c542 deposits a CONSTANT bank but warns about an unrecoverable argument -- is restoresEntryBank blind on MMC3?
description:
Split out of grm-evn 2026-08-16, when a hand pass settled the question that bead existed to ask
and left this one behind it. grm-evn asked "is FUN_c542 a real helper or a false one"; the answer
is REAL, smb3's golden was two lines stale, and it has been blessed. THE ROW IS GREEN NOW, WHICH
IS EXACTLY WHY THIS NEEDS ITS OWN BEAD -- nothing will trip over it again.

THE FINDING (user, disassembler, 2026-08-16):
    "c542: complex function that sets a specific value for PRG bank $1a (c5f5 is part of c542's
     function body) and then restores it later with a call to $ffc2."

*** THE WARNING TEXT IS WRONG, NOT MERELY PESSIMISTIC. *** Both smb3 sites say:

    867b / ac6d  "Bank state becomes unknown here: call to bank-switch helper FUN_c542 whose bank
                  argument could NOT BE RECOVERED at this call site"

But c542 takes no bank argument. It commits a CONSTANT -- bank $1a -- and later restores. A
helper that deposits a constant has nothing for a call site to supply, so "the argument could not
be recovered" describes a search that should never have been run. The right output at 867b and
ac6d is one of:
  - an annotation of bank $1a, if what survives c542's return is the constant; or
  - ownedMask = 0 with no annotation and NO WARNING, if c542 restores before returning -- the
    save/switch/restore trampoline answer.
Which one depends on whether the $ffc2 restore runs before c542 returns to 867b/ac6d or after,
which is the first thing to establish and is cheap to read off the listing.

HYPOTHESIS FOR THE MECHANISM, stated as such because it is NOT measured. c542 has (at least) two
switch sites -- the c5f5 write and the later restore through $ffc2. "Last switch wins" summarizes
the helper at the RESTORE, whose value comes from wherever ffc2 pulls it, and that is where the
argument search comes from. That is precisely the shape BoardBankAnalyzer.restoresEntryBank
exists to answer (grm-mej.3 increment 2) -- and it is evidently not answering here, because if it
were, the deposit would be ownedMask = 0 and these sites would emit neither annotation nor
warning.

*** THE MOST INTERESTING PART, AND THE REASON THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN TWO WARNING LINES: EVERY
restoresEntryBank CASE MEASURED SO FAR IS AxROM OR UxROM. smb3 IS MMC3. *** So the question is
not just "why does this one helper miss" but "does the trampoline model work at all on a board
whose switch is a two-write register/data pair rather than a single latch store". If it does not,
the same blind spot covers every MMC3 title in the corpus, and grm-8iy.4 (smb2, rcransom -- both
MMC3, both resolving zero instructions into overlay space) is sitting right next to it.

FIRST STEPS, cheapest first:
 1. Read c542's body: where does the $ffc2 restore sit relative to the RTS, and what does ffc2
    pull the bank from?
 2. Does c542 reach restoresEntryBank at all, or is it rejected by one of its guards (the
    branch-free walk, the mirror requirement on the pushed value, the fall-through requirement,
    writesStackPointer)? Instrument rather than reason -- the guards are numerous and the
    javadoc is explicit that each declines for a different reason.
 3. If the model does not apply to MMC3 by construction, say so in restoresEntryBank's javadoc,
    which currently reads as board-agnostic.

RELATED: grm-mej.3 (the model), grm-8iy.4 (MMC3 titles at zero resolution), grm-evn (settled,
the origin). Do NOT re-open the "is c542 a real helper" question -- it is answered.

title: realrom-test.sh runs the DEFAULT Ghidra install even when GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL names another (native A/B silently no-ops)
description:
Running the real-ROM tier against a NON-DEFAULT Ghidra install silently measures the DEFAULT one,
and the failure mode is the direction you want to hear ("nothing moved, my change is safe").

CAUSE. tools/banktest/lib/common.sh derives two knobs INDEPENDENTLY from GRM_TARGET_VERSION:

  grm_default_headless()       :53  GHIDRA_HEADLESS=D:/ghidra_${GRM_TARGET_VERSION}_PUBLIC/support/analyzeHeadless.bat
  grm_default_ghidra_install() :61  GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL=D:/ghidra_${GRM_TARGET_VERSION}_PUBLIC

GHIDRA_HEADLESS is what actually launches Ghidra, so it alone selects which decompile.exe and
sleigh.exe execute. GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL feeds gradle (GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR) and the
application.properties read. realrom-test.sh does not build, so on that script GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL
is very nearly inert -- the comment at :58-59 already says "the runners only ever need the
analyzeHeadless path above". Nothing is wrong with the code; the hazard is that the OBVIOUS knob
name is the one that does nothing here.

MEASURED (2026-08-15, grm-b3m Phase 0). With a patched decompile.exe installed in
D:/ghidra_12.1.2_PATCHED:

  GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL only ...................... pass=30 fail=1, 28/31 dumps byte-identical
  GHIDRA_HEADLESS + GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL ......... pass=19 fail=12, thousands of instructions moved

Same binary on disk, same command otherwise. The first run measured stock Ghidra and read as a
clean result.

WHY THE EXISTING SAFEGUARD DOES NOT CATCH IT. realrom-test.sh prints "installed extension: <sha>"
plus an A/B warning ("if it does not change, you are comparing a build against itself"). That
fingerprints THIS REPO'S EXTENSION ONLY. A native-side change (decompiler, sleigh) leaves the
extension hash identical by construction, so the guard is silent exactly when the native install
is what varies. Same family as the realrom-ab-needs-rebuild memory, different layer.

SUGGESTED FIX, in preference order:
 1. Derive GHIDRA_HEADLESS FROM GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL when the caller set the latter and not the
    former: GHIDRA_HEADLESS="${GHIDRA_HEADLESS:-$GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL/support/analyzeHeadless.bat}".
    Makes the obvious knob do the obvious thing; defaults unchanged when neither is set. Ordering
    matters -- grm_default_ghidra_install() must run first.
 2. Print the resolved install root in the run header next to the extension sha, so the log says
    which Ghidra actually ran. Cheap and it makes every past log self-describing.
 3. Optionally fingerprint the native binaries (sha of decompile.exe) into the same header line,
    which would make a native A/B against an unchanged install as loud as an unrebuilt extension.

ACCEPTANCE
 - GRM_GHIDRA_INSTALL=<other install> realrom-test.sh check --only megaman demonstrably runs the
   other install's decompile.exe (prove by installing a deliberately different binary and seeing
   rows move).
 - Header names the resolved install root.
 - Default invocation is byte-identical to today: full 'check --all' still gives the documented
   baseline (see realrom-expected-baseline-fails).

Label background-ok: this is shell/driver plumbing, no golden can move (verified by the last
acceptance bullet).

See memory realrom-ab-wrong-install-trap, realrom-ab-needs-rebuild; beads grm-b3m, grm-eyn.
close_reason: Closed
