title: Bandai FCG submapper 16.4 (FCG-1/2) decodes registers at $6000-$7FFF: db3's PRG writes are outside the modeled range
description:
Found by the project owner's hand disassembly of db3 (2026-08-15), and verified in-repo the
same day. This is the REAL root cause of grm-azv, and it retires that bead's stated one.

THE FINDING (owner, disassembler): db3 switches PRG by writing $6008, not $8008. Its helper at
db2f stores shadow $6a and register $6008. There are no occurrences of "99 00 60" or
"9D 00 60" -- the write is absolute, and it is ordinary code sitting in ROM.

WHY WE SEE NOTHING: machines/nes-bandai-fcg.yaml declares exactly one memory-latch mechanism,
start 0x8000 / end 0xFFFF. A store to $6008 is outside it, so no PRG-register write is
detectable on db3 by construction. Nothing about detection logic is broken.

THE DESCRIPTOR'S SUBMAPPER MAPPING IS BACKWARDS. Its module header says the LZ93D50
generation with $8000-$FFFF registers is "submapper 16.4/16.5", and that "the legacy
FCG-1/FCG-2 generation (submapper 16.1/16.2) instead exposes the same register file at
$6000-$7FFF". Checked against the NESdev per-mapper page
(https://www.nesdev.org/wiki/INES_Mapper_016), the actual submapper table is:

  16.0  unspecified -- emulate BOTH FCG-1/2 and LZ93D50 in their respective ranges
  16.1  deprecated -> use mapper 159
  16.2  deprecated -> use mapper 157
  16.3  deprecated -> use mapper 153
  16.4  FCG-1/2    -- responds ONLY in CPU $6000-$7FFF; IRQ counter not latched
  16.5  LZ93D50    -- responds ONLY in CPU $8000-$FFFF; IRQ counter latched

So 16.4 is the $6000 board, not the $8000 one, and 16.1/16.2 are aliases for 159/157 rather
than the legacy generation. The yaml's premise that "the real-ROM exercisers for this bead
(the Dragon Ball collection at Z:/nes/db) are all LZ93D50 boards" is false for db3.

THE HEADERS SAY SO, and we already parse them. All four pinned Bandai fixtures carry NES 2.0
headers ((h[7] & 0x0C) == 0x08), with the submapper in h[8]'s HIGH nibble:

  db3          4e 45 53 1a 08 20 00 18 40 ...   mapper 16,  submapper 4   -> $6000-$7FFF
  dbz2         4e 45 53 1a 10 20 02 18 50 ...   mapper 16,  submapper 5   -> $8000-$FFFF
  dbz_datach   4e 45 53 1a 10 00 d0 98 00 ...   mapper 157, submapper 0
  dbz_saiyan   4e 45 53 1a 10 20 f2 98 00 ...   mapper 159, submapper 0

That matches the owner's per-title observations exactly: dbz2 helper d12f -> register $8008,
dbz_datach cc28 -> $8008, dbz_saiyan c9c0 -> $8008, only db3 -> $6008. Also present locally
and unpinned: "Dragon Ball - Daimaou Fukkatsu (Japan)" (h[8]=0x40) is a second submapper-4
title, so db3 is not a one-off.

NesRomLoader.InesHeader.parse (NesRomLoader.java:137) uses h[8] only for the mapper's high
bits (`(h[8] & 0x0F) << 8`) and DISCARDS the high nibble. InesHeader carries no submapper
field. The distinguishing datum is in the file and we throw it away.

FIX SHAPE, in the order that gets db3 working:
 (a) Correct the yaml module header's submapper table (documentation-only, but it is the thing
     that will mislead the next reader).
 (b) Model the $6000-$7FFF register base. Cheapest correct option is NESdev's own submapper-0
     prescription: a SECOND memory-latch mechanism at start 0x6000 / end 0x7FFF with the same
     addr_mask 0xF / addr_match 0x8 / mask 0x0F, also `sets: [prg_bank]`. Both generations
     respond in only one range, so a board that models both is right for either and cannot
     double-count on a real image. Precedent that a mechanism need not sit inside a declared
     PRG window: nes-modetest.yaml already declares one at 0x6000-0x6FFF.
 (c) Optionally, plumb the submapper through InesHeader so the descriptor tier can be exact
     rather than permissive. Only worth it if (b) turns out to misfire on some title.

Option (b) alone should be enough, and is testable immediately against db3's db2f helper.

VERIFY WITH: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --all  (db3 is a curated-manifest row).

title: [bug] banktest gate cannot run from a .claude/worktrees worktree: Ghidra rejects the dot-leading path element
description:
FOUND 2026-08-15 by a Bucket-1 agent running the gate from a `.claude/worktrees/` worktree. It
broke EVERY fixture, C64 and NES alike, including ones the agent had not touched -- so the first
read is "my change destroyed everything", which is exactly the wrong conclusion and costs a
debugging cycle to unwind.

THE FAILURE:

    IllegalArgumentException: Path element starting with '.' is not permitted

thrown from Ghidra's ProjectLocator / NamingUtilities.checkName while building the headless
project path. Nothing to do with the change under test.

ROOT CAUSE. tools/banktest/lib/common.sh's grm_work_dir() defaults the headless work dir to
$REPO_ROOT/build/banktest-work. In an agent worktree REPO_ROOT is

    D:/git/ghidra-retro-machines/.claude/worktrees/agent-<id>

and Ghidra rejects the `.claude` segment outright -- a leading dot in ANY path element is
invalid for a project location. So the project can never be created and every fixture fails
before it starts.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. CLAUDE.md's parallelization rule is "one agent per git
worktree, never two agents sharing one working tree", and the Agent tool's worktree isolation
puts those worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` by construction. So the documented, recommended
way to run parallel agents currently CANNOT run the acceptance gate without a manual override.
Every such agent either burns a cycle rediscovering this or silently reports a red gate.

WORKAROUND THAT WORKS TODAY (verification only, no repo change): point the already-supported
env var outside the repo tree --

    export GRM_BANKTEST_WORK=/c/Users/cab/AppData/Local/Temp/grm-banktest-$$
    mkdir -p "$GRM_BANKTEST_WORK"
    bash tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh check

FIX OPTIONS, in rough order of preference:
  1. Make grm_work_dir() sanitize the derived path -- detect any dot-leading segment in
     REPO_ROOT and fall back to a temp location automatically, logging the substitution. Fixes
     it for every caller with no user action.
  2. Detect the condition and FAIL EARLY with a message naming GRM_BANKTEST_WORK, rather than
     letting 90+ fixtures fail with an unrelated-looking stack trace. Cheaper, but still
     manual.
  3. Document it in CLAUDE.md next to the parallelization rules. Necessary either way; not
     sufficient alone.

Prefer 1 with 2 as the guard for cases sanitizing cannot fix. Note the constraint that the work
dir must stay per-worktree distinct, or parallel agents will collide in it -- do not "fix" this
by pointing every worktree at one shared path.

ALSO CHECK, same root cause, not yet verified: run-banktest.sh's user-settings-dir relocation
and build/ghidra-home (the isolated extension install) derive from REPO_ROOT too. If Ghidra
validates those paths the same way, they have the same defect and the same fix.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-15 (commit 18d937c). grm_work_dir now detects a dot-leading segment in REPO_ROOT
and redirects the base to ${TMPDIR:-${TEMP:-/tmp}}/grm-banktest-work-<sanitized REPO_ROOT>,
printing a NOTE naming the substitution. Keyed off REPO_ROOT so parallel worktrees get distinct
dirs. Normal checkouts unchanged; GRM_BANKTEST_WORK still overrides.

Verified: from a .claude/worktrees worktree, `check nes-banking` failed all 14 NES fixtures with
the IllegalArgumentException before the fix and reported SUITE OK after. Full gate SUITE OK from
the main tree (normal path, no regression).

ALSO CHECK resolved, negatively: run-banktest.sh's settings-dir relocation (build/ghidra-home,
-Dapplication.settingsdir) does NOT have the same defect. The post-fix worktree run exercised
that path and passed -- NamingUtilities validates project LOCATIONS, not the settings dir.

INTEGRATOR NOTE. The predicate was rewritten from the subagent's `local IFS='/'` split loop to
a two-pattern case (`.* | */.*`). A segment starts with '.' exactly when the path contains "/."
or the path itself begins with '.', so the two are equivalent -- but the split form leaves $path
unquoted and therefore glob-expands it, and '[' is a legal character in a Windows directory name.
Verified against a table: repo.git/x and foo.bar are correctly clean (dot not at segment start),
D:/git/[test]/repo is clean under the case form and would have been mangled under the loop.

RESIDUAL, not fixed: if TMPDIR/TEMP itself contained a dot-leading segment the fallback would
land in the same trap. Not observed on any machine here and not worth a second guard.

title: Descriptor validation hardening: make the compiler enforce what the runtime requires
description:
Umbrella created by the 2026-08-11 priority review over the QR-* findings in docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md. Groups three findings that the review filed as peers but that share one root cause, one code area, and one shape of fix.

ROOT CAUSE: the descriptor build pipeline (tools/gdtbuilder MapCompiler, plus the per-file build.gradle tasks) and the shipped runtime (DescriptorSupport, BoardBankAnalyzer, NesBoardRegistry) hold SEPARATE and drifted contracts about what a valid descriptor is. The compiler accepts inputs the runtime then logs-and-discards, ignores, or resolves in an order-dependent way. The failure mode is uniformly silent: a descriptor compiles and ships successfully, then quietly does less than it says.

Children:
- grm-p7i (P2, QR-05): MapCompiler accepts multi-key/mixed-field/duplicate-value layout 'when' conditions that DescriptorSupport.planWindows logs and discards wholesale at runtime.
- grm-sf6 (P2, QR-08): MapCompiler accepts unknown mechanism strategy spellings (runtime logs and skips them) and does not validate ordinary region/window/subregion geometry the way the newer copied_from path already does.
- grm-7j5 (P3, QR-06): NesBoardRegistry.forMapper returns the first claiming board from an unsorted resource scan, with no collection-level uniqueness check at build time.

WHY GROUPED: all three are compile-time validation that should fail the build with descriptor context instead of degrading silently at runtime; all three touch the same one or two files; and each individually is too small to justify its own round of gate runs. The review's own suggested implementation order already puts QR-05/06/08 together as one series.

NONE of these has a live trigger today -- no shipped descriptor hits any of them. They are authoring traps for whoever writes the next descriptor, which is the argument for doing them as one deliberate pass rather than reactively.

SHARED ACCEPTANCE: every shipped descriptor compiles unchanged; every successfully compiled artifact is accepted by the runtime that consumes it; each new rejection names the offending descriptor and field in its message; the full gate (tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh check) is green at the end of the series.
acceptance_criteria: All three children closed. Shipped descriptors compile unchanged and the full gate is green. A negative-fixture test exists for each new compile-time rejection, and each rejection message carries descriptor context. No golden churn is expected; any that appears is reviewed before blessing.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
All three children closed. Shared acceptance verified:

- Every shipped descriptor compiles UNCHANGED -- no machines/*.yaml needed an
  edit, confirming they were already well-formed under every newly-enforced rule.
  The epic's prediction that none of these had a live trigger held exactly.
- Every successfully compiled artifact is accepted by the runtime that consumes
  it: the new compile-time rules were read off DescriptorSupport.planWindows and
  createIoSubregions directly and mirror them, including createIoSubregions'
  repeat_to > end > size precedence.
- Each new rejection names the offending descriptor path, field, and value.
- Negative fixture test per rejection, asserting message content not just
  exception type (MapCompilerTest: layoutWhenErrors, unknownStrategyErrors,
  geometryErrors), plus positive tests for the two cases a careless
  implementation would over-reject: a 1-byte region and a deferred strategy name.
- Full gate green: tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh check -> SUITE OK (check),
  exit 0. NO golden churn, as predicted -- compiled output is byte-identical
  because the derived ends are used only for validation and no emit order moved.

One residual gap recorded on grm-sf6 rather than papered over: the compiler's
hard-coded strategy vocabulary has no automatic link to the implementation
classes (no ClassSearcher in that build). The drift test catches removals and
orphaned set entries but not a new strategy class added with neither side
updated. If that ever bites, the fix is a generated vocabulary, not a better test.

title: Remove the developer-specific Gradle path from the harness
description:
Split out of grm-e7w (docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-10) during the 2026-08-11 priority review. This is the mechanical half of QR-10: no project-level decision needed, unlike the CI/dependency-verification half that stays on grm-e7w.

tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh:147 is:

    GRADLE="${GRADLE:-/d/gradle-8.13/bin/gradle}"

That default is one developer's install path. A contributor on any other machine must discover and export GRADLE before the gate runs at all; the reviewer's first two gate attempts failed before compilation for exactly this reason. The repo also has no gradlew/gradle/wrapper, so there is no in-repo Gradle to fall back to.

Note the deliberate design this must NOT disturb: the GHIDRA install resolution (ghidraInstallRoot composed with ghidraTargetVersion, plus the 'GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR= gradle ...' escape hatch) is intentional and documented in CLAUDE.md and the build-ghidra-install-dir memory. This bead is about the GRADLE BINARY only, which is a separate and genuinely hardcoded thing.
acceptance_criteria: A contributor with no GRM-specific environment can run the documented gate command from a clean checkout. Either a committed Gradle wrapper (with distribution checksum) is preferred by the harness, or the harness resolves gradle from PATH and fails with an actionable message when absent. The GRADLE env var still overrides. Ghidra install resolution and its escape hatch are unchanged. Full gate stays green.
close_reason: Landed afe399a. build-and-test.sh resolves gradle as $GRADLE -> committed ./gradlew -> gradle on PATH -> loud failure naming all three; wrapper committed (pins its distribution by sha256). Two details that are load-bearing: .gitattributes forces gradlew to LF (core.autocrlf=true would otherwise rewrite the shebang and break it with 'bad interpreter'), and gradlew is committed mode 100755 -- it was staged 100644 at integration, which Windows hides but which would make the [ -x ] probe false on a fresh clone elsewhere, defeating the portability this bead exists to provide. ghidraInstallRoot/ghidraTargetVersion composition and the GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR= escape hatch untouched.

title: Interrupt handler entries are seeded fully-known initial_state, but an interrupt fires from arbitrary mainline context
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 while answering grm-ii6. Real, but INVESTIGATED AND EXCLUDED as the cause of that
bead's two wrong annotations -- see 'why this is not grm-p9y' below before assuming they are the
same defect.

THE DEFECT. BoardBankAnalyzer.runDataflow (src/main/java/retromachines/BoardBankAnalyzer.java:
643-651) seeds EVERY function entry and every external entry point with

    BankState seedState = BankState.fullyKnown(board.mask(), board.initialState());

NesRomLoader.labelVectorTargets (src/main/java/retromachines/NesRomLoader.java:514-556) reads the
6502 vector table and markAsFunction()s all three handlers -- $FFFA NMI, $FFFC RESET, $FFFE IRQ --
so the NMI and IRQ handlers become ordinary dataflow seeds and are declared to START WITH THE BANK
FULLY KNOWN AT initial_state.

That is sound for RESET. It is not sound for NMI or IRQ: an interrupt fires asynchronously from
arbitrary mainline context, so the bank live on entry is whatever the interrupted code had. Both
nes-axrom.map and nes-uxrom.map declare initial_state 0, so today every NES interrupt handler is
told 'bank 0, certain' on entry.

THE FIX, in one line: seed NMI and IRQ vector targets with BankState.unknown(); RESET keeps
initialState(). The identity is already available at seeding time -- labelVectorTargets writes the
literal labels 'NMI', 'RESET' and 'IRQ' on those addresses, so runDataflow can distinguish them
without re-reading the vector table. (Prefer a mechanism sturdier than label-name matching if one
is cheap; the loader could equally record the three addresses as program properties.)

Note the 6502 vector table is a NES/6502-family fact but the seeding is generic, so decide whether
the weakening belongs in runDataflow (machine-independent, driven by data the loader supplies) or
behind a board/machine hook. Prefer the former: the loader knows the vectors, the analyzer should
just consume them.

WHY THIS IS NOT grm-p9y. grm-p9y's two wrong annotations (megaman d571, wizwarr ffa6) are NMI
restore stores, so the connection looks obvious -- and it is wrong. Both wrong banks come from
switches INSIDE the handler, not from the entry seed:
  * megaman's '4' comes from 'D54E STA $C004' (LDA #$04 immediately before).
  * wizwarr's '0' comes from 'FF9E STA $8000', which is itself a CORRECT annotation -- the
    preceding 'AND #$18' provably clears the PRG bits.
Fixing the seeding alone changes NEITHER wrong claim. The two beads are independent.

BLAST RADIUS: UNMEASURED, and that is exactly why it was kept out of grm-p9y -- weakening the
entry state will turn some currently-confident annotations inside interrupt handlers into
warnings, and those need reading on their merits before any golden is blessed. Some will be honest
losses (claims that were only ever true because of this seed); some may be recoverable another
way. Measure with a rebuilt real-ROM A/B (see the realrom-ab-needs-rebuild memory) and account for
every changed line, per the grm-mej.2 discipline.

RELATED PRIOR ART. The grm-1fv finding, archived in docs/human-research-todo.md's Answered table,
already named the general gap: 'bank state across an INTERRUPT boundary -- a handler that restores
banking on exit means the interrupted code's state is preserved, which the engine has no way to
express.' rcransom's FUN_ff07 / FUN_ff29 are interrupt-exit restore routines of the same family.
This bead is the entry half of that gap; grm-p9y is the exit half.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
PROMOTED P3 -> P2, 2026-08-15 (user concurred).

NEW EVIDENCE, and it bears directly on the "why this is not grm-p9y" exclusion recorded
in this bead. The user hand-traced two more sites (docs/human recon notes.txt, entries
under grm-ii6) and BOTH are the exact shape this bead describes:

  megaman d56e: LDA $42; TAX; STA $c000,X -- $42 correctly identified as a write-through
    shadow; the enclosing function is the NMI HANDLER and the store is near the end.
    Almost certainly restoring the bank before returning from the interrupt.
    "it should probably not specify bank 4 at this point"
  wizwarr ffa4: LDA $00; STA $8000 -- $00 correctly identified as a write-through
    shadow; enclosing function is the NMI HANDLER, store is immediately before the
    return sequence. Clearly restoring bank before returning.
    "it should probably not specify bank 0 though"

So: two independent titles, both NMI handlers, both a shadow RESTORE immediately before
return, both receiving a concrete bank annotation that is wrong -- and wrong in exactly
the way fullyKnown(initialState) seeding at a vector-marked function entry predicts.

ACTION BEFORE ANY IMPLEMENTATION: re-examine the investigated-and-excluded finding in
this bead body. That exclusion was reached against grm-ii6's two sites; there are now
four of the same shape. If the exclusion holds it needs a stronger statement of WHY,
because the correlation is no longer weak.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED, 2026-08-22. Blast radius is NO LONGER unmeasured; nothing blessed.

MECHANISM. NesRomLoader.labelVectorTargets now records the NMI and IRQ vector targets (never
RESET) in a new program-info property, DescriptorSupport.ASYNC_ENTRY_POINTS_PROPERTY ("Retro
Machines.Async Entry Points"), space-separated Address.toString() tokens. runDataflow reads it and
seeds those entries BankState.unknown() instead of fullyKnown(mask, initialState). Chose the
property over the label-name matching the bead body floats: the analyzer stays machine-independent
and merely consumes a loader-supplied fact, and no user renaming "NMI" can silently re-arm the
unsound seed. Unresolvable tokens are skipped, not raised -- degrading to pre-grm-913 behavior for
one entry must never cost a user their analysis.

THE EXCLUSION IN THE BEAD BODY HOLDS, and it is now settled EMPIRICALLY rather than by argument.
megaman d571 and wizwarr ffa6 are byte-identical between the A and B dumps: both already carry
"mechanism write with a genuinely undeterminable value" warnings at BASE (grm-p9y fixed them) and
still do at TIP. Weakening the seed changes neither.

AND THE 2026-08-15 PROMOTION COMMENT'S "TWO MORE SITES" ARE NOT TWO MORE SITES. megaman d56e and
wizwarr ffa4 are the SAME two sites as grm-ii6's d571/ffa6, re-described with their load
instruction included: d56e is "LDA $42", d570 "TAX", d571 the "STA $c000,X"; ffa4 is "LDA $00",
ffa6 the "STA $8000". So the correlation the comment called "no longer weak" was two sites counted
twice, not four. Neither dump contains an entry at d56e or ffa4 at all. The comment's demand to
re-examine the exclusion is discharged: it stands, for the reason the body gave.

MEASUREMENT (full A/B, both sides rebuilt+installed per realrom-ab-needs-rebuild, realrom-test.sh
check --all, dumps diffed against EACH OTHER). 14 of 31 rows moved; 17 byte-identical
(bionic contra db3 dbz2 dbz_datach dbz_saiyan dodge dragonpower drmario ironsword kicarus
lifeforce lwings megaman3 shenlong smb tetris).

  row        bankComments   warnings   claims weakened to "?"   new "requirement violated"
  blmaster      9 ->  9      32 -> 32            4                        0
  cv2           4 ->  4      23 -> 23            3                        0
  megaman2     75 -> 71      32 -> 36            0                        0
  rcproam      10 -> 10      22 -> 22            6                        0
  rcransom     38 -> 34       5 -> 23           11                       10
  smb2          4 ->  4       2 ->  9            3                        2
  smb3        104 -> 103     52 -> 52           19                        0
  tmnt         12 -> 12      28 -> 28            2                        0
  ultimaav      8 ->  8      17 -> 17            2                        0
  zelda        16 -> 16      13 -> 13            7                        0
  zelda2        6 ->  6      25 -> 25            2                        0
  ff1          75 -> 75      34 -> 34            0                        0   <- bistable, not ours
  megaman      161 -> 160    32 -> 32            0                        0   <- 12.1.3, not ours
  wizwarr      17 -> 17       7 ->  6            0                        0   <- 12.1.3, not ours

THE DOMINANT EFFECT IS CONFIDENCE WEAKENING, NOT CLAIM LOSS: ~59 bank comments keep their number
but gain "?" plus a per-bit "known: ... assumed from initial: ..." breakdown. Two rows lose whole
claims (rcransom 38->34, megaman2 75->71) and rcransom alone accounts for 10 of the 12 new
"Bank state requirement violated" warnings.

RCRANSOM IS THE EXPECTED EPICENTRE AND IS EVIDENCE THE CHANGE IS RIGHT. docs/human recon notes.txt
(grm-1fv) records that its ff07 is called immediately before the NMI handler returns and ff29
immediately before the IRQ handler returns, both restoring r6/r7 from shadows $fc/$fd -- textbook
interrupt-exit restores. The weakened claims are exactly the r6/r7 fields: "select=2,prg_mode=0,
r6=0,r7=1" becomes "...r6=0,r7=1? [known: select.*,prg_mode; assumed from initial: r6.*,r7.*]".
The old r6/r7 certainty came from the entry seed and nowhere else, which is precisely what this
bead says was unsound.

NOT YET DECIDED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT BLESSED. Whether each weakened claim is an HONEST loss (the
old confidence was fabricated by the seed) or a RECOVERABLE one (the bank really is knowable, by
propagating it through the interrupt boundary as grm-mej/grm-p9y contemplate) is a claim about a
real cartridge, per CLAUDE.md's "do not judge a row by a line whitelist". 10 rows and ~70 lines is
the class of work where a human with a disassembler is cheaper than an agent, so it is being put
to the owner rather than ground through. The code, the JUnit test and the nesnmitest fixture are
complete and the full synthetic gate is green either way.

NEW SYNTHETIC COVERAGE. nesnmitest.nes (mknesbanktest.py make_prg_nmi, criteria IRQ1/IRQ2/IRQ3 in
VerifyBankTest, nes-banking chunk) reproduces the idiom in miniature: a WRITE_THROUGH shadow $42
read back and re-committed inside the NMI/IRQ handler. VERIFIED TO FAIL WITHOUT THE FIX -- with
the seeding reverted it emits "bank -> 0 (bank=0)", the identical false claim wizwarr's ffa6
carried. IRQ1 is a control doing the same read-back on the RESET path, where the bank is known by
FLOW; it must and does keep resolving, so a change that weakened every entry fails the fixture.
Before this fixture no synthetic case exercised the seeding at all -- every other NES fixture
points NMI and IRQ at the same bare-RTI stub.

Also added: AEP1/AEP2/AEP3 criteria run on EVERY NES fixture, asserting the property exists and
names NMI/IRQ but not RESET. That guards the failure direction that reads as success -- if the
loader silently stopped writing the property, every seed would revert to the unsound state and no
other criterion would notice.

title: Write-through mirror read-back must prove shadow coherence: two confidently wrong banks at NMI restore stores (megaman d571, wizwarr ffa6)
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 by grm-ii6's answer (user disassembler pass, confirmed byte-exact against the
pinned ROMs). Read grm-ii6's ANSWERED comment for the full evidence; the essentials are below.

THE DEFECT. MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.mirroredByte (src/main/java/retromachines/
MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.java:294-312) answers a WRITE_THROUGH mirror load from tracked
in-state with no proof that the shadow cell is STILL COHERENT with the live bank. When a bank
switch writes the mechanism latch DIRECTLY, bypassing the shadow, the two diverge -- and every
later read of the shadow is answered with the wrong bank, confidently.

That bypassing switch is not an oddity. It is the standard interrupt-handler idiom: switch the
latch directly (leaving the shadow holding the pre-interrupt bank), do the work, then restore with
a bare 'LDA shadow / STA latch'. Both real-ROM instances are exactly that.

megaman (UxROM, NMI vector $D4A8 -- both addresses are inside the NMI handler):

  D54C: A9 04     LDA #$04
  D54E: 8D 04 C0  STA $C004    ; -> bank 4. Does NOT touch $42. ($C000 = 00 01 02 .. 07,
  D551: 20 00 90  JSR $9000    ;   the UNROM bus-conflict table, so $C004 reads back 04)
  D554..D56C                   ; loop, JSR $9003 -- NMI work, running in bank 4
  D56E: A5 42     LDA $42      ; shadow: still holds the INTERRUPTED bank
  D570: AA        TAX
  D571: 9D 00 C0  STA $C000,X  ; RESTORE          <-- WRONG: 'bank -> 4 (bank=4)'
  D574..D57F                   ; ... PLA / TAY / PLA -> RTI

wizwarr (AxROM, NMI vector $FF86):

  FF9A: A5 00     LDA $00
  FF9C: 29 18     AND #$18     ; masks the PRG bits away -> provably bank 0
  FF9E: 8D 00 80  STA $8000    ; -> bank 0. Does NOT store back to $00
  FFA1: 20 55 EE  JSR $EE55
  FFA4: A5 00     LDA $00      ; shadow: still holds the INTERRUPTED bank
  FFA6: 8D 00 80  STA $8000    ; RESTORE          <-- WRONG: 'bank -> 0 (bank=0)'
  FFA9: 68 AA 68 A8 68 40      ; PLA/TAX/PLA/TAY/PLA/RTI

The correct answer at both restore stores is UNKNOWN.

*** DO NOT BLESS megaman OR wizwarr UNTIL THIS LANDS. ***
Both rows FAIL on an unchanged tree because of these two lines and the counts they move
(megaman bankComments 156->157, wizwarr bankComments 17->18 / warnings 5->4). megaman
INDEPENDENTLY carries grm-g73 count-line jitter, so read the d571 line itself, never the count.

WHAT THIS IS NOT -- all three excluded on evidence, do not re-spend the tokens:
  * NOT a derivation bug. $42 and $00 genuinely ARE WRITE_THROUGH -- wizwarr's pairs are visible in
    FUN_ff69 at 'FF74 STA $00 / FF76 STA $8000' and 'FF7D STA $00 / FF7F STA $8000'.
    BankMirrors.Discovery is correct; do not re-tighten the typing rules or the SAVE_SLOT guard.
  * NOT the interrupt-entry seeding (that is real but separate, filed on its own bead).
  * NOT the $C5 / Rare PHA...PLA bracket that grm-ii6 originally suspected. wizwarr's shadow is
    $00, not $C5 ($C5 is ironsword's), and no stack save-restore is involved at ffa6.

THE HARD CONSTRAINT ANY FIX MUST MEET: wizwarr's 'ff9e bank -> 0' is CORRECT and 'ffa6 bank -> 0'
two instructions later is WRONG -- same value, same handler, same cell. The two cannot be told
apart by looking at the value. Only the coherence question separates them.

PROPOSED DESIGN (bounded backward walk; NO dataflow lattice change). Same idiom as the existing
BoardBankAnalyzer.restoresEntryBank and BankMirrors.Discovery.walkFromMechanismWrite scans:

  mirroredByte(target, inState):
    ROM_IDENTIFYING -> unchanged (a ROM byte cannot go stale)
    WRITE_THROUGH   -> if (!shadowCoherentAt(loadInstr, target)) return null;

  shadowCoherentAt(load, cell): bounded backward walk from the load
    hit 'ST<r> cell'                                        -> COHERENT
    hit a mechanism write NOT in writeThroughSites(cell)    -> STALE
    hit a call whose CallEffect ownedMask != 0              -> STALE
    reach the function entry                                -> COHERENT (the caller maintains it)
    budget exhausted, or ambiguous/unresolved predecessors  -> STALE (fail closed)

This needs BankMirrors to expose the per-cell write-through STORE SITES. Discovery.Cell already
collects them as cell.writeThroughStores (BankMirrors.java:309-319) -- they are simply not retained
on the built BankMirrors today.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVES, so they are not re-proposed as novel:
  * Withdraw WRITE_THROUGH from mirroredByte entirely (ROM_IDENTIFYING only). Cheapest and
    zero-risk, and both goldens return to committed values with no bless -- but it discards
    increment 2's write-through capability and forces its Tier-2 tests to be rewritten as
    decline-tests. Considered and passed over in favour of keeping the capability.
  * Per-cell coherence bit threaded through BoardBankAnalyzer's fixpoint lattice (set at
    write-through commits, cleared at bypassing mechanism writes, merged by AND). The most precise
    end state, but it changes the lattice, the StoredValueScanner.Hooks signature,
    effectDependsOnPriorState and MirrorProbe. Overkill for the two known instances; revisit only
    if the backward walk proves too imprecise.

ACCEPTANCE / REGRESSION CASES:
  * megaman d571 -> back to warning-only (bankComments returns to 156).
  * wizwarr ffa6 -> back to 'Bank state becomes unknown here' (bankComments 17, warnings 5).
  * wizwarr ff9e -> MUST KEEP 'bank -> 0 (bank=0)'. This is the discriminating case.
  * wizwarr FUN_ff69's own pairs at ff76 / ff7f -> must stay COHERENT and keep resolving.
  * Tier 2: a ProgramBuilder case per branch of shadowCoherentAt, alongside the existing
    BankMirrorConsumptionProgramTest cases.
  * Full gate plus a rebuilt real-ROM A/B (see the realrom-ab-needs-rebuild memory -- realrom-test
    .sh does NOT build, and skipping the rebuild fails silently in the direction you want).

SCORECARD, stated plainly: these two claims are increment 2's ENTIRE observable real-ROM output on
the WRITE_THROUGH half. That half is currently 0 for 2. grm-mej.2 must not close ahead of this.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
FIXED 2026-08-11 (commit 53059ed). The proposed design landed essentially as written.

WHAT SHIPPED
  BankMirrors.Cell gains pairedSwitchSites -- the mechanism writes whose own backward walk found
  this cell, i.e. the switches it is known to be kept in step with. Retained through build() and
  exposed as BankMirrors.pairedSwitchSites(Address). (This is also the plumbing grm-mej.4's naming
  pass wanted, so it is not single-use.)
  MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.shadowCoherentAt -- bounded backward walk from the load:
    store into the cell                         -> COHERENT
    mechanism write NOT in pairedSwitchSites    -> STALE   (the defect)
    a call                                      -> STALE
    join or non-fall-through predecessor        -> STALE
    containing function's entry, or no pred     -> COHERENT
    budget (64) exhausted                       -> STALE
  mirroredByte gates WRITE_THROUGH on it. ROM_IDENTIFYING is untouched -- a ROM byte cannot go
  stale.

ONE DEVIATION FROM THE PROPOSAL, deliberate: 'a call whose CallEffect ownedMask != 0 -> STALE'
became 'any call -> STALE'. The precise version needs the analyzer's call-effect map inside the
strategy, and it buys nothing measurable -- the write-through half resolves nothing else on any
real ROM, so there is no case the blunt rule costs. Recorded in the javadoc as available if the
walk ever proves too imprecise.

ALL THREE ACCEPTANCE CASES MET
  megaman d571  back to warning-only; bankComments returns to its committed 156.
  wizwarr ffa6  wrong bank gone; bankComments returns to its committed 17.
  wizwarr ff9e  KEEPS 'bank -> 0 (bank=0)'. The discriminating case.
  wizwarr FUN_ff69's own ff76/ff7f pairs: unaffected.
Full gate SUITE OK. 9 new Tier-2 cases in BankMirrorConsumptionProgramTest, one per branch --
including one driven off a REAL BankMirrors.Discovery rather than the BankMirrors.of test factory
(which returns empty paired sites), so a PAIRED switch site is proved still to resolve. That is
the case that shows the fix did not simply disable write-through consumption.

megaman IS now blessed: with this fix its only remaining diff was the new symbol lines from
grm-mej.4's dump extension. ironsword and wizwarr are still held -- not by this bug any more, but
by docs/human-research-todo.md's open FUN_ff69 question from grm-mej.3 increment 1.

SCORECARD UPDATE. The bead's 'the write-through half is 0 for 2' now reads: 0 for 0 -- both wrong
claims withdrawn, nothing wrongly asserted, and the capability retained for the coherent case that
nesmirrortest's M3 criterion and the new paired-site test both exercise. grm-mej.2 can close on
this.

title: Make banktest harness writes fail closed and atomic
description: From docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-09. Core shell drivers use set -u only and do not consistently check or atomically publish cache/golden/stamp writes.
acceptance_criteria: Injected write failures return nonzero and never claim success; interrupted writes cannot truncate final artifacts; intentional diff/probe nonzero paths still work.
close_reason: Landed afe399a. Added grm_atomic_publish / grm_atomic_publish_stdin (sibling temp, checked mv -f, temp cleaned on failure) and routed the harness write sites through them. Fail-closed where it matters: a failed golden write is now a row FAIL rather than a false BLESS, and a failed install-stamp write hard-fails rather than silently costing a reinstall every run. Cache writes soft-fail with a NOTE since build/ scratch is disposable.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: grm-aqi is implemented (ruled 2026-08-12), which lands the shared half of this bead: run-banktest.sh's golden writes now go through bless_candidate(), which fails closed on criteria failure and publishes atomically (sibling temp + mv, cleaned up on error). Remaining scope for grm-z34 is the OTHER harness write sites -- the candidate/.crit cache writes in run_one, and realrom-test.sh's golden and cache writes, none of which grm-aqi touched. Note realrom-test.sh has no criteria concept (no SUITE PASS/FAIL per row; its check is golden-diff plus the sha recheck), so the fail-closed half does not port there -- only atomicity does.

title: Close strategy vocabulary and address-range validation gaps
description: From docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-08. MapCompiler accepts unknown strategy spellings and fails to validate ordinary region/window/subregion geometry as rigorously as copied_from.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown strategies and invalid inverse/zero/negative/overflowed ranges fail with descriptor context; deferred strategy behavior is explicit; shipped descriptors pass.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Done in eae475e, both halves.

STRATEGY VOCABULARY. Hard-coded in MapCompiler as two sets: IMPLEMENTED_STRATEGIES
(register-write, memory-latch, select-data, serial-shift -- one concrete
BankSwitchStrategy each) and DEFERRED_STRATEGIES (io-port, mode-register). An
unknown spelling now fails the build naming both sets. The deferred names still
COMPILE, deliberately -- docs/SCHEMA.md:186-191 documents them as schema-valid
names with no analyzer support yet, so they are placeholders, not typos -- but
each emits a build-time NOTE to stderr saying the mechanism will be skipped at
analysis time. That is the "deferred strategy behavior is explicit" criterion.

RESIDUAL GAP, stated rather than papered over: nothing automatically links the
compiler's set to the actual implementations. MapCompiler is a separate,
non-Ghidra build with no ClassSearcher, which is the whole reason the vocabulary
is hard-coded. MapCompilerTest.strategyVocabularyMatchesImplementations narrows
it by instantiating all four classes and asserting each strategyName() is in the
set, plus a size-equality check -- so a class REMOVED without updating the
compiler, or a set entry with no class, both fail. What it still cannot catch is
someone adding a FIFTH strategy class and updating neither the compiler set nor
that test's hand-written list. The code comment on the sets says so.

GEOMETRY. validateRange (reversed / negative / past-the-address-space) now applies
to memory.regions[], memory.windows[] including layout windows, and occupant
subregions[]; copied_from keeps its own bespoke checks. end == start is legal (a
1-byte region), documented and covered by a positive test. Subregions additionally
must lie inside their parent window and must declare an extent, mirroring
DescriptorSupport.createIoSubregions' repeat_to > end > size precedence and its
hard error -- verified against that method rather than assumed, since getting the
precedence wrong would let a descriptor validate here and still fail to load.

The address bound is parsed from the Sleigh language ID's width field
(processor:endian:SIZE:variant) rather than assumed 16-bit, with a conservative
$FFFF fallback. Width is range-checked to 1..63 before shifting: Java masks long
shift distances to 6 bits, so a 64-bit language ID would have computed
(1L << 64) - 1 == 0 and rejected every address in the descriptor.

Tests: geometryErrors (6 sub-cases), unknownStrategyErrors, deferredStrategyCompiles,
strategyVocabularyMatchesImplementations, oneByteRegionCompiles.

No shipped descriptor tripped any new check -- all machines/*.yaml compiled
unchanged, confirming they were already well-formed under the newly-enforced
rules. Compiled output byte-identical (derived ends are validation-only, emit
orders unchanged), so no golden moved.

title: Replace BoardBankAnalyzer's count-only rerun fingerprint
description: From docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-07. The redundant-run cache keys only function and instruction counts, so same-count code/function edits can leave bank results stale.
acceptance_criteria: A same-count code or function-entry edit reruns and updates results; a sound unchanged fast path may remain; cancellation never records completion.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Done in bc8a1e4. RunStamp now holds Program.getModificationNumber() instead of the
count-only fingerprint; fingerprint()/reachedFixpoint() are untouched and still do
the separate structural entry/exit stability test, per the review's instruction.

TWO NON-OBVIOUS THINGS, both of which silently zero the cache's hit rate if got
wrong, and neither of which looks wrong in review:

1. The stamp must be read at run EXIT, not entry. Entry capture is right for the
   STRUCTURAL fingerprint -- there a run's own mutations should unmatch the next
   invocation and drive the fixpoint -- but this analyzer writes comments,
   bookmarks and references on every run, so an entry-captured modification number
   can never match on the next call. Cache sits at 0% forever, looking fine.

2. Same trap one level down: AnalyzerRunLog.markCompleted() writes an Options flag
   unconditionally, and Options fires a change event even setting true -> true,
   which itself advances the modification number. Called on every skip it keeps
   bumping the number the stored stamp is chasing, degrading the cache to
   hit/miss/hit/miss. Now gated on `verbose` (== isInitialRun) in both branches so
   it fires only on its one real transition, with the full-run branch snapshotting
   after it, not before.

The transaction question was settled empirically before building on it:
getModificationNumber() advances PER CHANGE, not per commit --
DomainObjectAdapter.fireEvent() increments unconditionally, before the
eventsEnabled gate, and ProgramDB.setChanged() calls it synchronously from every
mutating API. So an exit-time read already reflects the run's own writes
mid-transaction. Had it been commit-only the cache would have degraded to
never-hits, which is sound but pointless, and the review's fallback (drop the
cache) would have applied instead.

Real-ROM tier run --all: pass=28 fail=3, none of them ours. dodge matched its
documented jitter signature; wizwarr was byte-identical with and without the
change; megaman needed three runs to clear, one of which reproduced the no-change
baseline dump byte for byte (the row is multi-stable across refs, instrs AND
bankComments -- see the realrom-megaman-jitter-is-wider memory). wizwarr and
megaman are both off their blessed goldens on unmodified main; that is real and
pre-existing, filed as grm-9wl6 (P1). Nothing blessed.

title: Reject layout contracts that runtime would discard
description: From docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-05. MapCompiler accepts multi-key, mixed-field, and duplicate-value layout conditions that DescriptorSupport.planWindows logs and ignores at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid layout variants fail compilation with context; all compiled layouts are accepted at runtime; shipped descriptors and full gate pass.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Done in eae475e. buildLayouts now enforces all four planWindows rules at compile
time (exactly one when: field, same field across layouts, no duplicate value,
integral value) with the offending field/value in the message. The non-integral
case needed its own helper rather than reusing toInt(), because the runtime reads
these with JsonElement.getAsInt(), which truncates a fractional value silently --
so `when: { CR: 0.5 }` would otherwise have compiled clean and misbehaved at load.

Negative fixture test: MapCompilerTest.layoutWhenErrors, four sub-cases asserting
on message content. No shipped descriptor tripped any check; compiled output is
byte-identical (whenOut emit order unchanged), so no golden moved.

title: Make recovered transfer and decrypt identity address-space aware
description: From docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-04. COPY_<offset> and DECRYPTED_<offset> names/idempotence collide when different overlay spaces use the same CPU offset.
acceptance_criteria: Distinct overlay spaces at the same offset both materialize; rerunning the same recovery is idempotent; generated names are deterministic and legal.
notes: Priority review 2026-08-11: demoted P1->P2. Confirmed real (TransferMaterializer.java:143-144 keys idempotence on getBlock("COPY_"+offset), which matches across ALL spaces; C64DecryptLoopAnalyzer does the same with DECRYPTED_). But it is latent: it needs two overlay spaces with recoveries at the identical CPU offset, and no shipped fixture does that. Per the review's own rubric P1 means wrong results in a SUPPORTED path, so P2 fits. Note the fix touches a project-wide convention, not just a call site -- BoardBankAnalyzer.java:3056-3062 documents offset-in-name as deliberate.

title: rcransom f1d0/f21d: are FUN_ff07/FUN_ff29's select=6,prg_mode=0,r7=1 values real, or the same firstSite artifact as smb3's r7=7?
description:
HUMAN RESEARCH, filed 2026-08-09. Blocks landing grm-67g's soundness fix.

grm-67g's fix (held, uncommitted) turns these two rcransom bank comments into warnings:
    f1d0  bank -> select=6,prg_mode=0,r6=0,r7=1 via FUN_ff07   -> warning
    f21d  bank -> select=6,prg_mode=0,r6=0,r7=1 via FUN_ff29   -> warning
bankComments 40 -> 38, warnings 3 -> 5. Nothing else on the title moves.

THE QUESTION: were those two values ever right? They were produced by the SAME code path that
shipped smb3's confident wrong r7=7 -- MMC3 (select-data), value read at the helper's firstSite,
rendered 'via FUN_xxx'. If ff07/ff29 have the same two-write shape as smb3's ffc2 (an $8000
register-select write and an $8001 data write holding DIFFERENT values), then firstSite held the
select byte and these comments are artifacts, and the fix is removing garbage. If instead each
helper has a single data write, or its firstSite genuinely holds the bank, then the comments were
real and the fix costs two true recoveries.

WHAT TO LOOK AT (same shape as the smb3 trace that settled grm-bj6):
  - Disassemble FUN_ff07 and FUN_ff29. How many writes into $8000-$9fff does each contain, at what
    parity (even = select, odd = data), and what value reaches each?
  - Does either reload the bank from RAM (a shadow) the way smb3's ffc2 does with $0720?
  - At the call sites f1d0 and f21d, what is in A, and is there a 'LDA #bank ; STA <shadow>' before
    the call?
  - Sanity check on the reported value itself: 'select=6' with 'r7=1' is odd on its face -- select 6
    routes a data write to R6, so a comment naming r7 while selecting 6 deserves a second look
    regardless of how it was produced.

CONTEXT: grm-8iy.4 already records that rcransom has ZERO constant-arg call sites and that its real
PRG switching is FUN_ff07/FUN_ff29 with undeterminable writes at ff21/ff25/ff4b -- which leans
toward these two comments being artifacts, but is not itself evidence about f1d0/f21d.

REPRO: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --all --only rcransom H:/emulators/nes/roms
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ANSWERED BY HUMAN DISASSEMBLY 2026-08-09. VERDICT: BOTH COMMENTS WERE ARTIFACTS. The grm-67g fix
is correct to remove them -- rcransom is a SECOND correctness win, not collateral damage.

    ff07:  LDA #6 ; STA $8000 ; LDA $fc ; STA $8001    <- select R6, data from shadow $fc
           LDA #7 ; STA $8000 ; LDA $fd ; STA $8001    <- select R7, data from shadow $fd
           then  $8000 = ($ff != 0) ? $ff : $fb
    ff29:  same two register writes, bracketed by $ff bookkeeping, ending  LDA $fb ; STA $8000
    $fc = R6 shadow, $fd = R7 shadow, $ff and $fb = shadows of $8000 itself.
    ff07 is called immediately before the NMI handler returns; ff29 immediately before the IRQ
    handler returns. These are interrupt-exit RESTORE routines, not ordinary bank switches.

WHY THE OLD COMMENTS WERE WRONG, two separate ways:

  1. SELECT. Each helper contains FOUR-plus mechanism writes, and its LAST select write loads
     $8000 from a RAM shadow ($ff/$fb). So on return the select register holds a statically
     unknown value. The old 'select=6' is the state after the FIRST select write, not the helper's
     net effect -- precisely the firstSite-vs-switchSite defect grm-67g names, on a title where
     firstSite is not even the only select write.
  2. r6/r7. Both helpers demonstrably WRITE R6 and R7, from $fc and $fd. Their values are RAM and
     unknowable statically. Yet the golden lines carry NO '[known:...]/[assumed...]' bracket at
     all, i.e. every field is claimed FULLY KNOWN -- 'r6=0,r7=1'. Those numbers are stale in-state
     values that survived because the mis-anchored deposit owned only select+prg_mode and never
     poisoned r6/r7 across a helper that overwrites both. A confident stale bank is the same class
     of defect as smb3's confident wrong one.

So the honest answer at f1d0/f21d is a warning, which is what the fix produces.

STABLE UNDER THE PLANNED FOLLOW-UP, so this bless will not need redoing: the inbound-argument-cell
work (grm-mej) restores values that the CALLER writes to a cell just before the call. Here the
data comes from $fc/$fd, written elsewhere entirely, and the final select from $ff/$fb. Nothing
the caller does makes these knowable, so 'unknown' remains the right answer afterwards.

WORTH CARRYING FORWARD, beyond this bead: bank state across an INTERRUPT boundary is a real modeling
gap this exposes. A handler that restores the pre-interrupt banking on exit means the interrupted
code's bank state is preserved -- which is information the engine currently has no way to express,
and the opposite of what a naive read of these helpers ('they clobber everything') would conclude.
That belongs with grm-mej's shadow propagation, not here.

title: Shared shell library for the banktest scripts: one ext_identity, one settings-base derivation, one native()
description:
PROPOSED 2026-08-09 while investigating grm-3t8 (contra). The contra hunt was slowed by having to
prove that four near-duplicate copies of the same logic actually agreed. They mostly do -- but
nothing enforces it, and one of them is silently weaker.

THE DUPLICATION, measured:
  native()                 build-and-test.sh, run-banktest.sh, realrom-test.sh, measure-overlay-scale.sh
  SETTINGS_BASE derivation build-and-test.sh:205 DERIVES and INSTALLS; the other three CONSUME via
                           BANKTEST_SETTINGS_BASE with a build/ghidra-home fallback + NOTE warning
                           (realrom-test.sh:388-401, measure-overlay-scale.sh:59-71 -- near-verbatim)
  REPO_ROOT                build-and-test.sh:36  git rev-parse --show-toplevel
                           other three         cd $SCRIPT_DIR/../.. && pwd
  ext_identity()           run-banktest.sh:155  jars ONLY
                           realrom-test.sh:417  jars PLUS loose Extensions files
  GHIDRA_HEADLESS_JAVA_OPTIONS injection  three verbatim copies

THE ONE REAL DEFECT, and it is NOT what it looks like. run-banktest.sh's weaker ext_identity
CANNOT corrupt a check: EXT_ID feeds only *_cache_key(), the cache is READ solely under
[ "$MODE" = bless ] (realrom-test.sh:589), and the two scripts use SEPARATE cache dirs
(build/banktest-cache vs build/realrom-cache) so their keys never meet. It is a STALE-BLESS
hazard, bounded to run-banktest.sh's bless path.

Whether that hazard is live is a judgement, not a bug: run-banktest.sh's fixtures are SYNTHETIC and
its descriptors are pinned by the mk*.py generators, so loose-file drift may genuinely not reach
its dumps. realrom dumps DO depend on the installed compiled descriptor, which is why :427 added
the loose branch. The library should either unify on the strong version (cheap, strictly safer) or
keep two variants with an explicit comment saying why -- what must NOT persist is an UNDOCUMENTED
divergence that reads as an oversight.

REPO_ROOT: the two derivations agree here (scripts sit exactly two levels below the toplevel, both
emit forward-slash MSYS paths). Unify anyway -- 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' is the honest one
and fails loudly outside a repo.

title: Run argumentSurvivesPrologue per-register, not on argReg alone -- a clobber of an unread register suppresses contra's wrapper recoveries
description:
SPLIT OUT OF grm-2dr increment 2 (2026-08-09), deliberately not fixed there.

recoverCallArgument hands the strategy the call site's WHOLE register environment via
callSiteRegisters (BoardBankAnalyzer, the RegisterEnv built at the depositHelperArgument call),
so a strategy that can do better than the argReg convention -- memory-latch does, Contra's helper
takes its bank in Y while findHelpers can only see the STA's A -- can re-evaluate its own switch
site under the caller's registers.

THE GAP. argumentSurvivesPrologue is run for argReg ONLY. For a WRAPPER model (pass-through, from
grm-2dr increment 1, or call-edge, from increment 2) the wrapper's body sits between the caller and
the helper and may freely write X or Y -- nothing in either admission predicate forbids it.
isPassThroughInto admits any instruction with no flows, LDX #imm included. So the caller's X/Y are
handed over as though they reached the helper, when the wrapper may have overwritten them.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN INCREMENT 2. The exposure is NOT new to call-edge wrappers -- increment 1's
pass-through wrappers already carry it identically, and the 19-title corpus showed no wrong banks.
Forcing X/Y to unknown for wrapper models was considered and rejected for this increment: it changes
behavior on an axis nothing measured, and it can only DECREASE annotations, which increment 2's
acceptance criteria forbid. Deferring keeps one rule for both wrapper kinds.

THE FIX, when it is worth doing. argumentSurvivesPrologue already takes a segment list
(grm-2dr increment 2). Run it once per register over the same segments and pass through only the
survivors, leaving the rest BankState.unknown(). That is uniform across ordinary helpers, pass-through
wrappers and call-edge wrappers, and is strictly more precise than either current option.

HOW TO TELL IF IT MATTERS. The shape needed is a MEMORY-LATCH helper behind a wrapper whose body
writes X or Y. contra is the title to read: it is the corpus's memory-latch/index-register case.
If no such shape exists in the corpus this can be closed as unreachable rather than implemented.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on real ROMs. The bead's own hypothesis was wrong and is corrected in the comments: memory-latch overrides consumesHelperArgument() to false, so recoverCallArgument's argumentSurvivesPrologue gate is never reached and argReg plays no part. The real cause was that RegisterEnv.stopsAt is an exact address match tested BEFORE the control-flow-join refusal, while insideHelperEntry hands the WRAPPER's entry as the stop -- so a direct call's stop IS the join and wins the race, while a wrapper call's stop is further back and the join refusal kills the walk at the wrapped helper's entry. Shipped both parts: RegisterEnv.crossableJoin (one licensed join, derived as the entry of the function containing firstSite and admitted only when stop < nominee <= firstSite, so ordinary helpers and mid-body entries nominate nothing) and the bead's own prescribed per-register prologue filter on callSiteRegisters (which closes the call-edge wrapper soundness hole this bead was filed on). Rejected and documented: moving the stop instead of crossing the join. MEASURED: contra bankComments 2->5 (c094->1, c0a2->1, c21b->6), warnings 10->7, refs.intoOverlay 257->298, instrs.inOverlay 849->1044; plus two unanticipated titles of the same shape, wizwarr (15->17 comments via the AxROM wrapper FUN_ce89) and lifeforce (2->4 via FUN_e619). Three goldens blessed after reading the diffs; 22 others byte-identical; zero annotations lost anywhere, which retires grm-2dr increment 2's deferral premise on measurement. smb3 still fails on grm-evn alone (proven pre-existing, deliberately not blessed). Full gate green.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
THIS BEAD'S OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER INVERTS IT (contra def-use pass by hand,
2026-08-09; full table on grm-hum).

The bead asks: "The shape needed is a MEMORY-LATCH helper behind a wrapper whose body writes X or
Y. contra is the title to read... If no such shape exists in the corpus this can be closed as
unreachable."

READ. The shape does NOT exist in the direction feared, and the shape that DOES exist is the
opposite defect -- so this bead should be RETITLED and PROMOTED, not closed.

CONTRA'S WRAPPERS, from the ROM:
  c139  LDA $8000 / STA $07ec  -> falls through into c13f    ; writes A. Y UNTOUCHED.
  c146  LDY $07ec / JMP $c13f                                ; writes Y, but from a shadow --
                                                             ; the value is unknown anyway
  c14c  save A+Y / STA $07ed / LDY #1 / JSR $c13f / restore  ; writes Y, but to a CONSTANT 1,
                                                             ; and its site c157 already resolves
                                                             ; to bank 1 -- the right answer
No wrapper in contra hands a caller's stale X/Y to a mechanism that would then ship a wrong bank.
The soundness exposure this bead was filed on is, on the corpus, unreachable.

THE REAL DEFECT IS THE MIRROR IMAGE: a wrapper that PRESERVES the argument register still loses
the argument. c094, c0a2 and c21b are LDY #1 / LDY #1 / LDY #6 followed by JSR $c139, and all
three WARN today -- while c0cb and c157, the identical LDY #imm idiom calling c13f DIRECTLY,
both resolve and are the golden's only two bank comments. c139 preserves Y; the engine drops it
anyway.

MECHANISM (hypothesis from reading BoardBankAnalyzer, not yet verified by a run -- verify before
implementing). argReg is 'A', the STA's store register (:1714), because findHelpers can only see
STA $ffd0,Y. memory-latch is supposed to recover contra by re-evaluating its own switch site under
callSiteRegisters, which sees Y. But recoverCallArgument (:1748) gates the whole path on
argumentSurvivesPrologue(..., reg) with reg = argReg = 'A', and c139's prologue is LDA $8000 --
A is dead across it. So the survival test is run on the NOMINAL argument register rather than on
the registers the strategy will actually read, and a clobber of a register nobody reads suppresses
a recovery that would have been correct. Note :1727 already asserts "memory-latch's Contra helper
is a prologue-clobber case that must keep resolving" -- that claim holds for the direct helper and
appears to fail one level up, at the wrapper.

THIS BEAD'S OWN PROPOSED FIX IS THE FIX. "Run argumentSurvivesPrologue once per register over the
same segments and pass through only the survivors, leaving the rest BankState.unknown()" gives
A=dead / Y=alive at c139, memory-latch re-evaluates STA $ffd0,Y with the caller's Y, and the three
sites resolve. It is strictly more precise in BOTH directions -- it closes the X/Y soundness hole
this bead was filed on AND recovers contra.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ACCEPTANCE. The original deferral reasoning was "it can only DECREASE annotations,
which increment 2's acceptance criteria forbid." That premise is now false: on contra it INCREASES
them by 3 (c094 -> bank 1, c0a2 -> bank 1, c21b -> bank 6), and expect refs.intoOverlay to move
with them. Re-check the deferral.

Contra's other four unrecovered call sites will NOT move under this fix and should not be expected
to: c9c0 is a five-valued ROM table, and c0d3/c149/c164 are shadow/read-back restores (grm-mej).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED (2026-08-09). The bead's hypothesized mechanism was WRONG; the real one is recorded
below and in the code. Full gate green (`build-and-test.sh check`, SUITE OK) with EVERY golden
byte-identical -- but the contra recovery itself is NOT yet verified end-to-end, because the
real-ROM tier needs user-supplied ROMs. See OUTSTANDING at the bottom.

WHY THE FILED HYPOTHESIS IS WRONG. The comment of 2026-08-09 22:41 blamed recoverCallArgument
gating on argumentSurvivesPrologue(..., reg = argReg = 'A') at :1748/:1764. That gate is never
reached for contra: it is conditioned on strategy().consumesHelperArgument(), which
MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy overrides to FALSE (:360) precisely so the mini-inline is exempt
from it. The gate is skipped entirely and argReg plays no part in the failure.

THE REAL MECHANISM, from the code (no run needed to establish it; the golden supplies the rest):
RegisterEnv.stopsAt is an EXACT address equality, and StoredValueScanner tests it BEFORE the
control-flow-join refusal (:226 vs :243 -- the ordering is deliberate and commented). Meanwhile
insideHelperEntry (:2118) hands the WRAPPER's entry, c139, as the scan's stop for a
pass-through wrapper. So:
  - c0cb / c157 (direct JSR $c13f): stop == c13f. The scan reaches c13f, stopsAt fires first,
    the caller's Y is adopted. RESOLVES -- the golden's only two bank comments.
  - c094 / c0a2 / c21b / c9c0 (JSR $c139): stop == c139, two instructions further back. The scan
    reaches c13f, stopsAt does NOT fire, isControlFlowJoin runs -- and c13f IS a join, because
    the five direct callers JSR straight to it -- so the walk returns unknown and never gets
    near the env at all. WARNS.
The bead's own diagnosis that "c139 preserves Y; the engine drops it anyway" is exactly right;
the reason is the join, not argReg.

THE FIX, two parts, both landed.
1. SOUNDNESS (this bead's original filing). callSiteRegisters now filters the env PER REGISTER:
   each of A/X/Y passes through only where argumentSurvivesPrologue holds for THAT register over
   prologueSegments, unknown otherwise. This is the bead's own prescribed fix and it closes the
   real hole -- a CALL-EDGE wrapper, where the scan stops at relay.calleeEntry() and the
   wrapper's prefix is never walked, so an unfiltered env hands over registers the wrapper may
   already have overwritten. On contra it gives A=dead / Y=alive, as predicted.
2. PRECISION (what actually recovers contra). RegisterEnv gains `crossableJoin`: ONE join the
   scan may walk through, honored in all three StoredValueScanner backward walks and suppressing
   ONLY the join refusal (linkage, mechanism-write abort and MAX_BACKWARD_SCAN still apply).
   Crossing is sound by exactly the argument the entry stop already rests on: the query is
   context-sensitive to one call site, and on the path that call took (c094 -> c139 -> c13c ->
   c13f) c13c genuinely IS c13f's predecessor; the span between stop and join is one
   isPassThroughInto has already proved straight-line, disassembled, inert and unconditional.
   The nominee is derived (BoardBankAnalyzer.crossableWrapperJoin), not stored: it is the entry
   of the function containing firstSite, admitted only when stop < nominee <= firstSite. That
   window makes an ordinary helper and a MID-BODY ENTRY nominate nothing -- which is why the
   whole gate stayed byte-identical.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, recorded in the javadoc: simply MOVING the stop to the wrapped helper's
entry. Smaller, and wrong -- the scan would then adopt part 1's filtered values and discard
whatever the wrapper's own body supplies, so an `LDY #3 / fall-through-into-helper` wrapper
would report Y unknown where today's scan reads the LDY directly. Crossing keeps the walk going
through the prefix, so the wrapper's writes and loads are read natively.

Note part 1 is redundant-but-harmless for pass-through wrappers once part 2 lands (the scan
walks the prefix and meets any clobber itself) and load-bearing for call-edge wrappers.

TESTS. MemoryLatchStrategyProgramTest: helperMiniInlineCrossesTheWrapperSplitJoin (contra's real
geometry behind FUN_c139, with a direct JSR laid in so c13f is a GENUINE join -- without it the
test would pass for the wrong reason), helperMiniInlineWithoutTheLicensedJoinStaysUnknown (the
mechanism pin: same fixture, no licence, must not resolve), and
wrapperClobberOfAnUnreadRegisterDoesNotSuppressTheRecovery. HelperWrapperProgramTest: the four
window cases -- pass-through wrapper nominated, ordinary helper not, mid-body entry not (the
non-regression that matters most), firstSite outside any function not.

OUTSTANDING -- HUMAN/ROM-SIDE. The real-ROM tier cannot run here (no ROM dir; GRM_ROM_DIR unset).
The prediction to check with
  bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check <romdir>
is: contra c094 -> bank 1, c0a2 -> bank 1, c21b -> bank 6, bankComments 2 -> 5, warnings 10 -> 7,
refs.intoOverlay up. c0d3/c149/c164 (shadow restores, grm-mej) and c9c0 (five-valued ROM table)
must NOT move. All 30 other titles are expected byte-identical; any that move needs reading
before blessing.

title: smb3 realrom golden is CORRECT; 788f09b regressed ca23/ca2e to r7=7 (blocked on grm-67g)
description:

  count instrs.inOverlay   4263 -> 4173
  count bankComments       104  -> 105

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ANSWERED BY HUMAN DISASSEMBLY 2026-08-09. VERDICT: REGRESSION. DO NOT BLESS smb3.

The bead asked whether ca23/ca2e moving from r7=27/26 to r7=7 is a genuine improvement or the
helper argument being taken from the wrong site. It is the WRONG SITE, and the proof is arithmetic.

THE HELPERS (human trace):
  ffc2:  LDA #$47 ; STA $0721 ; STA $8000 ; LDA $0720 ; STA $8001      -- sets R7 ($A000 window)
  ffd1:  LDA #$46 ; STA $0721 ; STA $8000 ; LDA $071F ; STA $8001      -- sets R6
  ffbf:  JSR $ffd1 then FALLS THROUGH into ffc2                        -- sets both R6 and R7
MMC3 is a TWO-WRITE protocol: $8000 takes the register-SELECT byte, $8001 takes the BANK byte.
Both writes live inside the one helper.

THE ARITHMETIC. Decoding the dump's own 'known:' bit fields:
  ca23 OLD  r7.5..r7.0 = 011011 = 27 = $1B
  ca2e OLD  r7.5..r7.0 = 011010 = 26 = $1A
  ca23 NEW  r7.5..r7.0 = 000111 = 7  = $07   <-- and ca2e NEW is byte-identical to it
  $47 & $3F = $07
So the new value is EXACTLY the low six bits of the LDA #$47 register-select constant -- the byte
bound for $8000 -- mis-attributed to the R7 bank field written at $8001.

THREE INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATIONS that 7 is the artifact and 27/26 were correct:
  1. BOTH call sites collapse to the SAME value. Two distinct callers yielding one number is the
     signature of a value sourced from the helper's own constant, not from the call site.
  2. The direct sites are a built-in control. c5f5/c9f7 are LDA #$47 ; STA $8000 ; LDA #$1a ;
     STA $8001 -- forcing bank $1A with no shadow update -- and the golden already reports
     c5fc/c9fe r7=26? = $1A. So $1A is a bank this game demonstrably uses, corroborating ca2e's
     old 26. The value 7 corresponds to no call-site constant anywhere in the trace.
  3. The pre-788f09b recovery had a correct MECHANISM. The bank reaches ffc2 through RAM shadow
     $0720, via the idiom 'LDA #bank ; STA $0720 ; JSR $ffc2'. That is exactly grm-mu7's
     argumentCells/argumentReloadSource save-restore model, and it was working. 788f09b's wrapper
     re-keying broke it.

COUNT MOVEMENT CORROBORATES rather than complicates: a wrong bank retargets into a wrong or absent
overlay, so refs.intoOverlay 846->822 and instrs.inOverlay 4263->4173. A 90-instruction LOSS is
what a wrong bank looks like; a fix would not shed instructions. c631 GAINING 'r7=7? via FUN_ffc2'
is the same defect at a third site, and f894 losing its bankcomment is downstream of it.

BANK SHADOW MAP, for grm-hb6/grm-mej and the per-game tier:
  $0721  shadow of the $8000 select/mode byte
  $0720  shadow of R7's bank value
  $071F  shadow of R6's bank value
  The IRQ handler rewrites $8000 from $0721 on exit, after manipulating it for CHR banking.
  HAZARD: c5f5/c9f7 write $8000/$8001 directly and do NOT update the shadows, so the shadows can
  legitimately desync from the hardware. Any model that trusts the shadow must survive that.
  PRG MODE 1 CONFIRMED -- $8000 bit 6 set at every observed write, so R6 drives $C000 and $8000
  is the fixed window. The dump's W8000_M1 / WC000_M1_B0 block names agree, so the descriptor is
  already right about this.
  Call frequency: many calls to ffc2, only 2 (plus ffbf) to ffd1 -- R7 switches far more than R6.
  All disassembled direct writes to $8000 are accounted for by the above.

STILL UNEXPLAINED, and NOT covered by this trace: the new warnings at 867b and ac6d name FUN_c542,
a helper neither the golden nor this trace knows. Tracking separately -- do not fold it in.

ACCEPTANCE UPDATE: the 'determine whether the new values are right' half is DONE (they are not).
This bead now blocks on the fix, not on a human. smb3 stays unblessed and its golden stays the
correct baseline.

title: Copy-loop SOURCE bytes are never disassembled: three RAM-resident bank-switch routines invisible (wizwarr ce38/ce4b/ce5b)
description:
Found by hand during the wizwarr def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-06). Three bank-switch
routines exist in ROM, are never disassembled, and between them carry two constant non-home
banks on a title that resolves ZERO instructions into overlay space.

THE SITUATION. FUN_cdaf initialises RAM and copies a number of blocks from the ceXX region to
03xx, after which the game calls them at their RAM addresses. CopyLoopAnalyzer NOTICES these
loops and declines them for lack of jump refs. Three of the copied blocks are code and ALL THREE
WRITE THE AxROM REGISTER AT $8000:

  ce38 -> 033d   LDA $00; PHA; AND #$F8; ORA #2; STA $8000; LDA ($9D),Y; TAY; PLA; STA $8000; RTS
                 A far read: switch to BANK 2 (constant), fetch one byte through ($9D),Y,
                 restore the previous register byte.

  ce4b -> 032d   STA $8000; <send PPU data>; ...; STX $8000 with X=0; RTS
                 Switch to A, do PPU work, return to bank 0.

  ce5b -> 0300   STA $00; STA $8000; <send PPU data>; LDA #3; STA $00; STA $8000; RTS
                 Switch to A, do PPU work, EXIT ON BANK 3 (constant) -- it does not restore.

  The other copied blocks appear to be data.

WHAT IS DIFFERENT FROM grm-azv (DB3). Both titles execute bank-switch code from RAM. But DB3's
problem is that the stub's behaviour is unknown; here THE ROM IMAGES ARE PRESENT AND READABLE at
ce38/ce4b/ce5b, and hand-reading them took minutes. Nothing seeds disassembly at those addresses
because their only inbound "reference" is a copy loop that was declined. This is a SEEDING gap,
not a materialisation gap, and it does NOT need the grm-1.7 self-modifying-code epic or a bounded
copy loop -- the bytes can simply be disassembled where they sit.

TWO ROUTES:
  (a) DISASSEMBLE IN PLACE. Treat the SOURCE of a recognised copy-shaped loop as a code seed when
      its bytes decode plausibly. Cheapest, and enough to recover the bank values, but the
      resulting listing is at ROM addresses while the code actually executes from RAM, so
      references computed inside it will be wrong.
  (b) MATERIALISE THE TRANSFER properly (RunFromElsewhere / TransferMaterializer, grm-1.7 and
      grm-7pp) so the code appears at its RAM addresses with correct references. The right answer,
      and much more work.
  For the BANKING result specifically, (a) suffices: the two constants (bank 2 at ce38, bank 3 at
  ce5b) are visible in the ROM bytes regardless of where the code runs.

NOTE THE DECLINE REASON IS ITSELF WORTH A LOOK: "lack of jump refs". These blocks are called at
their RAM addresses, so the refs exist -- they just point at 03xx, not at ceXX, and nothing
connects the two. If the copy loop were bounded, the destination-to-source correspondence would
supply exactly that link. Overlaps with grm-7pp (db3's three copy loops recognised but unbounded).

WHY IT MATTERS HERE MORE THAN ELSEWHERE: wizwarr is AxROM, so its single window covers all of
8000-ffff and ONE recovered non-home value cascades across the whole address space. Two constants
are sitting in unread ROM bytes.

ACCEPTANCE: ce38, ce4b and ce5b are disassembled as code, their $8000 writes are recognised as
mechanism writes, and banks 2 and 3 become known non-home banks on wizwarr.

title: Entry point interior to another instruction: the 6502 BIT-skip idiom hides a bank call site (wizwarr bc08)
description:
Found by hand during the wizwarr def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-06). Hides a bank-switch call
site carrying a non-home constant on a title that resolves ZERO instructions into overlay space.

THE IDIOM. The 6502 "BIT skip" (also skip2 / skipword): a BIT with an absolute operand whose two
operand bytes are themselves a valid instruction. Entering at the BIT consumes those bytes as
data; entering two bytes later executes them as code. Two entry points, one shared tail.

    bc05:  LDA #2
           BIT $03A9         ; assembles as 2C A9 03
           JMP $FF69
    bc08:   LDA #3           ; <-- the A9 03 operand bytes of the BIT above
           JMP $FF69

WHAT GOES WRONG. bc05 is disassembled first, so bc08's bytes are already claimed as BIT's
operand. Ghidra cannot create a function -- or an instruction -- at bc08, because the address is
interior to an existing instruction. The LDA #3 call site into FUN_ff69 (wizwarr's far-call bank
helper) therefore does not exist in the program, and bank 3 is never seen.

On AxROM this is expensive out of proportion to its size: the single window covers all of
8000-ffff, so ONE recovered non-home value cascades across the whole address space.

SAME CLASS AS grm-o59, which records nesuxhelpertest's NMI/IRQ vectors pointing into the middle
of an instruction. That bead sits at P4 with only a synthetic fixture. This is the same
underlying problem -- a real entry point interior to an already-disassembled instruction -- with
a real-ROM instance and a measurable cost. Consider merging, or at least re-rating grm-o59 in
light of it.

WHY IT IS HARD, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A REASON TO IGNORE IT. Ghidra's disassembly is
single-stream: an address belongs to at most one instruction. Genuinely overlapping streams need
either a second interpretation at that address, or a decision about which stream wins. Options,
none costless:

  (a) SEED FROM THE CALL REFERENCE. If some site references bc08 (a JSR/JMP target, a vector, a
      jump-table entry), that reference is evidence an instruction starts there. Clearing the
      containing instruction and re-disassembling from the referenced address resolves it in
      favour of the referenced stream -- but it destroys the other one, which is equally real.
  (b) RECOGNISE THE IDIOM SPECIFICALLY. A BIT (or LDA/CMP) absolute whose operand bytes decode
      to a valid instruction ending in a shared tail is a narrow, checkable pattern. Narrow
      enough to be safe, and it covers the overwhelming majority of real occurrences.
  (c) DO NOTHING IN THE DISASSEMBLY, but let the BANK ANALYZER read the hidden bytes directly
      when a reference points into an instruction interior. Least invasive, purely local to our
      analyzer, and sufficient to recover the bank value even though the listing stays wrong.

  (c) is probably the cheapest route to the banking result and does not require touching
  Ghidra's disassembler. (b) is the better user-facing fix. Decide which problem is being
  solved before building either.

FIRST: MEASURE INCIDENCE. Scan the GME set for BIT/LDA/CMP absolute instructions whose operand
bytes decode to a plausible instruction AND which are the target of any reference. If wizwarr is
alone, take (c) and move on; if the idiom is common, (b) earns its cost.

ACCEPTANCE: wizwarr's bc08 site is recognised as a call into FUN_ff69 with a constant argument
of 3, and bank 3 becomes a known non-home bank.
acceptance_criteria:
The 6502 skip idiom is recognised and repaired by a shipped script: the hidden entry becomes an instruction and a function, references to it resolve, and the VISIBLE stream through the carrier is unchanged (it still falls through to the shared tail, not into the exposed bytes). Tiered so an uncorroborated carrier is reported and not applied. Pinned by a synthetic fixture with one site per tier, and measured on the real wizwarr ROM (7 carriers, all repaired; bc08 becomes LDA #$03 as FUN_bc08 with nine dangling call refs resolving to it).

REVISED 2026-08-16 by user ruling. The original second half -- "and bank 3 becomes a known non-home bank" -- moved to grm-v60, where the remaining work lives: the recovered bank is live only for FUN_ff69's inner call, so what bc08 unlocks is PLACEMENT of that callee into bank 3's overlay, not state propagation to the caller. See this bead's 2026-08-16 comments for the trace.
