comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
USER RULING 2026-08-15 -- SCOPE SET: adapt Ghidra's EXISTING offcut-fixup script to our purposes
and ship it as a script with the extension. Not a core change, not an upstream PR, not overlay
machinery. A ghidra_scripts/ deliverable.

*** THE FRAMING IN THIS BEAD NEEDS CORRECTING: Ghidra ALREADY HANDLES THIS CASE. *** Researched
2026-08-15 against D:/git/ghidra @ Ghidra_12.1.2_build. It was assumed Ghidra models overlapping
instructions poorly. It does not -- it models them deliberately, with maintained machinery, and
x86 is the flagship case. What is missing is only the TRIGGER.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS UPSTREAM (all verified at the tag):
  Instruction.setLengthOverride(int)         Instruction.java:232-246, cap MAX_LENGTH_OVERRIDE=7
      SHRINKS an instruction's code-unit footprint without changing its parse (getParsedLength()
      still reports the true bytes), freeing the tail bytes to be disassembled separately. This
      is exactly the primitive the BIT-skip needs, and our case needs only 2 of the 7 bytes.
  InstructionErrorType.OFFCUT_INSTRUCTION    InstructionError.java:64-72, isOffcutError() :167-169
      A named conflict class, distinct from plain INSTRUCTION_CONFLICT.
  SetLengthOverrideAction                    the "Modify Instruction Length..." GUI action;
      truncates, re-disassembles at the freed address, clears the stale error bookmark.
  FixOffcutInstructionScript.java            Ghidra/Features/Base/ghidra_scripts/ -- ***THE ONE
      TO ADAPT.*** Scans for a flow reference landing offcut inside an instruction
      (getQualifiedOffcutAddress :99-131), validates the offcut construction with
      PseudoDisassembler (canDisassembleAt :168-182), then setLengthOverride + disassemble +
      swaps the ERROR bookmark for INFO (fixOffcutInstruction/fixBookmark :133-166).
  Its own doc comment names the applicable cases: "polyglot instruction executable size
  optimizations, LOCK prefix issues, and offcut code used for code obfuscation." The help text
  (DisassemblerPlugin/Disassembly.htm:285-335) describes the x86 LOCK-prefix skip in terms that
  fit the 6502 BIT-skip exactly. Test fixture: FixOffcutInstructionScriptTest.java:65-77.

*** THE GAP, AND IT IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM: the upstream script requires a flow reference to
ALREADY LAND at the offcut address before it will act *** (isOffcutFlowReference,
SetLengthOverrideAction.java:158-165; the reference scan at FixOffcutInstructionScript.java
:109-129). At wizwarr bc08 no such reference exists -- that IS the bug. So the tool that would
repair it is gated on the very thing the bug prevents. Chicken-and-egg.

WHAT OUR SCRIPT MUST THEREFORE ADD: seed the reference itself from a PATTERN MATCH rather than
waiting for one. Detect an absolute-operand instruction (BIT is the canonical 6502 carrier; also
consider LDA/CMP absolute) whose two operand bytes decode to a plausible instruction, validate
with PseudoDisassembler exactly as canDisassembleAt does, then drive the same
setLengthOverride + DisassembleCommand + bookmark-swap sequence. Net-new LOGIC (the 6502 pattern
match); ZERO net-new Ghidra machinery.

RELATED DEFECT ON OUR SIDE, worth fixing in the same pass or filing separately:
BoardBankAnalyzer.addOverlayRef (:3879-3887) guards on getInstructionAt(addr) == null before
firing DisassembleCommand. getInstructionAt matches only instruction START addresses, so that
guard is TRUE at an offcut address -- we already attempt disassembly at interior addresses. Per
CodeManager.checkInstructionSet (:330-394) and addInstructions (:489-499) that attempt FAILS
SILENTLY: the block is truncated before the conflicting unit is added, nothing is thrown,
DisassembleCommand just returns fewer addresses, and the only trace is an ERROR bookmark
("Failed to disassemble at X due to conflicting instruction at Y", InstructionBlock.java
:260-277). We do not check for that today.

DELIBERATELY NOT DOING (recorded so it is not re-litigated):
  - Sleigh-level modelling. Wrong layer -- overlap is a property of the instruction stream, not
    of decode; no sleigh construct expresses it on any architecture.
  - Overlay space per entry point. NO upstream precedent -- core Ghidra overlays always mean
    genuinely different memory contents, never two readings of one byte range. Net-new machinery
    for no gain when a 2-byte length override does the job.
  - An upstream PR. Still plausible LATER as a generalization of FixOffcutInstructionScript that
    seeds its own reference (it would serve the x86/68000/ARM analogues equally, since none of
    this is architecture-specific), but the user's call is to ship a script first.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-16 against the real Wizards & Warriors (U) ROM (sha 463018ac..., the pinned
'wizwarr' GME row), headless, with a first cut of ghidra_scripts/FixSkipInstructions.java.

INCIDENCE IN WIZWARR: 7 carriers, all BIT abs, ALL of them real.
  822d hides 822e LDA [REFERENCED]      d4f1 hides d4f2 INC [REFERENCED]
  9225 hides 9226 LDA [REFERENCED]      d511 hides d512 INC [REFERENCED]
  bc07 hides bc08 LDA [REFERENCED]      e543 hides e544 LDA [REFERENCED]
  cf0f hides cf10 LDY [STRONG]
Zero WEAK candidates -- i.e. on this ROM the structural test alone (operand bytes decode to an
instruction that ends exactly where the carrier ends, and the next byte is already code) produced
no uncorroborated hits at all. Precision is better than the bead feared.

*** THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS WRONG ON ONE POINT, AND IT MATTERS: A REFERENCE DOES LAND AT bc08. ***
Six of the seven are REFERENCED -- something already flows there. bc08 alone has NINE incoming
UNCONDITIONAL_CALLs (8857, e90a, c94d, c952, c957, c95c, c966, c96b, e7c2). They were references
to an address holding no instruction, which is the bug at its purest, but it means the
chicken-and-egg framing in the 2026-08-15 ruling is not quite the situation: upstream's
FixOffcutInstructionScript is gated not on "a reference" but on a reference whose type
isJump() && hasFallthrough(), and a 6502 JSR is neither. The pattern match still earns its keep
(cf0f has no reference at all), but the honest description of the gap is upstream's REFERENCE
TYPE FILTER, not the absence of a reference.

THE REPAIR ITSELF WORKS. After the script: bc07 is BIT len=1 parsed=3 OVERRIDDEN, bc08 is
LDA #0x3 as FUN_bc08 with all nine calls resolving to it. No failures on any of the seven.

*** A DEFECT IN UPSTREAM'S SEQUENCE, FOUND BY MEASURING: TRUNCATION SILENTLY CORRUPTS THE
VISIBLE STREAM. *** A length-overridden instruction falls through to the address after its
OVERRIDDEN length. For an x86 LOCK prefix that is correct -- the prefix really is followed by
the instruction it modifies. For a skip carrier it is exactly wrong: entering at bc07 consumes
all three PARSED bytes, so bc07's true fallthrough is bc0a. Measured on the first cut:
FUN_bc05's body went from [bc05,bc07][bc09,bc0c] to [bc05,bc07], with "bc08 <-bc07:FALL_THROUGH"
-- i.e. the LDA #$02 path now appeared to execute LDA #$03 and then JMP $FF69. That is a WRONG
BANK asserted at a REAL call site, strictly worse than the missing one we started with.
Fixed by also calling Instruction.setFallThrough(tail) on the carrier (option fallthrough:,
default true). Both readings are then correct at once, which is as close as a single-stream
disassembler gets to two entry points. Anyone adapting FixOffcutInstructionScript for a
skip idiom on any architecture needs this; upstream does not do it.

*** THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERION CANNOT BE MET BY THE SCRIPT, AND NOT BECAUSE OF THE
SCRIPT. *** "bank 3 becomes a known non-home bank" does not happen, and the RealRomDump for
wizwarr is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after the repair. The reason is FUN_ff69 itself, which is
not the "far call with the bank in A" the bead assumes:

    ff69  STY $1b        ; target vector low, into ZP
    ff6b  STA $1d        ; *** the caller's bank argument goes to RAM ***
    ff6d  LDA $00        ; the bank SHADOW in ZP $00
    ff6f  PHA
    ff70  AND #$18       ; keep the bits this call does not set
    ff72  ORA $1d        ; *** and read the argument back out of RAM ***
    ff74  STA $00        ; update the shadow
    ff76  STA $8000      ; the AxROM latch  <- warns: no tracked bank bit pinned
    ff79  JSR $ff83      ; JMP ($1b) -- call the far routine
    ff7c  PLA / STA $00 / STA $8000 / RTS   ; restore the previous bank

The bank value passes THROUGH ZERO-PAGE RAM ($1d) and is merged with a RAM-held shadow ($00).
So this is grm-mej (bank-state read-back and shadow propagation), and it is the whole barrier:
even with bc08's LDA #$03 fully visible and its nine call sites resolving, the value is lost at
the STA $1d / ORA $1d round trip. Both ff76 and ff7f already carry the "genuinely undeterminable
value" warning, and they still do afterwards. Note this equally blocks the ALREADY-VISIBLE
bc05 (LDA #$02) site -- so wizwarr's zero-instructions-into-overlay result was never bc08's
fault alone, and grm-8iy.5's read of this title should be updated accordingly.

WHAT THIS BEAD CAN HONESTLY DELIVER, then: the script, the repair, and the nine recovered call
references -- with the bank recovery itself blocked on grm-mej. Retarget the acceptance
criterion accordingly rather than leaving one that cannot pass.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the comment above, same session: THE "TRUNCATION CORRUPTS THE VISIBLE STREAM"
DEFECT DOES NOT EXIST. Ghidra already gets this right, and the paragraph claiming otherwise was
reasoning from the API contract instead of from the listing.

What I got wrong: I read "a length-overridden instruction falls through to the address after its
OVERRIDDEN length" off setLengthOverride's contract. It does not.
InstructionDB.getDefaultFallThroughOffset (:940-943) returns proto.getLength() -- the PARSED
length -- so getDefaultFallThrough is unaffected by the override, and setLengthOverride ->
addLengthOverrideFallthroughRef (:897-906) even materializes it as an explicit FALL_THROUGH
reference. Confirmed in the listing both times: after the repair bc07's fallthrough is bc0a, the
shared tail, NOT bc08. The before/after runs were byte-identical in this region, which is what
sent me back to the source.

Instruction.setFallThrough(tail) is therefore not needed and would be actively misleading:
setFallThrough compares against the default and clears the override when they match
(InstructionDB.java:793-797), so the call is a no-op that hides where the behaviour comes from.
Reverted; the script now carries the mechanism as a comment plus a standing runtime check that
the carrier's fallthrough really did land on the tail, so a future regression in Ghidra would be
reported rather than silently corrupting the visible stream.

The one real body-level effect, worth knowing but not a defect: Ghidra will not overlap function
bodies, so the shared tail gets assigned to exactly one of the two functions. FUN_bc05's body
went [bc05,bc07][bc09,bc0c] -> [bc05,bc07] while FUN_bc08 took [bc08,bc0c]. Flow is still
correct through both entries; only the body attribution is one-sided.

Everything else in the previous comment stands, and the two load-bearing findings are unaffected:
the incidence measurement (7 carriers, 6 REFERENCED, 1 STRONG, 0 WEAK) and the finding that
bank recovery here is blocked on FUN_ff69's ZP round trip (grm-mej), not on the offcut.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DELIVERABLE LANDED 2026-08-16. The 2026-08-15 ruling's scope -- "adapt Ghidra's existing
offcut-fixup script to our purposes and ship it as a script with the extension" -- is met.

  ghidra_scripts/FixSkipInstructions.java   the script. Recognises a carrier whose operand bytes
      decode to an instruction ENDING EXACTLY WHERE THE CARRIER ENDS (the two streams converging
      on a shared tail is what makes it the idiom rather than a coincidence of bytes), with the
      shared tail already disassembled. Repairs with upstream's own sequence: setLengthOverride,
      disassemble, swap the stale ERROR bookmark for INFO -- plus a function at the recovered
      entry (a loose instruction belongs to no body, so no dataflow pass would ever evaluate it)
      and analyzeChanges when anything was applied. Options: carriers, weak, dryrun, function,
      reanalyze, range.

  CONFIDENCE TIERING is the net-new logic, and it exists because structural validity ALONE is too
  weak -- BIT $10A5 also "hides" a perfectly good LDA $10, and firing there would truncate a
  genuine read AND invent an instruction inside its operand. Three tiers, only the first two
  applied by default:
      REFERENCED  a flow reference already lands on the offcut (upstream's own criterion)
      STRONG      the instruction falling through INTO the carrier has the hidden one's mnemonic
                  -- two entries choosing between alternative parameter loads, which is what a
                  hand-written skip almost always looks like. THIS is what upstream cannot do.
      WEAK        structurally valid, uncorroborated. Reported, never applied without weak:true.

  tools/banktest/ nesskiptest.nes fixture (mknesbanktest.py make_prg_skip, VerifyBankTest
      checkNesSkiptest, run-banktest.sh in the nes-banking chunk, expected/nesskiptest.dump).
      One site per tier. S3 pins that the truncated carrier still falls through to the SHARED TAIL
      rather than into the bytes it exposed; S5 pins that the recovered entry actually moves the
      program's bank state (JSR $8010 retargets into PRG_LO_B1) rather than merely existing;
      S7 pins that the WEAK decoy is untouched. Script's own verdict line asserted by log grep
      (candidates=3 referenced=1 strong=1 weak=1 applied=2 failed=0) -- the only place the WEAK
      tier is observable, since not applying it leaves nothing in the program to see.

  BoardBankAnalyzer.addOverlayRef -- the related defect this bead named. getInstructionAt matches
      only instruction START addresses, so the pre-disassembly guard was true at an offcut address
      too and we fired DisassembleCommand at addresses where CodeManager truncates the block and
      throws nothing. Now distinguished and logged. Every synthetic golden byte-identical.

ACCEPTANCE AS WRITTEN IS STILL NOT MET, and should be retargeted or moved rather than left
standing: "bank 3 becomes a known non-home bank" on wizwarr does not happen, for reasons that have
nothing to do with the offcut -- see the two measurement comments above. The short version, now
traced through the code rather than inferred:

  - grm-mej.2 (BankMirrors) and grm-mej.3 increment 2 (BoardBankAnalyzer.restoresEntryBank) ARE
    ALREADY IN, and restoresEntryBank's javadoc transcribes Ironsword FUN_ffc0 -- which is
    wizwarr's FUN_ff69 byte for byte. So ff69 is already modelled as a save/switch/call/restore
    trampoline depositing ownedMask = 0.
  - That is CORRECT, and it is why bc0a carries neither an annotation nor a warning: after
    JSR $FF69 returns, the caller's bank genuinely is unchanged.
  - The bank recovered at bc08 is live only for the INNER call (ff79 JSR $ff83 -> JMP ($1b)). What
    it unlocks is therefore PLACEMENT, not state propagation: the callee's instructions belong in
    bank 3's overlay. That is grm-v60, whose own 2026-08-07 comment already records wizwarr ff69
    as the RESTORING variant of its shape, and which is blocked on grm-e7v as well.

SUGGESTED DISPOSITION: close this bead on the script + fixture + addOverlayRef fix, and move the
"bank 3 becomes known" criterion to grm-v60 where the remaining work actually lives. Left open
pending that call.

ONE THING FOUND ALONG THE WAY, FILED SEPARATELY AS grm-gpi: two fallthrough wrappers into one
bank-switch helper admit only ONE of the two, and which one is not deterministic -- adding an
unrelated call site elsewhere flipped it on otherwise identical bytes. Found on a synthetic image
while building this fixture. Possible relative of grm-g73/grm-4nr's run-to-run bistability.

NOTE ON THE GOLDEN, recorded so nobody reads it as a defect of this work: nesskiptest's dump has
"REF c009 -> PRG_LO_B2::8010 primary=false" alongside the primary B1 ref. A superseded reference
from an earlier fixpoint iteration is not pruned -- pre-existing behaviour, grm-bfb's subject.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
INCIDENCE MEASURED ACROSS THE WHOLE GME SET, 2026-08-16 -- this answers the "FIRST: MEASURE
INCIDENCE" question in the bead description, which the 2026-08-15 scope ruling superseded but
never actually answered. All 19 titles, dry run, nothing written to any program.

  title        candidates  REFERENCED  STRONG  WEAK        title       cand  REF  STR  WEAK
  wizwarr           7          6         1      0          bionic        0    0    0    0
  dodge            20          0         1     19          cv2           0    0    0    0
  blmaster          6          0         0      6          drmario       0    0    0    0
  ultimaav          5          1         0      4          ff1           0    0    0    0
  lwings            1          0         0      1          kicarus       0    0    0    0
  megaman2          1          0         0      1          lifeforce     0    0    0    0
  zelda2            1          0         0      1          smb2          0    0    0    0
                                                           megaman3      0    0    0    0
  TOTAL            41          7         2     32          rcproam       0    0    0    0
  WOULD APPLY       9                                      rcransom      0    0    0    0
                                                           tetris        0    0    0    0
                                                           tmnt          0    0    0    0

THREE CONCLUSIONS, and they settle the design questions the bead left open.

1. *** THE IDIOM IS RARE, AND WIZWARR IS A GENUINE OUTLIER. *** 12 of 19 titles have no carrier at
   all. Only NINE candidates across the entire corpus would be applied by default, and SEVEN of
   those nine are wizwarr's. The bead asked "if wizwarr is alone, take (c) and move on; if the
   idiom is common, (b) earns its cost." The honest answer is neither extreme: wizwarr is nearly
   alone, but not quite -- ultimaav has one REFERENCED carrier and dodge one STRONG -- and the
   script cost about what option (c) would have, while producing option (b)'s user-facing result.
   No revision to the shipped approach is indicated.

2. *** THE WEAK TIER IS OVERWHELMINGLY JUNK, WHICH VINDICATES REPORT-ONLY AS THE DEFAULT. *** 32 of
   41 candidates are WEAK -- 78% -- and the hidden "instructions" say what they are. Distribution
   of hidden mnemonics over the whole sweep:
       SEI 8, BRK 6, LDA 5, BVS 5, INC 3, CPX 3, SBC 2, ROR 2, PHP 2, TAY/PLA/LDY/BVC/BEQ 1 each
   A hidden BRK or SEI is not a bank-switch entry point; it is a run of $00s or a coincidence
   inside a real operand. Had the script applied on structural validity alone -- which is what
   this bead's option (b) would have been without the tiering -- it would have truncated 32 real
   instructions across the corpus and invented 32 imaginary entry points, on 7 titles that have
   no skip idiom in them at all. THE TIERING IS NOT DEFENSIVE POLISH; IT IS WHAT MAKES THE SCRIPT
   SAFE TO SHIP. Do not add a "just apply everything" mode.

3. *** DODGE'S 20 CANDIDATES ARE AN ARTEFACT WORTH KNOWING ABOUT, NOT A SECOND WIZWARR. *** 19 of
   its 20 are WEAK and they cluster inside overlay banks (W8000_M3_B1/B3/B4), hiding BRK/BVS/SEI.
   dodge is also a grm-g73 jitter row and a title with known jump-table trouble. Reading the two
   together: over-read regions decode into plausible-looking nonsense, and a structural-only
   detector would find "entry points" there in bulk. Filed as corroboration on grm-eyn.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, recorded so it is not re-litigated: filtering the WEAK report by hidden
mnemonic (dropping BRK, say) was considered and declined. WEAK is already never applied, so the
filter would only prettify a diagnostic -- and it would layer an inference (which opcodes can
begin a real entry) on top of an inference, in the one output a human actually reads. The raw
report is the honest artefact; the sweep table above is how you read it.

title: Pre-body entry: staggered helper entry points below the function start are invisible to helper detection (cv2 c183/c185)
description:
Found by hand during the cv2 def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-06). Gates 13 of cv2's 16 bank
call sites, including all NINE that select a non-home bank, on a title that currently resolves
ZERO instructions into overlay space.

THE SHAPE. A bank-switch routine has several STAGGERED ENTRY POINTS that fall through into a
common tail. Ghidra creates its function at the TAIL, so the earlier entries lie BELOW the
function start and are not recognised as helper entries at all. Calls to them never reach "a
bank-switch helper function", so their arguments are never considered.

CV2, the motivating instance:

    c183:  STA $1C            ; entry: set bank to A AND remember it
    c185:  LDA $1C            ; entry: restore bank from the shadow
    c187:  5x STA/LSR $FFFF   ; entry: set bank to A without remembering  <-- FUN_c187 starts HERE

  Byte arithmetic confirms the fallthrough chain: STA $1C zp is 2 bytes (85 1C) landing exactly
  on c185; LDA $1C is 2 bytes (A5 1C) landing exactly on c187.

  Call sites: 10 to c183 (9 preceded by LDA #4, 1 by LDA #0), 3 to c187 (all LDA #0), 3 to c185
  (restores). Sixteen sites, thirteen with an adjacent immediate. The analyzer sees
  reachableCallSites 5 / constArg 2, both resolving to home, and zero non-home banks.

WHY NO EXISTING DETECTOR CATCHES IT. grm-nju's reachableEntries follows Ghidra thunks and
one-instruction JMP trampolines, and its midBodyEntry flag catches a call landing INSIDE a
function's body. This is the opposite: the call lands BEFORE the function's start. grm-nju
measured cv2 at midBodyEntry=0 / viaThunkOrTrampoline=0 and grm-8iy.3 used those numbers to rule
grm-nju's shapes out for cv2 -- correctly, and misleadingly, because the detector cannot express
this case. PRE-BODY ENTRY is a distinct shape.

POSSIBLE SHAPES FOR A FIX, not yet chosen:
  (a) EXTEND BACKWARD FROM A KNOWN HELPER. When a function is identified as a bank-switch helper,
      walk backward from its entry while the preceding instruction falls through into it and is
      itself the target of a call, treating each such address as an additional entry with its own
      argument semantics. Cheap and local; needs a guard against walking into an unrelated
      routine that merely abuts.
  (b) REPAIR THE FUNCTION BOUNDARY so c183 becomes the function entry and c185/c187 become
      ordinary mid-body entries, which grm-nju's existing machinery already handles. Fixes the
      disassembly for the user too, but is a more invasive change and interacts with (b) in
      grm-78b.
  (c) TREAT CALL TARGETS AS ENTRY CANDIDATES DIRECTLY -- any address that is the target of a call
      and reaches a mechanism write by fallthrough is a helper entry, without reference to
      function boundaries at all. Most general; most likely to surprise.

NOTE EACH ENTRY HAS DIFFERENT ARGUMENT SEMANTICS and a fix must preserve that: c183 takes a bank
in A and writes the $1C shadow; c185 takes NO argument and reads the shadow; c187 takes a bank in
A and does not touch the shadow. A model that assumes one signature per helper function will get
two of the three wrong.

RELATED. grm-78b is the same class of defect from the other direction -- a function body that
over-extends and swallows an unrelated routine (blmaster f1ca absorbing RESET at f23b). Two
function-boundary defects found by hand in two titles suggests checking the rest of the GME set
before assuming either is isolated. Anything keyed on "which function contains this mechanism
write" inherits both.

ACCEPTANCE: cv2 reports 16 reachable call sites with 13 constant arguments, recovers bank 4 at
the nine c183 sites, and resolves a non-zero instrs.inOverlay. The 3 c185 restores additionally
need the $1C shadow (grm-mej.2, easy case) and are not required for this bead.
close_reason: NO INSTANCES. Both candidate instances were inferred from bead prose locating a chain ('chains around FUN_c187', 'inside FUN_c310') rather than from checking where a function starts, and both inferences were wrong. Ghidra creates functions at tmnt cea5 AND cea7, and at cv2 c183, c185 AND c187. Nothing is pre-body. Both titles are argument-marshalling wrapper cases instead, moved to grm-2dr along with the 20 call sites this bead claimed. Refile if a genuine pre-body case turns up -- the shape is conceivable, it just does not occur in any title traced so far.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SECOND INSTANCE, ON TMNT, AND A MORE VALUABLE ONE (2026-08-06, from the tmnt def-use pass on
grm-8iy.5).

    cea5:  STA $21            ; entry: set PRG bank to A AND remember it
    cea7:  <serial chain>     ; entry: set PRG bank to A without remembering

STA $21 zero-page is 2 bytes (85 21), landing exactly on cea7 -- the same fallthrough
construction as cv2's c183/c185/c187. grm-8iy.5 records tmnt's fifth mechanism chain as
ceaa..ceba, i.e. inside cea7's body, so Ghidra's function almost certainly begins at cea7 with
cea5 below it. CONFIRM THIS before relying on the payoff below.

WHY IT IS THE BIGGER PRIZE. Every one of cea5's SEVEN call sites carries a non-home constant:
LDA #1 (x3), LDA #6 (x2), LDA #3, LDA #4. tmnt's home bank is 7 (startup sets control $1F, PRG
mode 3, then PRG bank 7). That is the highest concentration of recoverable non-home banks found
in any title traced by hand so far -- cv2's equivalent is nine sites at a single bank 4.

The restores differ from cv2 in an instructive way. cv2 packs restore into a third fallthrough
entry (c185); tmnt uses SEPARATE FUNCTIONS -- ced0 restoring from $21, cf0b restoring from $59.
So the staggered-entry construction and the restore mechanism are independent choices, and a fix
must not assume the cv2 layout. What is common is the SEMANTIC SPLIT: set-and-remember,
set-transient, restore. That triple is the thing to model.

RUNNING COUNT: two of four titles traced by hand show pre-body entry, and in both it gates the
title's largest block of recoverable non-home banks.

ALSO NOTE for the fix design: tmnt strengthens the warning already in this bead's description
that each entry has different argument semantics. cea5 takes a bank in A and writes $21; cea7
takes a bank in A and writes nothing; ced0 and cf0b take NO argument and read different shadows.
Four semantics, one mechanism chain.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-06: TMNT IS *NOT* AN INSTANCE OF THIS BEAD. Withdrawing the previous comment.

Ghidra creates functions at BOTH cea5 and cea7 (confirmed by hand). Nothing about tmnt is
pre-body: cea5 is a complete two-byte function in its own right. My inference that Ghidra's
function must begin at cea7 was drawn from grm-8iy.5 recording tmnt's fifth chain as
ceaa..ceba, which was circumstantial and wrong.

tmnt's cea5 is instead an ARGUMENT-MARSHALLING WRAPPER that reaches its helper by FALLING
THROUGH into the next function -- filed as its own bead alongside blmaster's e61b. The seven
non-home call sites are still real and still unrecovered; they are gated by that bead, not this
one.

THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE NOW NEEDS THE SAME CHECK IT JUST FAILED ON TMNT. The cv2 claim rests on
Ghidra having a function at c187 but NOT at c183/c185, and that was inferred the same way -- from
grm-8iy.5's phrasing "chains around FUN_c187" -- never confirmed. If Ghidra also created
functions at c183 and c185, then cv2 is a wrapper case too and THIS BEAD HAS NO INSTANCES AT ALL
and should be closed.

DO THIS BEFORE ANY WORK HERE: check whether functions exist at cv2 c183 and c185. One lookup.
If they exist, close this bead and move cv2's nine bank-4 sites to the wrapper bead. If they do
not, this bead stands on cv2 alone and its priority should be reconsidered on that basis.

LESSON WORTH KEEPING EITHER WAY: "the bead says chains are around FUN_x" is not evidence about
where a function STARTS. Both of my inferences from that phrasing were unsafe; one is now known
wrong.

title: Set-valued bank state: two constants merging before the switch collapse to unknown (blmaster c9a4)
description:
Found by hand during the blmaster def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-05). Not blmaster-specific:
a two-armed branch that selects between two constants and then merges BEFORE the switch is an
ordinary code shape, and the current known/unknown bank state cannot express its result.

OBSERVED. blmaster FUN_c9a4, the highest-value unrecovered site in the title:

    c9a4: LDX #$40
          LDA $14
          AND #$08
          BEQ c9ae      ; skips ONLY the next instruction
          LDX #$60
    c9ae: TXA
          PHA
          JSR ea3a      ; unpacks with 4x LSR at ea41, then JSR e61b -> bank 4 or 6
          PLA
          LSR A x4
          AND #$0F
          STA $D3       ; = c9ba
          ; ... reads pointers from $8000, dispatches through an indirect jump

Both arms converge at c9ae, so X holds {$40,$60} at the merge and the bank is {4,6} at the
switch. Every consumer -- the JSR ea3a, the stack round trip, the unpack, the $D3 write and the
pointer dispatch -- sits AFTER the merge, on the single merged path. There is no per-path
constant to recover: single-valued dataflow must fold the merge to unknown, and does.

WHY IT MATTERS. This is a banked-dispatch site: it selects a bank, reads a pointer table from
$8000, and jumps indirectly. One recovered bank yields as many entry points as the table has
entries, so it is the only site found in blmaster with the shape to move instrs.inOverlay
meaningfully. Losing it to a two-element merge loses the title's best prospect.

DESIGN QUESTION, NOT YET DECIDED. Options, roughly in increasing cost:
  (a) SET-VALUED BANK STATE -- allow a small bounded set (cap at 2-4) alongside known/unknown,
      and realize the union of the implied overlays. Honest, but every downstream consumer that
      assumes one bank needs auditing, and reference retargeting has no single target.
  (b) PATH FORKING -- analyze the merged tail once per incoming arm and reconcile. Exact, but
      cost multiplies with each such merge and needs a fork budget.
  (c) DECLINE EXPLICITLY -- keep single-valued state, but classify this as a recognized
      'multi-valued at merge' stop reason rather than a generic undeterminable value, so it is
      diagnosable and countable (fits grm-3ou's stop-reason classification).
  (c) is cheap and strictly better than today even if (a) or (b) follows later. Recommend
  starting there so the shape stops hiding inside 'genuinely undeterminable'.

NOTE c9a4 ALSO requires three other unimplemented things, so fixing this alone does not recover
it -- see grm-8iy.5 section 5. The other three are PHA/PLA stack pairing across the JSR
(grm-mej.3), the 4x LSR + AND #$0F mask algebra, and the $D3 shadow with a wrapper-call
discovery route (grm-mej.2 spec gap). This bead covers only the merge.

FIRST STEP: measure incidence before choosing. Count sites across the GME set where a mechanism
write or wrapper call is dominated by a merge of two blocks that each assign a different
constant to the argument register. If blmaster is alone, take (c) and move on; if it is common,
(a) or (b) earns its cost.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
PAYOFF MEASURED BY A HUMAN RE PASS (2026-08-08). This bead's FIRST STEP asked for incidence
before choosing a design; the human-research TODO asked the complementary question -- how big is
the prize, and are the pointers read before or after the switch. Both are now answered for
blmaster, and the answer is large enough to change the recommendation.

TABLE SIZES -- THE COMBINED PAYOFF ESTIMATE. ~136 entries in bank 4, ~145 in bank 6, so roughly
281 dispatch targets. blmaster today sits at instrs.inOverlay=0 / refs.intoOverlay=0, so this one
site is the difference between a title that recovers nothing and a title with ~281 entry points.
That is the number grm-wul + grm-mej.2 + grm-mej.3 + the mask algebra have to be judged against
COLLECTIVELY, since all four are required before c9a4 resolves at all.

TARGETS STAY IN-BANK. Nearly every target address lies in the same bank as its table. So once the
bank resolves, reference retargeting is unambiguous -- the pointers land in W8000_M3_B4 /
W8000_M3_B6 respectively, no cross-bank fan-out to adjudicate. That removes the retargeting
objection this bead raises against option (a) ("reference retargeting has no single target"): the
problem is choosing the bank, not choosing the target once the bank is known.

THE TABLES ARE IN THE SWITCHED WINDOW, read AFTER the switch. The bank switch happens BEFORE the
first pointer fetch; the first pointer is loaded from $8000 in bank 4 or 6. So the tables are not
sitting in base space waiting to be read -- they are only reachable once the bank is resolved.
There is no shortcut that reads them without solving the merge first.

STRUCTURE, and the detail that bears on the DESIGN QUESTION. The indirect jump's address comes
from a table at 4:$8006 or 6:$8002, indexed by $46 - 1, and the code has explicit handling for
indexes > 128 (consistent with the 136/145 sizes).

  Note the table base DIFFERS PER BANK -- $8006 vs $8002 -- and is itself reached via the pointer
  at $8000 in the selected bank. So the two elements of the merged set {4,6} are NOT
  interchangeable downstream: each implies a different derived base address. A set-valued state
  (option (a)) that merely realizes "the union of the implied overlays" is therefore NOT
  sufficient here -- it would have to keep each set element CORRELATED with the values derived
  from it, which is most of the machinery of option (b) path forking anyway. That is an argument
  for (b) over (a) that this bead did not previously have, and it is worth re-reading option (a)
  in that light before committing.

RECOMMENDATION UNCHANGED IN ORDER, STRENGTHENED IN JUSTIFICATION: still take (c) first -- the
explicit 'multi-valued at merge' stop reason -- because it is cheap and stops the shape hiding
inside 'genuinely undeterminable'. But (c) is now clearly not the end state for this site: 281
targets in the single highest-value title-level gap is enough to fund (b), whereas the pre-
measurement guess of "as many entries as the table has" could not justify anything.

STILL OPEN, and unaffected by this measurement: the INCIDENCE question this bead asks -- how many
sites across the GME set have the two-constants-merging shape. The payoff above is blmaster's
alone. If blmaster is the only instance, (b) is being funded by one site; that is still arguably
worth it at 281 targets, but it is a different decision than funding it across a family.

title: The full gate cannot see real-ROM regressions: build-and-test.sh does not run the real-ROM tier
description:
PROVEN COST, 2026-08-04. grm-mu7's first increment passed 'bash tools/banktest/build-and-test.sh check' with 44 of 45 goldens byte-identical and 379 criteria green, was committed and pushed on that evidence, and had destroyed three pinned real ROMs: kicarus -215 overlay instructions, dodge -10692, cv2 -2 bank comments. It was found only because an unrelated task (grm-8iy.3) happened to run realrom-test.sh a day later.

THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM. The acceptance gate documented in CLAUDE.md as 'the full acceptance gate' covers the synthetic goldens and the JUnit suite. The real-ROM tier is a separate script (tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh) that nothing invokes for you. So the ONE tier that exercises real cartridge idioms is the one tier a normal commit never runs -- and synthetic fixtures, by construction, only contain idioms someone already thought of. grm-mu7's guard was correct against every idiom the fixtures encode and wrong against the first save/restore it met.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY 'ADD IT TO THE GATE'. The real-ROM tier needs ROMs the repo cannot ship (hash-pinned, user-supplied, H:/emulators/nes/roms here) and takes ~20-25 minutes for 19 titles. It cannot be a hard gate for a contributor who has no ROMs. Options, roughly in increasing cost:

  1. DOCUMENT IT. CLAUDE.md's 'Build & Test' section currently presents build-and-test.sh as the full gate without saying what it does not cover. At minimum it should say: changes to BoardBankAnalyzer / any BankSwitchStrategy / StoredValueScanner MUST also run the real-ROM tier when ROMs are available, and say so in the commit message either way. Cheapest, and would have caught this.
  2. A FAST SUBSET. A named handful of titles chosen for idiom coverage (cv2 for save/restore, dodge for the memory park, bionic for RAM-shadow argument, ff1 as the working control) rather than all 19 -- a few minutes, SKIPping cleanly when the ROMs are absent, so it can be advisory-by-default.
  3. WIRE IT IN. build-and-test.sh gains a chunk that shells out to realrom-test.sh and SKIPs (not FAILs) with a loud note when GRM_ROM_DIR is unset. Highest confidence, and the SKIP path needs care or it degrades to noise everyone ignores.

Recommend 1 immediately and 2 shortly after; 3 only if 2 proves it earns its runtime.

RELATED SHARPENING. The real-ROM tier has known-bistable rows (grm-4nr, grm-g73: ff1/megaman/dodge/rcproam), which is exactly the property that makes an automated gate hard and makes a documented manual step more attractive in the short run. Note also the discriminator that worked here: count-line-only movement is jitter, whereas a 'sample.bankcomment ... via FUN_xxx' line changing or vanishing is a real behavioural change. That rule is worth writing down wherever the tier is described.
close_reason: Landed afe399a as the RESCOPED version only -- the tier model is deliberately unchanged, per the 2026-08-15 ruling that the ROM-less contributor is hypothetical. Shipped: the CLAUDE.md pre-push requirement, a loud skip when GRM_ROM_DIR is unset, and build/realrom-cache/.last-verified surfaced as a REALROM STALENESS line on every run. The stamp updates whenever rows RAN, pass or fail -- required, not stylistic, since smb3 and dodge fail by design and a pass-gated stamp could never update on a normal run. PROVED ITSELF IMMEDIATELY: it fired on the first gate run reporting main had never had a real-ROM check, which led to running the tier and reopening grm-4nr. Follow-up in the same session: the requirement's wording was corrected to mandate --all (c4424cc), because a bare check reads only the 12 curated rows and all three grm-mu7 victims are GME rows.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
USER RULING 2026-08-15 -- SCOPE COLLAPSES. The open design question this bead carried
was "what should the default gate do on a machine with no ROMs?" That question is moot:
for both current contributors the ROMs are ALWAYS present. For a hypothetical future
contributor NONE will be present -- and that is fine, because they are hypothetical.

RESOLUTION: do not redesign the tier model. Make the real-ROM pass part of our LOCAL
pre-push requirements instead:
  1. CLAUDE.md: state that realrom-test.sh check is required before committing changes
     that touch analysis behaviour, alongside build-and-test.sh check.
  2. Make not-having-run-it VISIBLE rather than silent -- the failure mode in the
     grm-mu7 incident was that nothing told anyone the tier had not run. A staleness
     signal (last realrom run vs. current HEAD / extension identity) is the cheap fix.
  3. When GRM_ROM_DIR is unset, skip LOUDLY and say what is being skipped -- never
     report a clean gate.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TRIAGE: this moves from "needs design, top of the planning list" to
"mechanical, farm-out-able." Priority stays P2 -- it is still the guard that would have
caught grm-mu7 destroying three pinned ROMs -- but it no longer needs user interaction.

title: A helper that supplies its own constant is modelled as caller-supplied, so the prologue guard declines it
description:
Found by the real-ROM tier while fixing grm-mu7's increment-2 regression (2026-08-04). Pre-existing modelling gap that the prologue guard turned from harmless into visible.

PROVEN CASE. kicarus FUN_eb07, disassembled from the pinned ROM:

    eb07  LDA #$0F
    eb09  STA $9FFF     <- firstSite; $9FFF decodes to MMC1 target 0 = Control
    eb0c  LSR A / STA $9FFF / ... (the rest of the 5-write chain)

This helper takes NO argument. It loads its own constant and commits mirroring=3, prg_mode=3 (0x0F = 0b1111: mirroring = bits 0-1 = 3, prg_mode = bits 2-3 = 3). Yet:

  1. findHelpers gives it argReg='A' (from the chain's STA -- the only evidence it has) and constState=null, because the constState test is 'result.knownMask() == site.effectMask()' and a Control-target write legitimately knows only mirroring+prg_mode while effectMask spans the whole mechanism including prg_bank. So a helper with a perfectly constant effect is routed into per-call-site recovery.
  2. recoverCallArgument then consults the grm-mu7 prologue guard, which sees the helper's OWN 'LDA #$0F' writing argReg between entry and firstSite and declines.

Net: 'bank -> mirroring=3,prg_mode=3 via FUN_eb07' at c024 is lost, along with prg_mode known-ness at every downstream site. kicarus loses 5 bank comments (31 -> 26). dodge shows the same class of loss (30 -> 29 comments, plus mirroring/prg_mode demoted to 'assumed from initial' at all 12 FUN_ff08 call sites) though its specific helper is not the LDA-#imm shape and is not yet identified.

NOT A grm-mu7 REGRESSION IN THE USUAL SENSE. Before the guard, these call sites resolved by depositing the CALLER's A -- which is unsound in general (the helper ignores it) and was right here only because the caller's value happened to agree. The decline is honest; it just forfeits an answer the engine could derive.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, both principled, probably wanting measurement before choosing:

  (a) FIX constState. The test should ask whether the effect covers the bits the site OWNS, not the whole mechanism mask -- exactly the ownedMask concept HelperDeposit already carries for the call-site path. A Control-target write owning mirroring+prg_mode and knowing both IS a constant effect, and would fold directly at every call site, never reaching recoverCallArgument or the guard at all. Narrow, and it fixes the root rather than the symptom.

  (b) MINI-INLINE serial-shift, as MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy already does. SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy would evaluate its own chain under the caller's RegisterEnv instead of consuming argValue, and would then read the helper's own LDA #$0F directly. This is what consumesHelperArgument() was explicitly designed to accommodate (it returns false for memory-latch precisely because that strategy re-derives the value inside the helper), and it would additionally make serial-shift immune to the whole prologue-clobber hazard the way memory-latch is -- i.e. it would retire the guard for this strategy rather than refine it.

(b) is the larger and more valuable change; (a) is likely a few lines. They are not exclusive.

REPRO: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --gme --only kicarus,dodge /h/emulators/nes/roms -- both FAIL at ea2df90 with only this residue; everything else about them was restored by that commit.
close_reason:
Fixed (0083b3a). When the prologue guard proves the caller's byte does not reach the helper's first switch site, recoverCallArgument now scans for what DOES -- from firstSite, with the caller's registers passed as explicitly UNKNOWN so the walk stops at the entry without adopting values it just proved do not survive. Strictly additive: it can only turn an unknown into a value derived from the helper's own code.

DIAGNOSIS IN THE BEAD WAS WRONG ON THE MECHANISM, right on the symptom. Candidate fix (a) -- 'constState's test compares against the whole effectMask rather than the owned bits' -- is NOT the cause. A serial-shift chain helper never has a constState for a simpler reason: writes 1-4 of a chain return inState (SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy:318-322) and write 5 commits, so findHelpers' MULTI-SITE DISAGREEMENT rule nulls it. That is deliberate and documented -- it is what routes chain helpers into per-call recovery at all, and grm-hum's mini-inline depends on it. So the fix had to be on the recovery side, not the classification side.

What made it tractable: computeSwitch's commit case ALREADY resolves the chain's seed byte by scanning back from chain start inside the helper. The helper's own body always knew the answer; only the call-site path ignored it. The fallback does the same scan from the same kind of instruction.

MEASURED, both movements confirmed by disassembling the pinned ROMs rather than inferred from counts:
  kicarus 31 -> 32 bank comments. FUN_eb07 (LDA #$0F / STA $9FFF chain) restored at c024, AND a previously-missed helper call at c14f via FUN_ca90 -- strictly better than the pre-grm-mu7 golden.
  dodge 30 -> 29, and this one is CORRECT rather than a loss. Its Control helper FUN_fe9b is 'PHA / JSR $FE8A / LDA $69 / STA $9FFF(chain)' -- bionic's RAM-shadow shape, with a separate entry at $FE96 (STA $69) that sets the shadow. The caller's A is genuinely not the byte written, so the old golden recorded an unsound guess. Recovering it properly needs the RAM write-through shadow: grm-mej.2.
  Both goldens re-blessed. dodge's refs.intoOverlay oscillates 2736/2739 across runs on identical code (grm-4nr/grm-g73), verified by re-running; blessed at 2739.

Candidate fix (b) from this bead -- mini-inlining serial-shift the way memory-latch does -- is NOT done and is still the better long-term answer: it would retire the prologue guard for this strategy rather than refine it. Left open as a possibility, not filed, since grm-mej.2/.3 cover the pieces it would need.

Full gate: SUITE OK, 0 criterion failures.

title: requiresOnEntry flags a full-overwrite helper as needing the bit it overwrites
description:
Observed while landing grm-mu7 (not caused by it -- grm-mu7 only made it VISIBLE in a golden).

WHAT. annotateBankRequirementViolations' ownRequires rule is: for each switch site whose strategy is not cacheable(), require the bits 'effectMask & ~inState.knownMask & ~effect.knownMask()' -- i.e. 'the site's effect came out unknown from an in-state that was also unknown, so the dispatch must have NEEDED that bit'.

That inference is right for a read-modify-write mechanism (a masked RMW really does need its prior value). It is wrong for a FULL-OVERWRITE mechanism reached as a caller-supplied helper. nesmmc1test's FUN_c200 is the plain Zelda/Metroid SwitchBank: a 5x STA/LSR chain that overwrites prg_bank outright and reads nothing. Analyzed standalone its argument register is unknown, so its effect is unknown from an unknown in-state -- and the rule concludes it requires prg_bank known on ENTRY. It does not; it requires its ARGUMENT REGISTER, which is a different thing and is not part of banking.state at all.

SYMPTOM. Any call site reaching such a helper with the bit unknown gets a 'Bank state requirement violated' WARNING that says the wrong thing. nesmmc1test's $C044 is now a pinned instance (criterion M14b) -- it carries a fully-resolved 'prg_bank=7' annotation AND a requirement warning at the same address, which is self-contradictory on its face: the call resolves its own argument fine.

Was invisible before grm-mu7 only because the fixture's one such call site ($C064) is deduped by alreadyWarned -- it already carries a helper-call warning of its own.

POSSIBLE SHAPE. The distinguishing fact is available: findHelpers already knows the function is a caller-supplied helper with an argReg, and BankSwitchStrategy could say whether a site's effect depends on prior state at all (serial-shift's chain does not; a masked RMW does). Excluding a full-overwrite site's own effectMask from ownRequires would keep every genuine RMW requirement and drop this class of false positive. Needs measuring against the real-ROM corpus before landing -- the requirement layer is annotation-only (never gates anything), so the cost of the false positive is user-facing noise, not wrong banks.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RAISED P3 -> P2 (2026-08-05). Two things changed, both from the blmaster pass on grm-8iy.5.

1. THE REAL-ROM MEASUREMENT THIS BEAD ASKED FOR PROBABLY ALREADY EXISTS. The description says
the fix "needs measuring against the real-ROM corpus before landing". blmaster looks like that
corpus instance, and a large one. It is MMC1 serial-shift, and its four caller-supplied helpers
(e63c PRG, e650 CHR1, e664 CHR0, e678 CTRL) are all 5x STA/LSR full-overwrite chains that read
nothing -- exactly the FUN_c200 shape this bead describes. grm-lwu records that ~80 of
blmaster 90 warnings are "requires mirroring known on entry", and HelperShapeProbe splits the
same 90 as switchUnknown=22 / violation=66 / other=2. Those 66 violations are
annotateBankRequirementViolations output on a full-overwrite board.

STRONG HYPOTHESIS, NOT YET CONFIRMED: this bead is the root cause of the bulk of grm-lwu 66-80
warnings, and grm-lwu is its symptom rather than an independent problem. Confirm by checking
whether blmaster violation bookmarks name the bits its own serial chains overwrite. If they do,
the ownRequires exclusion proposed here should drop most of them in one change, and grm-lwu
becomes an acceptance measurement rather than separate work. grm-lwu is now marked as blocked
by this bead on that basis; unlink if the check disproves it.

2. THE SEVERITY ASSESSMENT IN THE DESCRIPTION IS NOW OUT OF DATE. It reads: "the requirement
layer is annotation-only (never gates anything), so the cost of the false positive is
user-facing noise, not wrong banks." The first half is still true. The second half is not.

That noise corrupted a MEASUREMENT. HelperShapeProbe original helper population counted any
function holding any Warning bookmark as a bank-switch helper; on blmaster it turned 5 real
helpers into 36 and a constant-argument count of 2 into 13. grm-8iy.3 (P2) was filed on those
inflated numbers, spent its analysis on a nine-site shortfall that did not exist, named two
phantom helpers (eb98, f1ca) and missed two real ones (e650, e664). It has since been closed as
a measurement artifact.

So the cost is not only user-facing noise: warning traffic is an input to diagnosis, and false
warnings produce false diagnoses. Same class as grm-xym from the other direction -- a question
that does not apply to a site generating output as though it does.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CONFIRMED (structurally) BY A HUMAN RE PASS, with one refinement that changes the fix shape.
User-supplied trace of blmaster's best example, the violation bookmark at c2a1:

  c2a1  JSR dec2            (immediately preceded by LDX #$FF / TXS -- a stack-pointer reset)
  dec2: JSR df05            -> sets bank 5 via e61b
        JSR bfe5            (the actual banked work)
        JSR df0a            -> restores the bank held in $D3, via e61b
        RTS
  e61b: STA $DB immediately; later LDA $DB; JSR e63c, which does the PRG bank set directly.

WHY THIS SETTLES THE grm-lwu LINK. The warning at c2a1 -- and at c55f/c57a, which name e61b
ITSELF -- says "requires mirroring known on entry". Walk where mirroring could possibly enter
e61b's ownRequires:

  - e63c is the PRG helper: SerialShift target 3, whose COMMIT path deposits into prg_bank only
    and, per the strategy javadoc, "never poisons unrelated targets". An unknown commit value
    therefore yields effectMask = prg_bank, which can NEVER contribute mirroring.
  - There is no other mechanism contact anywhere in dec2 -> df05 -> e61b -> e63c. e678 (the
    control-register helper, the only writer of mirroring) is not in this chain.
  - The ONLY remaining path is SerialShift's POISON branch: bit 7 of the stored byte unknown ->
    "poison every field any target or the reset could touch", which spans mirroring, prg_mode
    and prg_bank.

And the user's trace predicts exactly that bit-7-unknown: A is round-tripped through $DB
(STA $DB ... LDA $DB) before e63c's chain, so StoredValueScanner cannot resolve the byte. The
bit-7 check runs BEFORE the chain walk, so a structurally perfect 5x STA/LSR chain still
poisons when its value is unresolvable. mirroring is then the bit that SURVIVES to the message
because it is the one never established board-wide -- see the ec53/e68e bankcomments, where
mirroring.1 is always "assumed from initial", never known.

So: same bug, different branch. This bead's description is the UNKNOWN-COMMIT branch
(nesmmc1test FUN_c200: full overwrite, unresolvable argReg). blmaster is the POISON branch.
Both hit the identical ownRequires rule -- effect came out unknown from an unknown in-state,
therefore "the dispatch must have needed that bit" -- and both conclusions are wrong for the
same reason: the unknown originates in an unresolved DATA value, not in missing bank state.

FIX SHAPE, REVISED. The exclusion as literally worded here ("exclude a full-overwrite site's
own effectMask") does NOT fire on a poison site -- a poison is not an overwrite, it is an
honest "I don't know what happened". Discriminating overwrite-vs-RMW is therefore the wrong
predicate. The right one is the one this bead's POSSIBLE SHAPE paragraph already gestures at,
stated at strategy level:

  Does this strategy's computeSwitch consult inState to produce its VALUE, or only to echo it?

SerialShift never resolves a load back to tracked state -- its own javadoc says so explicitly
(MMC1's shift register is write-only; its Hooks never resolve loads). It is non-cacheable only
because positions 1-4 and poison ECHO inState, which is not a requirement. So SerialShift
should contribute ZERO to ownRequires on every branch: commit, echo, reset, and poison alike.
That covers both this bead's nesmmc1test case and blmaster's 66 in one rule, and it leaves a
genuine masked-RMW mechanism's requirement intact, which is the case the rule was written for.

This also answers grm-lwu's question 1 in the negative: scoping the check to placement-relevant
fields would NOT fix this. It would only change the message to "requires prg_bank known on
entry", which is equally false.

KEEP THE grm-lwu DEPENDENCY. The "unlink if disproved" condition was not met.

RESIDUE, not a counter-argument, and the one place this could still die: not yet explained is
why ONLY mirroring ever appears in `missing` at all 66 sites, never prg_mode/prg_bank -- a
poison's effectMask covers all three, so the caller-side `required & ~callerIn.knownMask()`
narrowing must be dropping the other two everywhere. Consistent with mirroring.1 being the
only permanently-unknown bit, but unmeasured.

CHEAP CONFIRMATION, one run, not a loop: a verbose headless pass on blmaster and read the
[bank-summary] lines for e63c / e61b / dec2. If e63c's "requires on entry" names mirroring,
poison is measured and this is closed as diagnosed. If it requires nothing, the source is
outside the user's trace (bfe5's banked body is the candidate) and this analysis is wrong.

ACCEPTANCE, once fixed: blmaster's 66 violation bookmarks drop out of the dump; the 22
switchUnknown warnings must REMAIN (they are the honest signal), as must the ec53 prg_bank=5
recovery.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
FIXED AND LANDED (f8cd931). Implementation took the strategy-level shape this bead's POSSIBLE
SHAPE paragraph anticipated, not the overwrite-vs-RMW discriminator its opening proposed --
see the previous comment for why the poison branch forced that.

  BankSwitchStrategy.effectDependsOnPriorState()  default !cacheable()
  SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy                   overrides to false
  BoardBankAnalyzer:2372                          ownRequires gate: !cacheable() -> the new predicate

The default deriving from cacheable() is what keeps the blast radius at one mechanism:
memory-latch, register-write and especially select-data (MMC3, which genuinely consumes its
select field from prior state) all still answer true and still get their requirements.

MEASURED, whole nes-banking chunk: exactly two lines change, both a dropped Warning bookmark at
an address that already carried a fully-resolved bank annotation -- nesmmc1test c04c (the
self-contradiction this bead named; the description says $C044, the actual address is $C04C) and
neswrappertest c02c (same shape, "direct call to single_helper resolves prg_bank=2, no '?'"). No
comments, no retargeting, no other bookmarks, no criteria output moved.

CRITERION M14b WAS PINNING THIS BUG and is now inverted rather than deleted. It asserted
hasWarningBookmark(0xC04C), and its own comment said "filed as grm-izu, and deliberately not
touched here". It now asserts !hasWarningBookmark(0xC04C) && the resolved prg_bank=7 comment, so
it guards against the false warning returning. Its comment block was rewritten to record what
changed and why -- a later reader meeting a test that asserts the opposite of what it used to
needs that on the page.

Note what did NOT change: the honest poison still propagates through tracked state exactly as
M14 establishes. Only the false inference drawn from it is gone.

GATES: full `build-and-test.sh check` green -- 402 criteria PASS, SUITE OK, and the JUnit suite
includes a new SerialShiftStrategyProgramTest case pinning that serial-shift is non-cacheable yet
does not depend on prior state (12 tests, 0 failures).

CLOSING. The bead's own acceptance is met on its own fixture. The real-ROM measurement it asked
for ("needs measuring against the real-ROM corpus before landing") is NOT yet done -- it needs a
realrom run against a local ROM directory, which the agent does not have a path for. That
measurement lives on grm-lwu, which is now unblocked and carries it: ~66 blmaster violation
bookmarks predicted to drop, with the 22 switchUnknown warnings and the ec53 prg_bank=5 recovery
predicted to survive. REOPEN THIS BEAD if that measurement comes back wrong.

title: cv2, tmnt, wizwarr, blmaster: switching is dominated by DIRECT stores whose value recovers no bits (20/20, 24/30, 4/13, 20/21)
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-03 (build/reach-wave2, build/reach-smoke-after, build/helper-wave3,
build/consume-wave1). These three differ from their siblings in grm-8iy.3 (blmaster) and
grm-8iy.4 (MMC3) in WHERE the recovery has to happen: they barely use call-into-helper at all, so
the call-site path grm-nju built cannot carry them. Their bank switching is at DIRECT mechanism
stores, and those stores' values do not recover.

  title    board       sites  todayComment  todayWarn   callSites  constArg  nonHomeBanks
  cv2      MMC1         20         0            20          5          2          0
  tmnt     MMC1         30         6            24         13          6          3
  wizwarr  AxROM        13         9             4          8          7          0 (all home)

Compare the working controls, which resolve almost everything at CALL sites instead:
  ff1      MMC1         26         1            23        587        178         58
  megaman2 MMC1         30        11            14        395         85         59

ff1 recovers a value at exactly ONE of its 26 direct store sites and still reaches 7426
instrs.inOverlay -- so direct-store recovery is NOT how a title succeeds today, and these three
have no other path.

PER-TITLE DETAIL.

cv2 -- the purest case: 20 of 20 direct stores recover NOT ONE BIT ("mechanism write with a
genuinely undeterminable value"), clustered c143..c19e in four-plus 5-write serial chains around
FUN_c187. Its 2 bank comments both come from its 2 constant-arg call sites, and both resolve to
the HOME bank, so nothing retargets. walk.sites 0.

tmnt -- 24 of 30 stores recover nothing, in five unrolled 5-write chains (c31b..c327, ce59..ce69,
ce74..ce84, ce8f..ce9f, ceaa..ceba) inside FUN_c310/FUN_ce56/FUN_ce6f. It DOES get three
fully-known non-home banks (c003 prg_bank=2, c340 prg_bank=7, c354 prg_bank=7) but none reaches a
consumer: BankConsumerProbe walks them 77/7/36 steps to EXIT/SWITCH/NOFLOW with consumers=0, so
tmnt classifies STATE-UNCONSUMED rather than pure VALUE-RECOVERY. Note also
'helper FUN_c310 endsWith=JMP stackOps=1 trampolineShape=YES' -- it holds 7 of tmnt's 10 switch
sites and has grm-v60's far-call-trampoline shape; worth checking whether the consumer is that
JMP.

wizwarr -- AxROM, and the one that most looks like a false alarm but is not. 9 of 13 stores DO
recover, but every recovered value is bank 0, which IS the home bank, so retargeting nothing is
correct GIVEN THOSE VALUES. The bug is that the sites which actually switch recover nothing:
ce8b, ff76, ff7f, ffa6 (undeterminable) plus the helper arg at bc0a -> FUN_ff69. Banks 1-3 are
realized as overlays and a 4x32K game runs from them. Do NOT record this title as "correct, not a
bug" -- and note grm-6pi's removal of the 0/3/7 convention fallback (73740f2) remains RIGHT; it
was shipping a wrong bank, not a right one. Because AxROM's single window is the whole
8000-ffff space, ONE recovered non-home value here would cascade the way tetris's does.

WHAT THIS NEEDS THAT THIS PASS DID NOT PRODUCE: the VALUE-FLOW SHAPE feeding those stores. All
three probes count and locate sites; none reports what the stored value is computed FROM. The
warning text guesses ("a load of an unrelated address followed directly by the store, with no
AND/ORA immediate to constrain it") but that is a default message, not a measurement. Next step is
either a fourth probe reporting the def-use chain into each undeterminable store, or reading the
five tmnt chains by hand -- tmnt is the better subject, since it is the only one of the three with
any non-home success to compare against.

Adjacent: grm-mej (bank shadow / read-back), grm-mu7 (helper argReg), grm-m95 (value arrives via
variable/table).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the re-measure command in this bead's description: use the plain single ROM dir. All 19 GME titles are at depth 1 of H:/emulators/nes/roms and the harness indexes by sha256, so filenames not matching manifest ids does not matter:

  REALROM_WORK_DIR=$PWD/build/x REALROM_EXTRA_POSTSCRIPT=<Probe>.java     bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --gme --only <ids> H:/emulators/nes/roms

The Z:/git/game-music-extraction/nes/<dir> paths in the description are byte-identical copies and do work, but they are depth-2 so each title needs its own positional arg. I originally believed the H: copies were absent; that was a tooling error on my part -- python does not resolve Git-Bash /h/ paths, so the hash scan silently globbed nothing and looked like 'not present'. A recursive scan with H:/ paths matches 31 of 31 hashes across both manifests. Measurements in this bead are unaffected: the harness verifies the sha256 of the bytes it imported against the manifest pin either way.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
BLMASTER JOINS THIS BEAD (2026-08-04), transferred from grm-8iy.3 which closed as a
measurement artifact. Retitled to match; it is now four titles, not three.

WHY IT MOVED. grm-8iy.3 held blmaster out as 'THE MOST TRACTABLE OF grm-8iy's SIX' on the
strength of 13 constant-arg call sites resolving to only 4 comments -- i.e. a call-site gap,
the grm-nju shape that worked on ff1. That measurement came from a warning-derived helper
population (any function holding any Warning bookmark, no mechanism check), which inflated 5
real helpers into 36 and constArg 2 into 13. The production-aligned mechanism-derived count is
2 constant-arg call sites against 5 bank comments in the golden. Nothing is going missing.

WHAT BLMASTER ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE -- this bead's shape, not grm-nju's:

  title    board   sites  todayComment  todayWarn  callSites  constArg  nonHomeBanks
  cv2      MMC1      20        0            20         5          2          0
  tmnt     MMC1      30        6            24        13          6          3
  wizwarr  AxROM     13        9             4         8          7          0 (all home)
  blmaster MMC1      21        1            20         7          2          1

  (blmaster sites/todayComment/todayWarn from BankReachProbe per grm-8iy.3; callSites/constArg
  from HelperShapeProbe TALLY.mech. Note the golden's bankComments 5 counts call-site comments
  too, so it does not equal todayComment 1.)

20 of 21 direct mechanism stores recover nothing -- the same dominance as cv2 (20/20) and
tmnt (24/30). Its 7 reachable call sites are too few to carry the title even if all resolved,
which is precisely this bead's thesis.

RULED OUT FOR BLMASTER, DO NOT RE-DERIVE:
  - grm-nju's relay shapes: viaThunkOrTrampoline=0, midBodyEntry=0.
  - grm-mu7 (helper argReg clobbered by prologue): constArgRegMatch=2, constArgRegMismatch=0,
    constArgRegMixed=0. Both constant args match the helper's own store register.
  - Site discovery: sites.total 21, orphan 0, invisible-reachable 0.
  - Consumer-side gating: BankConsumerProbe finds 18 consumers of 8000-bfff, 3 direct flow refs
    from the fixed bank; control.fixedToFixed.flow 963 proves the fixed bank is real code.
  - Missing overlay space.

ADVANTAGE AS A HAND-RE SUBJECT: blmaster's helper set is small and now known exactly -- 5
mechanism-derived helper functions, 7 reachable call sites. That is a far smaller surface than
cv2's or tmnt's chains, so the def-use question this bead asks can be answered exhaustively
rather than by sampling.

CARRIED OVER FROM grm-8iy.3, the one datum that survived it: the single fully-known non-home
bank, ec53 prg_bank=5, dies two instructions later -- 'BANKCONSUME walk ec53 steps=2
stop=UNKNOWN'. That is a state-LIFETIME question rather than a value-recovery one, and it is
the same failure mode as tmnt's three known banks reaching consumers=0. Worth treating as a
shared sub-question of this bead rather than a per-title quirk.

RELATED, AND UPGRADED BY THIS FINDING: grm-lwu. blmaster's 90 warnings split
switchUnknown=22 / violation=66 / other=2, and those violation bookmarks sit on 32 functions
that write no mechanism at all. grm-lwu records ~80 of the 90 as 'requires mirroring known on
entry', a PRG-irrelevant field. That noise channel is what manufactured grm-8iy.3's phantom
population -- so grm-lwu is a correctness problem, not a cosmetic one.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
BLMASTER DEF-USE PASS, HAND-DERIVED 2026-08-04/05 (Chris). This is the value-flow shape this
bead asked for and no probe produced. It answers blmaster; the method transfers to cv2/tmnt/wizwarr.

=== 1. THE HELPER SET IN grm-8iy.3 WAS WRONG; THE MECH POPULATION WAS RIGHT ===

grm-8iy.3 named blmaster's helpers as e63c, e678, e68c, eb98, f1ca. Hand inspection shows eb98
and f1ca contain NO mechanism store at all -- eb98 is pure JSRs (to e664 CHR0, e650 CHR1, e63c
PRG), and f1ca's apparent writes belong to a different routine merged into it by a function-
boundary error (filed separately, see section 7). Two writers that list never mentioned DO exist:
e650 and e664.

  ACTUAL MECHANISM-WRITING SET (5, matching TALLY.mech helperFuncs=5):
    e63c  $FFFF PRG    5x STA/LSR serial shift    arg in A from caller
    e650  CHR1         5x STA/LSR                 arg in A from caller
    e664  CHR0         5x STA/LSR                 arg in A from caller
    e678  $9FFF CTRL   5x STA/LSR                 arg in A from caller
    e68c  $FFFF        LDA #$80; STA; RTS         NO ARGUMENT (constant body), MMC1 reset
    fff4  $FFF4        INC (RMW)                  NO ARGUMENT, self-INC reset (grm-4kc idiom)

  Partition confirmed against TALLY.delta (both=4, mechOnly=1) and the probe's per-function tag:
  mechOnly={e68c} -- it resolves cleanly so carries no Warning bookmark -- and
  both={e63c,e650,e664,e678}. eb98 and f1ca are 2 of the 32 warnOnly phantoms.

=== 2. THE ARGUMENT PATH: WHY RECOVERY SEES NOTHING ===

blmaster routes essentially all PRG switching through ONE argument-marshalling wrapper, e61b,
which is NOT itself a mechanism writer:

    caller: LDA #5  --JMP-->  e61b: STA $DB  --JSR e627-->  e63c: 5x STA/LSR $FFFF

Three independent reasons recovery fails, any one sufficient:
  (a) The constant is TWO FRAMES from the store. Recovery looks for an immediate adjacent to a
      call into a HELPER; e61b is a wrapper, so df07's 'LDA #5' is adjacent to the wrong thing.
  (b) Five of twelve call sites reach e61b by JMP (tail call), not JSR. Consistent with
      TALLY.mech tailCall=0 -- the tail calls land on e61b, which is not in the mech set.
  (c) The value transits ZP $DB between frames.

THIS IS BIONIC'S SHAPE (grm-nju: 'argument passed through RAM shadow $65 across a JMP') WITH A
DIFFERENT VARIABLE. grm-8iy.3 ruled grm-nju out on viaThunkOrTrampoline=0/midBodyEntry=0. That
measurement was correct but narrow: those flags detect Ghidra thunks and ONE-INSTRUCTION JMP
trampolines. e61b is neither -- it is a real multi-instruction function entered by JMP. The
shape fell between the two detectors. Widening the relay rule to 'tail-JMP into a non-mechanism
wrapper' is the fix, and it is NOT the same change grm-nju made.

=== 3. ALL 12 CALL SITES INTO e61b ===

  site   reach  arg class            value   notes
  c55f   JSR    immediate            0       home
  c57a   JSR    immediate            0       home
  e2c3   JSR    immediate            2       NON-HOME
  df07   JMP    immediate            5       NON-HOME
  e694   JMP    immediate (relay)    0       home; STA $D3 then JMP; from c32e after LDA #0
  ea41   JSR    computed (4x LSR)    varies  inside FUN_ea3a; see section 5
  cc6a   JMP    RAM load $D3         --      restore
  df0c   JMP    RAM load $D3         --      restore
  e304   JSR    RAM load $D3         --      restore
  e9cb   JSR    RAM load $D3         --      restore
  e9ff   JSR    RAM load $D3         --      restore
  f026   JMP    RAM load $D3         --      restore

  Tally: 5 immediate, 1 computed, 6 shadow-fed. Reach 7 JSR / 5 JMP.
  Plus ec53 (imm 5) and ec5b ($DB) calling e63c directly from inside eb98.

=== 4. TWO SHADOWS, AND A GAP IN grm-mej.2's DISCOVERY RULE ===

  $DB -- the LIVE bank. Written by e61b on every entry, immediately before reaching e63c.
  $D3 -- DUAL ROLE, same address, opposite directions of information flow:
         as INPUT (a requested bank) at c251, e692, c9ba;
         as SAVE SLOT (a copy of $DB stashed across a region) at e9bb, e9d5.

  $D3 WRITERS:
    c251   immediate 0            home; then JSR dec2 (df05 -> bank 5, JSR bfe5, restore)
    e692   immediate 0 (relay)    home; from c32e LDA #0
    c9ba   SET-VALUED {4,6}       see section 5 -- the only high-value one
    e9bb   copy from $DB          save slot; restored at end of e9b8 via LDA $D3 -> e61b
    e9d5   copy from $DB          same idiom, different callees

  GRM-MEJ.2 SPEC GAP. Its write-through-shadow discovery rule scans THE MECHANISM-WRITE SITE'S
  OWN BASIC BLOCK backward for a ST<r> S matching the stored register. That rule finds $DB
  (e61b stores A to $DB right before reaching e63c) but can NEVER find $D3, which is written in
  five different functions, none containing a mechanism write. blmaster needs a SECOND discovery
  route: a variable loaded into the argument register immediately before a call to a bank-switch
  WRAPPER. Recording this against grm-mej.2 as a design input.

  The e9bb/e9d5 pairs are grm-mej.3's save/restore idiom via a MEMORY slot rather than the
  stack -- covered by that bead's 'cross-block memory forwarding' half.

=== 5. c9a4/c9ba IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE SITE AND NEEDS FOUR THINGS AT ONCE ===

Non-home banks inventoried: 2 (e2c3), 5 (df07, ec53, dec2), 4 and 6 (c9ba). The first three are
single sites worth a few hundred bytes. c9ba is different in KIND: it selects a bank, then reads
POINTERS FROM $8000 and dispatches through an indirect jump -- the classic banked-dispatch
idiom, where one recovered bank yields as many entry points as the table has entries. It is the
only thing found in blmaster with the shape to move instrs.inOverlay meaningfully.

  FUN_c9a4:
      LDX #$40
      LDA $14
      AND #$08
      BEQ c9ae        ; skips ONLY the next instruction
      LDX #$60
    c9ae:
      TXA
      PHA
      JSR ea3a        ; body does 4x LSR at ea41, then JSR e61b -> bank 4 or 6
      PLA
      LSR A x4
      AND #$0F
      STA $D3         ; = c9ba; records the same bank ea3a just selected
      ; ... pointer resolution from $8000, indirect jump

  NOTE the $40/$60 values are NOT an attempt to set bank $40/$60 (which would mask to 0):
  ea3a unpacks them with 4x LSR before switching, and the post-PLA 4x LSR/AND #$0F is the same
  unpack applied to the saved copy. The two agree. Nothing sets bank 0 here.

  FOUR SEPARATE UNIMPLEMENTED THINGS, ALL REQUIRED:
    (i)   SET-VALUED BANK STATE. The BEQ skips only 'LDX #$60'; both paths MERGE at c9ae, so X
          is {$40,$60} at the merge and single-valued dataflow must call it unknown. Filed
          separately -- this is not blmaster-specific.
    (ii)  PHA/PLA STACK PAIRING across the JSR ea3a -- grm-mej.3's first half, exactly.
    (iii) 4x LSR + AND #$0F mask algebra on the recovered value.
    (iv)  The $D3 shadow with the section-4 second discovery route.
  Any one missing and c9ba recovers nothing. This is why blmaster's best site is also its hardest.

=== 6. RULED OUT / CORRECTED, DO NOT RE-DERIVE ===

  - ea41's OTHER callers (cc74, d97c) load A from tables that are CHR DATA copied to the PPU,
    not code bank selectors. Deprioritised as a disassembly source. c9a4 is a third caller of
    ea3a and is the one that matters.
  - PRG MODE 3 holds throughout: nothing writes MMC1 CONTROL except the fff4 INC reset and
    f25f's e678 call with A=#$1E (4K CHR, PRG mode 3, vertical mirror). So $8000-BFFF is the
    switchable 16K window and $C000-FFFF is fixed to the last bank.
  - HOME BANK for $8000-BFFF is 0: the RESET routine at f23b JMPs to c24f, which immediately
    sets $D3 to 0. Consequence: the three 'LDA #0' call sites (c55f, c57a, e694) resolve
    CORRECTLY to home and retarget nothing. Do not read them as failures.
  - grm-mu7 ruled out: constArgRegMatch=2, constArgRegMismatch=0, constArgRegMixed=0.

=== 7. FILED SEPARATELY FROM THIS PASS ===
  - Function-boundary over-extension merging the RESET routine into FUN_f1ca.
  - No-argument helpers (e68c) reporting helperArgReg=A and a spurious unrecoverable-arg warning.
  - Set-valued bank state at a pre-switch merge.
