title: Jump-table size recovery: a737 table over-read by 239 bytes plants ~32 spurious code seeds (megaman)
description:
Ghidra's decompiler switch recovery over-reads an indexed jump table on megaman (UxROM, bank 5)
and manufactures ~32 bogus COMPUTED_JUMP targets, which act as spurious disassembly seeds at
arbitrary byte offsets. This is the ROOT CAUSE of grm-g73's flaky golden; that bead is the
symptom and depends on this one.

THE CASE, measured from the ROM (H:/emulators/nes/roms/MEGAMAN.NES, bank 5 file offset 0x14010):

  PRG_LO_B5:a734  JMP ($a737)          -- 3-byte indirect jump
  PRG_LO_B5:a737  the address table    -- REAL extent: 8 entries, 16 bytes, a737..a746
                  a747 a76d a784 a7a1 a7cd a7fa a827 a893   (all sane, all in-window)

Ghidra instead read to a835 -- 255 bytes, 239 PAST the end -- straight through the code the table
dispatches to, reinterpreting instruction bytes as little-endian addresses. All 40 recovered
COMPUTED_JUMP targets map back to even offsets in a737..a835. ~120 garbage values were produced;
the 40 that happened to land in the $8000-$BFFF bank window became references.

Signature of the garbage: "targets" one byte apart -- a960/a961/a963/a964, a9a7/a9a8/a9a9,
8502/8503. Real dispatch tables do not do that.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE TITLE. Every bogus target is a disassembly seed at an arbitrary offset,
and 6502 instruction alignment is 1, so every byte is a legal instruction start. A spurious seed
and the legitimate flow produce two different, self-consistent decodings of the same bytes, and
whichever arrives first wins permanently (Disassembler :489). That is exactly grm-g73's
bistability, and it corrupts real disassembly regardless of which side wins.

NOT OURS. grep -rE 'COMPUTED_JUMP|JumpTable|createJumpTable|switchTable' over src/main/java finds
nothing. Source is Ghidra's DecompilerSwitchAnalysisCmd (:126,133,136 -- removes refs, labels,
disassembles table targets). BoardBankAnalyzer.retargetReferences only re-homes them into the
bank overlay, which is why they present as PRG_LO_B5-to-PRG_LO_B5.

NO CONFIGURATION WORKAROUND. Forcing every thread pool to 1 (-Dcpu.core.override=1) leaves the
table untouched (still 40 refs), loses ~50 bytes of real disassembly, and does NOT restore
determinism (11/12 runs at 1698/7413, one at 1703/7430). See grm-g73 for the full arm data.

CANDIDATE HEURISTIC, and it is exact on this case: A TABLE CANNOT EXTEND PAST ITS OWN LOWEST
TARGET. Here min(targets) = a747 and a737 + 8*2 = a747 -- the real table ends precisely where its
first target begins, giving 8 entries with no slack. Cheap to test and needs no per-game data.

Caveat recorded up front (user, 2026-08-02): recovering true table size is genuinely an ART, not
a rule. It depends on the density of target locations and on how any FOLLOWING data or
instructions happen to correspond to plausible program addresses. The lowest-target bound is a
starting point, not a general answer -- it fails whenever a legitimate target sits below the
table, and it says nothing about a table followed by more data rather than by its own targets.
Expect to need several signals combined, and expect to have to decline (leave the table
unrecovered) rather than guess when they disagree.

DIRECTIONS TO EVALUATE, none chosen yet:
  1. Bound the recovered table by the lowest in-window target (above).
  2. Determine whether Ghidra exposes any control over switch-table extent for a language whose
     decompiler cannot bound the index range, or whether the table length can be pinned per site.
  3. Per-game descriptor hint (grm-hb6.11 vocabulary): express "the table at a737 has 8 entries"
     as curated per-title data. Heaviest, but it is the mechanism this repo already has for
     exactly this class of per-title fact.
  4. Whether disabling Decompiler Switch Analysis for 6502 is a net win or loses real recovery.

TOOLING ALREADY IN PLACE: tools/banktest/DeterminismProbe.java emits every overlay instruction
(address + length) and every ref into an overlay, unbounded and sorted, attachable via
REALROM_EXTRA_POSTSCRIPT at no extra import cost. That is what localized this; use it to evaluate
any fix.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION + SHARPENING, from decoding the actual dispatch (bank 5, file offset 0x14010).
This bead's description says the jump is `JMP ($a737)`. IT IS NOT. The real code is:

  a720  AA        TAX
  a721  0A        ASL A            ; index * 2
  a722  A8        TAY
  a723  F0 05     BEQ  a72a
  a725  B5 6A     LDA  $6A,X
  a727  D0 01     BNE  a72a
  a729  60        RTS
  a72a  B9 37 A7  LDA  $A737,Y     ; table LOW byte
  a72d  85 04     STA  $04
  a72f  B9 38 A7  LDA  $A738,Y     ; table HIGH byte
  a732  85 05     STA  $05
  a734  6C 04 00  JMP  ($0004)     ; indirect through ZERO PAGE $04/$05
  a737  47 a7 6d a7 84 a7 a1 a7 cd a7 fa a7 27 a8 93 a8    ; 8 entries, 16 bytes
  a747  A2 02     LDX  #$02        ; first target -- code starts here

So the jump is a ZERO-PAGE INDIRECT (`JMP ($0004)`), and the table base is not an operand of the
jump at all -- it is reached only by tracing the two `LDA $A737,Y` / `LDA $A738,Y` loads that
stage the pointer into $04/$05. Ghidra traced that correctly and found base a737; what it could
not do is bound Y.

THIS IS A LO/HI INTERLEAVED TABLE, stride 2: low bytes at a737,a739,... and high bytes at
a738,a73a,... Ghidra sees TWO bases one byte apart (a737 and a738), which is worth keeping in
mind for any fix -- the "table" is one 16-byte region indexed by two loads, not two tables.

THE DECISIVE POINT FOR THIS BEAD: THERE IS NO BOUNDS CHECK. No CMP #$08, no BCS, nothing. The
BEQ/`LDA $6A,X`/BNE at a723-a729 special-cases index 0 and tests a parallel zero-page byte; it
does not constrain the index range. The table's length of 8 is a CALLER-SIDE INVARIANT that
appears nowhere in this function. So no amount of dataflow analysis at this site can recover the
count -- exactly the "identifying true table size is an art" case (user, 2026-08-02). Any
correct answer here must come from a STRUCTURAL signal, not from the index arithmetic.

Which is why the lowest-target bound is worth testing first: min(target) = a747 = a737 + 8*2,
i.e. the table ends exactly where its own first target begins, with zero slack. On this case the
structural signal is available and exact even though the dataflow signal does not exist.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
FOUR SITES, NOT ONE -- AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME SHAPE. megaman's bank 5 has four COMPUTED_JUMP
sources, together carrying 184 of the 1704 overlay refs (~11%):

  site   table  stride  bound present in code        Ghidra targets   assessment
  a734   a737     2     NONE (caller invariant)            40         real = 8. Badly over-read.
  a380   a383     2     AND #$3F  -> index <= 63           22         bound EXISTS; 22 <= 64,
                                                                       plausibly CORRECT.
  aa38   aa3b     2     NONE (index from RAM $06E0,X)      60         real unknown; over-read
                                                                       likely, extent unproven.
  99b5   99bb     3     linear key search, DEY DEY DEY     62         NOT AN INDEX TABLE.

All four share the staging idiom -- `LDA tbl_lo,r / STA $04 / LDA tbl_hi,r / STA $05 / JMP ($0004)`
-- so the jump operand is always zero page and the table base is only reachable by tracing the
two loads. The differences are what matter:

a380 HAS A BOUND AND GHIDRA MAY BE RIGHT. `LDA $5F / AND #$3F / ASL A / TAX` caps the index at 63,
so up to 64 entries; 22 distinct in-window targets is consistent with a correct recovery over a
table with repeated entries. Do not "fix" this one without evidence.

99b5 IS THE INTERESTING FAILURE -- STRIDE 3, NOT 2. It is a key/address SEARCH table of 3-byte
records (key, lo, hi) walked BACKWARD by `CMP $99BB,Y / BEQ / DEY DEY DEY / BPL`, defaulting to
entry 0 via `LDY #$00`. Decoded at stride 3 every entry is sane:
    n=0 key=19 -> 99eb   n=1 key=27 -> 9a6a   n=2 key=32 -> 9a06   n=3 key=36 -> 9a49
    n=4..9 keys 4c,4d,4e,4f,50,51 all -> 9a9d
Decoded at STRIDE 2, which is what a table-of-addresses assumption produces:
    n=0 -> 99eb (in)  n=1 -> 6a27 OUT  n=2 -> 329a OUT  n=3 -> 9a06 (in)  n=4 -> 4936 OUT ...
So for this site the recovery is not merely over-long, it is STRUCTURALLY WRONG: the stride
assumption does not match the data layout, and the occasional in-window hit is coincidence.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX. "Bound the table" is not one problem. At minimum:
  (i)   tables with a real dataflow bound (a380) -- leave alone;
  (ii)  stride-2 index tables with no bound (a734, aa38) -- need a structural bound;
  (iii) non-index tables (99b5) -- need to NOT be treated as index tables at all.
The lowest-target heuristic is exact on a734 (min target a747 == a737 + 8*2, zero slack) but
LOOSE on aa38 (min target aad1 => 75 entries, almost certainly far more than real). So it is a
useful upper bound, not an answer -- consistent with the "this is an art" framing.

UPSTREAM SEARCH (NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra). Confident NEGATIVES: no existing issue about
6502 indirect-jump table over-read; none proposing a lowest-target bound; none about 1-byte
instruction alignment making bogus table entries into valid disassembly seeds. So our case is
not already filed. Relevant existing work:
  * #6189 "Enhance jumptable recognition through user hints" (OPEN, 2024-02-02) -- feature request
    for exactly our need: let the user specify table bounds when Ghidra cannot infer them. No
    implementation. This is the natural upstream home for a fix.
  * #6694 Borland switches (OPEN) -- Ghidra emits "completely unrelated references far away from
    the function"; the suggested remedy is to sanity-check that targets lie in/near the function,
    and the stated WORKAROUND IS A MANUAL SwitchOverride. Names the user-facing override we should
    evaluate.
  * #8963 / PR #8964 PowerPC (OPEN) -- three concrete switch-recovery bugs, one of which is
    "targetList not cleared between switches (leaking targets)". Worth ruling in/out here given we
    have four sites in one bank; NOTE it does not explain a734, whose 40 targets all map to even
    offsets within a737..a835, i.e. genuine over-read of its OWN table, not leakage.
  * #8049 (OPEN) -- Ghidra does not validate that recovered targets land in sensible/executable
    regions; same family.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
HEURISTIC REFINED AND TESTED -- and it discriminates correctly on all four sites.

Refinement (user, 2026-08-02): the signal is not "lowest target" but "THE FIRST ENTRY POINTS TO
THE BYTE JUST PAST THE END OF THE TABLE" -- a very common but NOT universal 6502 idiom. That is
strictly better because it is SELF-CHECKING: entry[0] fixes N directly (N = (entry[0] - base) /
stride), and you can then VALIDATE by decoding all N entries and asking whether each is a
plausible code address. A high proportion of implausible entries falsifies the assumption, so the
heuristic can be applied speculatively and withdrawn safely.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE TEST ITSELF, which changes a verdict: the first pass treated only
$8000-$BFFF (the switchable window) as valid. On UxROM $C000-$FFFF is the FIXED bank and is
equally valid code, so a dispatch table may legitimately point there. With the correct
$8000-$FFFF window:

  site   base   stride  N implied by entry[0]   entries valid    verdict
  a734   a737     2              8                8/8  (100%)   ACCEPT
  aa38   aa3b     2             75               75/75 (100%)   ACCEPT
  99b5   99bb     3             16               16/16 (100%)   ACCEPT
  a380   a383     2            451              193/451 ( 43%)  REJECT

Every verdict is right:
  * a734 -> 8, and 8 is the independently verified truth. The heuristic catches THE defect.
  * a380 -> correctly REJECTED. This site has a real dataflow bound (`AND #$3F`, index <= 63), so
    451 is absurd and the validation says so. Dataflow bound wins where one exists.
  * aa38 -> ACCEPTED at 75 entries, all 75 plausible.
  * 99b5 -> ACCEPTED at 16 entries at stride 3.

WHICH RETRACTS AN EARLIER CLAIM IN THIS BEAD: aa38 is NOT over-read. The previous comment listed
it as "over-read likely, extent unproven" on the strength of its 60 targets. With a genuine
75-entry table, 60 distinct targets landing in the switchable bank is consistent -- the remainder
point into the FIXED bank, which DeterminismProbe does not count because that region is not an
overlay space. So the probe's per-site target counts UNDERCOUNT for any table that also targets
$C000-$FFFF, and must not be read as the table's size. Same caution applies to 99b5 (62) and
a380 (22).

SO THE DEFECT NARROWS TO a734 ALONE among these four: 40 overlay targets against a real table of
8. The other three are plausibly correct or differently-shaped, and a fix must leave them alone --
which the heuristic does.

FAILURE MODE IS SAFE. When the idiom does not hold (table not immediately followed by its own
first target; a target below the table; table followed by unrelated data), validation rejects and
you fall back to the dataflow bound if there is one, or decline to bound at all. It never has to
guess. That is the property that makes a fallible heuristic usable here.

STILL TO ESTABLISH: whether this can be applied at all from where we sit -- i.e. whether a table's
extent can be pinned programmatically so re-analysis honours it (SwitchOverride and friends), or
whether this only ever becomes an upstream change / a per-game descriptor fact. Research pending.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ALGORITHM SETTLED: LOWEST-TARGET FIXPOINT. Supersedes both earlier formulations.

User's second refinement (2026-08-02) is the one that makes it work: the entry pointing just past
the table need NOT be the FIRST entry -- tables occur where some LATER entry is the lowest. So the
rule is not "entry[0] fixes N" but a fixpoint over a running minimum:

    n = 0 ; minTarget = INF
    while base + stride*(n+1) <= minTarget:        # next entry's BYTES must stay below the
        e = decode(base, n)                        #   lowest target seen so far
        if not plausible(e): break                 # plausibility guard (in $8000-$FFFF here)
        minTarget = min(minTarget, e)
        n += 1

It grows the table one entry at a time and stops as soon as the next entry's own bytes would
collide with the lowest target found so far. Subsumes the first-entry idiom, tolerates
out-of-order tables, and needs no upper bound supplied in advance.

RESULT ON ALL FOUR megaman SITES:

  site   stride  N     lowest target   stop reason
  a734     2      8    a747 (entry 0)  entry 8's bytes would reach a747     <- VERIFIED CORRECT
  a380     2      8    a393 (ENTRY 1)  entry 8's bytes would reach a393
  99b5     3     16    99eb (entry 0)  entry 16's bytes would reach 99eb
  aa38     2     75    aad1 (entry 0)  entry 75's bytes would reach aad1

a380 IS THE CASE THAT PROVES THE REFINEMENT. Its entry[0] is a709, but its entry[1] is a393 --
and a393 is exactly a383 + 8*2, the byte immediately after an 8-entry table. The first-entry rule
computed N=451 there and had to be rejected by validation; the fixpoint gets N=8 directly and
cleanly. Without the user's point this site would have had no answer.

AND IT RETRACTS THE `AND #$3F` READING. That mask bounds the index to 0..63, and the previous
comment concluded a380 therefore "plausibly correct" at 22 targets and should be left alone. The
fixpoint says the table is 8 entries; the mask is simply OVER-PERMISSIVE -- a cheap guard, not the
true count. So a380 is ALSO over-read (22 targets vs 8 real). A dataflow bound is an UPPER bound
and must not be mistaken for the answer.

REVISED SCORECARD -- three of the four sites are over-read, not one:

  site   Ghidra targets   fixpoint N   over-read?
  a734        40               8       YES  (verified independently)
  a380        22               8       YES
  99b5        62              16       YES (and wrong stride besides -- 3, not 2)
  aa38        60              75       NO   (probe undercounts; extra targets are in the
                                             FIXED $C000-$FFFF bank, not an overlay space)

So a734 is not a lone defect -- it is the one whose ground truth we happened to verify by hand.
The same over-read is present at a380 and 99b5.

CAVEATS TO CARRY FORWARD:
 * The fixpoint assumes the table is followed by code that some entry targets. It fails when a
   table is followed by unrelated data, when every target lies below the table, or when the table
   is not contiguous. It must therefore stay speculative, with the plausibility guard and a
   willingness to DECLINE rather than guess -- the failure mode has to be "no bound recovered",
   never "wrong bound asserted".
 * It needs the correct STRIDE. 99b5 is stride 3 (key,lo,hi records); assuming 2 there produces
   garbage regardless of any length bound. Stride recovery is a separate sub-problem.
 * Plausibility must include the whole mapped code range. Restricting to the switchable bank
   alone mis-rejected aa38 at 97%.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
UPSTREAM MECHANISM PINNED EXACTLY, and there IS a practical local lever. Ghidra 12.1.2 source.

HOW THE COUNT IS DECIDED. Not a memory scan. The entry count is jrange->getSize() -- the
cardinality of a CircleRange (integer interval WITH A STRIDE) computed for the normalized switch
variable (JumpBasic::getTableSize, jumptable.hh:415; calcRange, jumptable.cc:1135-1171). The
table bytes are then read by EMULATING the address computation once per value in that range
(JumpBasic::buildAddresses, jumptable.cc:1451-1477) -- a loop with NO validity test in it.

THE DEFECT, and it is a precise off-by-assumption. jumptable.cc:1198-1207 exists to stop exactly
our case:
    // Don't accept a 1-byte switch variable unless there is an explicit guard
    // or a table lookup between the byte and the indirect jump.
    // "goto *(#const + byteVar)" should not be interpreted as 256 case switch
    if (sz != 256 || pathMeld.getVarnode(i)->getSize()!=1 || pathMeld.isLoadInPath(i)) {...accept...}
It tests `sz != 256`. But sz is the range CARDINALITY, which is already divided by the stride.
A DOUBLED index -- the universal 6502 idiom for a 2-byte table -- makes the NZMASK low bit
known-clear, so getStride (jumptable.cc:449-461) returns 2 and
    CircleRange(0, 0, /*bytes=*/1, /*stride=*/2).getSize() == 128
128 != 256, so THE GUARD DOES NOT FIRE, and no explicit guard and no LOAD-in-path is required.

CONFIRMED, NOT INFERRED, FOR a734. The research could only infer "1-byte stride-2 unguarded
variable" from the byte arithmetic. The decoded dispatch settles it -- a720 is
    TAX / ASL A / TAY / ... / LDA $A737,Y / LDA $A738,Y
Y is a 1-byte register holding A<<1: a doubled 1-byte index with no bound anywhere. Exactly the
shape that slips past the sz!=256 test. And the arithmetic closes: 128 values 0,2,...,254, each
emulated as a737+val reading 2 bytes, covers a737..a836 = 256 bytes against a real table of 16.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. JumpBasic::sanityCheck (jumptable.cc:1589-1628) truncates at the first
"unreasonable" address, but its test is |addr0 - addr_i| > 0xffff followed by a data-availability
probe. IN A 16-BIT ADDRESS SPACE THAT DIFFERENCE CAN NEVER EXCEED 0xffff, so the probe is DEAD
CODE on 6502 and the only thing that can truncate a table here is an entry that is literally
0x0000. That is why 239 bytes of garbage passed unchecked.

Also: max_jumptable_size = 1024 (architecture.cc:1432) and exceeding it REJECTS the model rather
than truncating it. It is settable only via the decompiler option <jumptablemax>; nothing in the
Java tree ever sets it, so it is effectively fixed at 1024 with no script or GUI lever. 128 is
nowhere near it.

NO OVERLAP CHECK EXISTS ANYWHERE. jumptable.cc/.hh, funcdata_block.cc, flow.cc and the Java
analyzer/cmd contain nothing that compares a table's byte extent against its own targets, the
containing function body, or any code unit. The extent is a CONSEQUENCE of the count
(LoadTable::collapseTable, jumptable.cc:60-111), never a constraint on it. So our lowest-target
fixpoint is PURELY ADDITIVE -- it conflicts with nothing Ghidra checks.

THE PRACTICAL LEVER -- a table can be pinned in program state and re-analysis honours it verbatim:
  (a) CHEAPEST: DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer skips any site that already carries a computed reference
      (DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer.java:413-422, `if (referenceType.isComputed()) return null;`).
      So simply creating our OWN 8 correct COMPUTED_JUMP refs on the JMP at a734 makes
      re-analysis leave the site alone entirely.
  (b) AUTHORITATIVE: JumpTable.writeOverride(Function) (JumpTable.java:320-348) writes plain
      USER_DEFINED CodeSymbols into <function>/override/jmp_<opAddr>/{switch, case_0..case_n}.
      On re-analysis JumpBasicOverride::buildAddresses (jumptable.cc:1997-2001) is literally
      `addresstable = addrtable;` -- our exact list -- and JumpTable::sanityCheck returns early
      for overrides (:2316-2317), so it is never truncated or re-validated. Shipped user path is
      the script Ghidra/Features/Decompiler/ghidra_scripts/SwitchOverride.java; there is NO
      right-click decompiler action for it in 12.1.2.
  (c) NARROW: marking the vector bytes read-only forces the single-value path
      (jumptable.cc:1241-1248). Applies to a genuinely bare JMP (abs), not to our staged form.

RULED OUT as the culprit: AddressTableAnalyzer / AddressTable (the classic scan-while-valid code)
is INERT on 6502 -- its value reader handles pointer sizes 3/4/8 only and 6502's default pointer
size is 2, so getEntry returns null immediately (AddressTable.java:1084-1117).

DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer registers exactly ONE option, "Analysis Decompiler Timeout (sec)"
(:85-88). There is no table-size or validity option; nothing on the analyzer can bound the count.

TWO ACTIONABLE PATHS NOW EXIST:
  1. LOCAL: pre-create correct COMPUTED_JUMP refs (and/or a JumpTable override) for sites where
     the lowest-target fixpoint accepts, before DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer runs. Needs a priority
     earlier than it. This is implementable in this extension today.
  2. UPSTREAM: the sz!=256 guard should account for stride -- a 1-byte variable with stride 2
     covering the full byte range is exactly as unbounded as stride 1. Small, well-localized, and
     no existing issue covers it (see the upstream search comment). Good candidate to file.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
NO ANALYZER OPTION TUNES THIS -- checked, because it is the obvious first question and the answer
is counterintuitive (there ARE switch-table options, they are just on a different code path).

WHAT EXISTS: OperandReferenceAnalyzer ("Operand Reference Analyzer") registers
    "Switch Table References"      default FALSE  (OperandReferenceAnalyzer.java:108, :1271)
    "Address Table Alignment"      default 1      (:109, :1273)
    "Address Table Minimum Size"
    "Create Address Tables"        default true
    "Respect Execute Flag"
These drive the AddressTable scanner (:720, :773) -- the classic scan-while-pointers-look-valid
recovery. IRRELEVANT to this bead for two independent reasons: the switch option is OFF by
default, and AddressTable is INERT on 6502 anyway (AddressTable.getEntry's value reader handles
pointer sizes 3/4/8 only; 6502's default pointer size is 2, so it returns null on entry 0).

WHAT PRODUCED OUR BUG: DecompilerSwitchAnalyzer, whose registerOptions (:85-88) declares EXACTLY
ONE option -- "Analysis Decompiler Timeout (sec)". No size, aggressiveness or validity knob.

AND THE DECOMPILER-SIDE CAP IS UNREACHABLE FROM GHIDRA: max_jumptable_size (1024,
architecture.cc:1432) is settable only via the decompiler option <jumptablemax>
(options.cc:833-845); nothing in the Java tree ever sets it, and DecompileOptions has no such
field. Effectively frozen at 1024 -- and 128 is nowhere near it regardless.

CONCLUSION: there is no configuration that would have prevented this, which is exactly why the
fix has to be code (grm-b3m upstream, or the local pre-created-refs lever).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: Root cause filed upstream as ghidra#9447 (2026-08-02): https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra/issues/9447 . Our PR to fix it is tracked as grm-b3m.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SECOND TITLE INSTANCE: contra (human def-use pass, 2026-08-09). This bead's evidence has been
megaman-only; it is not a one-ROM curiosity.

Contra has a switch table at 8492 whose recovery OVER-READS, and the fallout is visible in the
blessed golden as two of its ten bank warnings:
  8efc  data mistakenly disassembled as code, purely because of the 8492 overrun
  811a  a call site that exists only because it picked up 8efc's bogus reference; its apparent
        target FUN_PRG_LO_B1__8259 is likewise cruft
The human-research list had 811a down as "a THIRD helper living in a switched window, worth
confirming is real before tracing it." It is not real. Do not trace it.

WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING HERE. It confirms the failure is generic to the 6502 dispatch idiom
rather than specific to megaman's bank-5 table, which strengthens the upstream case in grm-b3m.
It also shows the SECOND-ORDER cost concretely: every bogus target is a disassembly seed, and here
those seeds manufactured a plausible-looking bank-switch helper in overlay space that a human was
about to spend a def-use pass on. That is the "heaviest cost is downstream" argument with a
worked example attached.

Contra's 8492 dispatch has NOT been decoded to the level megaman's a720 was (stride, index
provenance, table extent) -- if a second worked case is wanted for the upstream issue text, that
is the cheap next read.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN MEGAMAN. The project owner's 2026-08-15 disassembly pass over
dragonpower found THREE separate over-read jump tables in ONE title, and their phantoms account
for HALF that title's warned bank sites:

  $8F00  real extent $1E (30) entries; the over-read produces the "FUN_8eeb" seed and the
         warned site 8ee4. There is no bank switching anywhere in the region.
  $91AF  over-read reinterprets data as code at e3bb -- a warned "mechanism write" that is not
         code.
  $9076  over-read produces BOGUS MID-INSTRUCTION DISASSEMBLY at e906 -- another warned
         "mechanism write" that is not code.

Why this matters beyond one more instance:

1. DENSITY. megaman motivated this bead with one table (a737) and ~32 spurious seeds.
   dragonpower has three tables in a 128 KiB image. This is not a rare pathology.

2. IT MANUFACTURES A FAKE HELPER. The $8F00 over-read is why grm-hum recorded "FUN_8eeb" as a
   co-equal second bank-switch helper alongside FUN_ffbe, and why the human-research list
   carried "Is FUN_8eeb PRG or CHR?" as its highest-payoff open question. The answer is neither:
   it is not code. So the over-read did not merely add noise, it created a phantom entry in the
   project's model of a board's switch engine and sent analysis after it. Same failure mode as
   contra's 8efc/811a -> "FUN_PRG_LO_B1__8259", now seen a second time.

3. IT INFLATES THE HEADLINE METRIC. dragonpower and shenlong sit at 0 refs / 0 bank comments /
   6 warnings. Three of the six are phantoms. The real unresolved population is 3, and one of
   those is the helper's own mechanism write. Any "warnings" count on these titles overstates
   the gap by ~2x until this is fixed -- worth remembering when reading grm-8iy's scorecard.

Add dragonpower to this bead's evidence set alongside megaman. Its three tables are also a
better regression corpus than a737 alone, since they exercise three distinct downstream effects
(spurious function seed, data-as-code, mid-instruction resync).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
FINAL COUNT on the GxROM pair (owner follow-up, 2026-08-15): shenlong's two remaining warned
sites are also over-read phantoms --

  a03f  mid-instruction disassembly from an over-read jump table at $87D0
  d9a9  mid-instruction disassembly from an over-read jump table at $9076

That brings this bead's dragonpower/shenlong evidence to FOUR distinct over-read tables
($8F00, $87D0, $9076, $91AF) producing SIX phantom warned sites across two titles, three per
title -- exactly HALF of each title's warned population.

TWO THINGS WORTH KEEPING:

1. $9076 IS OVER-READ IN BOTH TITLES, at the same table address, yielding different downstream
   garbage (dragonpower e906, shenlong d9a9). The two ROMs share a codebase well beyond the
   $FF88-$FFF9 switch engine the owner byte-compared, so the same table exists in both and the
   over-read reproduces across images. That makes it the best available REGRESSION PAIR for a
   fix here: one root cause, two ROMs, two distinct observable symptoms.

2. EVERY title-unique warned "mechanism write" on both titles -- 4 for 4 -- was this artifact.
   The pre-existing hypothesis those four sites supported (per-bank code switching that bypasses
   the helper) was entirely manufactured by this bug and is now dead. Combined with the fake
   "FUN_8eeb" helper noted in the earlier comment, this bead has now been shown to corrupt the
   project's MODEL of a board's switch engine, not merely its counts, on three separate
   occasions (contra's FUN_PRG_LO_B1__8259, dragonpower's FUN_8eeb, and this four-site
   hypothesis).

Symptom coverage for a fix's acceptance criteria, all four downstream effects now attested:
spurious function seed (8ee4/8eeb), data-as-code (e3bb), and mid-instruction resync (e906,
a03f, d9a9) -- plus megaman's original one-byte-apart bogus COMPUTED_JUMP targets.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEASURED ON A FORK BUILD, 2026-08-15: THIS BEAD'S PHANTOM PREDICTIONS ARE CONFIRMED, AND THE
LOWEST-TARGET FIXPOINT IS NOW THE ONLY LIVE FIX DIRECTION. Full A/B data and the fork
infrastructure are on grm-b3m; recording here what it means for THIS bead.

WHAT WAS TESTED. grm-b3m's stride-aware guard (test span = sz*step against 256 instead of the
count against 256) built into a real decompile.exe and run over all 31 real ROMs, against a
control build proven byte-identical to stock on 29 of 31 dumps.

1. THE PHANTOM PREDICTIONS WERE RIGHT, AND PRECISELY SO. The 2026-08-15 comments here claimed the
   over-read manufactures HALF of dragonpower's and shenlong's warned population. Killing the
   over-read moved both titles from 6 warnings to 2 -- exactly the predicted count. dragonpower's
   removed four are 8ee4 (the fake FUN_8eeb helper), e3bb, e906 and 9913. contra shed its 8efc/
   811a phantoms too (warnings 7->5, refs 298->228, instrs 1044->910). So the "phantom warned
   site" model of this bug is now experimentally verified, not just inferred from hand
   disassembly.

   CAVEAT WORTH A LOOK LATER: 9913 also disappeared, and the human recon notes have 9913 as a
   REAL call site ("ffbe: called from $9913 as first instr of function"). Under this patch that
   may be collateral rather than a phantom. It is not decisive for anything now, but if the
   fixpoint fix ever lands, check that 9913 SURVIVES it.

2. "REJECT THE VARIABLE" IS NOT "BOUND THE TABLE" -- and the difference is most of the corpus.
   Rejecting the scaled byte makes JumpBasic fall back to a far larger range, the model is
   discarded, and the site produces NO targets. Real dispatch dies with the spurious targets:
   megaman instrs 7429->5342 and bankComments 156->119, tmnt refs 44->0 / instrs 103->0,
   rcproam refs 1298->256 / instrs 4810->1275, plus dodge, ff1, lwings, rcransom, ultimaav.
   This bead's DIRECTIONS-TO-EVALUATE list should now be read with that distinction in front of
   it: any fix that works by DECLINING to recover loses more than the over-read costs, on every
   title where the idiom drives real code.

3. WHICH PROMOTES DIRECTION 1 (bound by the lowest-target fixpoint) TO THE FIX. It is the only
   evaluated option that keeps the switch and truncates it, so it can shed dragonpower/shenlong/
   contra's phantoms WITHOUT costing megaman its 2087 instructions. The algorithm is already
   settled in the "ALGORITHM SETTLED: LOWEST-TARGET FIXPOINT" comment above and already scores
   4-for-4 on megaman's sites (a734->8 verified, a380->8, 99b5->16, aa38->75). What is still
   unestablished is unchanged from that comment: WHERE to apply it. The two candidate homes
   remain (a) the local pre-created-COMPUTED_JUMP-refs lever, which needs no fork at all and is
   implementable in this extension today, and (b) upstream inside buildAddresses/sanityCheck.
   The fork now makes (b) cheap to prototype -- ~60s rebuild, ~2min for a 31-ROM arm.

4. AND IT SHARPENS THE UPSTREAM STORY. The guard at jumptable.cc:1198 assumes an unguarded 1-byte
   index means "not really a switch". On 6502 that shape is the NORMAL legitimate table idiom and
   the real count is a caller-side invariant absent from the site -- so the premise fails here,
   which is why fixing the guard's arithmetic makes things worse rather than better. That is a
   more interesting and better-evidenced report than the original off-by-assumption framing, and
   it is the substance worth adding to ghidra#9447 if a maintainer engages.

STATUS: this bead stays open and its root-cause analysis stands unaltered. What changed is that
one of the two actionable paths in the "TWO ACTIONABLE PATHS NOW EXIST" comment (the upstream
guard fix) has been tried and measured, and it is not the answer. The other path is untouched.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
THE LOWEST-TARGET FIXPOINT IS IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED, AND IT WORKS -- WITH ONE UNRESOLVED
TITLE. Second fix attempt of 2026-08-15, after the grm-b3m stride guard was measured and rejected.
Fork branch grm/jumptable-lowest-target, commit 475cf359, built from tag c0f584bf (12.1.2).

WHERE IT LIVES, and this turned out to be the good news. JumpBasic::sanityCheck (jumptable.cc
:1595) is the natural home: it ALREADY exists to "cut off at the first unreasonable address" and
already owns the truncation machinery (addresstable.resize / jrange->truncate / loadpoints.resize).
This bead previously established its existing test is DEAD CODE on 6502 (the |diff| > 0xffff probe
cannot fire in a 16-bit space), so the slot was effectively vacant.

AND THE ENTRY EXTENT DOES NOT HAVE TO BE INFERRED. JumpTable::recoverAddresses calls sanityCheck
BEFORE LoadTable::collapseTable (jumptable.cc:2661-2662), so loadpoints still hold ONE ENTRY PER
LOAD IN EXECUTION ORDER, and loadcounts[i] gives the running count of LOADs consumed through entry
i. So entry i's table bytes are read directly off the LOADs entry i actually performed. NO STRIDE
INFERENCE IS NEEDED -- which retires the "it needs the correct STRIDE" caveat from the ALGORITHM
SETTLED comment above, at least for the implementation. 99b5's stride 3 needs no special handling
because nothing ever assumes 2. Required adding public getAddr()/getSize()/getNum() accessors to
LoadTable, which had none.

SAFETY GUARDS, since this must not regress non-6502 targets:
  * Only runs when loadcounts is non-null -- i.e. only on the path that collected per-entry LOADs.
  * Declines unless minTarget > tableStart, so a table stored ABOVE the code it dispatches to
    (the normal x86 .rodata arrangement) is untouched. This is the guard that makes the rule safe
    to apply unconditionally rather than gated on an architecture.
  * Only ever SHRINKS a table; never widens, never rejects a model outright.

RESULTS (31 real ROMs, vs a control build proven behaviourally identical to the shipped binary;
pass=22 fail=9, against control pass=27 fail=4 and the stride guard's pass=19 fail=12):

  THE PHANTOMS GO, exactly as this bead's 2026-08-15 hand analysis predicted:
    dragonpower  warnings 6 -> 2   (8ee4/FUN_8eeb, 9913, e3bb, e906 all gone)
    shenlong     warnings 6 -> 2
  AND REAL CODE IS RECOVERED, WHICH IS THE PART THE STRIDE GUARD GOT BACKWARDS:
    megaman   refs 1704 -> 1656 (-48, ~the bogus population)  instrs 7429 -> 7471 (+42)
    dodge     refs 2739 -> 2503 (-236)                        instrs 10692 -> 11185 (+493)
    ff1       refs 1847 -> ~1865                              instrs 7382 -> ~7494
  Instructions going UP while refs go DOWN is the signature of the intended effect: bogus targets
  removed, and the spurious disassembly seeds they planted no longer race the legitimate flow, so
  correct decoding wins more bytes than the garbage occupied.
  NO COLLATERAL: tmnt, contra and lwings PASS unchanged. The stride guard took tmnt to 0 refs.

  STILL OPEN -- these are ROM-ground-truth questions, not analysis questions:
   1. rcproam LOSES: refs 1298 -> 931, instrs 4810 -> 4094. This is the documented failure mode of
      the rule -- a legitimate target sitting close below the table bounds it shorter than reality.
      The site is 8068 (a COMPUTED_JUMP into W8000_M0_B0); targets 80a2/80f0/812a/8500/8509 are the
      ones lost. Needs a human read of the dispatch at 8068 to say what the real extent is.
   2. megaman sheds 12 bankComments (156 -> 144), in the 8d1f..8dbf region, all "bank -> 5 via
      RESET". Real losses or comments that were attached to phantom code? Not adjudicated.
   3. rcransom bankComments 38 -> 36; ultimaav refs 225 -> 228 with bankComments 8 -> 7.
   4. contra is UNCHANGED, so the 8492 over-read recorded in this bead's 2026-08-09 comment is NOT
      caught by this rule. One known instance remains unfixed.

A HYPOTHESIS WAS RAISED AND REFUTED, recorded so nobody re-spends it: rcproam's loss was guessed to
come from the per-entry byte extent being the MAX over ALL of an entry's LOADs, so that one
unrelated fixed-address lookup at a high address would bound the table to nothing. A second build
added a per-slot filter (the k-th LOAD of every entry is the same instruction; ignore slots whose
address does not MOVE with the index, since a fixed load is not a table). MEASURED: byte-identical
on 30 of 31 titles, the only mover being ff1, which is bistable anyway. rcproam was UNCHANGED at
931/4094. So the extra loads are not the cause and rcproam's truncation comes from genuine table
LOADs. The filter is kept in the commit but is measurably inert on this corpus and can be dropped
for a smaller upstream diff.

NOT YET SUITABLE FOR UPSTREAM and no golden may be blessed on it: every moved count line is a claim
about a real cartridge, and items 1-3 are exactly the class this project requires a human to
adjudicate. What it IS: the first fix in this bead's history that moves the corpus in the right
direction on both axes at once.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
BOTH BLOCKING QUESTIONS ANSWERED BY HAND, 2026-08-16 (user, disassembler). This retires
docs/human-research-todo.md item 1b in full -- both bullets -- and BOTH ANSWERS FAVOUR THE FIX
(fork branch grm/jumptable-lowest-target, commit 475cf359).

--- Q1: WHAT IS THE REAL EXTENT OF RCPROAM'S JUMP TABLE AT $8068? ---

  "8068: jump table at 806b has 6 entries; first is 8077 which is first addr after table. valid
   targets are 8077, 818a, 8675, 884d (818a is target of three indexes)."

SIX ENTRIES, at $806B (the table proper starts three bytes after the computed-jump site at
$8068). The six slots hold FOUR distinct targets, with $818A repeated three times:

    8077, 818a, 818a, 818a, 8675, 884d      (6 slots, 4 distinct)

*** THE DECISIVE PART: THE FIVE TARGETS THE BOUND STOPS RECOVERING ARE NOT VALID TARGETS. *** The
item recorded them as 80a2, 80f0, 812a, 8500, 8509. Not one appears in the real table. So
rcproam's refs 1298->931 and instrs 4810->4094 are NOT a loss -- they are the removal of code
that was only ever seeded by an over-read past the end of a six-entry table. What was recorded as
"the only clear loss in the corpus" is the fix working, on the very title that looked worst.

CONSEQUENTLY THE DECLINE CONDITION THE ITEM CONTEMPLATED IS NOT NEEDED FOR THIS CASE, and should
not be built on rcproam's evidence. The item's hypothesis was "a legitimate target sits close
below the table, so the rule truncates where it should decline". There is no such target here.
Do not add a decline condition to accommodate rcproam.

NOTE $8077 IS THE FIRST ADDRESS AFTER THE TABLE -- entry 0 points at the byte immediately
following the six entries. That is a self-terminating layout and a genuinely useful corroboration
signal: a table whose lowest target equals its own end is exactly consistent, and it is what the
lowest-target bound is designed to key on. Worth noting as evidence the rule's PREMISE is sound
here, independent of the count.

STILL TO MEASURE (agent work, not human): does the fork build actually recover all four distinct
targets? The answer above settles what the table IS; it does not by itself confirm the bound
computes six rather than truncating further and losing 8675/884d as well. One `--only rcproam`
run against the PATCHED install, checking for refs to 8077/818a/8675/884d, closes that -- and
both env vars are required (grm-k0h, realrom-ab-wrong-install-trap) or it silently measures
stock Ghidra.

--- Q2: ARE MEGAMAN'S 12 SHED BANK COMMENTS REAL LOSSES OR PHANTOMS? ---

  "8d1f-8dbf: all data, no code. overruns at e000 (e0ed, actual length 18), e121 (e2a2, actual
   19), e44e (e55a, actual 10) are the sources of the bad refs."

PHANTOMS. $8D1F-$8DBF IS ALL DATA. The twelve "bank -> 5 (bank=5) via RESET" comments were
attached to instructions that existed only because a bogus jump target seeded disassembly into a
data region. Losing them is the fix working, and bankComments 156->144 is a CORRECTION, not a
regression. This also explains the counts moving against each other (instrs +42 while comments
-12): the fix removes phantom code in one region and recovers real code elsewhere.

BONUS FINDING, AND IT IS THE MORE ACTIONABLE HALF -- THE OVER-READS ARE NAMED, WITH THEIR TRUE
LENGTHS. Three tables, each recorded as "declared/over-read extent (true entry count)":

    e000  over-read to e0ed   true length 18
    e121  over-read to e2a2   true length 19
    e44e  over-read to e55a   true length 10

These are "the sources of the bad refs" on megaman. Note this bead's title case is the a737 table
(over-read by 239 bytes, ~32 spurious code seeds); these three are ADDITIONAL sites on the same
title, so the title's over-read problem is at least four tables, not one. Three exact ground-truth
lengths is a directly usable acceptance set: a correct bound must produce 18 / 19 / 10 at those
three sites. Pin them as test expectations rather than re-deriving them.

--- DISPOSITION ---

Nothing here blocks the bless any longer: both count-line movements the item held it for are now
adjudicated, and both are correct. The remaining gate is the agent-side rcproam confirmation
above, which is measurement rather than judgment. See also grm-eyn's sibling data point: the
grm-pfp GME sweep run the same day found dodge's jump-table-adjacent regions full of WEAK
skip-idiom candidates whose "hidden" instructions are BRK/BVS/SEI -- i.e. more evidence that
over-read regions decode into plausible-looking nonsense.

title: megaman real-ROM dump is intermittently nondeterministic (flaky golden)
description:
Observed while verifying grm-8cq. Four fresh imports of the SAME megaman ROM against the SAME build produced two different dumps:

  3 runs: REALROM count refs.intoOverlay 1704, instrs.inOverlay 7429  (matches the golden -> PASS)
  1 run:  REALROM count refs.intoOverlay 1703, instrs.inOverlay 7431  (-> FAIL)

Every other line was identical; only those two counts moved, and they moved in OPPOSITE directions (one fewer ref, two more instructions).

NOT caused by the probe that was running in three of the four. BankReachProbe is genuinely read-only (grep for disassemble/createFunction/createData/setComment/addReference/createLabel/clearListing finds only comments), it runs as a -postScript AFTER RealRomDump.java has already printed, and two subsequent runs WITH the probe both passed. The one control run without it also passed. So the variable is the analysis, not the observer.

WHY IT MATTERS: a FAIL in this tier may be noise. The whole value of hash-pinned real-ROM goldens is that a diff means a real change, and an intermittent +-1 ref / +-2 instr makes that untrue for this title. It also puts a question mark over history: megaman is the title deliberately held back at a pre-regression golden TWICE (grm-g73, then grm-hum), and it is worth checking whether some of what was read as regression was this. That is a question to answer, NOT a claim -- the recorded regressions may be entirely real.

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP: run 'realrom-test.sh check --only megaman <romdir>' ten times and count the split, to establish the rate and confirm only these two counters move. Then look for an ordering/threading dependency in whatever produces refs.intoOverlay and instrs.inOverlay -- a set iterated in hash order, or an analyzer that races with another. Worth checking whether other titles flake at a lower rate; ironsword reproduced byte-identically twice earlier in the same session, so this may be specific to megaman's shape rather than universal.

Rate observed: 1 in 4. Small sample -- do not treat as the true rate.
close_reason: Duplicate of grm-g73 (same defect: megaman real-ROM dump bistable, refs -1 / instrs +2 in opposite directions). h4k's new evidence -- the 3/1 rate and the BankReachProbe exoneration -- has been merged into grm-g73 as a comment. Work continues there.

title: Bank argument passed through a RAM shadow + thunk defeats value recovery (bionic)
description:
Why Bionic Commando resolves ZERO banks despite every switch site being found. Verified against the real ROM with a HelperShapeProbe run (function boundaries, callers, and pre-site instructions are measured, not inferred).

STRUCTURE (all confirmed):
- FUN_dca8 (body dca8-dcbd): 'LDA $65' at dca8, then 5x ('STA $E000'; 'LSR A') at dcaa/dcae/dcb2/dcb6/dcba -> target 3 = prg_bank.
- FUN_dcc3 (body dcc3-dcd6): 5x ('STA $9FFF'; 'LSR A') at dcc3..dcd3 -> target 0 = mirroring + prg_mode.
- RESET (ffe0-ffe6): 'INC $FFE1' -- separate issue, see the RMW-reset bead.
- Per the user's reversing: dcbe stores A to shadow $65 then JMPs to dca8; dcaa sets the bank from A directly.

SITE DISCOVERY IS NOT THE PROBLEM. All 11 sites are found and correctly classified as two unrolled serial chains plus the reset. This is a grm-m95 VALUE-RECOVERY failure, NOT the grm-2yx site-discovery shape -- correcting what grm-8iy originally said about this title.

WRITES 2-5 ARE ALREADY FINE: SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy's precededByLsrA shortcut gives them bit7 known-clear by construction. Only write 1 of each chain needs the general backward scan.

THE BLOCKER, in two layers:
1. THE VALUE CROSSES A FUNCTION BOUNDARY THROUGH RAM. Write 1 at dcaa is preceded by 'LDA $65' (dca8), and $65's producer is 'STA $65' inside dcbe -- a DIFFERENT function reached by JMP. StoredValueScanner.forwardedStoreValue is deliberately local: it ends the walk at a basic-block boundary, at a control-flow join, at any call, and at the caller-env entry ('RegisterEnv describes a call site's REGISTERS, and says nothing whatever about memory'). grm-mej.1 delivered LOCAL store-to-load forwarding; this needs it across a tail-call/fallthrough edge.
2. THE CALL PATH IS THUNKED. The game does not call the helper directly: FUN_c000 does 'JSR $d6bb' and 'JSR $d751' into a jump table of 3-byte thunks (d6bb JMP dca8, d6c1 JMP da21, d6e2 JMP dcaa, d73c JMP e17f, d751 JMP dcc3, d7cc JMP dcbe). findHelpers only models functions that CONTAIN a switch site, so the thunks and dcbe are invisible to it; composeTailCalls repairs a helper that tail-CALLS, it does not promote a non-helper trampoline into one. Note d6e2 jumps to dcaa directly, PAST the LDA -- that path really does take the bank in A.

TWO CANDIDATE FIXES:
(a) Extend forwarding across a tail-call/fallthrough edge so dcbe's 'STA $65' reaches dca8's 'LDA $65'.
(b) Narrower and a better fit for the existing machinery: recognise the argument-relay idiom 'STA <zp>; JMP helper' where the helper's first act is 'LDA <same zp>', and model the trampoline with argReg='A'. Ordinary call-site recovery then works, provided it can also see through a one-instruction JMP thunk.

UNPROVEN AND WORTH CHECKING FIRST: whether the callers actually pass CONSTANTS. If A at 'JSR $d6bb' is itself computed, this plumbing buys nothing for bionic. Measure before building.

LIKELY BLAST RADIUS: bionic's 11 sites sit in one centralised routine, unlike megaman2's 324 sites spread from $8026 (inline switching, much of which resolves directly). A single centralised bank-switch routine reached through a shadow cell is a plausible house style, and cv2/blmaster/ff1/tmnt are MMC1 titles that also resolve zero overlay instructions -- check whether they share the idiom before sizing the work.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MEASURED REFINEMENT (HelperShapeProbe, real ROM) -- the user's instinct was right and it changes the recommended fix.

    site  dcaa  STA $e000  functionAt=none  label=LAB_dcaa  incomingFlow=[d6e2(JMP), dcc0(JMP)]
    site  dcc3  STA $9fff  functionAt=FUN_dcc3            incomingFlow=[d751(JMP)]
    entry dca8  LDA $0065  functionAt=FUN_dca8            incomingFlow=[d6bb(JMP)]

CORRECTION to the reversing recorded above: 'STA $65' at dcbe is TWO bytes, so dcc0 is the next instruction and it jumps to DCAA, not dca8. dcbe therefore stores the shadow AND branches PAST the reload, leaving the bank in A. Both jump paths into dcaa (d6e2, dcc0) carry the bank in A; only the fallthrough from dca8 sources it from $65. So dcaa genuinely is 'entry taking bank in A'.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE: dcaa has a label and two incoming jumps but functionAt=NONE -- Ghidra kept it mid-body. findHelpers uses getFunctionContaining(site), which yields FUN_dca8, whose entry is dca8 -- and dca8's first instruction 'LDA $65' clobbers A immediately. So the helper model describes the argument at the WRONG entry, and the real A-taking entry is not a helper at all.

THE JOIN REFUSAL IS CORRECT, NOT A BUG. Three paths reach dcaa with different registers, so StoredValueScanner's isControlFlowJoin must abort the backward walk. Do not relax it. Instead READ THE JOIN AS EVIDENCE OF AN ENTRY POINT and recover from the incoming edges. This supersedes candidate fix (b) above (recognising the 'STA <zp>; JMP helper' relay idiom): the signal is structural and much cheaper -- an address with incoming flow references that is not its function's entry is a distinct entry with its own argument convention.

SECOND, SEPARABLE HALF: FUN_dcc3 IS a proper function entry with argReg='A' and incoming flow, yet still warns -- because the game's JSR targets d751, which Ghidra typed as thunk_FUN_dcc3. Check whether the call-switch machinery resolves Function.isThunk()/getThunkedFunction(); if not, every thunked call site is missed regardless of the entry-point work. This half is independently testable and probably much smaller.

Both halves are now detectable with tools/banktest/HelperShapeProbe.java, which reports incoming flow per SITE rather than only per function entry.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
GATE MEASURED (HelperShapeProbe section 5, real ROMs, all five mapper-1 titles). The premise HOLDS for bionic, and the blast radius is NOT what the bead guessed.

New probe section 5 prototypes the proposed reachableEntries (follow Ghidra thunks + one-instruction unconditional-JMP trampolines, bounded) over every call instruction, and reports whether the instruction before the call is an immediate load.

    title      reachableCallSites  constArg  viaThunkOrTrampoline  midBodyEntry
    bionic              5             4              5                  3
    ff1                59            54             56                  0
    cv2                 5             2              0                  0
    blmaster           71            13              0                  0
    tmnt               13             6              0                  0

BIONIC -- BUILD IT. Every one of its 5 helper call sites reaches the helper ONLY via a hop, which is exactly why it resolves zero today:

    c043  JSR $d6bb -> thunk -> dca8  FUN_dca8 entry     arg=computed  (prev JSR $d6ac)
    c04b  JSR $d751 -> thunk -> dcc3  FUN_dcc3 entry     arg=CONST     (prev LDA #$0e)
    c13f  JSR $d6e2 -> JMP   -> dcaa  FUN_dca8 MID-BODY  arg=CONST     (prev LDA #$0c)
    c14a  JSR $d6e2 -> JMP   -> dcaa  FUN_dca8 MID-BODY  arg=CONST     (prev LDA #$0c)
    c5e0  JSR $d6e2 -> JMP   -> dcaa  FUN_dca8 MID-BODY  arg=CONST     (prev LDA #$0c)

CORRECTION to the description: d6bb and d751 are NOT untyped 3-byte thunks -- Ghidra typed BOTH as thunk functions (thunk_FUN_dca8, thunk_FUN_dcc3), because their targets are function entries. Only d6e2 escapes thunk typing, and precisely because dcaa is mid-body. So the bead's two halves map cleanly onto the two hop forms, and neither subsumes the other.

The c043 path (the \$65 RAM shadow) stays declined and that is correct -- but after thunk resolution it declines HONESTLY (a WARNING at the call site) instead of being a silent miss. Cross-function forwarding for it remains grm-mej.3.

Confirmed: dcaa is the LOWEST-addressed site in FUN_dca8, so the planned 'entry at or before every recognized site' guard admits it (no AFTER-A-SITE flag on any row).

FF1 IS THE BIGGER PRIZE, AND IT IS PURE THUNK. All 59 of its call sites are 'JSR \$fe03' -> thunk_FUN_fe1a -> FUN_fe1a, 54 of them preceded by LDA #imm. Zero mid-body. So the small, unconditional half of this bead (thunk resolution in calledHelper) is worth ~10x more on ff1 than the larger half is on bionic.

CV2 / BLMASTER / TMNT ARE NOT THIS BEAD. viaThunkOrTrampoline=0 and midBodyEntry=0 for all three: their call sites already reach a helper function directly, so neither half of grm-nju can explain their zero resolution. Their warnings sit on direct switch sites, not on unreachable call sites. grm-8iy should not expect this fix to move them -- they need their own root-cause pass.

title: MMC1 reset via INC/RMW is poisoned instead of recognised
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
LANDED, but NOT with the design in the description -- the stated justification does not hold, and the real one is better.

WHY THE PROPOSED GATE CANNOT WORK. The description justifies reading the byte with "the target is in the FIXED PRG window (PRG_HI c000-ffff, overlay=false in bionic's golden)". PRG_HI is a UxROM/Bandai block name. bionic uses nes-mmc1.map, whose real layout is:

    block W8000              8000-bfff  overlay=false
    block WC000              c000-ffff  overlay=false
    block W8000_M0_B0..B15   8000-ffff  overlay=true    <- 32K mode, blankets \$FFE1

MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.bankInvariantRomByte refuses any address an overlay shadows, so it would refuse \$FFE1 -- and every address on every MMC1 board, because the descriptor always emits 32K-mode overlays spanning the whole window. The block-gated tier is dead code by construction for serial-shift, so it was not built.

THE REAL REASON THE BYTE IS KNOWABLE, which the description names without drawing the conclusion: INC \$FFE1 sits AT \$FFE1. It reads the byte the CPU just fetched as its own opcode. Invariance comes from SELF-REFERENCE, not from the memory map -- no block reasoning, no shared-helper extraction, and it stays correct while executing out of an overlay.

THE RULE IS AN OR, NOT AN AND (user-supplied nesdev wiki text, decisive). A 6502 RMW puts two writes on the bus, the unmodified byte then the modified one. The wiki: "it ignores every write after the first ... This restriction only applies to the data being written on bit 0; the bit 7 reset is never ignored." Two named games pin both halves -- Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure INCs a location holding \$FF (set then CLEAR) and needs the reset, proving an AND would decline a real one; Shinsenden uses illegal \$7F (RRA abs,X) to set bit 7 on the SECOND write and crashes if that reset is ignored. So: reset iff bit 7 set in EITHER write. An earlier draft of this work used AND and would have been wrong.

TWO TIERS FELL OUT, AND THE FIRST NEEDS NO MNEMONIC TABLE:
  A. The first write is always the unmodified byte, so (b & 0x80) != 0 => reset WHATEVER the op is. Covers bionic (\$EE) and Bill & Ted (\$FF), and is correct for ASL/LSR/ROL/ROR and undecoded illegal RMW opcodes without enumerating them.
  B. Only the clear-then-set direction needs the op. INC and DEC only. LSR can never set bit 7 (returning false there is exhaustive, not a gap); ASL/ROL would be bit 6 but no surveyed game spells it that way; ROR/RRA put the CARRY in bit 7 and are underivable. Unmodeled spellings fall through to poisonAll, which WARNS -- so an instance surfaces rather than hides. Pinned by tests so adding them later is deliberate.

MEASURED (real ROMs, before -> after; instrs.inOverlay and refs.intoOverlay unchanged everywhere -- this trades warnings for knowledge, not coverage):

    bionic     bankComments 4 -> 5    warnings 14 -> 12
    blmaster   bankComments 3 -> 5    warnings 93 -> 90
    megaman2   bankComments 74 -> 75  warnings 333 -> 332

The 'seed every later inference hangs off' claim is now visible rather than asserted. bionic's ffe1 resolves fully ('bank -> mirroring=0,prg_mode=3,prg_bank=0', no '?'), and DOWNSTREAM the requirement violation at c04b narrows from 'requires mirroring,prg_mode,prg_bank known' to 'requires prg_bank known'; the violation at ffe4 disappears outright.

BLMASTER IS A BONUS. grm-8iy had it as one of three titles ruled out for grm-nju; it uses this idiom instead. Still 0 instrs.inOverlay, but 3 fewer requirement violations and mirroring.0 now known at e68e.

DEFERRED TIER, now with a concrete motivator: Bill & Ted INCs a ROM LOCATION containing \$FF -- a real reset that is NOT self-referential and needs the byte read from memory. On an MMC1 board the overlay test can only ever say no, so it would need content-verified invariance (grm-e7v), not the overlay test. File under grm-e7v if it ever matters.

Also delivered: SerialShiftStrategyProgramTest, the first JUnit coverage this strategy has ever had (it was headless-fixture-only), and nesserialtest's F-rmw-reset case, placed immediately after F-partial-bit7 so it restores prg_mode from UNKNOWN rather than idempotently re-asserting a known 3.

title: 8 of 19 GME titles resolve zero instructions into overlay space
description:
First real-ROM data from the expanded game-music-extraction set (19 titles, grm-tlv). 'REALROM count instrs.inOverlay' across expected/*.dump:

ZERO instructions in any overlay (8): bionic (MMC1, also 0 bankComments and 0 refs), cv2 (2 bankComments), blmaster (3), ff1 (4), smb2 (4), tmnt (10), wizwarr (15), rcransom (38).
Resolving normally (11): megaman2 74 bankComments/6683 instrs, lwings 37/4649, dodge 30/10692, kicarus 31/215, rcproam 10/4810, zelda2 6/1405, megaman3 8/693, tetris 2/944, drmario 2/1650, lifeforce 2/796, ultimaav 1/678.

CORRECTION (this bead originally mis-framed bionic): bionic is NOT the grm-2yx site-discovery shape. Its warning bookmarks show all 11 mechanism writes ARE found and correctly classified -- two unrolled 5-write MMC1 serial chains (dcaa/dcae/dcb2/dcb6/dcba to $E000 = prg_bank; dcc3..dcd3 to $9FFF = control) plus the reset at ffe1. Every site is discovered; only the VALUE is unrecoverable. That is grm-m95, not grm-2yx. Diagnosed in full in grm-nju (argument passed through RAM shadow $65 across a JMP, behind a jump table of thunks) and grm-4kc (the ffe1 'INC $FFE1' reset idiom poisoned because storeRegister() only knows STA/STX/STY).

Warning counts do NOT predict success: tetris has 24 warnings and still resolves 944 instrs; megaman2 has 324 and resolves 6683. What distinguishes bionic is that not one of its sites resolved, and that its banking is CENTRALISED in a single routine -- so one idiom blocks everything, where megaman2's 324 sites spread from $8026 include many that resolve inline.

STILL TO CHECK: whether cv2/blmaster/ff1/tmnt (MMC1, also zero overlay instrs) share bionic's centralised-shadow idiom. Their site addresses cluster similarly (e.g. tmnt: c31b..c327, ce59..ce69, ce74..ce84, ce8f..ce9f, ceaa..ceba -- five chains). If they do, grm-nju's fix has a much larger payoff than one title.

Re-derive after any analyzer change with 'realrom-test.sh check --gme <romdir>' and diff the counts.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
grm-nju LANDED. Two of the eight zero-resolvers are fixed, and three are now RULED OUT as instances of it -- measure again before assuming the remaining ones share a cause.

Real-ROM goldens, before -> after (instrs.inOverlay / refs.intoOverlay / bankComments / warnings):

    bionic     0 -> 706      0 -> 127     0 -> 4     11 -> 14
    ff1        0 -> 7426     0 -> 1880    4 -> 75    26 -> 618

ff1 was the bigger prize and it came entirely from the SMALL half (thunk resolution): all 59 of its bank call sites are 'JSR \$fe03' -> thunk_FUN_fe1a -> FUN_fe1a, 54 preceded by LDA #imm. bionic needed both halves -- 2 sites through Ghidra thunks, 3 through a jump-table slot into a mid-body entry (\$D6E2 -> \$DCAA).

STILL ZERO, AND NOT FOR THIS REASON: cv2, blmaster, tmnt. HelperShapeProbe section 5 measured viaThunkOrTrampoline=0 and midBodyEntry=0 for all three -- their call sites already reached a helper function directly, so no amount of relay-following can help them. Their warnings sit on DIRECT switch sites, not on unreachable call sites. They need their own root-cause pass; do not carry grm-nju's diagnosis over to them.

    cv2        5 call sites reachable, 2 with a constant arg, 0 hops
    blmaster  71 call sites reachable, 13 with a constant arg, 0 hops
    tmnt      13 call sites reachable, 6 with a constant arg, 0 hops

Remaining zero-resolvers after this: cv2, blmaster, tmnt, smb2, wizwarr, rcransom (6 of 19).

SIDE EFFECTS ON TITLES THAT ALREADY WORKED, both blessed: megaman2 warnings 324 -> 333 and dodge 289 -> 299, with coverage and every recovered bank VALUE unchanged. Those are previously-SILENT misses (calledHelper returned null, which runDataflow folds as a call that does nothing) becoming conservative ones. megaman2 additionally reports mirroring/prg_mode as 'assumed from initial' at 10 sites where it used to claim them known -- same values, honest provenance.

Re-measure with: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --gme <romdir>

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
BOTH BLOCKERS NOW CLOSED (grm-nju, grm-4kc). Current state of the 19-title GME set.

FIXED -- no longer zero-resolvers (2): bionic 0 -> 706 instrs.inOverlay, ff1 0 -> 7426.

STILL ZERO (6): cv2, blmaster, smb2, tmnt, wizwarr, rcransom.

grm-4kc did move blmaster even though grm-nju could not: bankComments 3 -> 5 and 3 fewer bank-state requirement violations, because it uses the INC/RMW reset idiom. Still 0 instrs.inOverlay though -- the reset seed alone is not enough for it.

WHAT IS RULED OUT FOR THE REMAINING SIX. HelperShapeProbe section 5 measured cv2/blmaster/tmnt at viaThunkOrTrampoline=0 and midBodyEntry=0, so grm-nju's shapes cannot explain them; their call sites already reach a helper directly and their warnings sit on DIRECT switch sites. grm-4kc is now also applied everywhere it can be. So the remaining six need a fresh root-cause pass rather than another idiom from this family -- do not assume they share a cause with each other either.

NO BEAD EXISTS FOR THAT PASS YET. 'bd search' finds nothing for cv2/blmaster/tmnt; grm-m95 is the adjacent bead but it is scoped to Bandai FCG / GxROM titles, not these MMC1 ones. Worth filing before the context is lost.

Re-derive any time with: bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh check --gme <romdir>

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ROOT-CAUSE PASS OPENED (2026-08-03). Findings below are from reading the goldens + descriptors +
BoardBankAnalyzer directly; they are independent of the probe measurement still in flight, and
they RULE THINGS OUT so the next reader does not re-derive them.

THE FRAMING WAS INCOMPLETE. bankComments and instrs.inOverlay measure DIFFERENT POPULATIONS.
Comments are written at SWITCH SITES (annotateBankSwitch:1617). Overlay refs come only from
retargetReferences (:2026) -> addOverlayRef (:2163); instrs.inOverlay only from that method's
DisassembleCommand (:2202), gated on refType.isFlow(). And retargetReferences is handed the
instruction's IN-state (:327) -- so a site that recovers a bank never helps its OWN references,
only its CFG successors'. "Zero resolution" therefore covers two independent failures, and the
six titles do not all have the same one.

>>> THE FACT THAT REFRAMES THE BEAD. tmnt and blmaster each have a FULLY-KNOWN NON-HOME bank:
    tmnt     c003 prg_bank=2 via FUN_cea7 / c340 prg_bank=7 / c354 prg_bank=7 via FUN_ce56
    blmaster ec53 prg_bank=5 via FUN_e63c
MMC1 initial_state 12 = mirroring 0 / prg_mode 3 / prg_bank 0 (decoded from nes-mmc1.map,
fields LSB-first: mirroring lsb0 w2, prg_mode lsb2 w2, prg_bank lsb4 w5). All four sites are in
HOME mode 3 with a NON-HOME bank, so they clear the home gate at :2137 -- and still produce zero
refs. VALUE RECOVERY IS NOT THE ONLY FAILURE HERE. Something on the CONSUMER side is also
failing, and nothing in the repo measured that until now (grm-8iy.1).

RULED OUT for tmnt: the missing-overlay-space gate (:2167). tmnt's block list contains
W8000_M3_B1..B7 at 8000-bfff (B0 absent precisely because it is home, in base space) and
WC000_M2_B0..B7. The space W8000_M3_B7 that c340 would need EXISTS. Remaining candidates are the
consumer not being in flow.stateIn(), no base-space reference to retarget (indirect dispatch), or
state loss between site and consumer.

WHY UNKNOWN AND HOME LOOK IDENTICAL FROM OUTSIDE: BankState.effective (BankState.java:65) folds
unknown bits to initialState. A title with no recovery and a title genuinely sitting in the home
bank produce byte-identical zero counts. That is why five of the six looked like one bug.

WIZWARR IS NOT "CORRECT, NOT A BUG" -- correcting my own earlier read. Its 15 comments are all
'bank -> 0 (bank=0)' and AxROM home bank is 0, so retargeting nothing FROM THOSE SITES is correct.
But AxROM's single window is the whole 8000-ffff space and banks 1-3 ARE realized as overlays; a
4x32K game runs from them. The real switching is the 4 undeterminable writes (ce8b, ff76, ff7f,
ffa6) plus the unrecoverable helper arg at bc0a -> FUN_ff69. The narrow true statement: retargeting
nothing from the 15 zero sites is right GIVEN THOSE VALUES, and grm-6pi's removal of the 0/3/7
convention fallback (73740f2) remains right -- it was shipping a WRONG bank. The bug is that the
sites which do switch recover nothing.

RCRANSOM'S 38 COMMENTS OVERSTATE ITS HEALTH. All 38 are select=0..5. nes-mmc3.map declares
targets {"6": "r6", "7": "r7"}, so select 0-5 are CHR selects that no-op for PRG -- and indeed
every comment shows r6=0,r7=1, which decodes as exactly initial_state 1024. Its PRG switching is
entirely inside FUN_ff07 / FUN_ff29, both with unrecoverable args (f1d0, f21d), plus 3
undeterminable writes (ff21, ff25, ff4b).

SMB2 IS A DETECTION QUESTION, NOT A VALUE ONE: 4 comments + 2 warnings = ~6 recognized mechanism
sites in the ENTIRE ROM. Compare megaman2's 324 warnings + 74 comments.

TOOLING GAP FOUND WHILE PLANNING: BankReachProbe.loadMechanisms (:707) hard-filters
strategy == "memory-latch". MMC1 is serial-shift, MMC3 is select-data -- so the probe ran on
exactly ONE of the six (wizwarr). smb2's question was unanswerable. Filed as grm-8iy.2.

CHILDREN FILED SO FAR: grm-8iy.1 (BankConsumerProbe -- the missing consumer-side instrument),
grm-8iy.2 (BankReachProbe strategy coverage + authoritative today=), grm-jwh (RealRomDump's
refs.intoOverlay conflates retargets with intra-overlay refs, so it is not an honest fix metric),
grm-lwu (blmaster's ~80 'requires mirroring known' warnings drown the 4 that are about PRG).
Per-title failure-class beads are deliberately NOT filed yet -- they get their titles from the
measurement.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
=== MEASUREMENT COMPLETE (2026-08-03). ROOT CAUSE FOUND, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THIS BEAD ASSUMED. ===

Instruments: grm-8iy.1 (BankConsumerProbe, new) + grm-8iy.2 (BankReachProbe, extended to
serial-shift/select-data). All 8 titles measured -- the 6 zero-resolvers plus ff1 and megaman2 as
working controls. Commands and raw logs: build/consume-wave1, build/reach-wave2, build/consume-wave2.

THE HYPOTHESIS THAT MOTIVATED grm-8iy.1 IS REFUTED BY ITS OWN INSTRUMENT. tmnt and blmaster having
a fully-known non-home bank yet zero overlay refs looked like a consumer-side gate bug. It is not.
Consumers exist on every title, in the same order of magnitude as the working controls:

  title      refs.total  consumers(sw range)  fromFixed.flow   control.fixedToFixed.flow
  ff1   *      8514           1937                  44                1261
  megaman2 *   6700           1548                  56                 584
  smb2         2587            307                  33                 494
  rcransom     2622             69                  19                 721
  cv2           906            251                   4                  97
  tmnt         2237            400                   3                 324
  blmaster     2743             18                   3                 963
  wizwarr      2153            873                   0 (no fixed window at all -- AxROM)
  (* = working control)

smb2's 33 direct cross-boundary flow refs are comparable to ff1's 44. Consumers are NOT the
discriminator. Nor is indirect dispatch (indirect.total is 1-10 on the failing titles, and 22-24
on the WORKING ones -- the wrong way round for that hypothesis). Nor is a missing overlay space:
tmnt's W8000_M3_B7 exists. Nor site discovery: BankReachProbe now reports orphan-sites 0 and
invisible-reachable-sites 0 on every failing title.

>>> THE DISCRIMINATOR IS WHERE THE BANK IS RECOVERED: AT THE CALL SITE, NOT AT THE STORE. <<<

  title      bankComments  at STORE sites  at CALL sites  fully-known NON-HOME
  ff1   *         75             1              74               58
  megaman2 *      75            11              64               59
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  tmnt            10             6               4                3
  blmaster         5             1               4                1
  rcransom        38            32 (all CHR)     6                0
  wizwarr         15             9               6                0
  smb2             4             4               0                0
  cv2              2             0               2                0

The two working MMC1 titles are carried almost entirely by HELPER-ARGUMENT recovery at call sites
-- 64 and 74 of them, yielding ~58 fully-known non-home banks each. The six failures get 0-6 call
sites and 0-3 non-home banks. Direct store-site recovery is WEAK EVERYWHERE and is not what makes
a title work: ff1, the best performer in this corpus, recovers a value at exactly ONE of its 26
direct store sites (BankReachProbe: sites 26, todayComment 1, todayWarn 23).

So overlay population on these boards rides on ONE mechanism -- resolving the bank argument at
calls into a centralized switch helper -- and grm-8iy's remaining six are all failures of THAT
path. This is grm-m95's family (bank arrives via variable/table/argument rather than an
immediate), now measured on MMC1/MMC3/AxROM rather than Bandai FCG/GxROM, and it is adjacent to
grm-mu7 (helper argReg wrong when the prologue clobbers it).

rcransom deserves a specific note: its 38 comments are the HIGHEST count among the failures and
are worth NOTHING -- 32 are CHR selects (select=0..5; nes-mmc3.map declares targets {6:r6, 7:r7}),
and r6/r7 never leave initial_state 1024. Comment count is not a health metric.

FINAL CLASSIFICATION (BankConsumerProbe verdict.class, after the rule fix noted below):
  WORKING           ff1, megaman2      retargeted 41 / 29
  VALUE-RECOVERY    cv2, smb2, rcransom, wizwarr   -- walk.sites 0: not ONE non-home bank
                                                      recovered anywhere in the ROM
  STATE-UNCONSUMED  tmnt (3), blmaster (1)         -- non-home banks recovered, but none reaches
                                                      a consumer before the state is lost
  blmaster's single non-home site ec53 (prg_bank=5) survives TWO instructions: 'walk ec53 steps=2
  stop=UNKNOWN'. tmnt's three walk 77/7/36 steps to EXIT/SWITCH/NOFLOW, never touching a consumer.

A RULE DEFECT I INTRODUCED AND FIXED. My original verdict thresholds had no WORKING class, so ff1
and megaman2 -- the titles that demonstrably work -- both scored STATE-LOST; and on AxROM, which
has no fixed window, fromFixed.flow is vacuously 0, so wizwarr scored NO-CONSUMERS while having
873 consumers. Both fixed in BankConsumerProbe section 5 and documented in its header; STATE-LOST
renamed STATE-UNCONSUMED ("lost" implied it had once reached the consumer). The raw counters were
right throughout -- only the labels were wrong.

INCIDENTAL FINDING, FILED: ff1 is BISTABLE (grm-4nr). Five plain runs gave 1880/7426/618 three
times and 1847/7382/604 twice. bankComments is 75 in both, so value recovery is deterministic and
only the downstream placement cascade varies. ff1's golden was blessed by grm-nju one day ago at
the more common value, so ff1 now FAILs check ~40% of the time. This is a second, much larger
instance of grm-g73 (megaman flaps 1 ref / 2 instrs and NO warnings; ff1 flaps 33/44/14). It makes
ff1 a weak control -- megaman2 corroborates independently, so nothing above rests on ff1 alone.

TRIAGE CORRECTION 2026-08-04: this bead's three children are now TWO. grm-8iy.3 (blmaster)
CLOSED as a measurement artifact -- its 13 constant-arg call sites came from a warning-derived

Current partition of the six:
  grm-8iy.4  smb2, rcransom            MMC3, zero constant-arg call sites (grm-m95 shape)
  grm-8iy.5  cv2, tmnt, wizwarr, blmaster  direct stores whose values recover no bits

LESSON FOR FUTURE TRIAGE HERE, alongside the existing 'bankComments is not a health metric':
A PROBE POPULATION IS ITSELF A CLAIM. grm-8iy.3 was filed on a number nobody had audited, and
the number was wrong in BOTH directions -- 31 phantom helpers, and one real helper invisible
