comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: Still reproduces at HEAD on 2026-08-10, unchanged. Measured while proving grm-mej.2 increment 1 moved nothing: ran the smb3 realrom row twice on the same build, once with the mej.2 change and once against a stashed clean HEAD, and the two .diff files are BYTE-IDENTICAL -- warnings 50 -> 52, the two FUN_c542 'bank argument could not be recovered' warnings at 867b and ac6d, and c6b5/c6c5 falling off the end of the sample.warn window as a consequence rather than as a second finding. So this is stable and build-independent, not intermittent, and it remains the only thing between smb3 and a clean row.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ESCALATED TO THE HUMAN TODO 2026-08-16: added to docs/human-research-todo.md section 1a as a
"small decisive check".

This bead's own gate has fired. It said to re-check after grm-67g landed and to ask for a human
look ONLY IF the two FUN_c542 warnings survived. grm-67g is closed and they survived -- stably,
build-independently, byte-identical .diff files on 2026-08-09 and 2026-08-10. They are now the
sole line still differing on smb3 (warnings 50 vs 52), so this bead alone blocks grm-bj6 (P2).

The question handed over is exactly the bead's own (a)/(b): what does c542 do, and where does its
argument come from at 867b and ac6d? Minutes with a disassembler; a build/measure cycle per
question for an agent, with a worse answer.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ANSWERED BY HAND, 2026-08-16 (user, disassembler). This retires docs/human-research-todo.md item
1a, which was this bead's own gate.

  "c542: complex function that sets a specific value for PRG bank $1a (c5f5 is part of c542's
   function body) and then restores it later with a call to $ffc2."

*** FUN_c542 IS A REAL BANK-SWITCH HELPER. IT IS NOT A FALSE POSITIVE. *** The item posed a
two-way question -- real helper (warnings honest, golden stale by two lines) or false helper
(something is admitting a bogus helper, worth its own bead). It is the first. c5f5 -- already
accounted for in the user's earlier smb3 trace as a DIRECT write to $8000/$8001 -- turns out to
be INSIDE c542's function body, which is why the earlier trace listed the site but never named
the containing function. So nothing is being invented: c542 writes the mapper register, and the
engine is right to call it a helper.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GOLDEN: the two warnings at 867b and ac6d are HONEST, the production output
is correct, and smb3's golden is STALE BY TWO LINES. That is the disposition the item itself
pre-committed to for this branch of the answer. Note this INVERTS the standing rule in CLAUDE.md
("smb3 FAILs by design -- golden correct, output wrong; never bless it"), which was written when
the diff still contained the ca23/ca2e regression. grm-67g closed that half; only the +2 warnings
remain. CLAUDE.md needs updating in the same change that blesses, or the next session will read
the bless as a mistake.

*** BUT THE WARNING TEXT IS NOW THE INTERESTING PART, AND IT POINTS AT A SECOND GAP. *** The
warnings say "call to bank-switch helper FUN_c542 whose bank argument could NOT BE RECOVERED at
this call site". The user's description says c542 sets A SPECIFIC VALUE -- bank $1a -- not a value
passed in by the caller. A helper that deposits a CONSTANT has no argument to recover, so the
right output at 867b/ac6d is an annotation of bank $1a, not a warning about a missing argument.

The likely mechanism, stated as a hypothesis to be measured rather than a finding: c542 has TWO
switch sites -- the c5f5 write and the later restore via $ffc2 -- and the "last switch wins"
summary lands on the RESTORE, whose value comes from wherever ffc2 pulls it. That is the same
save/switch/restore shape as wizwarr ff69 / Ironsword ffc0, so BoardBankAnalyzer.restoresEntryBank
is the machinery that should be answering here, and evidently is not (it would deposit
ownedMask = 0 and emit neither annotation nor warning). Worth measuring before filing: is c542
failing restoresEntryBank's guards -- the branch-free walk, the mirror requirement on the pushed
value, the fall-through requirement -- or is it not reaching that path at all? smb3 is MMC3, and
every restoresEntryBank case measured so far has been AxROM/UxROM.

SO THE HONEST SUMMARY: the warnings are honest as far as they go, the golden is stale, and
underneath the stale golden there is a real recovery that is being missed. Blessing settles the
row; it does not settle whether $1a should have been recovered.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SPLIT AND CLOSED 2026-08-16. The question this bead asked -- real helper or false one -- is
ANSWERED (real; see the comment above). smb3's golden was two lines stale and has been BLESSED:
the diff was exactly warnings 50->52 with the two c542 lines added, c6b5/c6c5 sliding off the
25-line sample cap, and the 19-line grm-mej.4 symbol block this frozen golden had never received.
refs, instrs, bankComments and ca23/ca2e all matched line for line.

The curated manifest now has NO expected failure. CLAUDE.md's "golden correct, output wrong --
never bless it" paragraph and the realrom-expected-baseline-fails memory were both rewritten in
the same change, so the next session does not read the bless as a mistake; the
realrom-expected-baseline-fails-smb3-symbols memory was deleted, its debt having been paid.

WHAT IS LEFT IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT and now lives on grm-gyi: c542 deposits a CONSTANT bank ($1a),
so "bank argument could not be recovered" describes a search that should never have run -- and
every restoresEntryBank case measured so far is AxROM/UxROM while smb3 is MMC3, which makes it a
question about the trampoline model's board coverage rather than about this one helper.

title: Does the $F0 interrupt guard defeat StoredValueScanner's backward scan? (tmnt; original interleaving premise disproven)
description:
Found by hand during the tmnt def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-06). Plausible direct cause of
tmnt's "24 of 30 direct stores recover nothing", which is a different failure from cv2's
(a boundary problem) and blmaster's (an argument-path problem).

THE SHAPE. tmnt guards every MMC1 serial write against interruption. All four of its A-taking
helpers (ce56 CONTROL, ce6f CHR0, ce8a CHR1, cea7 PRG) replace the FIRST LSR of the five-write
serial sequence with SEC followed by ROR $F0, and execute ASL $F0 just before returning. Bit 7
of $F0 is therefore set for the duration of the switch and cleared at the end; the NMI handler
tests it and returns early, so an interrupt cannot land mid-sequence and corrupt the MMC1 shift
register.

This is good defensive 6502 and is likely to recur -- any game that switches banks from both
main-line and interrupt context needs some form of it.

WHY IT MATTERS TO US. The mechanism chain now contains INTERLEAVED NON-SHIFT INSTRUCTIONS. A
strategy that matches a strict 5x(STA/LSR) sequence will either reject these chains outright or
mis-parse the shift sequence, and in either case the stored value does not recover.

TWO READINGS, NOT YET DISTINGUISHED, WITH DIFFERENT FIXES:

  (a) FLAG ONLY. The bank value stays in A; $F0 is purely a lock byte. The chain is then an
      ordinary 5x(STA/LSR A) sequence with two extra instructions bracketing it. Fix is
      tolerance: allow unrelated memory writes to interleave without breaking the match.

  (b) THE VALUE LIVES IN $F0. SEC/ROR $F0 both sets the lock bit AND performs the first shift,
      making the chain STA reg / LSR $F0 rather than STA reg / LSR A. The serial shift then runs
      on MEMORY, not the accumulator. A register-based serial-shift strategy will not match this
      at all, and the value's provenance becomes a memory location rather than a register.

  (b) is the more consequential and would explain why tmnt's values recover nothing even where
  its sites ARE found. DETERMINE WHICH BEFORE DESIGNING ANYTHING -- read the full instruction
  sequence of ce56 (the simplest of the four) and record it verbatim on this bead.

ACCEPTANCE (provisional, pending the above): tmnt's four helper chains are recognised as
serial-shift mechanisms with their argument register identified, and the guard writes to $F0 are
not mistaken for mechanism activity. Measure against tmnt's direct-store recovery rate, today 6
of 30.

RELATED: grm-i7v (tmnt's cea5 is a second pre-body-entry instance, and the two together are what
gate this title). grm-lwu / grm-xym for the principle that a mis-parsed mechanism generates
warning traffic that then pollutes anything keyed on warnings.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-06: THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL PREMISE IS WRONG. The guard does NOT interleave with
the serial chain; it BRACKETS it. Verbatim sequence, confirmed by hand:

    SEC
    ROR $F0            ; set bit 7 -- lock
    STA $xFFFF
    LSR A / STA $xFFFF     (x4)
    ASL $F0            ; clear bit 7 -- unlock

Five stores and four shifts, contiguous and standard. The bank value is carried in A throughout;
$F0 is ONLY a lock flag and is otherwise unused. My earlier reading -- that the first LSR was
replaced by SEC/ROR $F0, implying the shift might run on memory -- is disproven. Reading (a) in
the description is correct and reading (b) does not occur.

CONSEQUENCE: a strict 5x(STA/LSR) matcher should match these chains without modification, so
this bead is NOT the explanation for tmnt's "24 of 30 direct stores recover nothing". Dropping
P2 -> P3 accordingly, and tmnt's diagnosis moves to grm-2dr (the cea5 wrapper) plus whatever
explains the remaining direct stores.

WHAT IS LEFT THAT IS STILL WORTH ASKING -- a much narrower question than the original framing:

  Does StoredValueScanner's backward scan survive the guard? Walking back from the first STA it
  encounters ROR $F0, a read-modify-write to memory, before reaching the instruction that loaded
  A. grm-hum records that the scanner aborts when it steps over a mechanism write, on the
  grounds that a base value read further back would predate it. ROR $F0 is NOT a mechanism write
  -- $F0 is zero page, outside any declared mechanism range -- but if the scanner is
  conservative about memory writes generally, or about RMW specifically, it would abort here and
  every one of tmnt's four helpers would lose its argument for a reason unrelated to the chain.

  CHEAP TEST: compare tmnt's argument recovery at cea7 against a helper with no guard on another
  MMC1 title (blmaster e63c, cv2 c187). If tmnt alone fails, the guard is implicated; if all
  three behave alike, close this bead.

KEEPING THE BEAD OPEN ONLY FOR THAT TEST. If the scan is unaffected, close as not-a-bug -- the
guard idiom is then simply well-written 6502 that costs us nothing. The idiom itself is still
worth having documented here: an NMI-safe bank switch is likely to recur in any game that
switches banks from both main-line and interrupt context.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ANSWERED -- NOT A BUG. Closing per this bead's own stated close condition ("if all three behave
alike, close the bead as not-a-bug"). Human recon supplied the two comparison helpers
(user, 2026-08-08); the checked-in goldens supply the outcomes.

THE THREE-WAY TABLE. "Walk-back" = instructions between function entry and the first mechanism
STA. In-body warns = the five unrolled serial stores inside the helper itself.

  helper          walk-back from first STA        admitted?  in-body warns  call-site recovery
  blmaster e63c   NONE -- STA $FFFF *is* the      yes        5              FAILS, caller-side
                  entry instruction, preceded                               ($DB shadow at e627,
                  only by the previous fn's RTS                             ec5b) -- grm-mej.2
  cv2 c187        PHA / LDA #1 / STA $0103 / PLA  yes        5 (c18e..c19e) WORKS (c0ed, c10a)
  tmnt cea7       SEC / ROR $F0                   yes        5 (ceaa..ceba) WORKS (c003, cec7,
                                                                            cedb)

(The user wrote "blmaster e36c"; that is e63c. Byte arithmetic independently confirms both hand
sequences: cv2 c187's PHA/LDA #1/STA $0103/PLA is exactly 7 bytes, putting the first STA at c18e,
which is where the warnings begin, stride 4 = STA abs + LSR A. tmnt cea7's SEC/ROR $F0 is 3 bytes,
first STA at ceaa, same stride. cea5 = STA $21 two bytes before, i.e. the fallthrough entry.)

THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE IS POSITIVE. tmnt's golden carries real recoveries THROUGH the guarded
helpers -- c003 prg_bank=2 via FUN_cea7, cec7 and cedb via FUN_cea7, c354 via FUN_ce56, and six
sites via FUN_cea5 (c359, cfcf, d01f, d8e9, d8f7, dbc4, dbe1). Those comments cannot exist if the
SEC/ROR $F0 bracket defeated helper admission or argument identification. The guard is empirically
harmless.

Stated at evidence level deliberately: the goldens prove the OUTCOME (recovery works with the
guard present, identically to an unguarded helper), not the MECHANISM. Whether StoredValueScanner
walks back over the ROR $F0 or whether post-grm-2dr admission takes another path entirely is a
read of BoardBankAnalyzer's scan loop, not a golden grep. Not needed for this close.

cv2 c187 IS THE CONTROL THIS BEAD WANTED, and it is a stronger one than expected: between entry
and its chain sit an unrelated memory write (STA $0103) AND a PHA/PLA save-restore of the very
parameter being tracked -- and recovery still works. So the pipeline is not conservative about
intervening non-mechanism writes in general, which was the worry. blmaster e63c turns out to test
nothing on this axis (zero walk-back distance); its failure is caller-side and already parked on
grm-mej.2.

READING (a) CONFIRMED -- consistent with the 2026-08-07 correction comment. The value stays in A;
$F0 is purely a lock byte; the guard BRACKETS the chain rather than interleaving with it. No
tolerance work is needed.

REFRAME OF THE ORIGINATING METRIC. "24 of 30 direct stores recover nothing" (grm-8iy.5) was
counting the IN-BODY serial stores. Those are parameter-valued by construction in EVERY MMC1
title -- five per helper, warning identically in cv2 (c18e..c19e, c143..c17f) and blmaster
(e63c..e688). It is a metric artifact of MMC1's serial write protocol, not a tmnt pathology. The
recovery that matters happens at CALL SITES, and tmnt now has 18 bank comments and 103
instrs.inOverlay against the 0 it had when this bead was filed.

CAVEAT ON COMPLETENESS: tmnt's dump caps its warning sample (count 28, 25 sample lines), so this
is not an audit of every tmnt warning. blmaster (24/24) and cv2 (23/23) are complete. The close
rests on the positive recoveries, which are all in the sample.

title: No-argument helpers report helperArgReg and emit a spurious unrecoverable-argument warning (e68c, blmaster)
description:
Found by hand during the blmaster def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-05).

THE DEFECT. A helper whose stored value is a constant loaded inside its OWN body takes no
caller argument, but the model still assigns it an argument register and then reports that
argument as unrecoverable. 'This helper needs no argument' and 'this helper's argument could
not be recovered' collapse into the same output, and only the second raises a warning.

OBSERVED (blmaster). FUN_e68c is the whole of the MMC1 reset:

    e68c: LDA #$80
    e68e: STA $FFFF
    e691: RTS

HelperShapeProbe reports it, and its single call site at f25a:

  helper FUN_e68c entry=e68c body=e68c-e691 pop=MECH-ONLY strategy=serial-shift mechSites=1
    mechFirst=e68e mechLast=e68e latch=ffff storeReg=A
  call f25a flow=UNCONDITIONAL_CALL JSR 0xe68c ... arg=computed/unknown immReg=NONE
    helperArgReg=A regMatch=NA prev=BPL 0xf255

helperArgReg=A is wrong: A is a LOCAL of e68c, not a parameter. arg=computed/unknown then
follows mechanically because the instruction before the call is a BPL rather than a load --
but there is nothing at f25a that COULD load it, and nothing that should.

PROPOSED RULE. Set helperArgReg=NONE when the helper's own body loads the store register with
an immediate on every path reaching the mechanism write, and classify such calls as
arg=not-required rather than arg=computed/unknown. This is grm-mu7's prologue-clobber machinery
taken to its limit -- there the prologue clobbers the caller's value, here the prologue IS the
entire value source. regMatch=NA suggests something already half-notices. The same treatment
should cover the fff4 INC/RMW reset (grm-4kc), which likewise takes no argument.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN TOLERATING. It is the same failure mode as grm-lwu from a
different direction: a question that does not apply generating warning traffic. That traffic is
not merely noise -- any population keyed on warnings inherits it, which is precisely how
grm-8iy.3 was filed on 31 phantom helpers and 11 phantom constant-arg sites. Suppressing
inapplicable questions is a correctness measure for every downstream count, not an ergonomics
one.

ACCEPTANCE: e68c reports helperArgReg=NONE; f25a produces no unrecoverable-argument warning;
blmaster's warning total drops accordingly with no loss of genuine findings.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DONE 2026-08-16 (commit d7de9bd) -- BUT HALF THIS BEAD WAS ALREADY A PHANTOM WHEN PICKED UP, and
that is the more useful finding. Measured on blmaster before changing anything.

*** ACCEPTANCE ITEM 2 WAS ALREADY SATISFIED, AND ITEM 3 IS THEREFORE MOOT. *** The bead asks that
"f25a produces no unrecoverable-argument warning" and that "blmaster's warning total drops
accordingly". f25a DOES NOT WARN and has not for some time -- it ANNOTATES:

    f25a bank -> mirroring=0,prg_mode=3,prg_bank=0 via FUN_e68c [switch-value flow]

blmaster's 32 warnings are 8x FUN_e61b, 2x FUN_e63c, and 22 mechanism-write warnings; NONE
belongs to e68c. So the warning total cannot drop and must not be expected to. The production
half of this bead was fixed as collateral by the grm-mu7 / grm-67g / grm-cxb work that landed
after it was filed (2026-08-06) -- valueSuppliedInsideHelper is exactly the "helper's own
constant" path this bead proposed, reached via recoverCallArgument's second attempt.

Note this had to be measured with RealRomDump's SAMPLE raised: f25a sits past the 25-line
address-sorted sample window, so the golden alone cannot answer the question. See the
realrom-diff-sample-cap memory.

*** WHAT WAS STILL LIVE: THE PROBE. *** HelperShapeProbe still reproduced the filed output
verbatim, and probe output is what populations get filed FROM:

  before: call f25a ... arg=computed/unknown immReg=NONE helperArgReg=A    regMatch=NA
  after:  call f25a ... arg=not-required      immReg=NONE helperArgReg=NONE regMatch=NA

Self-supplied sites are now counted as argNotRequired and EXCLUDED from constArg*, since a caller
that happens to hold an immediate before calling an argument-less helper is a coincidence, not a
passed constant.

*** THE SINGLE-SITE RESTRICTION, AND THE FALSE POSITIVE THAT FORCED IT. *** The bead's proposed
rule ("the helper's own body loads the store register with an immediate on every path reaching the
mechanism write") is NOT sufficient as stated, because "the mechanism write" is ambiguous for
multi-site helpers. Implemented naively against firstSite it produced a FALSE POSITIVE on smb2
FUN_ff88:

    ff88  ASL A       <- doubles the CALLER's A (its call site at ec7e does LDA #$02)
    ff89  PHA         <- stashes it
    ff8a  LDA #$86    <- an immediate, but it is the MMC3 register-SELECT byte
    ff8c  STA $8000   <- firstSite: the SELECT write
    ff90  STA $8001   <- the DATA write, where the caller's stashed byte actually lands

i.e. it called "takes no argument" a helper whose entire body is argument handling -- the same
shape that shipped smb3's confident wrong r7=7. Walking to the LAST site instead is not the fix
either: a serial-shift chain clobbers A four times between its first and last write BY DESIGN, so
that declines every serial-shift helper. Restricted to mechSites==1, where first, last and
consuming site are one instruction. Production already solves the general case properly via
helperValueSite / suppliesHelperValueAtFirstSite; the probe does not model strategy, so it
declines instead.

MEASURED, 8 titles: blmaster 1 (e68c), megaman 62, wizwarr 4, and 0 for smb2, tmnt, cv2, ff1,
bionic. smb2 and tmnt were false positives before the restriction. Every survivor hand-checked
single-site with its own immediate: megaman c3b3 (PHP/PHA/LDA #$5/STA $0042/STA $C005 -- confirms
grm-432's note that c3b3 latches bank 5), c53d and d131 (LDA #$6, matching the documented "only
own site is $D135 STA $C006"), wizwarr cf81.

THE fff4 RMW RESET half of the proposal (grm-4kc) NEEDS NOTHING: the probe SKIPS read-modify-write
mech sites outright (bionic reports "mechsites.rmwSkipped 1"), so such a helper never acquires a
mech aggregate and never had an argument question asked about it. Already NONE by construction.

LIMITATION, deliberate: no test covers this. HelperShapeProbe is a diagnostic postscript, not part
of the extension or any golden, and no tier runs it. Verification was the 8-title measurement
above. Worth a bead if probe regressions ever bite.

OBSERVATION FOR SOMEONE ELSE, not chased: that f25a annotation asserts mirroring=0 and prg_bank=0
alongside prg_mode=3, but an MMC1 reset write only forces prg_mode. Those two most likely come
from the folded post-call state (annotateOrWarn renders stateAfter when recovery succeeded) seeded
at the RESET entry -- which is grm-913's territory. Not verified; flagging rather than claiming.

title: Function body over-extends past an always-looping BNE/BEQ pair: RESET routine f23b merged into FUN_f1ca (blmaster)
description:
Found by hand during the blmaster def-use pass (grm-8iy.5, 2026-08-05). Directly caused a
wrong bead to be filed (grm-8iy.3), so it is a measurement-integrity issue, not cosmetic.

OBSERVED (blmaster, MMC1). FUN_f1ca's body extends past f237 and absorbs the routine at f23b.

  - f1ca proper touches NO MMC1 register.
  - The real end of f1ca is f237: a BNE/BEQ pair that always loops back, so control never falls
    through to f23b.
  - f23b is the guts of the hardware RESET routine. It calls e68c (MMC1 reset) and e678 with
    A=#$1E (MMC1 control: 4K CHR, PRG mode 3, vertical mirror), and finishes by JMPing to c24f.

CONSEQUENCE. f1ca appears to perform MMC1 register activity that belongs to RESET. grm-8iy.3
listed FUN_f1ca among blmaster's five bank-switch helpers on that basis; hand inspection shows
it is not one. The genuine mechanism-writing set is e63c/e650/e664/e678/e68c (see grm-8iy.5).

ROOT CAUSE NOT YET CONFIRMED -- two candidates, and the fix differs:
  (a) Ghidra's function-body assignment continued past an always-taken backward branch pair it
      could not prove terminates flow, so f23b was absorbed as fallthrough.
  (b) f23b is genuinely reached only via the RESET vector / an internal JMP and simply never got
      its own function created, leaving its bytes attributable to the preceding body.
  Check what the RESET vector at $FFFC points to and whether anything references f23b directly.
  If (a), this is a candidate for the same upstream treatment as grm-b3m / grm-6xh; if (b) it is
  a seeding gap on our side.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE FUNCTION. Any analysis keyed on 'which function contains this
mechanism write' inherits the error. A body that swallows an unrelated routine mis-attributes
that routine's registers, its call sites and its warnings -- which is exactly how a phantom
helper reached a bead. Worth checking whether the other GME titles show the same over-extension
before assuming it is blmaster-specific.

ACCEPTANCE: FUN_f1ca's body ends at f237; f23b is a separate function; blmaster's helper
enumeration no longer lists f1ca.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SECOND FUNCTION-BOUNDARY DEFECT FOUND BY HAND, OPPOSITE DIRECTION (2026-08-06). grm-i7v records
cv2's FUN_c187 starting TOO LATE, orphaning the routine's real entry points at c183 and c185
below the function start and hiding 13 of 16 call sites. This bead is a body extending TOO FAR
and swallowing an unrelated routine.

Two such defects in the first two titles traced by hand suggests neither is isolated. Anything
keyed on "which function contains this mechanism write" inherits both, and both have already
caused a wrong measurement -- this one manufactured a phantom helper that got a bead filed on
it (grm-8iy.3), and grm-i7v's makes cv2 look like it has no recoverable arguments.

Worth a survey pass over the GME set for the general shapes before either fix is designed:
functions whose body contains an always-looping branch followed by more code, and call targets
that fall through into a known helper from below its entry.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ROOT-CAUSE FORK RESOLVED BY A HUMAN RE PASS (2026-08-08): it is (a), body over-extension --
NOT (b), a seeding gap. The bead asked to "check what the RESET vector at $FFFC points to and
whether anything references f23b directly." Answer, user-supplied:

  RESET -> fff4, which is a self-referencing INC RESET -- the classic MMC1 reset idiom, where
  the read-modify-write's double store presents a bit-7-set byte to the mapper -- followed by
  JMP f23b. f23b is the bulk of the reset handling: SEI / CLD / LDX #$FF / TXS, then the usual
  hardware register init. No other references to f23b.

So f23b IS reached, by a JMP from the RESET entry. Candidate (b) said it "simply never got its
own function created" for want of a reference; that is falsified. The inbound flow exists, and
the reason f23b's bytes ended up attributed to FUN_f1ca is that f1ca's body had already claimed
them by continuing past the always-looping BNE/BEQ pair at f237 -- Ghidra function bodies cannot
overlap, so whoever claims a range first wins, and the over-extension beat the JMP. Same family
as grm-b3m / grm-6xh, and a candidate for the same upstream treatment.

CORROBORATION FROM OUR OWN GOLDEN: blmaster.dump already carries a bankcomment at fff4 --
"bank -> mirroring=0,prg_mode=3,prg_bank=0 [switch-value flow]", fully known, no assumed bits.
So the analyzer already recognizes the INC-triggered reset at the RESET entry. The RESET path is
seen; only the body attribution downstream of it is wrong.

ACCEPTANCE NEEDS A SMALL CORRECTION. As written it asks that "f23b is a separate function".
That is probably not the right target and could never be met by fixing (a) alone: f23b is a JMP
target, not a call target, so in stock Ghidra its flow is absorbed into the body of the function
that jumps to it. With the over-extension fixed, the correct outcome is that f23b belongs to the
RESET function at fff4, not that it becomes its own function. Restate as:

  - FUN_f1ca's body ends at f237;
  - f23b is attributed to the RESET function entered at fff4 (or, failing that, is at least not
    part of FUN_f1ca);
  - blmaster's helper enumeration no longer lists f1ca.

title: RealRomDump: refs.intoOverlay conflates retargets with intra-overlay refs, so it is not an honest fix metric
description:
RealRomDump.java:107-115 counts every reference whose TARGET space is an overlay, regardless of
where the source lives. Once addOverlayRef bootstraps one instruction into an overlay,
Ghidra disassembles that overlay's code and its intra-overlay branches/calls/data refs resolve
WITHIN that overlay space -- and all of them count. For a working title that second term
dominates: megaman reports 1704 refs.intoOverlay, of which only a small fraction are actual
retargets.

CONSEQUENCE. The counter is fine as a coarse did-anything-happen signal (which is what grm-8iy
used it for: 0 vs nonzero), but it is NOT a fix-effectiveness metric. A change that doubles the
retargets and one that merely disassembles deeper inside an already-reached overlay move the same
number.

FIX. Split into two counters keyed on the SOURCE space:

    refs.intoOverlay.retargeted    srcSpace == default space && dstSpace.isOverlay()
    refs.intoOverlay.intraOverlay  srcSpace.isOverlay()      && dstSpace.isOverlay()

COST, AND WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: it rewrites every one of the ~31 golden dumps. Do it standalone
so the bless diff is reviewable on its own and cannot be confused with a behaviour change.

INTERIM. grm-8iy.1's BankConsumerProbe emits both numbers, so the investigation is not blocked;
the analyzer's own verbose summary line (BoardBankAnalyzer.java:348-350) is the other source.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: SEQUENCING (2026-08-15 triage): labelled needs-bless-review, but HOLD IT until the ff1/megaman bistability settles. Splitting refs.intoOverlay into retargets vs intra-overlay refs is trivial code that re-blesses EVERY realrom golden -- and grm-4nr was reopened the same day when ff1 reproduced its 1847<->1880 / 7382<->7426 flip, while megaman keeps its own grm-g73 jitter. Re-blessing 31 goldens on top of two live nondeterministic titles means blessing noise into the record and losing the ability to tell a real movement from a flip. Do this AFTER the fork work makes megaman deterministic, or at minimum after a DeterminismProbe run localizes ff1.

title: NES board gap: mapper 9 (MMC2) has no shipped descriptor
description: Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! is iNES mapper 9 (MMC2), which no machines/nes-*.yaml claims -- shipped coverage is mappers 0,1,2,3,4,7,16,34,66,157,159 (plus synthetic 100/222). MMC2 exists essentially only for Punch-Out, so this is a narrow but self-contained board: PRG is 8K-switchable at 8000-9fff with three fixed 8K banks above, and its distinguishing feature is latch-driven CHR banking triggered by PPU tile fetches (irrelevant to PRG analysis). Nominating the GME set will confirm this and may surface others; 'realrom-test.sh nominate' reports any unclaimed mapper as a board gap. Decide whether a nes-mmc2 descriptor is worth shipping once the full nomination list exists -- this bead exists so the finding is not lost, not as a commitment to build it.
close_reason: Landed c4424cc. machines/nes-mmc2.yaml ships iNES mapper 9 with a synthetic fixture and golden; gate green, no pre-existing golden moved. Full NESdev-cited fact sheet is on this bead. Power-on PRG bank is NOT documented upstream -- the descriptor assumes 0 per this project's standing convention for undocumented-reset boards and says so explicitly as convention rather than hardware fact. CHR latch banking deliberately not modelled: it is driven by PPU tile reads, so there is no CPU-recoverable switch to find. Two traps surfaced and are recorded in the bd memory fixture-dispatch-two-sided, one of them now bead grm-ugi.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SAMPLES ARE AVAILABLE LOCALLY -- this bead is not blocked on finding a ROM (surveyed 2026-08-03).

'realrom-test.sh nominate' over the local NES library turns up seven mapper-9 dumps, all
Punch-Out!!, which is the canonical MMC2 title (MMC2 was built for it):

  Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! (JU) (V1.0) [!]
  Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! (JU) (V1.1) [!]
  Mike Tyson's Punch-Out!! (PRG 1) (U)
  MikePOut
  Punch-Out!! (U)
  Punch-Out!! (U) [!]
  Punch-Out!! (U) (VC) [!]

All under H:/emulators/nes/roms (the depth-1 dir and the GoodNES USA/Japan-USA subdirs). There is
also a punchout/ directory in the game-music-extraction tree, so this title is already in that
corpus.

HOW TO GET A PASTE-READY MANIFEST ROW (no Ghidra needed -- nominate decodes the iNES header
itself and only reports the board a shipped descriptor claims):
  bash tools/banktest/realrom-test.sh nominate H:/emulators/nes/roms
It prints 7-field TSV rows for claimed mappers and '# NO SHIPPED BOARD claims mapper N' comments
for unclaimed ones -- so once a nes-mmc2 descriptor ships, the Punch-Out rows flip from comment to
row automatically and can be pasted into manifest-gme.tsv.

CONTEXT FOR SIZING THE WIDER BOARD GAP, same survey, mappers with NO shipped descriptor ranked by
how many local dumps claim them:
  mapper 5 (MMC5)  16    mapper 9 (MMC2)   7    mapper 118  5    mapper 69 (Sunsoft FME-7)  4
  mapper 87  3    mapper 206  3    mapper 68  2    mapper 23  2    mapper 18  2    mapper 119  2

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
MMC2 FACT SHEET, derived 2026-08-15 from the NESdev wiki (https://www.nesdev.org/wiki/MMC2 --
reached from the mapper index at /wiki/Mapper as "009" -> INES_Mapper_009, which redirects to the
same page). Recorded here in the shape docs/human-research-todo.md section 3 asks for, so the next
board does not have to re-derive the format.

WINDOW LAYOUT. CPU $8000-$9FFF: one 8 KiB PRG window, SWITCHABLE. CPU $A000-$FFFF: three 8 KiB
windows, ALL FIXED to the last three banks of the image in file order -- $A000 = third-to-last,
$C000 = second-to-last, $E000 = last.

REGISTER ADDRESS / DECODE. PRG bank select is at $A000-$AFFF; ANY address in that 4 KiB range
works, there is no canonical single address. It is distinguished from its siblings purely by
ADDRESS RANGE, not by an addr_mask/addr_match trick over a mirrored file the way Bandai FCG is:
$B000/$C000/$D000/$E000 each own a distinct 4 KiB slice for the four CHR latch-target registers.

BIT LAYOUT. xxxx PPPP -- bits 3-0 select the 8 KiB PRG bank (16 reachable, exactly Punch-Out!!'s
128 KiB = 16 x 8 KiB). Bits 7-4 unused.

WRITE PROTOCOL. Single write. No latch or serial-shift protocol. The wiki states explicitly that
this register has NO bus conflicts.

PRG MODE. Not switchable -- this is the only arrangement MMC2 has. No mode bit exists.

*** POWER-ON / RESET PRG BANK: NOT DOCUMENTED. *** Checked both /wiki/MMC2 and
/wiki/INES_Mapper_009; neither states a reset value for the $A000-$AFFF register. The descriptor
ASSUMES 0, matching this project's standing convention for every other undocumented-reset NES
board here (UxROM, MMC1, MMC3, Bandai FCG). Flagged as CONVENTION, NOT HARDWARE FACT, in both the
descriptor and its validation.checks. This is the fact-sheet gap section 3 predicted would be the
common one, and it was.

CHR BANKING -- DELIBERATELY NOT MODELLED. MMC2's defining feature is PPU-read-triggered 1-bit
latches (reading tile $0FD8/$0FE8 for latch 0, $1FD8-$1FDF/$1FE8-$1FEF for latch 1) selecting
between two of four CHR registers. Out of scope on its own merits, not merely by instruction:
it is driven by PPU READS, not CPU instructions, so there is no CPU-recoverable switch for this
engine to find at all.

--- WHAT SHIPPED ---

machines/nes-mmc2.yaml, following the house pattern (nes-uxrom / nes-mmc1 / nes-mmc3 /
nes-bandai-fcg) with NO new schema constructs. board.ines_mappers [9], previously unclaimed --
and note grm-7j5's new cross-descriptor uniqueness check now makes a duplicate claim a loud
failure rather than a coin flip.

Two modelling choices worth recording because they are non-obvious:
  1. The three FIXED windows carry on_write: mechanism. Real hardware routes EVERY write in
     $A000-$FFFF to some register -- PRG or CHR -- never to plain ROM. Same aliasing pattern
     MMC3's IRQ registers use against its fixed windows.
  2. The third-to-last bank is expressed as "second_last - 0x2000", using only the existing
     last/second_last keywords plus the existing operators. There is no third_last keyword, and
     inventing one would have been a schema change -- so it was flagged rather than invented.

The mechanism is a single memory-latch strategy, start 0xA000 / end 0xAFFF / mask 0x0F /
bus_conflict false. The RANGE ALONE is the decode -- no addr_mask/addr_match needed, unlike
Bandai's fully-mirrored register file.

FIXTURE. make_prg_mmc2() in mknesbanktest.py (8 x 8 KiB PRG). RESET at $E000 (in the fixed home
window) selects prg_bank=2 via a deliberately NON-canonical write to $A005 -- proving the range
decode rather than a hardcoded address -- then writes a DECOY to $B000 (the CHR0 register) that
would corrupt prg_bank to 5 if the decode range were wrong, then JSR $8005, which must resolve
into the W8000_B2 overlay. Five criteria; golden tools/banktest/expected/nesmmc2test.dump.

TWO BUGS SURFACED WHILE BUILDING IT, both worth knowing for the NEXT board:
  1. _write_rom's prg_banks parameter counts 16 KiB iNES HEADER units, not the fixture's internal
     bank size. Passing a count in 8 KiB units doubles the declared PRG size and truncates the
     load. nesmmc3test.nes already relies on the default for this reason.
  2. *** A FIXTURE NAME NOT REGISTERED IN VerifyBankTest.java's DISPATCH CHAIN FALLS THROUGH TO
     THE C64 checkBanktest() DEFAULT AND PRINTS NONSENSE *** (RAM_A000, "under BASIC ROM")
     instead of failing. Adding a board fixture is a TWO-side job -- run-banktest.sh registration
     AND a Java check method. Silent wrong-output rather than an error, so budget for it.

title: Stack PHA/PLA pairing and cross-block memory forwarding: the save/restore idiom
description:
Increment 3 of grm-mej -- the piece the parent bead says to scope carefully, deferred out of the
1+2 session on purpose. This is a NEW DATAFLOW DOMAIN: StoredValueScanner today models A/X/Y and
the board state and nothing else. transferSource (:543-551) deliberately excludes TSX, 'the stack
pointer is not tracked'; PLA is an opaque clobber in A_MODIFIERS (:115); PHA is invisible to the
walk entirely (it does not modify A, so the scan walks straight past it).

TWO HALVES, both needed for the same idiom -- save current bank / switch / restore:

  STACK SLOTS. Pair a PHA with its PLA well enough to carry a value across a save/restore.
    contra NMI:  C0C1 LDA $8000 / PHA .. PLA / C0D2 TAY / C0D3 JSR $C13F
    shenlong:    LDA #bank / PHA / JSR $FFDC   (the far-call trampoline takes its bank via PHA)
  Note MAX_BACKWARD_SCAN = 16 (:98) may bind across a real save/restore span.

  CROSS-BLOCK MEMORY FORWARDING. grm-mej.1 forwards only WITHIN one basic block. Contra's
  C139 LDA $8000 / STA $07EC .. C146 LDY $07EC / JMP $C13F crosses blocks, and $07EC is NOT a
  write-through shadow (it is not adjacent to a mechanism write), so grm-mej.2's discovery route (a)
  will not find it either. Note $07EC/$07ED are RAM but NOT zero page -- any design here must
  stay address-range-agnostic, same ruling as .1 and .2.

WHY IT IS BLOCKED ON grm-mej.2: pairing a PLA to a PHA of an UNKNOWN value buys nothing. Contra's
c0d3 only becomes recoverable once LDA $8000 resolves, which is exactly what .2's bank-identifying
ROM offset delivers.

TWO SOUNDNESS TRIPWIRES THIS WILL HIT, both already documented in code:
1. BoardBankAnalyzer.callSiteRegisters (:1220-1229) scans the CALLER with NO_HOOKS, so no
   strategy's load resolution applies there. Resolving contra's LDA $8000 at a call site needs
   those caller-side scans to see mirrors -- i.e. NO_HOOKS must become mirror-aware.
2. That immediately invalidates callSiteRegCache's stated soundness argument (:573-579):
   'callSiteRegisters is a function of (program, call address) alone, since its three scans use
   NO_HOOKS and never consult tracked state.' Make the caller-side scans state-dependent and the
   memo must be re-keyed or dropped. This is a second tripwire in the same family as
   MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.cacheable()'s -- treat it the same way.

UNBLOCKS grm-v60 (far-call trampoline), jointly with grm-e7v.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
PRIORITY RAISED IN PRACTICE BY grm-6pi (2026-08-02). wizwarr's 7 FUN_ffc0 call sites now WARN
rather than assert a wrong bank. That is honest but not optimal: the true post-call effect of a
switch/call/restore trampoline is UNCHANGED, which HelperDeposit can already express as
ownedMask = 0. Claiming it requires VERIFYING the pair -- pairing the PHA at $FFC6 with the PLA at
$FFD3 -- which is exactly this bead. So this bead now has a concrete, measurable payoff on a
pinned ROM: 7 warnings should become verified no-ops, and wizwarr's analysis gets strictly better
without inventing anything.

SECOND HALF, and the more interesting one: the requested bank IS live -- but only for the INNER
call. $FFD0 JSR $FFDA -> JMP ($00C1) runs the target routine in the requested bank. So a complete
model of this trampoline says 'callee runs in bank N, caller resumes unchanged', which is
grm-v60's far-call shape in a JSR-and-return variant rather than GxROM's return-address-rewriting
one. Worth handling together.

MEASURED CONTEXT for whoever picks this up (from grm-6pi):
  Call sites: 80c2 (bank 7), d56e (3), d691 (1), e5b1 (1, reached by JMP not JSR), e924 (4),
              e92b (6), e942 (4).
  $C1/$C2 is the indirect target pointer; the caller passes the LOW byte in Y (STY $C1) and the
  bank in A. e.g. $80BE LDY #$03 / $80C0 LDA #$07 / $80C2 JSR $FFC0.
  Every writer of the $C5 shadow in the image: 80ad, 8be8 (LDA $C5 / EOR #$10 / STA $C5 -- a
  mirroring toggle, note it touches bit 4 which is OUTSIDE the 3-bit tracked field), d682, and the
  trampoline's own ffcb/ffd4.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
PARTIAL, NARROW IMPLEMENTATION LANDED (grm-mu7 increment 2, 2026-08-04) -- this bead is NOT closed by it, and the distinction matters.

WHAT LANDED. BoardBankAnalyzer.argumentSurvivesPrologue now models BOTH halves this bead names, but as a PRESERVATION model rather than a value model. It answers only 'does the caller's byte still reach the helper's first switch site', never 'what is it' -- the value still comes from the ordinary caller-side scan. So it needs no stack-slot value domain in StoredValueScanner, no cross-block forwarding, and nothing from grm-mej.2; it is not blocked the way this bead is.

  STACK HALF: a shadow stack over the entry..firstSite walk. PHA pushes 'is this the argument', PLA pops it back, PHP/PLP are modelled only to keep the DEPTH honest so an interleaved status push cannot make a later PLA pop the wrong byte. Anything else that moves the stack pointer abandons the model. (Note: comparing the written register to CompilerSpec.getStackPointer() must be done by BASE register -- the 6502 declares SP (2-byte) and S (1-byte) over the same bytes, and TXS's p-code writes the one getStackPointer() does not answer. An equals() test silently reports that TXS leaves the stack alone.)

  MEMORY HALF: the set of cells the walk watched the argument being stored to and which nothing has written since; a load from one is a restore. Straight-line only -- any non-fall-through flow clears it, because 'restored' is a claim that points the UNSAFE way if a branch could skip the restore. Indexed store clears everything (runtime-dependent target).

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT DO, i.e. what is left for this bead: carry a VALUE through a save/restore. contra's 'LDA $8000 / PHA .. PLA / TAY / JSR $C13F' and shenlong's 'LDA #bank / PHA / JSR $FFDC' both need the value, not just the knowledge that A survived. Likewise the wizwarr FUN_ffc0 payoff in the comment above (7 warnings -> verified no-ops) needs pairing to prove ownedMask=0, which preservation alone cannot assert. Still blocked on grm-mej.2 for exactly the reason stated.

THREE NEW MEASURED SHAPES for this bead's corpus, all GME-set MMC1, all disassembled from the pinned ROM bytes (not inferred):

  cv2 FUN_c187 -- stack only:
    c187 PHA / c188 LDA #$01 / c18a STA $0103 / c18d PLA / c18e STA $FFFF (chain)
  kicarus FUN_c17f -- stack, with a shadow write after the restore:
    c17f PHA / c180 LDA $0100 / c183 AND #$7F / c185 STA $2000 / c188 PLA / c189 STA $B6 / c18b STA $FFFF (chain)
  dodge FUN_ff08 -- stack AND memory, the interesting one:
    ff08 PHA / ff09 SEI / ff0a LDA $FF / ff0c AND #$7F / ff0e STA $2000 / ff11 PLA / ff12 STA $0103
    / ff15 LDA $FF / ff17 PHA / ff18 AND #$7F / ff1a STA $FF / ff1c LDA $0103 / ff1f STA $FFFF (chain)
  dodge is why the memory half is not optional: the argument comes off the stack and is IMMEDIATELY parked in RAM because A is needed again for the mirroring shadow, then reloaded just before the chain. A stack-only model declines it. Note this store/reload is straight-line and within one block, so it is grm-mej.1 territory rather than this bead's cross-block case -- but the guard does not use the scanner, so it needed its own model.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the process matters more than the code: grm-mu7's first increment guarded on 'does anything write argReg between entry and firstSite', which is a poor proxy -- real helpers routinely save and restore. It passed all 45 synthetic goldens (not one of them saves and restores) and cost the real-ROM tier kicarus's 215 overlay instructions, dodge's 10692, and cv2's bank comments. build-and-test.sh does NOT run the real-ROM tier, so the full gate was green throughout.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
TWO CONCRETE BLMASTER INSTANCES from the hand pass on grm-8iy.5 (2026-08-05), one for each half
of this bead.

CROSS-BLOCK MEMORY FORWARDING (the memory-slot save/restore). FUN_e9b8 and its sibling at e9d5
copy $DB into $D3 at entry, call out to routines that switch banks freely, then reload A from
$D3 and call e61b to restore. Same idiom as a stack save but through a fixed RAM slot. Also
FUN_eb98: JSR e63c with an immediate 5, JSR deeb, then JSR e63c with $DB to restore -- which is
why the one non-home bank blmaster does recover, ec53 prg_bank=5, dies two instructions later
(BANKCONSUME walk ec53 steps=2 stop=UNKNOWN). The walk hits the unknown restore leg; the real
consumer is the JSR deeb in between. Recovering the restore would keep the state alive across it.

STACK PHA/PLA PAIRING. FUN_c9a4 pushes the packed bank selector, calls out, and pops it back:
    TXA / PHA / JSR ea3a / PLA / LSR A x4 / AND #$0F / STA $D3
The JSR ea3a in the middle itself switches banks, so this is a genuine cross-call stack forward,
not an intra-block one. Note c9a4 needs three other things besides this to recover (see
grm-8iy.5 section 5 and grm-wul), so it is a test case for this bead but not an acceptance
target on its own.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SECOND MOTIVATING CASE, measured by hand 2026-08-10: smb2 (MMC3). Full trace on grm-8iy.4.

  ff85: STA $06f2                                   ; wrapper stashes the raw arg, falls through
  ff88: ASL A
        PHA / LDA #$86 / STA $8000 / PLA / STA $8001   ; R6 = raw*2
        ORA #1
        PHA / LDA #$87 / STA $8000 / PLA / STA $8001   ; R7 = raw*2+1

The bank value crosses a PHA/PLA pair TWICE, and in both cases the intervening code is an
LDA #imm / STA $8000 that clobbers A -- so this is the save/restore idiom in its purest form:
the stack slot is the ONLY carrier of the bank across the select write. Every one of smb2's four
PRG mechanism sites is behind one of these pairs, so smb2 recovers nothing until this lands, and
the whole title flips on it alone.

TWO DETAILS THAT SHAPE THE FIX:
  * The pairs are INTRALEAVED with an unrelated STA to the mechanism register itself. Any
    implementation that stops scanning at a mechanism write, or that treats a write to $8000 as
    invalidating tracked state, will still miss this.
  * Pairing alone is not sufficient here -- the pushed value is ASL A of the argument, and the
    second push is ORA #1 of that. The restored value needs the arithmetic applied. Ironsword's
    AND/ORA splice in the epic description is the same requirement seen from a different angle.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
INCREMENT 1 LANDED 2026-08-10 (commit 3ce8477): the save/restore trampoline is now PROVED a no-op,
so its call sites deposit ownedMask = 0 instead of warning. This is the payoff the 2026-08-02 comment
on this bead asked for -- '7 warnings should become verified no-ops' -- and it measured as 7 on
ironsword plus 1 elsewhere.

SCOPE RULING TAKEN THIS SESSION. The obvious first increment was intra-block PHA/PLA VALUE carrying.
Tracing the CONSUMERS rather than the scanner showed it moves nothing on any pinned ROM, so it was
deferred in favour of this:
  cv2 c187, kicarus c17f   MMC1. SerialShiftBankSwitchStrategy overrides only the 5-arg
                           depositHelperArgument, NOT the 6-arg RegisterEnv form -- only
                           MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy takes an env. They already resolve via the
                           PRESERVATION route (argumentSurvivesPrologue, which has modelled PHA/PLA
                           since grm-mu7). Pairing cannot improve them.
  dodge ff08               pairing works, but the restored byte is parked at $0103 and
                           StoredValueScanner.inStackPage refuses the whole stack page.
  wizwarr/ironsword, blmaster   cross-CALL.
  shenlong                 cross-FRAME.
  contra c0d3              also needs mirror-aware NO_HOOKS (tripwire 1).
  smb2 ff88                also needs the mechanism-write abort relaxed AND bit-wise ASL.

WHAT SHIPPED: BoardBankAnalyzer.restoresEntryBank, a forward walk of the helper body from
insideHelperEntry to switchSite, computed ONCE per helper after mirror derivation (never in the
fixpoint), consumed by a short-circuit at the top of recoverCallArgument. The claim is RELATIONAL --
what comes out equals what went in -- so it needs no value domain, which is why it could land before
the stack work this bead is named for. It IS blocked on grm-mej.2 exactly as this bead said: the
proof that the saved byte is the ENTRY bank is that it was loaded from a WRITE_THROUGH /
ROM_IDENTIFYING mirror BEFORE any mechanism write. A load after one reads the bank the helper just
installed (sawMechanismWrite). SAVE_SLOT and INPUT are refused per H2.

CROSSING THE INNER JSR IS AN ARGUMENT, NOT AN ASSUMPTION -- and the user pushed on exactly this,
correctly. 'Assume the callee is stack-balanced' fails SILENTLY: the pop reports 'this is the entry
bank' while the hardware pulls another byte, and ownedMask = 0 emits neither comment nor warning. It
does not need assuming. The pushed byte sits BELOW the return address; RTS pops exactly the two bytes
at SP+1,SP+2; a callee with non-zero net delta at its RTS returns somewhere other than the
fall-through, so the restore never runs. REACHING THE FALL-THROUGH IS THE WITNESS that the callee was
balanced and the slot intact. TXS in the callee is covered the same way. Analysing the callee is NOT
an alternative: ironsword's inner call is JSR $FFDA -> JMP ($00C1), so any callee-inspecting guard
declines and the payoff evaporates.

THE DELIBERATE UNBALANCED CONSTRUCTIONS the user raised are handled: the 6502 push-target-and-return
idiom (LDA #hi / PHA / LDA #lo / PHA / RTS) is refused inside the body, over-determined by the
stack-pointer guard (RTS's own p-code decrements SP) and the fall-through requirement. That
requirement is phrased 'must have a fall-through' rather than 'must have no outgoing flows' because
an UNRESOLVED computed jump writes no SP and names no flow target -- nothing else in the walk can see
it. That case has its own test; the RTS one is documented as over-determined so nobody reads it as
pinning that line.
RESIDUAL, far narrower than 'an unbalanced callee': a routine that BOTH returns to the fall-through
AND consumed the slot beneath its own return address. Constructed, not incidental.

MEASUREMENT (rebuilt A/B, wizwarr/ironsword/contra/megaman/lifeforce/lwings/dragonpower/shenlong):
  ironsword  warnings 11 -> 4; the seven that went are 80c2, d56e, d691, e5b1, e924, e92b, e942 --
             EXACTLY the seven FUN_ffc0 call sites grm-6pi hand-traced. Strong corroboration.
  wizwarr    warnings 4 -> 3 (bc0a, a DIFFERENT helper, FUN_ff69).
  all others byte-identical. No refs.intoOverlay or instrs.inOverlay moved anywhere, so nothing was
  retargeted on the strength of this and no disassembly rests on it.
17 Tier-2 cases in BankSaveRestoreTrampolineProgramTest; full gate SUITE OK.

GOLDENS DELIBERATELY UNBLESSED. A vanished warning is a positive claim that a call changed nothing.
ironsword's seven are covered by grm-6pi's hand trace; wizwarr's FUN_ff69 is not, and is now an open
item in docs/human-research-todo.md section 1.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD, in the order they now make sense:
 2. Intra-block PHA/PLA value carrying (designed, not built). Its stack model pairs by DEPTH, not
    address; RULING TAKEN: accept the aliasing assumption as a named javadoc paragraph -- it needs a
    ~253-byte-deep stack, games use low cells like $0103 as scratch precisely because the stack never
    reaches them, and argumentSurvivesPrologue already makes the identical assumption over dodge.
 3. Cross-block memory forwarding (contra c139/c146, blmaster $DB->$D3) -- trips tripwire 2,
    callSiteRegCache's state-independence argument.
 4. Mirror-aware NO_HOOKS (tripwire 1) for contra c0d3.
 5. smb2: mechanism-write abort + bit-wise ASL.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
ANSWERED 2026-08-11 (user disassembler pass, wizwarr): FUN_ff69 IS a save/restore trampoline.
Increment 1's bc0a claim is CORRECT and the goldens it was holding are now unblocked.

The question (docs/human-research-todo.md section 1) was narrow: does ff69 read the byte it saves
from the bank shadow BEFORE its own switch, and is the restore on every path out? Both halves hold.

TRACE AS REPORTED:
  - saves Y in $1b
  - pushes $00 (wizwarr's composite bank shadow) on the STACK
  - sets the bank to A, via $1d
  - JSR $ff83, which is JMP ($1b) -- the indirect far call
  - restores $00 and sets the bank from the stack

So the calling convention is: target address through $1b (Y supplies a byte of it), requested bank
in A. The save of $00 PRECEDES the switch, which is the exact ordering the increment assumes, and
the restore reloads both the shadow cell and the latch from the pushed value on the way out. Net
effect on the caller's bank state is nil -- ownedMask = 0 is the right deposit, and the
"bank argument could not be recovered" warning at bc0a correctly disappears.

Note the shape difference from ironsword's FUN_ffc0 (the seven grm-6pi sites): wizwarr saves through
the STACK, ironsword does not. Increment 1 recognizes both, which is a real generality result rather
than one idiom fitted twice.

CONSEQUENCE -- BLESSING IS NOW UNBLOCKED FOR BOTH REAL-ROM GOLDENS:
  ironsword: was blocked only by this item (its own seven sites were already verified by grm-6pi).
  wizwarr:   was blocked by this item AND by grm-p9y (the ffa6 coherence bug). grm-p9y is now CLOSED
             (fix 53059ed), so both blockers are clear.
Neither has been blessed yet -- that is the next concrete step on this bead. Expected diff is
warnings only: ironsword 11 -> 4, wizwarr 4 -> 3, with no refs.intoOverlay / instrs.inOverlay
movement on any row. Review the diff against that expectation before blessing; anything that moves a
count line is NOT this change. Remember to clear build/realrom-cache first (see grm-g73's answer --
a stale cache dir has caused a bad bless before).

DO NOT RE-TRACE ff69. The save/restore ordering is settled byte-level against the pinned ROM.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
BLESSED 2026-08-11 (b25f2db). Both goldens increment 1 was holding are now green.

Procedure followed: rm -rf build/realrom-cache, then build-and-test.sh check nes-banking (the
rebuild is not optional -- realrom-test.sh does not build), then check on BOTH manifests before
blessing anything. Note wizwarr is in the GME manifest, not the curated one, so it needs --gme; a
plain 'check' does not cover it.

ironsword  warnings 11 -> 4. The seven removed are exactly 80c2, d56e, d691, e5b1, e924, e92b,
           e942 -- the FUN_ffc0 sites grm-6pi hand-traced, matching the A/B prediction exactly.
wizwarr    warnings 5 -> 4, removing exactly bc0a (FUN_ff69). bankComments held at 17, so
           grm-p9y's fix is intact and was not disturbed.

NOTE the wizwarr number differs from this bead's earlier A/B, which said 4 -> 3. That A/B was
measured before grm-p9y landed, when the golden was mid-regression. Against the current golden the
move is 5 -> 4. Same single warning either way; only the baseline shifted.

SECOND, UNRELATED COMPONENT IN BOTH DIFFS, expected and benign: both gained the sample.symbol
category (18 lines, 'REALROM count symbols 18') from grm-mej.4's 725a1c9. These two were the ONLY
goldens in either manifest still missing it -- precisely because they were the two held back -- so

sample.symbol lines across the expected/ dir before blessing. No refs.intoOverlay or
instrs.inOverlay movement on either row, so no disassembly rests on the change.

FULL-TIER STATE AT THIS COMMIT (curated 12 + GME 19, both run):
  curated: 11 PASS, smb3 FAIL (grm-evn/grm-bj6, expected -- warnings 50->52, deliberately unblessed)
  GME:     18 PASS, dodge FAIL (grm-g73 jitter -- refs.intoOverlay 2739->2736, count-line-only,

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
INCREMENT 2 LANDED 2026-08-11 (commit ba1efc3): intra-block PHA/PLA VALUE carrying, plus the
stack-page forwarding relaxation it is useless without. 11 cases in PushPullValueCarryingProgramTest.

ZERO REAL-ROM MOVEMENT, EXPECTED AND CONFIRMED. This is a foundation, and increment 1's scope ruling
already predicted it: cv2/kicarus resolve via the preservation route, everything else is
cross-CALL or cross-FRAME, and dodge ff08 -- the one case pairing reaches -- is ALREADY resolved by
argumentSurvivesPrologue. So the correct acceptance result was 'nothing moves', and that is what
was measured: full gate SUITE OK; curated real-ROM 11 PASS with only the known smb3 fail; GME 19/19
PASS (dodge's grm-g73 jitter landed golden-side this run). Do NOT read the zero as the increment
failing, and do not go looking for the payoff on a pinned ROM -- it arrives with item 5.

WHAT SHIPPED. StoredValueScanner.findMatchingPush, a backward search from a PLA pairing by stack
DEPTH not address: counter starts at one push owed, PHA/PHP decrement, nested PLA/PLP increment, so
an inner pair balances before an outer pairing is considered. A PLA matching a PHP returns unknown
(a status byte is never a value). The (aAcc, oAcc) accumulators survive the pop, so arithmetic
composed AFTER the pop still applies -- that is what makes 'PLA / AND #imm / STA' work rather than
only a bare 'PLA / STA'. The search spends from the SAME MAX_BACKWARD_SCAN budget as the enclosing
walk via an explicit step count, so a pair spanning more than the budget degrades to unknown instead
of quietly scanning further.

THE NON-OBVIOUS BUG, caught in orchestrator review, not by the gate -- worth remembering because the
class will recur. The pairing search's whole job is to STEP OVER the PHA..PLA span, and that hid the
enclosing walk's own mechanism-write abort, which lives inside the skipped region:
    LDA <write-through mirror> / PHA / STA <mechanism> / PLA / STA <chain>
The main walk resumes before the PHA and resolves the mirror load against inStateAtStore -- the
state AFTER the mechanism write -- attributing a pre-write read the post-write bank. A confident
wrong value, not a missing one, which is the failure direction this bead has repeatedly identified
as the unacceptable kind. Note it is ironsword's trampoline shape minus the JSR, so not exotic.
Fixed by aborting on hooks.isMechanismWrite inside the search, with a regression test built on a
mirror-load shape (an immediate would pass for the wrong reason, since its value does not depend on
inStateAtStore). GENERAL LESSON: any change that widens what a walk TRAVERSES must be audited
against every guard that lived in the newly traversed region.

DELIBERATELY NOT RELAXED, and the javadoc says so at the abort: smb2's ff88 needs exactly that
mechanism-write abort gone, but relaxing it here would reinstate the hazard above. It belongs to
item 5, which must first distinguish a value fully determined by immediates (safe to cross a
mechanism write) from one resolved out of in-state (not safe). smb2 resolves to unknown either way
today because ASL A is still an opaque A-modifier.

STACK-PAGE RELAXATION (the second half). forwardedStoreValue no longer refuses $0100-$01FF;
inStackPage is deleted and its reasoning moved into forwardedStoreValue's javadoc, including the
residual risk (a genuinely ~253-byte-deep stack at the moment of the push) as accepted rather than
eliminated. The user's ruling, implemented as recorded. BankMirrors KEEPS its blanket refusal and
its comment now states its OWN reason rather than citing the deleted method: a wrongly nominated
mirror poisons every later query against it, not just one query.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD, unchanged in order:
 3. Cross-block memory forwarding (contra c139/c146, blmaster $DB->$D3) -- trips tripwire 2,
    callSiteRegCache's state-independence argument.
 4. Mirror-aware NO_HOOKS (tripwire 1) for contra c0d3.
 5. smb2: mechanism-write abort + bit-wise ASL. THE PAYOFF ITEM -- the whole title flips on it, and
    increment 2 is now the prerequisite it was waiting on.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: Increment 2's accepted residual (stack-page aliasing) is now an open item in docs/human-research-todo.md section 1: does any corpus title run S below ~$20? Emulator question, unanswerable statically. A confirmed 'never' retires the concern; a counter-example would justify a narrowed guard refusing only the upper page.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
STACK-DEPTH QUESTION CLOSED BY RULING, NOT BY MEASUREMENT (2026-08-12, project owner). The human-research item "does any corpus title run the stack deep enough to reach the low stack page?" is RETIRED -- do not run the min-S emulator trace, and do not re-open it as a measurement question. A trace answers only for the titles traced; a movable threshold covers the corpus and every future title at once.

THE RULING: assume S never descends below $40. So $0100-$013F is fair game for finding shadows and stashed arguments, and $0140-$01FF is refused as possible stack. $40 is an explicit ESTIMATE, not a measurement.

IMPLEMENTED as retromachines.StackFloor (DEFAULT_FLOOR = 0x40, STACK_PAGE = 0x0100, mayAliasStack(program, cell)). Increment 2 had left the assumption tacit and, more importantly, made in three separate places with no shared statement of it. All three now consult the one floor:
  1. StoredValueScanner.forwardedStoreValue -- refuses a target at or above the floor (the guard increment 2 removed, narrowed rather than restored).
  2. BoardBankAnalyzer.argumentSurvivesPrologue -- PHA/PHP now drop tracked argumentCells the push may have hit (forgetCellsThePushMayHaveHit). They were modelled=true and so skipped the generic removeIf, which is right for the register half and was wrong for the memory half.
  3. BoardBankAnalyzer.inboundArgumentCell -- refuses a cell at or above the floor. THIS IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST: the caller reached the helper through a JSR, which pushed two bytes at an address writesMemory cannot name, and a wrong answer here is a confident wrong bank rather than a forfeited forward.

CONFIGURABLE, three-level resolution, first match wins: the program-info property "Retro Machines.Stack Floor" (per program -- THE SEAM THE PER-GAME DESCRIPTOR TIER SHOULD WRITE when a game .yaml grows a field for it; deliberately unset today, since fixing the YAML key before grm-hb6 exists would fix the schema around a guess), then the JVM system property retromachines.stackFloor (per run, for a headless bisect without a rebuild), then DEFAULT_FLOOR. Both accept $40 / 0x40 / 64; malformed or out-of-range falls through to the next source rather than failing the analysis.

THE ENDPOINTS REPRODUCE BOTH HISTORICAL BEHAVIORS EXACTLY, which is the cheap way to bisect this later: floor 0 = the pre-increment-2 blanket refusal of the whole page; floor 0x100 = increment 2 as shipped. Pinned by StackFloorTest.

MEASURED COST: ZERO. Full gate green. Real-ROM curated 10/12 with only the two documented baseline fails (smb3 = grm-evn signature warnings 50->52 at 867b/ac6d plus the symbols format debt; megaman = grm-g73 jitter, refs 1704->1703 with instrs 7429->7431 moving opposite, bankComments/warnings constant). GME 19/19 -- including dodge, cv2 and kicarus, the exact titles the assumption was argued from, whose scratch cell $0103 sits well below the floor. dodge's own grm-g73 jitter did not fire.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: not a trace, but a TITLE -- a real ROM where a bank shadow or stashed argument stops resolving and the cell turns out to be at $0140 or above. The remedy then is to move the floor for that title, not to re-litigate the three walks.

title: Per-game hint vocabulary for banking FACTS (bank shadow, identifying offset, trampoline, invariant range)
description:
The analyst's question this answers: "I have worked out how this game switches banks -- how do I
tell the extension so a re-analyze picks up the right references?"

*** THE PLUMBING ALREADY EXISTS AS A DESIGNED TIER. DO NOT BUILD A PARALLEL ONE. ***
  grm-hb6.1  per-game identity keyed on PRG SHA-256                       -- DONE
  grm-hb6.2  user-directory descriptor overlay, so no extension rebuild   -- designed
  grm-hb6.4  analyzer-side consumption, explicitly handling a descriptor that arrives AFTER
             import (setSupportsOneTimeAnalysis + idempotent materialization;
             DescriptorCopyHintAnalyzer.java:57-61,93 explains why loader-side would make the
             common path unreachable)                                      -- designed
  grm-hb6.5  export script emitting YAML valid as both overlay file and PR -- designed
And ghidra_scripts/RunFromElsewhereTransfer.java + RunFromElsewherePlugin is the working
precedent for a UI-invocable action that also takes headless key:value args.

WHAT IS GENUINELY MISSING: the VOCABULARY. grm-hb6.4 speaks in SITE ADDRESSES ("treat this
address as a switch site"). This class of knowledge is not a site, it is a FACT about the game:

  bank_shadow: $42                 # RAM/ZP mirror of the current bank (megaman $42,
                                   #   shenlong $F2, dragonpower $F2/$F9)
  bank_identifying_offset: $8000   # offset K where bank N stores N (contra $8000; NOT megaman)
  far_call_trampoline: $FFDC       # inline far-call entry (dragonpower/shenlong)
  bank_invariant: $FF68-$FFF9      # cross-bank-identical range (derivable -- see grm-e7v --
                                   #   so this key may be unnecessary; decide when that lands)

DESIGN POINTS TO SETTLE IN THIS BEAD:
1. PRECEDENCE against auto-derived facts. Proposal: hint wins, and the annotation's provenance
   SAYS it was hinted, so a reader can tell a hint from a derivation.
2. Keep grm-hb6.4's "SEED, DO NOT INJECT" ruling. A wrong hint must produce NO annotation, never
   a confident falsehood. That ruling is load-bearing and this bead inherits it.
3. Which keys are worth having at all. grm-e7v may make bank_invariant derivable, and grm-mej's
   shadow discovery may make bank_shadow derivable. Prefer derivation; keep the hint for the
   cases where derivation is impossible or the analyst simply KNOWS better.
4. Guard against vision-doc section 10 item 9 -- "the hint tier as an excuse". Before curating a
   hint, the reason automation missed it must be understood and, if it is a defect, filed.
   Contra is the cautionary example: it looked like a hint candidate TWICE and both times was an
   analyzer bug (grm-3x1's reachability gap, then grm-hum's argument-register bug).

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RULING FROM grm-mej PLANNING (2026-08-02): two of the four proposed keys become DERIVED, so they are needed only as an ANALYST OVERRIDE, not as the primary source. This bead's own design point 3 ('prefer derivation') anticipated exactly this.

  bank_identifying_offset  -> derived in grm-mej.2 by content: for each switchable window and each
                              offset K, byte K of bank N == N for EVERY realized bank (require >= 3
                              realized banks so a two-bank coincidence cannot qualify). Contra
                              passes at $8000; Mega Man correctly fails (00 00 00 00 00 00 06 00).
  bank_shadow              -> derived in grm-mej.2 by discovery route (a): a store of the SAME
                              register into writable memory in the mechanism write's own basic
                              block, with no intervening modification, agreeing across >= 2 distinct
                              switch sites. Mega Man $42 and Ironsword $C5 both qualify.
  bank_invariant           -> already expected derivable via grm-e7v.
  far_call_trampoline      -> still the only key with no derivation path in sight (grm-v60).

WHY DERIVE RATHER THAN WAIT FOR THIS TIER: the per-game hint plumbing does not exist yet -- verified
during grm-mej planning that GAME_DESCRIPTOR_PROPERTY is DECLARED BUT NEVER WRITTEN
(DescriptorSupport.java:94-119), there is no machines/games/ or data/games/ directory, and the only
shipped hint vocabulary in the tree is memory.regions[].copied_from[]. Blocking grm-mej.2 on
grm-hb6.2 + .4 + this bead would have stranded it behind an entire unbuilt tier.

NOT ZERO-PAGE. The proposed 'bank_shadow: $42' examples are all zero page, but Contra's save slots
are $07EC/$07ED -- RAM, not zp -- and grm-mej.1/.2/.3 are all explicitly address-range-agnostic.
If this key ships, do not document or validate it as a zero-page value.

PRECEDENCE UNCHANGED: design point 1 still stands -- a hint wins over the derivation, and the
annotation's provenance must SAY it was hinted so a reader can tell a hint from a derivation.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
Two BANK SHADOW facts harvested 2026-08-10 while answering grm-ii6, offered as concrete input to
the hint vocabulary (both verified byte-exact against the pinned real-ROM images).

megaman (UxROM, mapper 2):
  * Bank shadow: ZP $42.
  * Bus-conflict table at $C000 in the FIXED bank: bytes 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07, indexed BY THE
    BANK NUMBER, so 'LDA $42 / TAX / STA $C000,X' is conflict-free by construction. Worth its own
    hint kind eventually -- it is a per-title data structure whose ADDRESS is a mechanism-write
    target and whose CONTENTS are the identity function on the bank field. Marking it would also
    keep it from being mistaken for code.
  * NMI vector $D4A8. The handler switches with a direct 'LDA #$04 / STA $C004' (bypassing $42)
    and restores at $D571 -- the 'trampoline' / 'save-restore bracket' shape, but spanning a whole
    interrupt handler rather than a helper.

wizwarr (AxROM, mapper 7):
  * Bank shadow: ZP $00, and it is a PACKED cell, not a bare bank: bits $18 are the CHR/mirroring
    field and only the low bits are PRG. 'FF9C AND #$18' is the game masking the PRG bits away to
    reach bank 0 while preserving the rest. A bank-shadow hint that cannot express a FIELD MASK
    would describe this cell wrongly.
  * Write-through pairs (the evidence that types the cell) live in FUN_ff69: 'FF74 STA $00 /
    FF76 STA $8000' and 'FF7D STA $00 / FF7F STA $8000'.
  * NMI vector $FF86, restore at $FFA6. Same bypass-then-restore shape as megaman.

The engine currently mis-annotates both restore sites; that is grm-p9y, not this bead. Recorded
here because a per-game descriptor could state 'this cell is the bank shadow, these bits are the
PRG field, this handler restores rather than switches' directly, and because the $C000 identity
table is a concrete argument for an 'identifying offset' hint whose target is a TABLE rather than
a single byte.

title: Content-verified bank invariance: unlock resolveLoad on fully-overlaid boards (AxROM/GxROM)
description:
MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.bankInvariantRomByte refuses any offset covered by an overlay
block, because on a switchable window the base-space content is merely the HOME bank. That is
correct but far too coarse for boards with no fixed window at all.

THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM. GxROM and AxROM declare a single PRG_ALL $8000-$FFFF window
(machines/nes-gxrom.yaml:52-57, nes-axrom.yaml:33-37) with NO fixed bank, so EVERY cart offset
is overlay-covered and bankInvariantRomByte returns null for every address those programs can
name. Dragon Power's and Shen Long's bus-conflict table at $FFCC is unreadable to the engine
even with a perfectly recovered index. grm-hum's increment 1 (known effective address) is
therefore STRUCTURALLY INERT on these boards -- verified: both titles stayed byte-identical
through the whole bead.

THE FIX. Read each window offset in the base block and in every overlay block; if all copies
are byte-identical, that byte IS invariant and resolveLoad may read it. Descriptor-free, sound,
memoizable per address, O(#banks) reads.

MEASURED, and it lands exactly where it matters (grm-hum, 2026-08-01):
  dragonpower  $FF68-$FFF9  146 bytes invariant across all four 32 KiB banks
  shenlong     $FEE0-$FFF9  282 bytes
Both regions contain the ENTIRE switch engine: the $FFBE helper, the $FFCC bus-conflict table,
and the $FFDC far-call trampoline.

*** IMPLEMENTATION TRAP -- READ THIS FIRST ***
Compute invariance PER OFFSET, never as a common suffix. $FFFA-$FFFF genuinely DIFFER per bank
(each bank carries its own NMI and IRQ handler; only RESET is common, $FF88 in every bank of
both games). A naive longest-common-suffix test therefore reports ZERO invariant bytes and the
whole idea looks dead. That is exactly what happened on the first measurement pass in grm-hum,
and it nearly produced the opposite conclusion.

RELATION TO OTHER WORK. Better than a descriptor `bank_invariant:` hint because it is derived
and cannot go stale. Does NOT by itself fix Dragon Power -- the index still arrives from ZP
$F2/$F9, which needs the read-back/shadow bead. Both are prerequisites for any GxROM attempt;
neither alone suffices. Also generalizes to every fully-overlaid board, not just these two.

title: BankReachProbe's today= column is stale: mirrors pre-grm-3x1 tier-1-only writesInRange
description:
tools/banktest/BankReachProbe.java's private writesInRange (:505-521) is documented as a
"VERBATIM re-implementation of MemoryLatchBankSwitchStrategy.writesInRange (:193-203)" -- but
that line range and that implementation both predate grm-3x1, which made writesInRange TWO
tiers: write references first, then operandStoresInRange() operand decode for the refless
indexed stores that were the whole point of grm-3x1.

The probe only reimplements tier 1. So its today= column answers "would the PRE-grm-3x1
production have seen this?", not "does production see this?". Every refless indexed store --
exactly the sites grm-3x1 exists to catch -- reports today=NO while production does see it via
tier 2.

MEASURED on megaman (grm-hum, 2026-08-01): all seven mode=IDX sites report write=NO today=NO,
including c3ab in FUN_c39c and d861 in FUN_d846. Both are demonstrably recognized by
production -- FUN_c39c is reported as a bank-switch HELPER in the same run's RealRomDump
output (it can only be one by containing a recognized mechanism write, and c3ab is its only
site), and d861 carries a per-site "genuinely undeterminable value" WARNING bookmark, which
only a recognized mechanism write can get.

COST: this actively misleads. In grm-hum it produced an apparently decisive "production does
not see these sites" reading that sent the investigation down a blind alley; the contradiction
(FUN_c39c cannot be a helper if its only site is invisible) is what exposed the staleness.

FIX: reimplement tier 2 alongside tier 1, or -- better, given the file header already
acknowledges the re-implementation hazard -- make the probe call production's predicate
directly if the packaging allows it, so it cannot drift again. If the verbatim copy has to
stay, add a comment at the copy naming the exact production version it mirrors and a note that
the two tiers must BOTH be reproduced. Consider also splitting today= into today.ref= and
today.operand= so a future divergence localizes itself.

Discovered during grm-hum. Not a production defect -- diagnostic only -- but it is the tool
reached for when production's reachability is in question, which is when being wrong costs
the most.
close_reason: Fixed in cb9cfaa. Tier 2 (operandStoresInRange) is now mirrored alongside tier 1, with both soundness rulings (RMW stays tier-1-only; indexed operand under addr_mask declines). Also fixed a SECOND staleness the bead did not name: tier 1's space test was strict equality, but production's inLatchRange now tests the PHYSICAL space so overlays count -- the file header's root cause (iii) asserted the old behaviour and now records what changed. today= is split into today.ref=/today.operand= so a future drift localizes. Verified on megaman: all seven mode=IDX sites flip to today=YES today.operand=YES, including c3ab/FUN_c39c and d861/FUN_d846; verdict.iii invisible-reachable-sites goes 7 -> 0. Did NOT take the 'call production's predicate directly' option: writesInRange is private, needs configured strategy state, and StoredValueScanner/LoopIdioms/DescriptorSupport are package-private -- the file header's existing ruling is that widening them for a diagnostic is the wrong trade. The re-implementation is instead pinned with an explicit BOTH-TIERS-MUST-STAY-MIRRORED note.

title: Bank-resolved references should replace the default base-space reference, not just add alongside it
description:
BoardBankAnalyzer.retargetReferences currently ADDS an overlay reference at a resolved
site, leaving Ghidra's default base-space reference in place. Consider instead making the
bank-resolved reference the authoritative one -- either replacing the default outright or
demoting it to non-primary -- so navigation, the decompiler, and the call graph follow the
occupant the access actually reaches rather than the window's home occupant.

WHY IT MATTERS: on a banked machine the base-space block at a resolved target is only the
HOME occupant of the containing window (the same asymmetry LoopIdioms.bankedAccessTarget's
javadoc documents for the read/write polarities). Keeping both references means every
resolved site presents two answers, one of which is known-wrong at that site, and the
known-wrong one may be the primary.

OPEN QUESTIONS TO SETTLE FIRST:
  - Precedence rule: delete the base ref, keep it as non-primary, or leave it and only
    flip primary? Deleting loses the fact that the loader placed something there.
  - Only when the bank state is FULLY known at the site? A partially-known state must not
    be allowed to demote a correct default.
  - What happens when the resolved bank IS the home bank (e.g. UxROM bank 0 -> base
    space): no overlay ref exists, so there is nothing to retarget and no change.
  - Blast radius on goldens: RealRomDump's sample.ref lines carry primary=<bool>, and
    VerifyBankTest criteria assert primary CALL refs, so any precedence change moves
    both the synthetic banktest goldens and the real-ROM goldens.
RELATED: grm-r6f (reference-precedence retargeting, base -> copied overlay) may already
cover this -- close as duplicate if so.

title: NES 2.0 exponent PRG-size form is unmodeled: window placement is wrong, and identity declines to key
description:
InesHeader.parse (NesRomLoader.java:127-134) does not model NES 2.0's exponent PRG-size form -- when h[9]'s low nibble is 0xF, the PRG-ROM size is 2^exponent * (multiplier*2+1) rather than a linear 16K unit count, and parse falls back to the low byte h[4] alone.

CONSEQUENCE 1 (the larger bug, pre-existing): prgSize() is then a guess, so window placement, the truncation guard and the $FFFA-$FFFF vector read all operate on wrong bounds for such an image.

CONSEQUENCE 2 (surfaced by grm-hb6.1): NesRomLoader.gameIdentity() declines to emit a per-game identity for these files, because the PRG slice bounds are unreliable and a wrong 64-hex key is invisible where an absent one is diagnosable. The header now carries a boolean exponentPrgSize component recording the fallback, and that is currently its only consumer.
