title: Collapse per-bit loops in StoredValueScanner to bit-parallel algebra
description: StoredValueScanner.java:188-233. combine() and fullyDeterminedByAccumulator() are per-bit for-loops that are pure bit algebra. fullyDeterminedByAccumulator == ((~aAcc | oAcc) & mask) == mask (one line). combine == knownMask = mask & (oAcc | ~aAcc | base.knownMask()); bits = mask & (oAcc | (aAcc & base.bits())). Deferred from /simplify because the derivation wants a unit-test pass to confirm (bit-priority oAcc>aAcc-clear>base must be preserved). Add a focused unit test first, then collapse. Quality-only, no behavior change intended.
notes: Done. Collapsed combine() and fullyDeterminedByAccumulator() to bit-parallel one-liners, gated by a new exhaustive equivalence check (tools/bitalgebra/BitAlgebraEquivalence.java + 'gradle verifyBitAlgebra', a new no-dep bitAlgebraCheck source set). The check CAUGHT A BUG in the bead's proposed derivation: 'bits = mask & (oAcc | (aAcc & baseBits))' omits the & baseKnown gate, so it sets result bits in UNKNOWN positions (known=0), diverging from the loop and breaking BankState.equals() (which findHelpers' const-merge relies on). Correct form: bits = mask & (oAcc | (aAcc & base.knownMask() & base.bits())) & 0xFF. knownMask = mask & (oAcc | ~aAcc | base.knownMask()) & 0xFF. fullyDetermined = ((~aAcc|oAcc)&mask)&0xFF == mask&0xFF. Proof is complete (bitwise-independent -> 256 enumerated per-bit cases) + 20M-case fuzz. Behavior also still guarded end-to-end by VerifyBankTest banktest2 C1/C2/C4/C6.

title: iNES parse ignores NES 2.0 and is vulnerable to DiskDude flags7 corruption
description: NesRomLoader.java:103. mapper = (h[7]&0xF0) | ((h[6]&0xFF)>>4) unconditionally merges flags7 high nibble; prgBanks = h[4]&0xFF ignores NES 2.0 size/mapper extension. NES 2.0 signaled by (h[7]&0x0C)==0x08, never checked. Failure: (a) a mapper-0 ROM with classic DiskDude! corruption in bytes 7-15 has h[7] high nibble 0x40 -> read as mapper 0x40, wrong/absent board; (b) NES 2.0 image with mapper>=256 or PRG>4MB truncated. title: M3: MMC3 — select-data + mode-register strategies, mode-swapped windows
description: Per docs/vision-board-banking.md M3: select-data strategy ($8000 even selects target state field R0-R7, $8001 odd writes it — model R6/R7 PRG fields; CHR fields deferred with PPU space) + mode-register ($8000 bit 6 swaps which of $8000/$C000 is switchable vs second-last-fixed). 8K banks: overlay-interim L4 hits ~64 overlays on one window per layout — measure and record the pain as evidence for the M5 core hook (RFC #9349). Function-level bank-state requirements + call-graph propagation land here (large MMC3 libraries need it). Acceptance targets: SMB3, Crystalis, Kirby's Adventure.
design:
DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, anchored to current engine post grm-5tl.12 refactor). Sub-bead split at bottom; shared prerequisite with grm-hsv flagged.

HEADLINE ENGINE GAP: memory.layouts[] is SCHEMA-COMPLETE BUT ENGINE-ABSENT. MapCompiler validates and emits layouts (cross-validating when: keys against banking.state), but NOTHING consumes them: BoardModel.parse reads only top-level windows[]; NesRomLoader.load reads only windows[] and hardcodes "bank field = first state field". nes-mmc3.yaml declares windows: [] with everything in layouts: — today's loader would create ZERO PRG blocks. Layout consumption is the shared prerequisite for BOTH MMC3 and MMC1 (grm-hsv says verbatim "mode-dependent layouts from schema v2") — file ONCE as a shared bead.

STATE BUDGET: prg_mode(1) + R6(6) + R7(6) = 13 bits of the 31-bit cap — no pressure. Real ceiling found instead: StoredValueScanner.combine masks & 0xFF (single 6502 register scale). Strategies must resolve the stored byte at <=8-bit scale locally then shift into board-state position (both existing strategies do this); passing a 13-bit board mask into resolveStoredValue would silently truncate — implementation pitfall, not schema limit.

MMC3 FACTS THAT MATTER STATICALLY: $8000-$9FFE EVEN = bank select (bits 0-2 target R0-R7; bit 6 PRG mode; bit 7 CHR — defer); $8001-$9FFF ODD = data to selected register. Mode 0: $8000=R6, $A000=R7, $C000=second-last fixed, $E000=last fixed. Mode 1: $8000<->$C000 swap. 8K granularity. MIRRORING: any even/odd address in the whole range works — the sketch's select_address:0x8000/data_address:0x8001 params are WRONG vs hardware; recognizer must be (addr & 1) over the range. Fix the sketch in sub-bead 2.

DESIGN A — select-data strategy (SelectDataBankSwitchStrategy):
- computeSwitch(program, instr, inState) ALREADY receives inState — no interface change needed for state-dependent dispatch.
- select = a genuine 3-bit tracked field of banking.state, written by even-address stores via existing resolveStoredValue machinery (bits 0-2). Odd-address store: if inState's select fully known and in targets {6:R6, 7:R7} -> recover byte, overwrite ONLY that field's bits (computeSwitch returns the whole new state, not a delta — merge inState's other fields back in, like MemoryLatch does).
- POISON POLICY (refined from bead text): select UNKNOWN -> R6 AND R7 both unknown (either could be written). Select KNOWN but 0-5 (CHR, untracked) -> leave R6/R7 UNTOUCHED — this case is per-frame-frequent in real code (CHR animation swaps); blanket poisoning would destroy PRG state constantly. Data byte unrecoverable with known select -> only the targeted field goes unknown. Test this CHR case explicitly.
- Table-driven loops (LDA table,X) resolve unknown at local scan — but those are the CHR idiom; PRG switches (only 2 registers) are typically direct immediate pairs, which the backward scan handles natively. Helper rescue is sub-bead 4/6 territory.

DESIGN B — mode register + layouts:
- CONFLICT: runDataflow's strategy loop is FIRST-MATCH-WINS (break on first non-null), but a $8000 write must update both select (bits 0-2) and prg_mode (bit 6). Resolution (a): select-data strategy co-emits the mode bit from the same recovered byte (params gain mode_bit -> prg_mode mapping) — narrowest fix, no engine change. Alternative (b) engine merges multiple strategies' field updates — bigger, defer until a board actually needs independent composition; record the limitation.
- Loader: layouts-only boards need per-layout window realization with MODE-QUALIFIED overlay names (same address range, different modes = unrelated content: e.g. W8000_M0_B<v>). Home block = layout matching initial_state's mode + that mode's home bank. Analyzer: ComputedWindowModel keyed by (mode value, window) not name alone; clampToResidence/retargetReferences look up the active layout from the effective state's mode field first.
- YAML: sketch's layouts:/when:{prg_mode:0|1} shape is already right; the gap is 100% runtime consumption.

DESIGN C — overlay scale + RFC evidence: RFC #9349 = OUR OWN posted ghidra GitHub Discussion (docs/rfc-banked-memory.md is source of record; cites upstream #6651/#5913/#7052/#2546/#1332). Measurement: MMC3 fixture at SMB3 scale (512K = 64 banks; 2 switchable windows x 64 banks, POSSIBLY x2 modes if placement differs per mode -> ~256 overlays worst case, confirm empirically). Metrics: block/space count, wall-clock import+analysis vs UxROM baseline, refsAdded, qualitative UI navigability. Record in docs (vision doc M3 section or docs/mmc3-overlay-scale.md), mirror into Discussion #9349.

DESIGN D — function-level bank-state (Phase 1.5): per-function FunctionBankSummary(requiresOnEntry, effectOnExit); effectOnExit = read-off of Phase-1 outStates at RTS/RTI merged; requiresOnEntry = backward property over call graph (bottom-up over SCCs; lattice already monotone/finite so terminates). Existing findHelpers/HelperModel is the single-write special case — NOTE: MMC3 select+data helpers store TWICE, so HelperModel's argReg reconciliation nulls out and current helper propagation degrades for MMC3 (expected temporary precision gap until this lands). M3 SCOPE: requires-bits derivation + violation WARNING bookmarks ONLY (read-only annotation); NO back-propagation/narrowing of Phase-1 state (mutual fixpoint, termination risk) — that's M4+.

SUB-BEADS (proposed):
1. layouts-runtime [SHARED with grm-hsv, blocks both; HIGH risk] — loader + analyzer consume layouts[]; mode-qualified overlay naming; synthetic 2-mode banktest fixture (two memory-latch fields + layouts, decoupled from select-data).
2. select-data-strategy [MEDIUM] — Design A + mode-bit co-emission (B resolution a) + sketch mirroring fix; cheap fixture (LDA #6/STA $8000/LDA #n/STA $8001/JSR); unit-testable standalone, end-to-end gated on 1.
3. mode-register-strategy — fold into 2 (co-resident on same address; Design B ties them).
4. function-summary-propagation [HIGH risk] — Design D, after 2; fixture: two-write helper called from consistent + violating contexts, WARNING only on violator.
5. overlay-scale-measurement [LOW risk, LAST] — Design C, needs 1+2 landed and acceptance titles loading.
6. (optional) select-data-idiom-hardening — two-write helper support in findHelpers if 2 reviews large; coordinate with 4.

RISKS: first-match-wins composition (above); layouts-only loader path completely unexercised today; mode-qualified naming may double overlay counts; HelperModel degradation between beads 2 and 4 (expected, document); CHR-select non-poisoning is THE easy-to-get-wrong case.

Intentionally kept in_progress: parked pending Chris updating the upstream discussion (RFC #9349 — the overlay-scale evidence from grm-6a7.3 feeds the M5 core-hook case). Not stale/stranded; blocked on an external (Chris-owned) upstream action, not on further code here.

title: M3: MMC1 — serial-shift strategy, mode layouts, bank-placement inference
description: Per docs/vision-board-banking.md M3: serial-shift strategy (5 sequential writes deliver one bit each; bit-7 write resets the sequence) as an instruction-sequence state machine over the dataflow engine; mode-register strategy for MMC1 control (PRG modes: 32K / fix-first / fix-last); mode-dependent layouts from schema v2. Flagship for BANK-PLACEMENT INFERENCE: MMC1's 16K banks fit either $8000 or $C000 — assign windows by following flows (recovered switch values, self-reference consistency of each bank's absolute refs, vector anchors) with provenance recorded and user override available; no upfront per-bank options (retires the GhidraNes BankAddressOption pattern, BankAddressOption.java:13-80). Acceptance targets: Metroid, Zelda, Final Fantasy (also a GME AKAO-adjacent interest).
design:
DESIGN (research 2026-07-10, NESdev wiki cross-checked live). Sub-bead split at bottom; shared prerequisite with grm-6a7 (layouts runtime) filed separately.

MMC1 FACTS THAT MATTER STATICALLY: any $8000-$FFFF write with bit 7 set clears the shifter AND ORs Control with $0C (prg_mode -> 3, mirroring untouched) — unconditional. Commit = 5 bit-7-clear writes, bit 0 each; address bits 14:13 matter ONLY on write 5 (00=Control, 01=CHR0, 10=CHR1, 11=PRG bank). Consecutive-cycle ignore: emulation-only, do not model. Control: bits 0-1 mirroring, 2-3 prg_mode (0/1=32K, 2=fix-first, 3=fix-last; 3 = reset-dance default), bit 4 CHR (defer). EMPIRICAL KEY: real games do the reset dance once, early, and never write Control again -> prg_mode is fully known (=3) nearly everywhere; placement "inference" is a rare-residual problem, not the main path.

DESIGN A — serial-shift (the crux):
- Bit-7 reset: ordinary single-write computeSwitch (recognize known bit-7 via existing backward scan; emit prg_mode=3 known, mirroring knownness pass-through). NO engine change.
- Fully-unrolled 5x STA/LSR: five DISTINCT static instructions; strategy statically walks the chain, returns null for writes 1-4, full BankState at write 5 (target from ITS address bits 14:13, value reassembled from the chain). NO engine change.
- CANONICAL LOOP (STA/LSR/DEY/BNE, inlined or JSR'd) — REJECTED APPROACH: shift-register position as hidden BankState fields fails PROVABLY: the loop-head join merges position 0 (entry) with 1-4 (back-edge) -> per-bit AND-agree makes position permanently unknown on the FIRST merge (monotone-shrinking within a pass) -> honest strategy must poison every commit -> 100% of the majority idiom unresolvable. Loop unrolling also rejected (p-code trace replay = emulator territory; listing-level duplication fights Ghidra).
- WORKABLE: idiom recognition, extending the findHelpers precedent one level down. New optional hook on BankSwitchStrategy — findIdioms(Program, Function) -> List<IdiomMatch(exitEdgeTarget, resultState)>, default empty — run per function like findHelpers; BoardBankAnalyzer folds matches into the same switchResults-shaped map, so merge/annotate/retarget/helper propagation need NO further changes (the load-bearing containment property). Recognize: STA-to-range as sole loop-body write + shift of same reg + counted dec-branch trip=5 (or 4+preloop); seed value resolved by the existing scanner applied ONCE to the pre-loop load; commit attached to the loop's EXIT edge (STA's own outState stays no-change).
- Honest degrade: table-driven/memory-seeded values -> existing WARNING path. CHR0/CHR1 targets: structurally recognized, zero tracked fields (verify "recognized but discarded" with a fixture).

DESIGN B — mode handling: MMC1 DOES NOT instantiate a mode-register mechanism — mirroring/prg_mode arrive inside the serial Control byte. serial-shift params need multi-field-per-target deposit:
  targets: {0: {fields: [{name: mirroring, shift: 0, bits: 2}, {name: prg_mode, shift: 2, bits: 2}]}, 3: {fields: [{name: prg_bank, shift: 0, bits: 5}]}}  # 1,2 (CHR) omitted
Params are strategy-opaque pass-through in MapCompiler — no compiler change. Layouts schema (memory.layouts[]/when:) is ALREADY compiled+validated; the gap is runtime consumption (shared bead). MMC1-specific layout wrinkle: 32K mode (0/1) is a genuinely DIFFERENT window (PRG32_B<v>, bank LSB ignored), not a merge of the two 16K windows; confirm during the shared bead that this needs no third window-shape concept. Naming: keep WINDOW_B<v> when shape doesn't vary by mode; WINDOW_M<mode>_B<v> only when it does.

DESIGN C — placement inference, two tiers:
- Tier 1 (primary, retires GhidraNes BankAddressOption by construction): loader materializes the (layout x bank) cross product (MMC1 acceptance titles are 128K = 8 banks; mode 2/3 has ONE switchable 16K window -> real count ~banks x 2, inside the tolerable ceiling); analyzer retargeting does the two-level (mode -> window-set -> bank) lookup from TRACKED state. No upfront user options; normal dataflow resolves placement.
- Tier 2 (rare residual, mode/bank partially unknown): (b) self-reference consistency scoring (candidate bank's absolute refs in-range at $8000 vs $C000; raw-byte operand-pattern scan as a pre-disassembly signal only); (c) vector/fixed-window anchors (last/second_last image offsets, like labelVectorTargets); unresolvable -> existing WARNING, never guess.
- Provenance: extend annotateBankSwitch EOL text with evidence tier ("[switch-value flow]" vs "[inferred: self-ref 7/8]"). Override: loader Option string ("bank=N:window" pairs) via PROGRAM_INFO options, matching BOARD_OPTION_NAME precedent. Analyzer-time overlay-block CREATION (for over-budget boards): legal per Memory API but unproven here (analyzer has no FileBytes; byte-array overload via Memory.getBytes) — DEFERRED from M3 explicitly.

SUB-BEADS (proposed order 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5; 2 can parallel 1):
1. layouts runtime [SHARED with grm-6a7 — filed as its own bead; MEDIUM-HIGH risk; existing goldens must not regress]
2. mode-register strategy class [LOW; MMC3 needs it, MMC1 doesn't; register-write-shaped]
3. serial-shift strategy [HIGH — the findIdioms hook is new engine surface; fixtures: unrolled, inlined loop, JSR'd loop, bit-7 reset alone, table-driven-unresolvable, CHR-write-discarded; build loop matcher from REAL commercial MMC1 disassembly patterns, not wiki-invented shapes]
4. nes-mmc1.yaml descriptor + registry wiring (ines_mappers: [1]) [LOW-MED; where the seams meet; end-to-end Metroid-shaped fixture]
5. placement Tier 2 + provenance/override [MED; not required for acceptance-title correctness]
+ manual acceptance gate: Metroid/Zelda/FF1 (real ROMs, CI-excluded per convention).

RISKS: findIdioms hook shape unproven — prototype against landed layouts plumbing BEFORE committing to the descriptor (a hook that doesn't fold into switchResults ripples back); loop-matcher brittleness (DEX vs DEY, 4+1 shapes) — source patterns from real disassemblies; bit-7 partially-known must not silently assume reset (explicit fixture); 32K-window identity question (above).
notes: Design attached 2026-07-10 (research: serial-shift loop idiom requires a findIdioms engine hook — lattice-position-field approach provably fails at the loop-head join; MMC1 needs NO mode-register mechanism, mode bits arrive in the serial Control byte; placement inference demoted to rare-residual Tier 2 since real games fix prg_mode=3 once). Shared layouts-runtime prerequisite = grm-5tl.18. Proposed sub-bead split in design; materialize as children when work starts. Prototype the findIdioms hook shape against landed grm-5tl.18 plumbing BEFORE writing the descriptor.

title: TMode-style bank tracking: model 6510 port as CPU register + per-bit context fields
description:
Adopt the ARM Thumb (TMode) tracking pattern for C64 bank state, per the priority rule: use existing Ghidra infrastructure before rolling our own.

How ARM does it (verified in D:/git/ghidra source):
1. Sleigh models the mode as a REAL CPU REGISTER: ISAModeSwitch (TB). Every mode-changing instruction's pcode writes TB (macro SetThumbMode, ARM.sinc:208-211), so mode changes are ordinary register dataflow visible to SymbolicPropogator, the emulator, and the decompiler.
2. TMode is a 1-bit CONTEXT FIELD controlling decode. Static direct branches stamp the target from sleigh itself via globalset (ARMinstructions.sinc:2416 'TMode done by HAddr24's globalset') — no Java involved.
3. ArmAnalyzer (a ConstantPropagationAnalyzer) bridges dynamic flows: reads the propagator-tracked TB value at computed flows (ArmAnalyzer.java:813) and stamps ProgramContext.setValue(tmodeRegister, target, target, value) (ArmAnalyzer.java:825); future disassembly consumes the context.

Mapping to C64 (hardware-truthful: the 6510 port at $00/$01 is ON THE CPU DIE, not external memory):
- Bundled 6510 sleigh adds a PORT register; specialized constructors for zp opcodes with operand==$01 (STA/LDA/etc $01) read/write PORT instead of memory. Then LDA $01 / AND #$F8 / ORA #$05 / STA $01 is pure register dataflow — whole-value tracking suffices whenever the incoming PORT value is known. SymbolicPropogator failed on this idiom only because the port was modeled as memory.
- c64bank context register gets three 1-bit fields LORAM/HIRAM/CHAREN (c64.yaml already anticipates 'TMode-style' at banking.context_register). RegisterValue natively supports per-bit partial knowledge (value+mask ctor RegisterValue.java:89; combineValues merge :205-233) — C64BankingAnalyzer's PortState(knownMask,bits) is a reimplementation of it.
- initial_state fallback = ProgramContext DEFAULT value on the context register (pspec / setDefaultValue), replacing the hand-rolled 'assumed from initial' logic.

Scope: blocked on bundling the 6510 language (grm backlog). When it lands, refactor C64BankingAnalyzer toward ConstantPropagationAnalyzer + PORT register tracking; keep the mask-algebra backward scan only as fallback for the stock-6502 fallback_language path, or delete it. Genuinely-partial bases (ORA into unknown PORT) still exceed whole-value tracking — per-bit context fields + defaults cover representation and fallback; evaluate whether the residual gap matters on real code.
notes:
Also refines the gib.2/RFC #9349 claim: 'SymbolicPropogator cannot resolve masked idioms' is true only while the port is modeled as memory. Precise upstream framing: whole-value tracking is sufficient once banking mechanisms are modeled as registers (as ARM does); what's missing in-tree is per-bit partial knowledge of VALUES (RegisterValue covers context/storage, not VarnodeContext propagation).
2026-07-07 abstraction refinement (user-driven): the general stack is 4 layers — (1) mechanism register definition [language, only when architecturally on-die]; (2) mechanism-write detection + value recovery [analyzer, strategy-driven]; (3) interpretation into bank state [descriptor data]; (4) application to decode/refs [context + RFC hook, universal]. What makes tracking cheap is layer-2 STATIC IDENTIFIABILITY of mechanism writes, not on-die-ness (Z80 'OUT (n),A' is equally identifiable with no CPU register). PORT-as-register is a per-CPU layer-2 optimization; layers 2-4 are needed by every banked system. See grm-bk6 note for the system-neutral language requirement.

title: BankingAnalyzer: resolve masked RMW bank switches (LDA $01 / AND #imm / ORA #imm / STA $01)
description: Optional improvement (user request, 2026-07-05). The backward scan in C64BankingAnalyzer.resolveStoredImmediate only recognizes a direct immediate load (LDA/LDX/LDY #imm), so the frequent bit-preserving switch idiom — LDA $01; AND #$F8; ORA #$05; STA $01 (preserving cassette bits 3-5) — currently degrades to UNKNOWN + warning bookmark. Two implementation routes: (a) extend the backward scan to evaluate AND/ORA immediate chains symbolically over just the bank bits: after AND #imm the tracked bits are prev&imm, after ORA #imm prev|imm; whenever (andImm & mechanism.mask)==0 the ORA fully determines the new state (state = oraImm & mask) with NO knowledge of the prior value — this covers the canonical idiom statically; chains that leave bank bits dependent on the unknown prior value stay UNKNOWN. (b) heavier: use SymbolicPropogator/VarnodeContext to ask for the register value at the store (handles loads from other addresses, TAX chains etc.) — more coverage, more machinery. Route (a) recommended first; keep (b) as a follow-on if real PRGs show patterns (a) misses. Gotcha reminder: bare immediates come from getOpObjects() Scalar, not CodeUnit.getScalar().
notes:
ORDERING REVISED (user, 2026-07-05): PREFER existing Ghidra register-value-tracking infrastructure over the custom backward scan — try route (b) FIRST: SymbolicPropogator/VarnodeContext (ghidra.program.util; the engine behind ConstantPropagationAnalyzer, confirmed in the gib.2 hook-point research to track register->value/space along flow) to ask for the stored register's value at the STA $01 site; also check whether ProgramContext already holds an analysis-set value there. If the infra route is impractical for our analyzer's position in the pipeline (e.g. constant propagation hasn't run yet at REFERENCE_ANALYSIS.after(), or 6502 coverage is weak), THEN fall back to route (a): extend the backward scan with the AND/ORA mask algebra (bits = (prev & andImm) | oraImm; known iff andImm clears all mechanism.mask bits). Scan route stays documented as the fallback, not the default.
DESIGN (2026-07-07, pre-dispatch): mask-algebra backward scan formalized — maintain (A_acc,O_acc) meaning final=(x&A_acc)|O_acc over unknown prior x; seed A_acc=0xFF,O_acc=0 at the store; stepping BACK over AND #a: A_acc'=a&A_acc; over ORA #o: O_acc'=(o&A_acc)|O_acc; bank bit determined iff A_acc bit==0 or O_acc bit==1; early-stop when all mechanism.mask bits determined (prior register content irrelevant); LDA #imm terminates fully-known with state=((imm&A_acc)|O_acc)&mask. Subsumes the existing immediate-load case. EOR/RMW-in-place stay UNKNOWN. INFRA EXPECTATION to verify: SymbolicPropogator tracks full values, so LDA $01 (memory read) poisons the chain — likely CANNOT resolve the masked idiom; subagent must time-box the infra investigation, report the conclusion, and implement the algebra as the core resolver either way (infra consult optional if trivially feasible).
DESIGN REFINEMENT (user, 2026-07-07): track PORT BITS individually, not just the combined PLA state — LDA $01/AND #$FE/STA $01 (BASIC off via LORAM bit 0) leaves bit0 KNOWN=0 with bits1-2 unknown; per-bit knowledge still determines windows whose occupant agrees across all consistent states. Representation: PortState(knownMask,bits); dataflow merge keeps agreeing known bits (knownMask' = k1&k2&~(v1^v2)). KEY COMPOSITION WIN: when the chain's base load is LDA $01 itself, x = the tracked in-state at the store — so masked RMW from a fully-known state resolves EXACTLY (7 -> AND #$FE -> 6), no heuristic. Bit known iff aAcc bit==0 (forced 0) | oAcc bit==1 (forced 1) | (base==port-load AND in-state bit known). FALLBACK (user): for still-unknown bits, assume initial_state values when resolving occupants; bank comments must distinguish known vs assumed bits; WARNING bookmark only when NO bank bit is known at a mechanism store. Abort composition if backward scan crosses another mechanism write.
close_reason: Implemented + independently re-verified (Ghidra 12.1.2 headless, banktest2 + banktest regression). Per-bit PortState(knownMask,bits) replaces the int state: dataflow merge keeps agreeing known bits only (monotone shrink, terminating); store resolution = backward mask-algebra scan with (aAcc,oAcc) accumulators composing AND#imm/ORA#imm, terminating at LDA#imm (fully known), a load of the mechanism address itself (base = tracked in-state — so LDA $01/AND #$FE/STA $01 from known state 5 resolves EXACTLY to 4), or any clobber incl. crossing calls (review fix: JSR fall-through passes the block-linkage check, so calls must clobber explicitly) and crossing mechanism writes (abort, unsound to inherit). Occupant resolution assumes initial_state for unknown bits (user fallback); partial switches get 'bank -> 7? (...) [known: LORAM=1; assumed from initial: HIRAM,CHAREN]' comments; WARNING bookmark only when NO bank bit is known. INFRA FINDING (step 0): SymbolicPropogator/VarnodeContext track whole register values — LDA $01 (unknown memory) poisons the chain; no per-bit partial-knowledge model exists in-tree, so the mask algebra is necessary, not a workaround. All 6 banktest2 criteria + 4 banktest regression criteria pass.

title: Descriptor schema: per-occupant executable override (CHARGEN font ROM should be x=false)
description: canExecute() in C64PrgLoader derives the execute permission purely from kind (rom->x=true), so the CHARGEN overlay is currently marked executable even though it is glyph bitmap data. Add an optional per-occupant/per-region 'executable:' override to the YAML schema + map compiler + loader (default stays kind-derived), and set chargen executable:false in machines/c64.yaml. Surfaced by the gib.2 RFC execute-mode discussion (2026-07-05): the RFC's analyzer-compat example claims a sensible descriptor marks font ROM non-executable — make our own descriptor do so.
design: DECISION (user, 2026-07-05): Option 1 — kind-derived defaults + sparse per-attribute overrides. Optional boolean fields readable:/writable:/executable: allowed anywhere a kind appears (region, occupant, subregion); kind supplies defaults: ram=r+w+x, rom=r+x, io=r+w (non-x). Rationale/rule for future cases: one-attribute deviation => override; multi-behavior cluster (perms+structs+volatility+storage like io) => new kind. Rejected: new kinds per combo (code change per quirk, taxonomy explosion — option-3-with-worse-ergonomics), required direct perms (abstraction inversion: descriptor states what hardware IS, tools derive treatment; boilerplate; allows kind-contradicting perms). Precedent: MAME address maps (.rom()/.ram() + per-range modifiers). Riders: (a) document kind->defaults table in SCHEMA.md (currently implicit in loader canWrite/canExecute); (b) derive volatile=true for io-kind blocks in loader (MemoryBlock.setVolatile) — stops decompiler folding repeated $D012 reads; (c) set chargen executable:false in machines/c64.yaml. Verify: rebuild + headless smoke shows CHARGEN x=false and IO blocks volatile.
close_reason: Implemented + headless-verified. Sparse readable/writable/executable overrides (kind supplies defaults: ram=r+w+x, rom=r+x, io=r+w) at region/occupant/subregion level across MapCompiler passthrough + loader Perms record/perms() helper; io-kind blocks now marked volatile (setVolatile). c64.yaml: CHARGEN executable:false (headline) + COLOR_RAM executable:false (review catch — kind:ram default would have flipped it x=true vs baseline; 4-bit cells, open-bus fetches; first organic use of the new override). SCHEMA.md gained the kind->defaults table + one-attribute-deviation=>override / multi-behavior-cluster=>new-kind rule; MAP_FORMAT.md documents the passthrough fields. Smoke: CHARGEN x=false, COLOR_RAM x=false vol=false, VIC/SID/CIA/P6510/IO1/IO2 vol=true, baseline otherwise unchanged, Import succeeded.

title: Upstream PR: RRA carry/overflow fix to anarkiwi/deity-informant (vendored 6510_illegal.sinc)
description:
grm-o9k fixed RRA's carry-out and signed-overflow computation in data/languages/6510_illegal.sinc.
That file is VENDORED, and its upstream is NOT Ghidra:

    https://github.com/anarkiwi/deity-informant
    commit 1ec8c31646f142e11e77b84215bfb970f7675fce
    ghidra/6510/data/languages/6510_illegal.sinc
    Copyright 2026 Josh Bailey, Apache-2.0

So this is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT upstream PR, to a different repo and maintainer than grm-ef46
(which targets NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra's 6502.slaspec for the ADC half).

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING, beyond good citizenship. The file's own banner reads "VENDORED THIRD-PARTY
FILE -- keep byte-identical to upstream so re-syncs stay a clean diff." Our RRA change is now the
ONLY divergence from upstream. Every future re-sync has to carry it by hand, and a re-sync that
forgets silently reintroduces the bug. An accepted PR retires that burden permanently and lets the
file go back to byte-identical.

THE BUG, in upstream's terms. RRA is ROR-then-ADC, and upstream's RRA deliberately mirrors stock
Ghidra 6502.slaspec's ADC idiom -- which is itself wrong (that is grm-ef46). So upstream inherited
two defects through a faithful copy of a faulty model:

  (1) C = carry(A, v) is evaluated BEFORE the carry-in is folded in, so a carry-out arising solely
      from the carry-in is lost.
  (2) V = C sets SIGNED overflow to the UNSIGNED carry; they are different flags.

THE PATCH, which is small and ports unchanged (our version, minus our vendoring-header note):

     local tmpC = C;
    +local oldA = A;
    -C = carry(A, v);
    -A = A + v + tmpC;
    +C = carry(A, v);
    +A = A + v;
    +C = C || carry(A, tmpC);
    +A = A + tmpC;
     resultFlags(A);
    -V = C;
    +V = ((oldA ^ A) & (v ^ A) & 0x80) != 0;

The two-step carry chain is required because SLEIGH's carry() tests exactly ONE addition. It is
exact, not conservative: tmpC <= 1 and a partial sum that already wrapped is small, so the two
partial carries can never both be set, making the OR the true carry-out.

ARR and ISC are NOT affected and should be left alone -- ARR uses its own bit6/bit5 formulas for
C and V, ISC routes through subtraction_flags1. Upstream's file header currently says the derived
illegals "mirror" the base spec's approximate ADC V; if the PR lands, that sentence needs updating
too, and our copy already carries the rewritten wording.

EVIDENCE TO OFFER. Four p-code vectors in AdcRraFlagVectorTest cover all four quadrants of the
C/V truth table for RRA on 6510:LE:16:undoc, reaching the same (A, op1, tmpC) triples as the ADC
set by choosing the pre-rotate byte and incoming C to suit. Note upstream validates its PYTHON VM
against a sidplayfp oracle; this is the SLEIGH half, which that oracle does not cover. Worth
saying plainly in the PR, since it explains how the defect survived.

BE HONEST ABOUT OUR COVERAGE in the PR. We have no corpus evidence for RRA -- every descriptor in
this repo selects a non-:undoc language variant, so RRA is undecodable in our whole real-ROM tier
(see grm-o9k's caveat comment). Vectors are the entire basis. Do not imply otherwise.

NEEDS THE OWNER'S GITHUB IDENTITY, and a look at whether deity-informant asks for a CLA or has
contribution guidelines. Same standing as grm-ef46, grm-b3m and grm-6xh.

title: Upstream Ghidra PR: 6502 ADC computes carry-out and overflow incorrectly
description:
grm-o9k fixed two genuine defects in ADC that this repo INHERITED VERBATIM from Ghidra's own
Ghidra/Processors/6502/data/languages/6502.slaspec:127-138 (verified identical at tag
Ghidra_12.1.2_build, and still present at 12.1.3). They are upstream's bugs, not ours, and every
Ghidra user disassembling 6502 code has them:

  (1) C = carry(A, op1) is evaluated BEFORE the carry-in is folded in, so a carry-out arising
      solely from the carry-in is lost. A=$FF, op=$00, C=1 -> real 6502 sets C=1; the spec clears
      it. This breaks the CLC / LDA lo1 / ADC lo2 / LDA hi1 / ADC hi2 idiom that every 16-bit add
      on the platform is built from.
  (2) V = C sets SIGNED overflow to the UNSIGNED carry. A=$50, op=$50, C=0 -> real 6502 sets V=1;
      the spec gives V=0. Any decompiled code branching on BVC/BVS after ADC is mis-modeled.

Our fix, already landed and gated here, is small and self-contained -- see grm-o9k's comment for
the two-step carry chain, the standard ((A^result)&(op1^result)&0x80) overflow formula, and the
eight-vector truth-table test. It ports to 6502.slaspec essentially unchanged.

SBC is NOT affected upstream either: it uses the subtraction_flags1 macro, which already
implements the correct bit formula. So the patch is confined to the ADC body.

NEEDS THE OWNER'S GITHUB IDENTITY, which is why this is a separate bead rather than part of
grm-o9k. Same shape as grm-b3m (jumptable.cc stride-aware guard) and grm-6xh
(ConstantPropagationContextEvaluator.setMinStoreLoadOffset wrong field); follow whatever
precedent those establish for CLA and PR framing. grm-phv is the in-repo precedent the original
bead pointed at for "fix locally, offer upstream afterwards".

Worth stating in any PR: we measured the blast radius on our side and it was ZERO across 29
real NES ROM regression rows. That is evidence the change is safe, not evidence it is
unimportant -- it is a correctness fix for decompiler output and flag-dependent control flow.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: Upstream is anarkiwi/deity-informant for the RRA half, NOT NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra -- 6510_illegal.sinc is vendored from there. This bead covers the Ghidra ADC half only; grm-c9hv covers the other. Both are tracked together in docs/human-research-todo.md section 5.

title: Analyzer log output is invisible headlessly: no criterion can assert what BoardBankAnalyzer concluded
description:
Nothing this project's analyzers write with log.appendMsg() is visible in a headless run, and
that is a structural gap in the test tier, not a missing flag.

VERIFIED AT 12.1.3 (grm-gpi, 2026-08-22), two independent ways:

  - SOURCE. An Analyzer's MessageLog is ghidra.app.util.importer.MessageLog, which reaches a
    console only when someone calls MessageLog.write(). The only non-test consumer of
    AutoAnalysisManager.getMessageLog() in the entire Ghidra tree is AutoAnalysisPlugin -- the
    GUI's Window > Analysis Messages. AnalysisScheduler merely passes it into AnalysisTask.
    HeadlessAnalyzer never references it at all.
  - EMPIRICALLY. neswrappertest.nes (a fixture with live wrapper/helper functions) through
    analyzeHeadless, grepping the whole log for "helper": the line never appears.

DO NOT CONFUSE THIS WITH THE LOADER CASE. CLAUDE.md's loader-validation convention ("a rejection
test must assert on log content, never on exit status") is about the IMPORTER's MessageLog, which
the import path does write. Loader log = visible headlessly. Analyzer log = GUI-only. The two
conventions look identical in code and behave oppositely.

WHAT THIS COSTS US, concretely. BoardBankAnalyzer.java:291 logs its sorted bank-switch-helper
name list -- the single most useful summary of what helper discovery concluded, and the natural
thing to assert in a banktest criterion. It cannot be asserted. grm-gpi is blocked on exactly
this: the two-wrappers-one-helper admission outcome is invisible to every headless probe, so a
fixture can only work around the contest (which make_prg_skip does, by giving site A its own
switch at $C152) rather than pin it. grm-5tl.19 is about the same log's content and has the same
problem from the other side -- it asks to suppress a line nobody can currently observe.

DIRECTIONS, none decided:

  (a) MIRROR TO Msg.info(). Cheapest. Analyzer logs a line both to the MessageLog (GUI) and via
      Msg.info(), which analyzeHeadless does print. Risk: noise in every headless run and in the
      GUI's own console; wants a level or an analyzer option so it is opt-in.
  (b) SURFACE AS PROGRAM STATE. Write the helper set into something a -postScript can read -- a
      program property map, a plate comment on each admitted helper, or a bookmark. Strictly more
      testable than text (VerifyBankTest already reads program state for everything else), and it
      survives into a saved project so the GUI benefits too. Heavier: it is a persisted artifact,
      so it needs a name, a format, and a decision about whether it ships to users.
  (c) A DEDICATED DUMP SCRIPT, committed. A ghidra_scripts/DumpBankHelpers.java that reconstructs
      and prints the set. Keeps production output unchanged, but reconstructs rather than observes
      -- it can drift from what the analyzer actually did, which is the one thing being tested.

(b) is the most useful if the goal is assertable criteria; (a) is the most useful if the goal is
just "an agent can see what happened". They are not exclusive.

Sizing note: this is filed P4 as a deliberate "chase later" at the owner's direction, not because
it is small. It unblocks grm-gpi and touches grm-5tl.19.

title: SNES machine target: 65816 descriptor, ROM loader, and LoROM/HiROM mapping
description:
SNES machine target: 65816 descriptor, ROM loader, and LoROM/HiROM mapping

PLACEHOLDER/SHAPING BEAD -- filed 2026-08-17 because the SNES side has been referenced
repeatedly (grm-1.7.3, the grm-c9d SPC700 epic, the .dis corpus) but has never had a bead of
its own. Nothing here is committed to; the point is that the work stops being invisible.

WHY IT IS COMING INTO VIEW NOW: grm-c9d has made SPC700 a first-class platform with a
vendored, vector-verified language, and grm-1.7.3 wants to extract SPC uploads FROM a SNES
ROM. Both of those need something to import the ROM in the first place, and today this
project has no SNES loader, no 65816 language, and no machine descriptor.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE, roughly, and each part is its own question:
 * 65816 LANGUAGE. Ghidra ships a 65816 processor -- CHECK IT FIRST rather than assuming, and
   if it exists, evaluate it the way grm-y7d evaluated SPCdra (decode coverage vs semantics),
   since the SPC700 exercise showed a shipped-looking spec can be badly wrong underneath.
   If it is sound this part is free, which would change the whole cost of this bead.
 * MEMORY MAP. LoROM vs HiROM vs ExHiROM is the SNES's banking problem and maps directly onto
   this project's existing descriptor/overlay machinery -- the same "which occupant is home,
   which are overlays" question already solved for C64/NES (see the
   ghidra-overlay-reference-resolution memory). The header at $FFC0/$FFB0 and its checksum
   complement identify the layout; detection must handle the 512-byte copier header, which
   the .dis corpus already shows varies (three of four sample ROMs need +0x200, lemmings.smc
   does not).
 * LOADER. .smc/.sfc/.fig, header detection, mirroring, and the hardware register block
   ($2100-$21FF PPU/APU, $4200-$43FF CPU/DMA) as typed IO -- directly analogous to the
   existing C64/NES loaders.

EXISTING ASSET, and the reason this bead is cheaper than it looks: the game-music-extraction
corpus (Z:/git/game-music-extraction/snes/) contains PER-BANK 65816 DISASSEMBLIES of four
titles -- som00-03 plus som7e (WRAM bank $7E), ff3's f3-00 through f3-07, fzero00, and
lem00/01/08 -- carrying both automated hardware-register annotations and the owner's own hand
comments. Concretely useful here for:
   - IO register naming: the automated comments are a ready-made $2100-$43FF register
     vocabulary ("Address for VRAM Read/Write (Low Byte)", "Number Bytes to Transfer (Low
     Byte) (DMA)", "APU I/O Port"), i.e. a starting point for the descriptor's IO typing
     rather than transcribing a wiki table.
   - Bank-layout evidence: the file naming and addresses show how each title's banks map,
     which is a cross-check on LoROM/HiROM detection.
   - Spot-checking any 65816 language we adopt against real shipped code.
See grm-uy9s for the automated-vs-hand comment discriminator (a frequency threshold) and for
the standing caveat that these listings are NOT an oracle -- the disassembler that produced
them may be less accurate than Ghidra's, and they cover only the chunks the owner needed.

RELATION TO grm-1.7.3: that bead can proceed without this one for the SPC700 side (it already
has extracted .bin uploads and hand-located uploader routines to work from), but a real
end-to-end "import a SNES ROM, find the upload, produce an SPC700 Program" needs this.

NOT SCOPED, NOT ESTIMATED, NOT SCHEDULED. This needs a product decision from the owner about
whether SNES becomes a supported machine or stays a means to the SPC700/music end -- the same
call that grm-y7d settled for SPC700. Filed at P4 pending that.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-17 to this bead's "MEMORY MAP" bullet, per the owner: LoROM/HiROM is
DECISIVE FROM THE ROM HEADER and is not an open question. My wording listed it as "its own
question", which wrongly implied a judgment call. There is none -- it is a lookup.

What is actually mechanical, so the bead does not overstate the work:
 * The header sits at a mapping-dependent offset -- $7FC0 for LoROM, $FFC0 for HiROM (and
   $40FFC0 for ExHiROM). The apparent chicken-and-egg is resolved the standard way: read the
   candidate locations and accept the one whose checksum and checksum-complement are
   consistent (they must sum to $FFFF), with the mapping byte at $xxD5 corroborating.
 * The only genuine wrinkle is the 512-byte copier header, which shifts every offset. The
   corpus already shows this is not uniform -- three of four sample ROMs need +0x200 and
   lemmings.smc does not -- so it must be DETECTED (file size modulo 32 KB is the usual test)
   rather than assumed. That is the one place a naive implementation goes wrong.

So the SNES memory-map work is: detect copier header, locate and validate the header, read the
mapping byte, then EXPRESS the resulting layout in this project's descriptor/overlay machinery.
Only the last of those is design work, and it is the same shape as the C64/NES descriptors
already shipped. Detection is a small amount of well-specified code.

THIS MAKES THE BEAD CHEAPER THAN IT READS. Combined with the possibility that Ghidra's shipped
65816 language is sound (untested -- evaluating it is agent work on the grm-y7d template), a
"yes" to the SNES machine target may be substantially less work than the original description
implies. The open item in docs/human-research-todo.md section 4 stands, but it is a product
decision about whether SNES is a supported machine, NOT a question about mapping detection.

title: Offer SPC700 semantic fixes upstream to qwertymodo/SPCdra (optional)
description:
Offer our SPC700 semantic fixes back to qwertymodo/SPCdra as pull requests. USER-REQUESTED
2026-08-16, and explicitly framed as optional: "it would be nice if we could PR our changes to
spcdra in case they want to incorporate them. but that a nice to have, not a requirement, and if
our stuff diverges so much that it's not worthwhile to make contributions upstream, that's OK."

So this bead may legitimately be closed as won't-do. It is NOT a gate on anything.

WHY IT IS PLAUSIBLE: upstream is alive (Apache-2.0, last commit 2026-03-04 porting to the Ghidra
v12 API, 2 open issues), the licence runs both ways, and the defects are real bugs rather than
matters of taste. Every fix below is independently useful to anyone using SPCdra as-is.

THE FIXES SPLIT INTO TWO CLASSES, and only one of them is realistically upstreamable:

 CLEANLY UPSTREAMABLE -- self-contained, one to a few lines each, no structural change:
   * CMP carry inverted (and the same inversion in aluSBC)
   * aluADC hardcoding $(NF) = 0; V never computed in aluADC/aluSBC
   * ASL/ROL carry: `$(CF) = (A & 0x80)` truncated to a 1-bit bitrange, so carry can never set
   * INC/DEC (all forms) setting no flags; likewise MOVW/INCW/DECW/ADDW/SUBW/MUL/DIV
   * MOV dp,X (0xD8) / MOV dp,Y (0xCB) adding the index to the address
   * ASL/LSR/ROL/ROR dp+X storing the 2-byte address to the unindexed location (4 instances)
   * OR1/AND1/EOR1 bit-test logic, including the `/`-complement forms
   * the AND1/OR1/MOV1 operand decode (packed 13-bit address + 3-bit index, not two bytes)
   * TSET1/TCLR1 flags; NOP emitting an opaque CALLOTHER
   * the 7 remaining author `#TODO`s

 PROBABLY NOT UPSTREAMABLE -- the ADDR8/ADDR16 double-dereference root fix. Whatever shape
 grm-c9d.3 settles on (change the subtable and revise every memory-touching body, or split into
 address-valued and dynamic subtables) it is a wide structural change to a spec whose author may
 have his own view. Offer it as an issue with the p-code evidence FIRST and let him rule on shape,
 rather than opening a large PR cold. This is the grm-b3m lesson applied early: the measurement
 was worth more than the patch, and asking about fix shape beat guessing.

CONSTRAINT THIS PLACES ON grm-c9d.3 -- recorded there too, and it is the only thing about this
bead that is time-sensitive:

  Keep the vendored spec on a tracked fork branch and land the semantic fixes as SMALL,
  INDIVIDUALLY-SCOPED COMMITS with real messages, so cherry-picking the upstreamable subset later
  is a `git cherry-pick`, not an archaeology exercise.

That costs nothing if we never PR, and is the entire difference between "possible" and "not worth
it" if we do. The infrastructure precedent already exists: D:/git/ghidra-fork on branch
grm/jumptable-lowest-target is exactly this arrangement for Ghidra itself.

ALSO WORTH CARRYING UPSTREAM REGARDLESS OF THE PATCHES: grm-c9d.2's vector harness results. "Here
are N opcodes failing against SingleStepTests/spc700, with the p-code" is a better contribution
than any single patch, needs no agreement on fix shape, and is exactly what a maintainer of an
untested spec cannot easily produce himself. Consider leading with that.

title: Settle Raikaru/ghidra-spc700 provenance vs SPCdra; mine its P-flag handling
description:
Diff Raikaru/ghidra-spc700's slaspec against SPCdra's and settle whether it is an independent
implementation or derived from SPCdra. Housekeeping, not blocking.

WHY IT MATTERS despite being P4: it is labelled MIT with a BLANK copyright line ("Copyright (c)
2026"), its slaspec is a similar size to SPCdra's (29 KB vs 31 KB), and its entire 14-commit
history was written in about six hours on 2026-04-26/27. If it is derived from the Apache-2.0
original then the MIT grant is not the author's to give, and anything we took from it would carry
a provenance problem into our repo. Cheap to settle, embarrassing to get wrong.

IF IT IS INDEPENDENT it is worth mining rather than adopting: it is the only SPC700 Ghidra module
with any automated verification (headless mnemonic/operand-text/semantic smoke tests in CI against
Ghidra 12.0.4), and its README claims direct-page P-flag tracking, which SPCdra does not implement
-- the P flag selects the $00/$01 direct page and our vendored spec ignores it entirely. That
specific feature may be worth reimplementing regardless of provenance, since it is a real ISA
behaviour and a correctness gap.

Do not adopt its decode table as a base without settling the provenance question first.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
SUPERSEDED IN PART by grm-c9d.2, and DEPRIORITIZED as a blocker. Ruled 2026-08-17: do NOT do
this before grm-c9d.3; barrel ahead with the rewrite and do not pull this in on the way.

THIS BEAD HAS TWO HALVES AND THEY NOW HAVE OPPOSITE FATES.

HALF 1 -- "mine its P-flag handling" -- IS SUPERSEDED. It was filed when reading another
implementation was the only route to direct-page P semantics. The vector harness is now a
strictly better oracle, measured rather than borrowed:

  sample cases: 8192, with P (PSW bit 5) set in 4120 of them = 50.3%
  E4 (MOV A,dp) alone: 18 of 32 sampled cases run with P=1
  worked example, E4 with P=1: initial ram [[372,15],...] -> final a=15, and 372 = 0x0174

That last line is the whole question answered by data: MOV A,$74 with P=1 must read 0x0174,
not 0x0074. The suite exercises P across every opcode, so grm-c9d.3 gets per-opcode ground
truth for free and needs nobody else's implementation to model it.

HALF 2 -- the provenance question -- SURVIVES, but REFRAMED AS A PROHIBITION rather than a
task. Raikaru/ghidra-spc700 is MIT with a BLANK copyright line, all 14 commits inside ~6
hours, and a slaspec close enough in size to SPCdra's (29 KB vs 31 KB) that derivation is
plausible. Until that is settled, DO NOT READ IT. Reading a possibly-mislabelled derivative
and then writing similar code muddies our own provenance for no informational gain -- and
grm-c9d.6 (offering our fixes back to SPCdra) depends on our changes being cleanly ours.
Risk unchanged, value now near zero: that is a bad trade, so the correct action is to leave
it alone rather than to investigate it.

WHY P MUST LAND INSIDE THE ADDR8 COMMIT, not as a follow-up: ADDR8 today is
"local tmp:2 = zext(imm8:1); export *:2 tmp" -- hardcoded page 0 AND the double-dereference.
Correct behaviour is a runtime (P ? 0x100 : 0) | imm8, and it must be RUNTIME rather than a
sleigh context assumption because SETP/CLRP mutate P during execution. So the P fix and the
double-dereference fix are the same edit to the same subtable. Sequencing this bead first
would not inform that edit; deferring P would mean restructuring ADDR8 twice.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN HALF 1: nothing routine. Only a case where the vectors are ambiguous about
intended p-code SHAPE (not behaviour) -- e.g. if a correct-by-vectors ADDR8 turns out to
decompile badly and we want to see how another implementation structured it. That is a
question about Ghidra ergonomics, not about SPC700 semantics, and it should be asked only
after the vectors are green.

title: SPC700 .spc loader: 64K snapshot, DSP block, correct register names, entry-point recovery
description:
Write our own .spc loader. SPCdra's is 5.4 KB / one file and is NOT worth vendoring -- reading it
was what established that the loader is not the valuable half of that project (grm-y7d).

WHAT SPCdra's LOADER DOES, as the baseline to beat: one 64K RAM block from file offset 0x100;
~15 hardware register labels at $F0-$FF plus IPL at $FFC0; entry PC read from file offset 0x25,
with a loader option to override it. That is the whole thing.

WHAT OURS SHOULD ADD:
 * The DSP register block -- SPCdra labels the DSP ADDRESS/DATA ports at $F2/$F3 but nothing
   behind them. The 128 DSP registers are where the interesting audio state lives.
 * Correct register names. SPCdra's $FC and $FF are labelled TIMER3/COUNTER3; they are timer and
   counter 2. Do not inherit the typo.
 * The IPL ROM contents at $FFC0-$FFFF, not just a label.
 * Descriptor-driven placement if it fits the existing machines/*.yaml pattern -- a .spc is a flat
   64K image with a fixed IO page, which is close to what the descriptor tier already expresses.

ENTRY POINT, and this is the real usability problem worth solving: the PC stored in the .spc
header is wherever the CPU happened to be when the snapshot was taken, NOT the driver entry point.
SPCdra's README works around this by telling the user to run bsnes-plus, set an execute breakpoint
on the S-SMP bus, and read the address by hand. That is a genuinely bad out-of-box experience and
it is the natural place for us to do better -- .spc rips are full 64K RAM snapshots, so the driver
is entirely present and reachable by analysis rather than by emulator archaeology. Worth its own
increment if it does not fall out cheaply.

Note the GME tie-in: .spc rips are the fastest path to an AKAO driver disassembly target and need
no SNES-side extraction at all, which is why this bead does not depend on grm-1.7.3.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
DEMOTED P3 -> P4 on 2026-08-16 (user). ".spc" loading is "a nice feature but not my primary
motivator" -- GME work runs from the GAME ROM via the grm-1.7.3 upload extraction, not from .spc
rips. This bead's description overstated the .spc path's importance ("the fastest path to an AKAO
driver disassembly target"); that sentence reflected the original grm-y7d framing, not the user's
workflow. Nothing depends on this bead; do not sequence around it.

The description's ENTRY-POINT section is still worth keeping, but it is no longer this bead's
problem to solve first. The ROM-side upload carries the start address in the IPL handshake, so
grm-1.7.3 recovers it natively; this bead should CONSUME that mechanism rather than build a second
one. If it lands first for some reason, the bsnes-plus-breakpoint workaround SPCdra documents is
the bar to beat, not the design to copy.

title: One-shot analyzer front-end for the 6502 skip-idiom repair, sharing one recognizer with the script
description:
Offer the 6502 skip-idiom repair as a ONE-SHOT ANALYZER (Analysis > One Shot > ...) in addition
to ghidra_scripts/FixSkipInstructions.java, which grm-pfp shipped and which stays the reference
implementation.

WHY A ONE-SHOT AND NOT AN ORDINARY ANALYZER. Automatic-on-import was considered when grm-pfp
shipped and rejected on measurement, and that ruling stands: the repair MUTATES THE INSTRUCTION
STREAM (setLengthOverride truncates a real instruction and disassembles inside its operand), and
the GME-wide sweep found the idiom rare -- 12 of 19 titles have NO carrier at all, and only 9 of
41 candidates corpus-wide are confident enough to apply. An analyzer that runs by default would
be doing nothing on most programs and doing something irreversible-looking on the rest, without
anyone asking. A one-shot is the honest middle: opt-in per program, but reachable from the
Analysis menu without going through the Script Manager.

WHAT IT BUYS OVER THE SCRIPT, concretely -- this is not just a second door:
  - THE ANALYSIS OPTIONS PANEL. An Analyzer gets registerOptions/optionsChanged, so carriers,
    weak and function become real, persisted, per-program options with descriptions and defaults.
    The script cannot have those in the GUI at all: the Script Manager passes no arguments, which
    is why grm-pfp had to add askYesNo prompts as the only way to reach dry-run interactively.
  - IT RUNS INSIDE THE ANALYSIS FRAMEWORK, so newly disassembled entries are picked up by the
    normal added()/re-run machinery instead of the script's explicit analyzeChanges call.
  - It appears where a user looks for it when they suspect the problem, next to the other
    RetroMachines analyzers, rather than in a script list.

API, verified against Ghidra_12.1.2_build: AbstractAnalyzer.setSupportsOneTimeAnalysis()
(AbstractAnalyzer.java:54-59) plus setDefaultEnablement(false). Every analyzer this repo ships
today sets setDefaultEnablement(true) and none is one-shot, so this would be the first -- expect
to learn something about how the one-shot path interacts with our re-run gates.

*** THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT THAT MATTERS: DO NOT FORK THE LOGIC. *** The recognizer (carrier
classification, the REFERENCED/STRONG/WEAK tiering, the convergence test) and the repair
(setLengthOverride + disassemble + bookmark swap + function) must live in ONE place that both
front-ends call. RunFromElsewhere/RunFromElsewhereTransfer is the shipped precedent for exactly
this split -- all the logic behind retromachines.RunFromElsewhere, with the script collecting
arguments and nothing else -- and the skip work should be refactored the same way as part of this
bead, not left as two copies that drift. The fixture (nesskiptest, nes-banking chunk) asserts on
the SCRIPT's console output, so it keeps covering the shared core after the move; the analyzer
front-end would want its own coverage.

ACCEPTANCE: the repair is reachable from Analysis > One Shot with carriers/weak/function exposed
as analysis options; the recognizer and repair live in a single shared class both front-ends
call; nesskiptest still passes unchanged; and the analyzer does nothing on a program with no
carriers (which per the sweep is most of them).

DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE: making it a default-enabled analyzer. See the first paragraph -- that
was measured and declined, and this bead existing is not a step toward it.

title: Make the acceptance gate reproducible and CI-enforced
description:
From docs/QUALITY_REVIEW_2026-08-10.md QR-10, NARROWED by the 2026-08-11 priority review.

QR-10 originally bundled four separable things. The mechanical one -- the developer-specific Gradle path default at build-and-test.sh:147, plus a committed wrapper -- was split out to grm-ycv and can proceed independently.

What REMAINS here needs a decision from the user before any agent work starts, per CLAUDE.md's 'stop and ask' rule on product judgment:

1. Should this repo have CI at all? Enforcing the synthetic gate means a CI runner that fetches and pins a Ghidra install (the version comes from gradle.properties' ghidraTargetVersion). Feasible -- Ghidra is publicly downloadable -- but it is a real ongoing cost and a hosting choice.
2. Is Gradle dependency locking + verification metadata worth it here? Version strings are already pinned in build.gradle. Full verification metadata is meaningful supply-chain hardening but carries real maintenance friction for a project this size.

The real-ROM tier must stay opt-in either way: the ROMs are copyrighted and machine-local via GRM_ROM_DIR.

Do not start implementation on this bead until those two questions are answered.
acceptance_criteria: Blocked on a user decision, not on analysis. Once decided: if CI is wanted, protected merges require the synthetic acceptance gate, the runner uses a pinned/verified Ghidra install, and logs are retained on failure; if locking is wanted, offline-cache reruns resolve exactly the locked and verified artifacts. Real-ROM checks remain explicitly opt-in. If either is declined, record the decision and close that half.
notes: Priority review 2026-08-11: kept P2 but rescoped. Facts in QR-10 all check out (no gradlew, no lockfile, no verification metadata, no CI workflow, Maven Central resolution at build.gradle:123-132,250,272-274). The disagreement was scope: this is a product decision, not a defect.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text: Parked as a DECISION in docs/human-research-todo.md section 4 (2026-08-11), with both questions (CI? dependency locking?) written out. A 'no' on either is a valid answer worth recording so a future review does not re-open it.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
USER RULING 2026-08-15: DEFERRED TO BACKLOG (P2 -> P4). We are the sole contributors,
so there is no integration to continuously integrate: CI would only re-run the testing
we already require before every push. Not worth the cost of a runner that fetches and
pins a Ghidra install.

REVISIT TRIGGER: outside contributors start submitting changes. At that point the
argument flips -- CI stops being redundant re-testing and starts being the only way to
trust a contributor's claim that the gate was green. Raise back to P2 then.

SEQUENCING: grm-9ut (release builds) has a similar shape but was promoted to P2 and
should land FIRST -- it serves people who want to USE the extension, which is a real
audience today, whereas CI serves people who want to DEVELOP it, which is not.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
HELD 2026-08-15 (user): status -> blocked, label blocked-on-human.

This is NOT blocked on another bead and not blocked on analysis. It is gated on a single
product decision that only the user makes: WHETHER AND WHEN TO CUT A PUBLIC RELEASE.
Until that call, work here is speculative -- there is no audience yet to serve.

The three beads in this hold, and why they are one group:
  grm-9ut  release-build strategy on GitHub  -- ships the artifact
  grm-fy0  end-user README                   -- tells a stranger what to do with it
  grm-e7w  CI enforcement                    -- only matters once outside contributors exist

UNBLOCK TRIGGER: the user decides to make a public release. At that point release order is
grm-9ut and grm-fy0 together (a release zip nobody can use is half a deliverable), with
grm-e7w still trailing until there are actual outside contributors -- see the separate
ruling on that bead.

Do not pick these up from a ready-queue scan. Ask first.

comments.author: Chris Bongaarts
comments.text:
RULED 2026-08-16 (user): NO RELEASE ANY TIME SOON. "i don't have any plans for cutting a release
anytime soon, so the CI and release and user docs beads can all stay on the back burner."

This answers the largest blocked-on-human item in docs/human-research-todo.md section 4, which has
been retired to that file's Answered table. All three beads STAY BLOCKED at their current
priorities -- grm-9ut P2, grm-fy0 P3, grm-e7w P4. Blocked is the correct state, not a bug to fix:
it keeps speculative work out of `bd ready` scans, which is exactly why they were set that way on
2026-08-15.

NOTHING TECHNICAL IS OUTSTANDING, and that is worth restating so nobody re-derives it. Already
decided: the trigger mechanism (workflow_dispatch, 2026-07-12), the hard floor at Ghidra 12.0, the
reference workflow, and the release order -- grm-9ut and grm-fy0 ship TOGETHER, because a release
zip nobody can use is half a deliverable. When the answer changes, the work starts from those

REVISIT TRIGGER IS AN AUDIENCE, not a date. The user gave no milestone and none was asked for --

when OUTSIDE CONTRIBUTORS start submitting changes. Same shape of signal, different population:
grm-9ut/grm-fy0 wait on users, grm-e7w waits on contributors.

DO NOT re-ask this in a subsequent session's "what should we work on" sweep. The answer is
recorded, the beads are blocked, and the section-4 item is gone. A new ask is only warranted if
